chapters.title: Chapter 638: Vanderbilt’s Suffering
paragraphs: [Columbia Royal Hospital]
The seals on the trauma pod hissed with the sterile dry gasp of pressurized nitrogen.
Inside the presidential suite on the seventy-first floor of the Columbia Royal Hospital, the air tasted of many different things that weren’t nice to smell at all.

Sunlight filtered through triple-pane blast glass, but none of its warmth reached the central bed as the suite was less a convalescent room and more an aerospace laboratory stripped down for emergency metabolic salvage.
Julian Vanderbilt Senior lay propped against an articulated titanium mattress with his breath rattling like wet gravel in an empty pail.
The mechanical ventilator hooked to his throat pulsed in rhythm with the intravenous pumps.
The official communiqués issued by the Executive Board had spoken of "minor lacerations and a back-blast sustained during the explosion." and due to that, the media reported third-degree burns.
However...
The media was lying through its teeth to preserve Columbia’s sovereign credit ratings.
Beneath the sheets, the President of Columbia was a ruined shell.
Both of his arms were gone from just below the clavicles with the stumps cauterized into jagged puckered knots of black tissue and silver surgical staples.
His left leg ended three inches below the knee, sheared away when the gloves had unraveled their secondary threads, and his right thigh was pinned with six external carbon-fiber stabilization struts.

Half of his face, the square-jawed granite profile that had graced forty years of corporate bank notes, was a landscape of weeping raw dermis with his left ear reduced to a shriveled notch of scarred cartilage.
And below his navel, the pelvic girdle had shattered under the directional blast wave.

The rare gloves had not simply backfired... the runes Rowenna had woven into the sub-threads had inverted the polarity of the charge, focusing the entire forty-billion-credit detonation directly inward between his hips.
’Gone,’ Vanderbilt Senior thought, his single bloodshot eye staring unblinkingly at the white tiles of the ceiling. ’Crushed... All of it... vaporized into grease.’
"The fluid," Vanderbilt croaked, his vocal cords scraping against the plastic tube in his windpipe. "Where is the immersion bath?"
At the foot of the bed, a senior surgical nurse in starched gray scrubs checked the digital telemetry monitor.
Her hands trembled slightly as she adjusted the drip rates.

"The synthetic marrow suspension is being routed from the Central City reserves, Mr. President," she said, her voice strained, keeping her eyes fixed firmly on the glass vials. "The shipping manifest cleared customs twenty minutes ago but, as the chief surgeon noted, because you do not possess an active Lord core or even a Mana core so cellular regeneration will be severely limited... The unawakened nervous system rejects accelerated stem-grafts."
Vanderbilt’s jaw clamped shut with the muscle bulging on the unburned side of his face.

He wanted to reach out and he wanted to wrap thick, manicured fingers around the woman’s throat and squeeze until her eyes bulged, just as he had throttled incompetent boardroom directors for forty years but he had no hands.
There were only phantom twitches in the empty air beside his shoulders, followed by a searing phantom ache that radiated from his missing collarbones.

"Get on with it," he rasped, his voice venomous with phlegm rattling behind his teeth. "I don’t give a damn about biological purity... Bolt titanium to the bone and wire the neural bridges to synthetic servos too. If the tissue won’t knit, graft military-grade cybernetics into the sockets... I have a budget hearing with the other Directors in eighteen days and I will not attend from a basket."
"Y-Yes, sir," the nurse whispered, ducking her head and stepping back toward the telemetry bank.
Vanderbilt let his head roll back against the sanitized foam.
’Kara White.’ The name carved through his skull like a dull scalpel. ’That single-armed bitch... That gutter-born rat...’

She had smiled when she agreed to give him the gloves. That bitch had stood there in her suit, looking like a saint while she handed him a live ticking landmine wrapped in silk and Aki, that useless, unawakened little royal brat.
If Aki had simply agreed to the private marriage contract with Junior, if she had allowed the Vanderbilt line to graft its industrial wealth to the royal bloodline, none of this would have happened.
...Columbia would have secured its seat at the right hand of the World Throne.
Instead, his fleets were bankrupt, his factory lines were stalled for lack of raw star-iron, and he was rotting in an ICU bed while the World King looked elsewhere for military suppliers.
The reinforced glass door slid open with a smooth chime.
Stepping into the room was a young man in a bespoke three-piece charcoal suit cut from imported void-silk.
His hair was slicked back with expensive pomade with his signet rings gleaming under the cold fluorescent panels.
...Julian Vanderbilt Junior.
Unlike his father, Junior had emerged from the Grand Assembly incident relatively intact.
As an Awakened noble with an active Lord core, his body had accepted the medical treatment.
The fractured vertebrae he had sustained after his humiliating confrontation in the corridor had been set by royal bone-shapers, leaving only a lingering stiffness in his lower spine.

"Father," Junior said, stepping toward the foot of the bed, his voice carrying the solemn gravity of an heir assuming command. "The board is secured... I have already initiated the legal injunctions against House Bloom for their trade interference and hopefully we will hold the northern contracts."
Vanderbilt Senior’s eye flickered toward his son.
A bitter warmth stirred in his chest... At least the boy was standing, so he trusted that at the very least the lineage had an heir who could walk into an executive suite without a wheelchair.
"The girl," Senior wheezed. "And the one-armed vagrant... Kara White."
Junior’s jaw hardened, his fists clenching at his sides.

"I will handle them. The family’s honor will be repaid ten times over... Once the Khemet containment perimeter falls, Kara White will face the full weight of Columbia’s private strike divisions! I swear it to you, Father! I will take revenge for what they did to this family!"
A rare proud breath passed through Vanderbilt Senior’s teeth.
"Good... That is my blood... Break them and strip the skin from—"
Junior paused mid-stride.
His sentence choked in his throat as his groomed face violently contorted, draining of every drop of color as his eyes bugged out of his skull.
"Ah, fuck," Junior whimpered, his voice pitching up into a shrill breathless squeak.
"Junior?" Senior rasped.
The young heir did not simply sit down as his knees completely buckled, and he collapsed sideways onto the polished linoleum floor with an undignified smack.

"MY BACK!" Junior shrieked, rolling onto his side, clutching his lumbar region with both hands, curling into a tight ball as fat tears burst from his eyes. "IT WENT OUT AGAIN! THE DISK POPPED! OH GOD, THE BONE-SHAPER DIDN’T SET THE SPINAL PIN... CALL THE SURGEON! CALL THE SURGEON, IT BURNS!"
The heart-rate monitors in the suite went wild, sirens chirping across the ward.
"Code blue! Assist in Room 701!" the nurse shouted into her intercom, dropping her clipboards as three orderlies rushed through the pneumatic doors with a heavy hydraulic gurney.
"Careful with his lower lumbar!"
"Administer two hundred milligrams of neural dampener!"
"Hold his shoulders, he’s thrashing!"
Vanderbilt Senior laid motionless on the bed and unlike what one would expect, he did not yell and he did not curse either.

He simply stared at the ceiling as his only son, the recognized heir to the Republic of Columbia, the boy who was supposed to march an army into Khemet to avenge the family name, was hoisted onto a canvas stretcher like a slaughtered calf, sobbing loudly into the linoleum, clutching his rear end as he was wheeled frantically down the corridor.
The doors hissed shut and the room fell silent, save for the mocking hiss-click of the ventilator.
"I’m finished."
A hollow despair settled into the marrow of Vanderbilt’s surviving bones.

’It started,’ he thought, his single eye clouding with a cold, dead glaze. ’All of it... Every shred of bad luck, every failed contract, every ruined bone in my body... It all started the exact second I laid eyes on that black-haired woman in the meeting.’
His gaze drifted toward the small laminate nightstand near the window.
Sitting beside a box of disposable sterile gloves was a newly opened cardboard package.
Resting on the polished surface was an eight-inch hand-painted collector’s figurine.
It was the Kara White commemorative sculpt from the Heroes of the Dust series, likely purchased by one of the day nurses on her lunch break.

The miniature Lord was standing upon a vitrified black ledge with one empty sleeve pinned neatly across her chest and her dark eyes looking down with a faint mocking smile while the tiny gold Dawn Blade rested casually at her side.
Vanderbilt stared at the little plastic woman and his breath grew rapid and shallow.
"Fuck... Fuck... Fuck!"

His hip twitched as he tried to draw his right leg up beneath the sheet, straining with every remaining fiber of his unawakened core to swing his foot out and kick the tiny, smiling toy off the table, to smash it against the tile, to grind it into powder... He wanted to do a lot of things with it but nothing moved.
His leg was an immovable, leaden stump pinned to the mattress by six steel rods.

The figurine simply stood there, bathed in the midday sun, smiling serenely down at him and Vanderbilt Senior closed his eye with a dry silent sob rattling in his throat as he cursed her into the dark.
Six hundred miles to the northwest, in the quiet tree-lined suburbs of Valoria City.
The mid-afternoon bell of the central shopping pavilion chimed with three clear brassy notes that drifted over the manicured hedges and clean asphalt.
Inside the high-end boutique of the Apex Manufactory’s regional outlet, the air was cool and smelled of expensive cardamom tea.

The young receptionist behind the glass counter, a girl with neatly pinned auburn hair and the crisp starched blazer of the retail company, looked down at the three identical massive master-cartons resting on the velvet checkout runner.

"Confirming your order, ladies," the receptionist said, her polished fingernail tapping the touch-screen terminal. "Three complete royal-tier collector’s sets... Heroes of the Dust, The Blessed Land Chronicles and First Edition. That includes all eleven primary sculpts, the interlocking display bases, and the authenticated certificate of authenticity stamped with Lord Vespera’s seal if you’re lucky!"
Standing on the customer side of the marble runner were three girls.
In the center was Lia Graves.
At eleven years old, she barely reached the clerk’s shoulder, wearing a simple comfortable denim jacket over a beige sweater with her dark hair pulled back into a practical no-nonsense ponytail.
Her sharp dark eyes, carrying that same stubborn observant intensity as her older brother’s, nodded once with firm solemnity.
To her left, Penelope Whitmore leaned against the counter, her soft purple hair falling over her cheek with her hands tucked neatly into the pockets of her pleated skirt.
And to her right stood Kaede.
The younger sister of Minamoto was practically vibrating on the balls of her feet with her hands resting impatiently on the edge of the glass counter.
"That will be sixty thousand Spirit Credits in total," the receptionist said, tilting the terminal forward. "Credit card or direct transfer?"
Before Lia or Penelope could reach for their bags for anything, Kaede’s hand was already moving.
A sleek black-and-gold corporate debit card, embossed with the triple-cherry-blossom crest of the Shogunate Isles, slid smoothly across the marble runner with an oily expensive glide.
"Slide and ching, baby," Kaede declared with a smug self-satisfied grin while crossing her arms over her chest.
Penelope slowly turned her head, looking at the girl with deadpan exhaustion.

"Kaede," Penelope muttered, adjusting the strap of her shoulder bag. "You have been watching too many western action serials on the hotel network... Nobody says ’slide and ching’ in a certified retail outlet."
Kaede didn’t even blink.
She snapped her right hand into the shape of a pistol, cocking her thumb back and pointing her index finger straight at Penelope’s forehead.

"Pew, pew," Kaede deadpanned, narrowing one eye like a veteran gunslinger. "Of course I say it... Action movies are pure cinema. The explosions are huge, the cars have eight exhaust pipes, and the heroes always pay for lunch with heavy gold coins, It builds character."
The receptionist maintained a professional smile, sliding the black card through the terminal’s magnetic groove.
"Pin, please," the clerk said smoothly.
Kaede leaned forward, tapped four numbers with her thumb, and the terminal let out a pleasant, high-pitched ping.
[TRANSACTION APPROVED: 60,000 SC.]

"Thank you for shopping with the Apex Syndicate," the receptionist said, using a small brass hook to slide the three heavy gold-ribboned cartons across the counter. "May the light guide your collections."
Kaede deftly snatched her card back, flicking it into her sleeve like a hidden throwing knife, and scooped up her carton by its reinforced canvas handle.
"Let’s roll, squad," Kaede muttered under her breath, turning toward the double glass doors.
Out on the sunlit sidewalk, the three girls paused beneath the shade of an ornamental maple tree with the breeze rustling the red leaves overhead.

chapters.title: Chapter 639: Master’s Finally Home
paragraphs: Each of them held a massive cardboard box.
The glossy high-definition printing across the front showed the ruins of Iunu, framed by swirling starlight, leaping flames, and the towering silhouette of a red dragon.
Lia looked down at the box in her hands as her fingers traced the embossed gold-leaf lettering... BLESSED LAND.
A quiet, complicated knot twisted in the pit of her eleven-year-old stomach.
’Eluned is a primary Hero of Blessed Land,’ Lia thought, her brows knitting together as she remembered the quiet miraculous garden beneath the falling skyscraper.
The memory was still burned into her eyes.

The massive roots holding thirty stories of concrete... The blooming lotuses and that breathtaking gentle woman who had sat on the grass with her, answering her questions with endless patience and calling her ’Little Sister.’
Eluned had said it plainly.
’Everything we are was granted to us by Lord Silas. If we are mountains today, it is because he provided the earth upon which we stand.’
Lia had looked at the television news reports for the past twelve days.
Every single broadcast had spoken of Lord Vespera, the terrifying, single-armed Lord who commanded Blessed Land, the one who held the Northern continent in an iron grip and laughed at rifts.
’If Eluned belongs to Silas, then Silas is Lord Vespera... My big brother is the Lord of Blessed Land.’
She clicked her tongue softly, a small irritated pout pulling at the corner of her mouth.

’Why does he keep everything a secret?’ she grumbled internally. ’He tells me to finish my homework. Meanwhile, he’s running around an active war zone pretending to be an immortal warlord and not telling his own sister a single damn thing... When he gets back, I’m hiding his favorite cups...’
Beside her, Kaede was already working her fingernails beneath the tamper-evident tape on her box.

"I need to see the dragon," Kaede muttered frantically, her tongue poking out between her teeth. "The box says the deluxe Talira has actual LED lights in the mouth... If I don’t see the fire right now, I’m going to combust."
"Don’t tear it open on the sidewalk," a calm mature voice called out from the curb.
The three girls looked up.
Parked smoothly against the granite curbing was a vehicle that looked like it had been dropped directly out of a royal motor show.
It was a Vell-965.
Unlike Silas’s sharp two-seater Zenith IVR, the Vell-965 was a massive, six-passenger luxury land-cruiser finished in deep liquid midnight-emerald.

The chassis was forged from heavy sound-dampening titanium-composite alloys, with tinted panoramic glass and active suspension that made it float over cobblestones without a single vibration reaching the cabin.
Standing by the open driver’s door, wearing an elegant gray wool coat over her spotless black maid’s dress, was Martha.
The older woman’s hair was pinned back in its usual tidy knot with her hands resting comfortably on the chrome frame of the door.
The car had been a gift from Penelope’s older sister, Harper Whitmore.

After being evacuated from the Iunu ruins aboard Evelyn’s private jet, Harper had spent four days recovering in a private clinic before immediately purchasing the luxury cruiser and having it delivered directly to the Silverleaf apartment.

Martha had adamantly refused to accept the keys at first, citing the obscene multi-million-credit maintenance costs, but Harper had practically forced the digital title into her hands, insisting that the Graves household required a secure armored vehicle to ferry the children around the city while Silas was away.

"Come along, girls," Martha said with a warm maternal smile, gesturing toward the spacious rear cabin. "The wind is picking up, and you can open your parcels properly on the rug at home. Into the carriage..."
"Yes, Miss Martha," Penelope sighed, nudging Kaede’s shoulder to stop her from ripping the cardboard.
The three girls climbed into the plush, heated leather seats of the second row, sliding their massive boxes onto the floorboards between their knees.
Martha slipped behind the steering wheel with her foot pressing the starter pedal.
The Vell-965 hummed to life with a quiet purr with the dashboard displays flaring in soft amber luminescence as she engaged the drive gear and pulled smoothly away from the curb.
Kaede leaned forward, resting her chin on the back of the front passenger seat.
"Miss Martha?" Kaede asked, tilting her head. "Is Master Silas coming back today?"
Martha glanced into the rearview mirror, her kind eyes softening with a hint of quiet worry.

"I don’t know, sweetheart," Martha answered honestly, steering the heavy cruiser through the wide suburban avenues. "He hasn’t sent a single communication through the encrypted terminal for more than ten days but the news bulletins reported that the main rifts in Khemet have been suppressed... Master Silas is very strong, and he is very responsible. He will return as soon as the work is finished."
Kaede looked down at her hands, fidgeting with the hem of her jacket.
"Um," Kaede murmured, a faint, shy blush tinting the bridge of her nose. "I wanted to give him a gift. When he comes back... To thank him for rescuing us from that horrible palace."
She paused, darting a sideways glance toward Lia sitting beside her.
"There’s no problem with that, right, Lia? Just a thank-you gift?"
Lia turned her head, crossing her arms over her chest, eyeing Kaede with the cold scrutiny of an older sister guarding her territory.
"As long as you’re not interested in my brother," Lia said, her voice entirely flat and unimpressed, "a gift is fine."
Kaede’s face instantly flushed a vibrant, incandescent pink.

"I-INTERESTED?!" Kaede squeaked, her hands flying up in a frantic, uncoordinated wave. "Not at all! Why would you even say that?! He’s an older man! He’s scary! He wears that dark cloak and probably cuts monsters in half! I’m just being polite! In my country, it’s standard cultural etiquette to repay a life-debt with an appropriate material tribute!"
Lia raised one eyebrow, leaning her cheek against her palm as she looked out the tinted window.
"You’re getting remarkably defensive for someone who is innocent,’" Lia remarked dryly.
Penelope let out a soft cultured giggle from the other side, covering her mouth with her sleeve.

"Now, now, girls," Martha chuckled softly from the front seat, her eyes twinkling in the mirror. "In the Shogunate Isles, reciprocal honor is indeed a sacred tradition... Master Silas will appreciate whatever gesture Kaede chooses to offer so there is no need to tease."
Kaede slumped back into her leather seat, crossing her arms and puffing her cheeks out in an embarrassed pout.
"See? Miss Martha understands international diplomacy."
The Vell-965 glided effortlessly through the northern residential district, eventually turning off the main avenue and approaching the private security gates of the Silverleaf Complex.
The automated transponder chimed as the heavy wrought-iron gates swinging open smoothly to grant them entry.
Martha guided the emerald cruiser down the cobblestone driveway, pulling into the private garage bay beside Silas’s low-slung matte-black Zenith IVR.
She put the car in park and switched off the turbines, turning around in her seat to face the three girls.
"Do we have any homework that requires attention this afternoon?" Martha inquired, adopting her firm no-nonsense tone.
"Math worksheets," Lia sighed, unbuckling her seatbelt.
"Ancient history essays," Penelope added with a polite nod.
"I have to translate three pages of Europa trade law into classical kanji," Kaede groaned, dragging her hands down her face. "It’s pure torture..."
"You’re the one that picked that subject, deal with it."
"Hey... you don’t have to be so rude about it..."
"Then you may have one hour with your boxes," Martha decreed with a decisive nod, opening her door. "And after that, books on the table until dinner is served... Understood?"
"Yes, Miss Martha," the three chorused, scooping up their heavy master-cartons and tumbling out of the cruiser onto the garage floor.
They carried the boxes into the ground-floor foyer with their sneakers scuffing against the polished limestone.
Kaede immediately kicked off her loafers, practically peeling off her stiff school uniform blazer and tossing it onto the banister with a loud groan of relief.
"Freedom!" Kaede cheered, stretching her arms above her head. "I want food before homework. Miss Martha, please tell me there is leftover pork cutlet."

"I prepared a cold noodle salad and glazed chicken breasts before I left to pick you up," Martha laughed, hanging her wool coat on the brass rack by the door. "Wash your hands first. I’ll just run upstairs to retrieve my phone from the study... I want to see if he answers my call this time."
"Okay!"
Martha stepped past the shoe cubbies and began ascending the carpeted staircase, humming a quiet cheerful tune under her breath.
She reached the third step from the top landing and suddenly, the heavy cedar floorboards above shifted.
A tall figure stepped out of the private master suite, moving with silent fluid momentum.
Martha, caught mid-step, looked up.
Her eyes locked onto the figure as her breath caught in her throat and her foot slipping on the edge of the stair.
"Aah—!"
Martha gasped, her balance violently giving way as she began to pitch backward toward the hardwood landing below.
A blur of motion tore through the upper air.
Before Martha could even register the fall, before her spine could meet the hard edge of the steps, a firm, warm arm wrapped smoothly around her waist.
The force of the fall was absorbed in a single effortless second, bringing her back upright with the gentle stability of a stone pillar.
"Careful, Martha," a low, familiar, slightly amused voice murmured from above her. "Those stairs are steep. I really on’t need my head housekeeper cracking her hip on the banister..."
Martha blinked rapidly, her heart hammering against her ribs as she clutched the lapel of the man holding her.
Down in the foyer, the three girls froze.
Lia, Penelope, and Kaede slowly turned their heads toward the staircase, their eyes drifting upward.
Standing at the top of the landing, holding Martha securely by the waist, was Silas Graves.
His dark hair was damp, curling slightly around his ears while smelling strongly of sweet mountain mint and lavender bath salts.

He wasn’t wearing his regular clothes, and he wasn’t wearing his boots either, instead he was casually draped in an oversized, plush white terrycloth bathrobe with a golden sun-crest embroidered along the collar with his bare feet planted firmly on the landing carpet.
The foyer fell into stunned silence.
Silas slowly released Martha, giving her shoulder a light reassuring pat as the older woman caught her footing on the landing.
He looked down over the banister, his dark eyes sweeping across the three girls standing frozen among their massive cardboard boxes.
Silas rubbed the back of his neck, letting out a soft self-satisfied chuckle.

"You know, Martha," Silas remarked casually, leaning his forearms against the polished mahogany railing, "we really need to upgrade our household soaps... I just spent the afternoon bathing in thirty fathoms of imported lavender mineral foam, and I’ve decided our current lavender bars are an insult to the skin... We need the luxury stuff, you know, the kind with the gold flakes."
Lia stood at the base of the stairs.
Her small hands clenched into tight fists at her sides and her cheeks puffed out into a furious rounded pout with her dark eyes glaring up at him with enough heat to melt lead.
"You meanie!" Lia barked, her voice echoing off the foyer ceiling. "You big meanie!"
Silas blinked, looking down at his little sister with an innocent, lopsided smirk.
He raised his hand, offering a lazy, two-fingered wave.
"Oh, hey," Silas chuckled, his voice warm and easy. "Did you miss me?"
Twenty minutes later, the dining room table of the Silverleaf apartment was groaning under the volume of porcelain platters covering the polished oak.
"Ehehehe~"
Martha was practically floating.
The older woman moved between the kitchen and the dining room with a light springy bounce in her step with a radiant smile lighting up her face as she carried plate after plate into the room.

There were braised short ribs in sweet soy glaze, steaming bowls of hand-pulled wheat noodles tossed in chili-garlic oil, two platters of crispy panko-crusted chicken breasts, three varieties of pickled mountain vegetables, a clay pot of bubbling seafood stew and a massive wooden bowl of fresh sweet melon slices as well.
Silas sat at the head of the table and his terrycloth bathrobe neatly cinched with a pair of wooden chopsticks resting in his right hand.
He stared at the mountain of food before him, his eyebrow twitching slightly.

"Martha," Silas muttered, looking up at her as she set down another dish of glazed dumplings. "There are five of us in this house... This is enough sustenance to feed a medium-sized mercenary group I think for a week. Are you trying to kill me with sodium?"
Martha stopped, resting her hands on her hips, her eyes crinkling with deep warmth.

"You have been fighting in that dreadful dusty desert for nearly two weeks, Master Silas!" Martha scolded him gently, though her cheeks flushed with a soft, pleased pink. "Look at your frame! You’ve probably been eating cold military rations and dry biscuits! You must eat every single delicacy on this table, or my heart will be utterly broken."

chapters.title: Chapter 640: Using Me For My Status
paragraphs: Silas let out a soft defeated laugh, shaking his head. "Alright, alright. I’ll clear the plates. I promise."
Martha beamed, pressing her hands to her cheeks, looking down at him with adoration.
"And no more disappearing for ten days without a single message," she added, wagging a finger that trembled just slightly. "The girls pretended they weren’t counting... I counted for all of us."
The apology rose in his throat before he could stop it.
"I’m sorry, Martha. It won’t happen again."
"It will," she said, with the weary, loving certainty of a woman who had raised more than one stubborn child. "But thank you for saying it..."
"Master Silas really is the sweetest young man," she murmured softly to herself, turning on her heel with a cheerful hum. "I will go fetch the chilled pear juice and the tea service!"
She bustled back into the kitchen with the swinging door clicking shut behind her as the dining room fell into a heavy silence.
Silas picked up his chopsticks, reaching toward a dumpling but he paused as he slowly looked across the table.
Sitting on the opposite side, arranged in a neat symmetrical firing squad, were the three girls.
They hadn’t touched their chopsticks and they hadn’t picked up their water glasses either.
Lia sat directly across from him with her arms tightly crossed over her chest and her chin tilted downward, glaring at him with open hostility.
To her left, Penelope sat with her spine rigid as a ruler, her violet eyes narrowed into sharp judging slits.
To her right, Kaede was leaning forward over the table, her hands clenched on the placemat, looking at him with an expression that was roughly seventy percent awe and thirty percent deep betrayal.
Silas slowly lowered his chopsticks back onto the ceramic rest. He cleared his throat.
"Is there an issue?" Silas asked, glancing between the three of them. "Did someone fail their history exam?"
Lia didn’t blink as her dark eyes bored directly into his skull.

"So," Lia spoke, her voice dropping into a calm tone that sounded shockingly identical to Silas’s own negotiating tone. "When, exactly, were you planning on telling us that you are the Lord of Blessed Land, huh? Big brother?"
Silas choked on his own saliva.
A sharp cough tore from his throat as he caught himself on the edge of the table.
’Well, fuck,’ Silas thought, his brain rapidly assessing the damage.
He knew he had sent Eluned to protect them.

He knew Eluned, in all her divine innocence, had probably mentioned his name while chatting with them but he had assumed, or rather foolishly hoped, that the connection between ’Silas Graves, local Europa orphan’ and ’Lord Vespera, Lord of Blessed Land’ would remain slightly blurred in an eleven-year-old’s mind.
’I should have remembered,’ Silas sighed inwardly, dragging a mental hand down his face. ’Lia isn’t stupid... She connects dots faster than Tasmin.’
Silas straightened his posture, schooling his features into a calm dignified expression.

"Lia," Silas began with his voice sounding very calm. "You have to understand the sensitivity of the situation... The World Council operates under very strict regulatory frameworks regarding Lords so I was planning on explaining the entire administrative background once the—"
"I don’t care about any of that boring stuff," Lia interrupted flatly.
Silas stopped.
"What?"
Lia reached beneath her chair with both hands as she hoisted the massive, gold-ribboned master-carton onto the table, shoving the ceramic platters aside without an ounce of remorse.
Her small fingers violently tore the packaging open, bypassing the Styrofoam, reaching deep into the velvet insert, and dragging out the pristine hand-painted collector’s miniature of Eluned.
Lia slammed the figurine down onto the polished oak right beside Silas’s rice bowl.
The tiny tree-spirit stood gracefully on her faux-moss base with her translucent jade robes catching the chandelier light, smiling serenely at Silas’s teacup.
Lia leaned across the table with her face inches from his, her dark eyes sparkling with a bright look.

"Eluned is the coolest person in the entire universe!" Lia squealed, completely dropping her stern interrogator act. "She held up a literal thirty-story skyscraper with giant tree roots! She grew pretty flowers in the middle of a war zone! She called me her Little Sister, and she gave me sweet nectar to drink, and she’s a million times cooler than you could ever be!"
Silas sat frozen as his mouth slightly parted.
"I want to meet her again!" Lia demanded, slamming both of her small palms onto the table. "Summon her! Right now! Summon her into the living room so we can have dinner together!"
Silas stared at his little sister then he looked down at the tiny, smiling plastic figurine of the Former Spirit of the World Tree standing beside his dumplings.
A visible drop of cold sweat rolled down the back of Silas’s neck.
’She does know that’s not how summoning works, right?’ Silas thought, his eye twitching in silent defeat. ’She thinks I’m running a magical daycare or something?’
The small plastic face of the World Tree’s former guardian smiled placidly up from the tablecloth with her tiny jade robes frozen in a breeze that didn’t exist.
Silas looked down at it and he looked back up at his sister as his left eyebrow climbed steadily toward his hairline.
"Lia," he said, speaking slowly, with the agonizing caution of a man trying not to startle an unpinned grenade, "is that honestly how you think summoning works? Like a takeaway menu?"
The triumphant shine in her eyes flickered.
Her lower jaw set, stubbornness hardening the line of her mouth for a second before the reality of the question caught up with her. Her shoulders sagged by an inch.
"N-no," she muttered, her voice dropping into a sullen murmur.

She poked the edge of the figurine’s stand with the tip of her forefinger, spinning it half an inch against the wood. "I know. It’s only when the rifts in the sky tear open and the energy spills out across the district... That’s what the news anchors kept saying every time the red lines crossed the map. ’The anchors only open when the veil bleeds.’ The Lords can’t pull anyone into the Earth unless the pressure between the worlds balances out."
Silas let out a soft breath through his nose, resting his elbow on the edge of the dining table and leaning his cheek into the palm of his hand.
The linen sleeve of the oversized terrycloth bathrobe bunched around his forearm, white and absurdly soft against the hard grain of the dining suite.
"Right," he said quietly. "Which means no, Lia. I can’t just snap my fingers and summon Eluned into the middle of the carpet so she can eat dumplings with us."
Her forehead puckered into a deep miserable crease as her chin dipped toward her chest and her dark ponytail sliding forward over her shoulder.
She looked every bit eleven years old, not the terrifyingly observant girl who read people like toys, but just a kid who had been promised something shiny and then told the store was closed.
Silas’s chest tightened with a familiar ache settling between his ribs.
"Hey," he said, his tone softening until the rasp of the desert battles had washed out of it completely. "Listen to me."
She didn’t look up, but her finger stopped spinning the toy.

"You can write to her," he said. "Get a sheet of that heavy paper Martha bought for your calligraphy drills... Write down whatever nonsense you want to tell her and when I head back into the Sovereign Realm to check the territory, I’ll hand it to her myself. I swear it."
Lia’s lashes lifted.
She peered at him from beneath her bangs, her dark brown eyes searching his face for any trace of older-brother mockery.
"You won’t read it?" she demanded, sharp as a rusted knife.
"Not a word," Silas said, raising his right palm flat. "I’ll be the best mailman in the world..."
She chewed the inside of her lower lip for three seconds, calculating the terms, before nodding once with firm solemnity.
"Fine but I’m using the lavender ink!"
"Use whatever ink you want."
She was already drafting it behind her eyes, he could tell.
Her lips moved faintly around half-formed sentences and he caught the words ’skyscraper’ and ’flowers’ and, bizarrely, ’please say hi to the dragon’ slipping past her teeth.
’Haah... She’s so cute.’
He decided that whatever Eluned made of that letter, she would treasure it, and that he would deliver it with a perfectly straight face.
Silas picked his chopsticks back up with his eyes lingering on the three of them across the table.

Penelope was calmly arranging her pickled radishes into a neat square on her ceramic plate, while Kaede was staring down at her own unopened carton with her fingers drumming an anxious silent rhythm against the edge of the table.
A thought struck him as he was slightly baffled.
’Wait,’ Silas thought, his brow knitting slightly as he rested his chopsticks on the porcelain bridge. ’Is that it? Are they seriously not going to grill me about being Lord Vespera?’

He had spent the last two weeks under an assumed name, wearing Kara White’s face, parading around on the back of an eighty-yard dragon while the entire international press corps turned the name "Blessed Land" into the most scrutinized military brand on the globe.

The territory had stopped being merely influential and become a bit of a world power that had helped evacuate people from an incursion single-handedly before the World Council Marshals arrived on Day 3.
...And his little sister had just skipped over the entire revelation because she wanted a green-haired spirit to come over for dinner?

"Lia," Silas said, his voice flat with lingering suspicion. "Aren’t you going to ask me anything else? You just dropped the fact that you figured out Blessed Land belongs to me. You don’t have... I don’t know, twenty other questions? No lectures about lying?"
Lia picked up her tea glass, took a small measured sip, and waved her free hand through the air with airy dismissal.

"Why would I?" she said. "I’m already a fan of Blessed Land. I’ve been watching the live-stream relays from the Khemet towers for two weeks... If you own it, that just means my favorite team has a home field."
Silas stared at her. "That’s your entire takeaway?"

"Well, duh," she said, rolling her eyes with a terrifying look that only an eleven-year-old girl could muster. "I’m not stupid, Big Bro. I know why you didn’t tell me. If the neighborhood knew you were a high-ranking lord with an unregistered territory, the apartment would be swarmed with news vans and recruiters every single morning... I wouldn’t be able to walk to the tram stop without three bodyguards with machine guns stepping on my heels. You were hiding it because you wanted me to have a normal life. Right?"
Silas paused.
The half-eaten dumpling in his bowl cooled slowly in its puddle of chili oil.
He looked at the girl across from him, her clean clothes, the books stacked neatly on the side table, the bright healthy color in her cheeks and then he nodded once.
"Yeah," he said, the word rough in his throat. "That was the idea."
Lia set her glass down with a soft hollow clink as the sharp teasing edge melted out of her face, leaving behind something small and painfully soft.
"Thank you, Big Brother," she murmured.
Her eyes were warm and bright with an unshakeable trust that made Silas feel like a giant who had spent his whole life kneeling in the dirt. "I really am glad. That’s why I love you so much."
Silas blinked, a sudden ridiculous tightness seizing the back of his throat as he looked away, clearing his throat into his fist.
"Right... Well... Don’t go getting sentimental over cold pork."
"Which is why," Lia continued, her voice instantly pivoting into a terrifying business-like chirp, "you’re going to do this for me!"
She dropped out of her chair before he could react, scurrying around the edge of the dining table with the cardboard lid of her collector’s carton clutched in both hands.
She thrust the heavy, gold-foiled cardstock directly into his face, nearly knocking his water glass off the table.

"Look!" she beamed, pointing her finger at the glossy white banner spanning the lower half of the box art. "It’s the limited-run packaging! The official ones signed by the Apex Syndicate sold out during the pre-order launch, but the blanks are the ones the collectors actually bid on! Sign it!"
Silas leaned back, batting the cardboard an inch away from his nose.
"Sign it? What are you talking about?"

"Sign your name!" she ordered, thrusting an indelible marker into his fingers. "I’m taking it to school tomorrow! Tommy from the fourth-grade track team said his uncle works for House Sterling and has a signed badge from Sir Gareth, but if I bring a box personally inked by Lord Vespera, his entire table is going to die of jealousy!"
Silas let out a wounded gasp, pressing his palm flat against his terrycloth lapel.

"You parasite," he groaned, narrowing his eyes at her with comic betrayal. "You don’t love me at all! You’re just using my battlefield trauma for playground clout! I survived a whole raid, and you want to use my signature to bully a ten-year-old named Tommy?!"

sentences.text: Silas let out a soft defeated laugh, shaking his head.
"Alright, alright.
I’ll clear the plates.
I promise."
Martha beamed, pressing her hands to her cheeks, looking down at him with adoration.
"And no more disappearing for ten days without a single message," she added, wagging a finger that trembled just slightly.
"The girls pretended they weren’t counting...
I counted for all of us."
The apology rose in his throat before he could stop it.
"I’m sorry, Martha.
It won’t happen again."
"It will," she said, with the weary, loving certainty of a woman who had raised more than one stubborn child.
"But thank you for saying it..."
"Master Silas really is the sweetest young man," she murmured softly to herself, turning on her heel with a cheerful hum.
"I will go fetch the chilled pear juice and the tea service!"
She bustled back into the kitchen with the swinging door clicking shut behind her as the dining room fell into a heavy silence.
Silas picked up his chopsticks, reaching toward a dumpling but he paused as he slowly looked across the table.
Sitting on the opposite side, arranged in a neat symmetrical firing squad, were the three girls.
They hadn’t touched their chopsticks and they hadn’t picked up their water glasses either.
Lia sat directly across from him with her arms tightly crossed over her chest and her chin tilted downward, glaring at him with open hostility.
To her left, Penelope sat with her spine rigid as a ruler, her violet eyes narrowed into sharp judging slits.
To her right, Kaede was leaning forward over the table, her hands clenched on the placemat, looking at him with an expression that was roughly seventy percent awe and thirty percent deep betrayal.
Silas slowly lowered his chopsticks back onto the ceramic rest.
He cleared his throat.
"Is there an issue?" Silas asked, glancing between the three of them.
"Did someone fail their history exam?"
Lia didn’t blink as her dark eyes bored directly into his skull.
"So," Lia spoke, her voice dropping into a calm tone that sounded shockingly identical to Silas’s own negotiating tone.
"When, exactly, were you planning on telling us that you are the Lord of Blessed Land, huh?
Big brother?"
Silas choked on his own saliva.
A sharp cough tore from his throat as he caught himself on the edge of the table.
’Well, fuck,’ Silas thought, his brain rapidly assessing the damage.
He knew he had sent Eluned to protect them.

He knew Eluned, in all her divine innocence, had probably mentioned his name while chatting with them but he had assumed, or rather foolishly hoped, that the connection between ’Silas Graves, local Europa orphan’ and ’Lord Vespera, Lord of Blessed Land’ would remain slightly blurred in an eleven-year-old’s mind.
’I should have remembered,’ Silas sighed inwardly, dragging a mental hand down his face. ’Lia isn’t stupid...
She connects dots faster than Tasmin.’
Silas straightened his posture, schooling his features into a calm dignified expression.
"Lia," Silas began with his voice sounding very calm.
"You have to understand the sensitivity of the situation...
The World Council operates under very strict regulatory frameworks regarding Lords so I was planning on explaining the entire administrative background once the—"
"I don’t care about any of that boring stuff," Lia interrupted flatly.
Silas stopped.
"What?"
Lia reached beneath her chair with both hands as she hoisted the massive, gold-ribboned master-carton onto the table, shoving the ceramic platters aside without an ounce of remorse.
Her small fingers violently tore the packaging open, bypassing the Styrofoam, reaching deep into the velvet insert, and dragging out the pristine hand-painted collector’s miniature of Eluned.
Lia slammed the figurine down onto the polished oak right beside Silas’s rice bowl.
The tiny tree-spirit stood gracefully on her faux-moss base with her translucent jade robes catching the chandelier light, smiling serenely at Silas’s teacup.
Lia leaned across the table with her face inches from his, her dark eyes sparkling with a bright look.
"Eluned is the coolest person in the entire universe!" Lia squealed, completely dropping her stern interrogator act.
"She held up a literal thirty-story skyscraper with giant tree roots!
She grew pretty flowers in the middle of a war zone!
She called me her Little Sister, and she gave me sweet nectar to drink, and she’s a million times cooler than you could ever be!"
Silas sat frozen as his mouth slightly parted.
"I want to meet her again!" Lia demanded, slamming both of her small palms onto the table.
"Summon her!
Right now!
Summon her into the living room so we can have dinner together!"
Silas stared at his little sister then he looked down at the tiny, smiling plastic figurine of the Former Spirit of the World Tree standing beside his dumplings.
A visible drop of cold sweat rolled down the back of Silas’s neck.
’She does know that’s not how summoning works, right?’ Silas thought, his eye twitching in silent defeat. ’She thinks I’m running a magical daycare or something?’
The small plastic face of the World Tree’s former guardian smiled placidly up from the tablecloth with her tiny jade robes frozen in a breeze that didn’t exist.
Silas looked down at it and he looked back up at his sister as his left eyebrow climbed steadily toward his hairline.
"Lia," he said, speaking slowly, with the agonizing caution of a man trying not to startle an unpinned grenade, "is that honestly how you think summoning works?
Like a takeaway menu?"
The triumphant shine in her eyes flickered.
Her lower jaw set, stubbornness hardening the line of her mouth for a second before the reality of the question caught up with her.
Her shoulders sagged by an inch.
"N-no," she muttered, her voice dropping into a sullen murmur.
She poked the edge of the figurine’s stand with the tip of her forefinger, spinning it half an inch against the wood.
"I know.
It’s only when the rifts in the sky tear open and the energy spills out across the district...

That’s what the news anchors kept saying every time the red lines crossed the map. ’The anchors only open when the veil bleeds.’ The Lords can’t pull anyone into the Earth unless the pressure between the worlds balances out."
Silas let out a soft breath through his nose, resting his elbow on the edge of the dining table and leaning his cheek into the palm of his hand.
The linen sleeve of the oversized terrycloth bathrobe bunched around his forearm, white and absurdly soft against the hard grain of the dining suite.
"Right," he said quietly.
"Which means no, Lia.
I can’t just snap my fingers and summon Eluned into the middle of the carpet so she can eat dumplings with us."
Her forehead puckered into a deep miserable crease as her chin dipped toward her chest and her dark ponytail sliding forward over her shoulder.
She looked every bit eleven years old, not the terrifyingly observant girl who read people like toys, but just a kid who had been promised something shiny and then told the store was closed.
Silas’s chest tightened with a familiar ache settling between his ribs.
"Hey," he said, his tone softening until the rasp of the desert battles had washed out of it completely.
"Listen to me."
She didn’t look up, but her finger stopped spinning the toy.
"You can write to her," he said.
"Get a sheet of that heavy paper Martha bought for your calligraphy drills...
Write down whatever nonsense you want to tell her and when I head back into the Sovereign Realm to check the territory, I’ll hand it to her myself.
I swear it."
Lia’s lashes lifted.
She peered at him from beneath her bangs, her dark brown eyes searching his face for any trace of older-brother mockery.
"You won’t read it?" she demanded, sharp as a rusted knife.
"Not a word," Silas said, raising his right palm flat.
"I’ll be the best mailman in the world..."
She chewed the inside of her lower lip for three seconds, calculating the terms, before nodding once with firm solemnity.
"Fine but I’m using the lavender ink!"
"Use whatever ink you want."
She was already drafting it behind her eyes, he could tell.
Her lips moved faintly around half-formed sentences and he caught the words ’skyscraper’ and ’flowers’ and, bizarrely, ’please say hi to the dragon’ slipping past her teeth.
’Haah...
She’s so cute.’
He decided that whatever Eluned made of that letter, she would treasure it, and that he would deliver it with a perfectly straight face.
Silas picked his chopsticks back up with his eyes lingering on the three of them across the table.

Penelope was calmly arranging her pickled radishes into a neat square on her ceramic plate, while Kaede was staring down at her own unopened carton with her fingers drumming an anxious silent rhythm against the edge of the table.
A thought struck him as he was slightly baffled.
’Wait,’ Silas thought, his brow knitting slightly as he rested his chopsticks on the porcelain bridge. ’Is that it?
Are they seriously not going to grill me about being Lord Vespera?’

He had spent the last two weeks under an assumed name, wearing Kara White’s face, parading around on the back of an eighty-yard dragon while the entire international press corps turned the name "Blessed Land" into the most scrutinized military brand on the globe.

The territory had stopped being merely influential and become a bit of a world power that had helped evacuate people from an incursion single-handedly before the World Council Marshals arrived on Day 3.
...And his little sister had just skipped over the entire revelation because she wanted a green-haired spirit to come over for dinner?
"Lia," Silas said, his voice flat with lingering suspicion.
"Aren’t you going to ask me anything else?
You just dropped the fact that you figured out Blessed Land belongs to me.
You don’t have...
I don’t know, twenty other questions?
No lectures about lying?"
Lia picked up her tea glass, took a small measured sip, and waved her free hand through the air with airy dismissal.
"Why would I?" she said.
"I’m already a fan of Blessed Land.
I’ve been watching the live-stream relays from the Khemet towers for two weeks...
If you own it, that just means my favorite team has a home field."
Silas stared at her.
"That’s your entire takeaway?"
"Well, duh," she said, rolling her eyes with a terrifying look that only an eleven-year-old girl could muster.
"I’m not stupid, Big Bro.
I know why you didn’t tell me.
If the neighborhood knew you were a high-ranking lord with an unregistered territory, the apartment would be swarmed with news vans and recruiters every single morning...
I wouldn’t be able to walk to the tram stop without three bodyguards with machine guns stepping on my heels.
You were hiding it because you wanted me to have a normal life.
Right?"
Silas paused.
The half-eaten dumpling in his bowl cooled slowly in its puddle of chili oil.
He looked at the girl across from him, her clean clothes, the books stacked neatly on the side table, the bright healthy color in her cheeks and then he nodded once.
"Yeah," he said, the word rough in his throat.
"That was the idea."
Lia set her glass down with a soft hollow clink as the sharp teasing edge melted out of her face, leaving behind something small and painfully soft.
"Thank you, Big Brother," she murmured.
Her eyes were warm and bright with an unshakeable trust that made Silas feel like a giant who had spent his whole life kneeling in the dirt.
"I really am glad.
That’s why I love you so much."
Silas blinked, a sudden ridiculous tightness seizing the back of his throat as he looked away, clearing his throat into his fist.
"Right...
Well...
Don’t go getting sentimental over cold pork."
"Which is why," Lia continued, her voice instantly pivoting into a terrifying business-like chirp, "you’re going to do this for me!"
She dropped out of her chair before he could react, scurrying around the edge of the dining table with the cardboard lid of her collector’s carton clutched in both hands.
She thrust the heavy, gold-foiled cardstock directly into his face, nearly knocking his water glass off the table.
"Look!" she beamed, pointing her finger at the glossy white banner spanning the lower half of the box art.
"It’s the limited-run packaging!
The official ones signed by the Apex Syndicate sold out during the pre-order launch, but the blanks are the ones the collectors actually bid on!
Sign it!"
Silas leaned back, batting the cardboard an inch away from his nose.

What are you talking about?"
"Sign your name!" she ordered, thrusting an indelible marker into his fingers.
"I’m taking it to school tomorrow!

Tommy from the fourth-grade track team said his uncle works for House Sterling and has a signed badge from Sir Gareth, but if I bring a box personally inked by Lord Vespera, his entire table is going to die of jealousy!"
Silas let out a wounded gasp, pressing his palm flat against his terrycloth lapel.
"You parasite," he groaned, narrowing his eyes at her with comic betrayal.
"You don’t love me at all!
You’re just using my battlefield trauma for playground clout!
I survived a whole raid, and you want to use my signature to bully a ten-year-old named Tommy?!"

chapters.title: Chapter 641: Kaede’s Gift
paragraphs: Lia puffed her cheeks out into two perfectly round and furious little dumplings, crossing her arms over her sweater.

"You left me alone for more than twelve whole days!" she declared fiercely. "You went to a burning desert, didn’t call once, and probably took a two-hour luxury bath before you even said hello... Exploiting your fame is the bare minimum restitution required by the sibling code!"
Silas stared at her furious pouting face for three seconds before a low helpless laugh broke through his chest.
"The sibling code, huh?" he muttered, shaking his head. "Unbelievable."
He uncapped the marker with a quiet click.
Resting the heavy cardboard against the edge of the oak table, his hand moved with fluid unhesitating grace.

He didn’t sign "Silas Graves." though... In clean sharp strokes that mimicked the handwriting that he used to sign the original boxes, he signed it Vespera with an aggressive sharp flourish at the tail.
Cap!
"There," Silas said, tossing the marker onto the table.

He reached out, planting his broad palm firmly on top of her dark head, ruffling her hair until her neat ponytail tilted sideways. "Take your spoils of war, you little monster... You’re cute, but you’re a menace."
Lia let out a triumphant squeak, clutching the signed box to her ribs like a stolen jewel, completely ignoring her disheveled hair as Penelope and Kaede giggled softly behind their hands.
The swinging kitchen door groaned open with a soft oiled whisper.

"Now, now," Martha’s warm, chiding voice drifted over the steam rising from the ceramic trays. "The master has only just returned from war, and you are already demanding tributes before the soup has cooled... Sit down, Lia. Eat your greens before I clear the rice."
"Yes, Miss Martha," Lia chimed, sliding back into her seat with an angelic unrepentant smile.
Silas watched the older woman move smoothly around the table, setting down a heavy stoneware pitcher of chilled barley tea and small dishes of pickled ginger.
Her hair was pinned into that same immaculate graying knot with her black dress and white apron were ironed to razor-sharp perfection.
’Thank you, Martha,’ Silas thought, picking up a tender strip of glazed short rib with his chopsticks.
It was a simple quiet thought.

If she hadn’t been here, if this house had been an empty concrete shell where kids were left to heat up canned beans while he went to the Sovereign Realm, coming back through that front door would have felt like returning to an armory.
She made the air smell like toasted sesame oil and clean starch... Honestly she made the world feel like something that had a right to exist.
Swipe!
A soft cool linen napkin brushed gently against the corner of his lip, dabbing away a stray fleck of sweet soy sauce.
Silas blinked, startled, his eyes tracking up the starched cuff to Martha’s face.

The head housekeeper was leaning down slightly with her expression looking serene and her eyes crinkling at the corners with a quiet pride that seemed to smooth away the last lingering static in his head.

"Eat slowly, Master Silas," she whispered, her voice low enough that the girls didn’t catch it over their bickering. "There is plenty more in the kitchen... You have carried enough iron for one season."
Across the table, Penelope lowered her voice until only Silas could hear it.

"My sister has not slept properly since Iunu," she said, pushing a radish around her plate with unusual care. "She says it is paperwork but it’s is not paperwork so I hope she’s happy when she sees you."
Then she took a composed sip of barley tea, as though she hadn’t said anything at all.
Silas felt a strange warm sheepishness touch his ears as he gave her a small lopsided smile, letting out a breath.

’You know what?’ he mused inwardly, chewing the beef as she pulled back to pour the tea. ’Martha really is quite beautiful... She’s elegant. She’s gentle... Is it just me, or am I completely surrounded by incredible women?’
Before he could follow that train of thought down its naturally ridiculous path, a small choked throat-clearing sounded from his immediate right.
Silas turned his head.
Kaede was half-out of her chair, sitting up very straight with her dark eyes fixed on the linen placemat.
Her fingers were knotted tightly around a small flat box wrapped in deep indigo mulberry paper and tied with a braided crimson cord.
"Big Brother Silas," she said, her voice stiff and careful like the way a shy child recites a speech she has rehearsed. "This is for you... A token from my place."
Penelope leaned back in her chair, resting her chin on her hands, watching with the cold gaze of an empress at the theater.
Silas set his chopsticks down.
"For me?"

"Yes," Kaede said, stepping forward and extending both arms straight out, offering the box with the rigid ninety-degree posture of a samurai delivering a dispatch. "Please accept it... It is standard protocol, to repay the debt of preservation..."
"Preservation, huh?"
Silas took the box from her hands.
The paper was textured, smelling of dried pine needle as he untied the red silk knot, peeling the paper back to reveal a shallow tray of polished black lacquer and resting inside was a bracelet.
Steel and gold had no part in it.
A single seamless strand of tightly braided midnight-black silk cord formed the band, woven through with five small, irregularly shaped beads of dark unpolished river-jade.
The stone possessed a calm damp coolness that seemed to settle against the skin like mountain rain.

"It is an old craft from the northern province of my clan," Kaede mumbled with her hands retreating to clutch the hem of her school skirt. "The river-jade is gathered from the sacred streams below the frost-line... It is said to anchor the spirit and keep the breath steady when the sky shakes, I searched seven different merchant houses before we left the capital to find one that hadn’t been tainted by modern alchemy."
Silas slipped the silk loop over his right hand and tightened it with a tug of his teeth and thumb.
The dark stone rested comfortably against his pulse point, completely unbothered by the monstrous, dormant heat of the Gold Core churning three inches beneath his ribs.
"It’s nice, Kaede," Silas said, turning his wrist under the dining room chandelier, admiring the clean, minimalist work. "Really... It fits well... Thank you."
Kaede let out a long shuddering breath, as though she had just spent three minutes submerged under ten feet of ice water.
"It is my honor!" she said, bowing so low and so fast from the waist that her forehead nearly clipped the rim of Silas’s water goblet. "I am glad that it pleases you!"
Lia rested her cheek on her fist from across the table, watching with deadpan merciless judgment.
"You’re bowing again, Kaede," Lia said. "He’s not a Shogun... You don’t have to break your back."

"Quiet, idiot!" Kaede hissed, snapping upright with her ears smoking with humiliation as she scurried back to her chair. "You have zero appreciation for the sacred aesthetic of martial reciprocation!"
"I have an appreciation for not getting hit in the nose with your skull," Penelope murmured smoothly, taking a dainty bite of her chicken.
Silas chuckled softly, resting his hand against his chin as the table dissolved back into comfortable bickering noise.
Two hours later, the afternoon light had deepened into long amber bars that stretched across the dark cedar floorboards of the living room.
The large dining table had been cleared of plates, transformed into an orderly battlefield of lined notebook paper, brass protractors, and leather-bound geography atlases.
Martha sat at the center with a pair of delicate wire-rimmed reading glasses perched on the bridge of her nose and her finger tapping rhythmically against the edge of Lia’s algebra workbook.
"Carry the third integer, little mistress," Martha murmured gently. "Do not rush the denominator... If the foundation is crooked, the spire falls."
"The denominator is stupid," Lia muttered under her breath, her pencil scratching aggressively against the paper.
Martha only smiled and turned the page.
Over the rim of her glasses she caught Silas’s eye across the room and gave him the smallest nod.
Ten feet away, sprawled horizontally across the massive L-shaped sectional couch in the center of the room, Silas was useless to the world.
’Finally, a break in my own house...’
He had kicked off his leather slippers, his bare feet hooked over the armrest and his head propped up by three oversized down pillows.

He was still wearing the fluffy white VIP bathrobe, the terrycloth belt tied loosely around his waist with one arm draped lazily behind his head while his right hand held his phone six inches from his nose.
"Haah..."
His face was a picture of pure satisfaction as his dark eyes flicked across the digital catalogs of the high-end Europa trade exchanges, his thumb scrolling with rapid efficiency.
Scroll!
[IMPERIAL SEABED ESSENCE: COLD-PRESSED MARITIME LAVENDER EXTRACT. 4,200 SC.]
[Add to Cart]
Scroll!
[RHYX COASTAL ALABASTER SALTS: INFUSED WITH SUN-DRIED CITRUS BLOSSOM. 6,800 SC.]
[Add to Cart]
Scroll!
[DIVINE SAPONIN BARS: TRIPLE-MILLED CELESTIAL MINT AND CRUSHED PEARL. 12,000 SC.]
[Add To Cart.]

’Ehehehe~’ Silas snickered silently, his lips curving into a wide shameless grin that would have terrified anybody within forty leagues. ’This is perfection... I have the exact names from Aki’s private bath. Every single bottle, every single mineral scrub, every single ridiculous luxury soap she had lined up along those marble basins... I memorized every damn label while I was scrubbing the desert off my skin.’

He had forty billion credits sitting in his major account from the Julian Vanderbilt bypass glove transaction, not to mention the gross twenty-five percent royalty stream currently flooding his commercial accounts from the Apex figurine sales... But that wasn’t the money he planned to use, he still hadn’t made any headway with the seventy five million from Ev.
He really needed to spend some money...

’I am buying thirty cases of each,’ Silas decided firmly, tapping the purchase confirmation repeatedly. ’I will never use that cheap two-credit pine-tar soap in this house ever again... Martha can take the cruiser down to the customs hub tomorrow and clear the crates.’
Somewhere beyond the veil, he reflected, Aki was standing on her first scrap of soil, staring at an empty plain and a blinking blue tab.
The thought tugged at the corner of his mouth.
’She’s fine.’
She had a Purple Core, an inventory full of cards, and the stubbornness of a woman who had spent a lifetime proving she belonged at tables that didn’t want her.
Still, he made a note to check on her the moment he could slip away, and went back to the soap.

At the dining table, Lia’s pencil paused mid-equation as she tilted her head, her dark eyes narrowing through the gap between her geography folio and the salt shaker, glaring across the room at the couch.
Silas was still grinning at his screen with his shoulders twitching with quiet muffled chuckles as he swiped through another luxury listing.
’Why is he smiling like that?’ Lia’s thoughts churned with dark suspicion. ’That’s the face people make in the cinema when they’re hiding something scandalous.’
Her mind flashed back to the ruined skyscraper in Iunu.
To the beautiful, green-haired goddess who had knelt beside her in the grass, smiling with that divine radiance.
’I belong to Lord Silas. In the sovereign realm, our souls are bound beneath the branches. In your mortal terms... you might consider us husband and wife.’
Lia’s eyes widened slightly.
’Is he... is he cheating on Miss Eluned?!’
The staggering scandal of the thought made her grip her pencil so hard the graphite snapped with a sharp crack.
Who was on that phone? Was it that wealthy, scary woman with the gold carriages who had visited the school? Or—
WHACK!
A heavy leather-bound volume of Classical Shogunate Prose and Grammar descended from above, smacking squarely against the top of Lia’s skull.
"Ow!" Lia yelped, clutching her head and glaring to her left.
Kaede was standing over her, holding the textbook like a club as her dark eyes burned with no-nonsense discipline.

"Focus, Lia," Kaede hissed in a fierce whisper, pointing a sharp finger at the half-finished quadratic formula on the notebook page. "If you don’t finish the third module before four o’clock, Miss Martha will not allow us to clear the carpet... The box has eleven figurines, Lia! Eleven! If we don’t start the setup now, we won’t finish anything before the sun goes down!"
