The paper was textured, smelling of dried pine needle as he untied the red silk knot, peeling the paper back to reveal a shallow tray of polished black lacquer and resting inside was a bracelet.
Steel and gold had no part in it.
A single seamless strand of tightly braided midnight-black silk cord formed the band, woven through with five small, irregularly shaped beads of dark unpolished river-jade.
The stone possessed a calm damp coolness that seemed to settle against the skin like mountain rain.
"It is an old craft from the northern province of my clan," Kaede mumbled with her hands retreating to clutch the hem of her school skirt.
"The river-jade is gathered from the sacred streams below the frost-line...

It is said to anchor the spirit and keep the breath steady when the sky shakes, I searched seven different merchant houses before we left the capital to find one that hadn’t been tainted by modern alchemy."
Silas slipped the silk loop over his right hand and tightened it with a tug of his teeth and thumb.
The dark stone rested comfortably against his pulse point, completely unbothered by the monstrous, dormant heat of the Gold Core churning three inches beneath his ribs.
"It’s nice, Kaede," Silas said, turning his wrist under the dining room chandelier, admiring the clean, minimalist work.
"Really...
It fits well...
Thank you."
Kaede let out a long shuddering breath, as though she had just spent three minutes submerged under ten feet of ice water.
"It is my honor!" she said, bowing so low and so fast from the waist that her forehead nearly clipped the rim of Silas’s water goblet.
"I am glad that it pleases you!"
Lia rested her cheek on her fist from across the table, watching with deadpan merciless judgment.
"You’re bowing again, Kaede," Lia said.
"He’s not a Shogun...
You don’t have to break your back."
"Quiet, idiot!" Kaede hissed, snapping upright with her ears smoking with humiliation as she scurried back to her chair.
"You have zero appreciation for the sacred aesthetic of martial reciprocation!"
"I have an appreciation for not getting hit in the nose with your skull," Penelope murmured smoothly, taking a dainty bite of her chicken.
Silas chuckled softly, resting his hand against his chin as the table dissolved back into comfortable bickering noise.
Two hours later, the afternoon light had deepened into long amber bars that stretched across the dark cedar floorboards of the living room.
The large dining table had been cleared of plates, transformed into an orderly battlefield of lined notebook paper, brass protractors, and leather-bound geography atlases.
Martha sat at the center with a pair of delicate wire-rimmed reading glasses perched on the bridge of her nose and her finger tapping rhythmically against the edge of Lia’s algebra workbook.
"Carry the third integer, little mistress," Martha murmured gently.
"Do not rush the denominator...
If the foundation is crooked, the spire falls."
"The denominator is stupid," Lia muttered under her breath, her pencil scratching aggressively against the paper.
Martha only smiled and turned the page.
Over the rim of her glasses she caught Silas’s eye across the room and gave him the smallest nod.
Ten feet away, sprawled horizontally across the massive L-shaped sectional couch in the center of the room, Silas was useless to the world.
’Finally, a break in my own house...’
He had kicked off his leather slippers, his bare feet hooked over the armrest and his head propped up by three oversized down pillows.

He was still wearing the fluffy white VIP bathrobe, the terrycloth belt tied loosely around his waist with one arm draped lazily behind his head while his right hand held his phone six inches from his nose.
"Haah..."
His face was a picture of pure satisfaction as his dark eyes flicked across the digital catalogs of the high-end Europa trade exchanges, his thumb scrolling with rapid efficiency.
Scroll!
[IMPERIAL SEABED ESSENCE: COLD-PRESSED MARITIME LAVENDER EXTRACT.
[Add to Cart]
Scroll!
[RHYX COASTAL ALABASTER SALTS: INFUSED WITH SUN-DRIED CITRUS BLOSSOM.
[Add to Cart]
Scroll!
[DIVINE SAPONIN BARS: TRIPLE-MILLED CELESTIAL MINT AND CRUSHED PEARL.
[Add To Cart.]
’Ehehehe~’ Silas snickered silently, his lips curving into a wide shameless grin that would have terrified anybody within forty leagues. ’This is perfection...
I have the exact names from Aki’s private bath.
Every single bottle, every single mineral scrub, every single ridiculous luxury soap she had lined up along those marble basins...
I memorized every damn label while I was scrubbing the desert off my skin.’

He had forty billion credits sitting in his major account from the Julian Vanderbilt bypass glove transaction, not to mention the gross twenty-five percent royalty stream currently flooding his commercial accounts from the Apex figurine sales...
But that wasn’t the money he planned to use, he still hadn’t made any headway with the seventy five million from Ev.
He really needed to spend some money...
’I am buying thirty cases of each,’ Silas decided firmly, tapping the purchase confirmation repeatedly. ’I will never use that cheap two-credit pine-tar soap in this house ever again...
Martha can take the cruiser down to the customs hub tomorrow and clear the crates.’
Somewhere beyond the veil, he reflected, Aki was standing on her first scrap of soil, staring at an empty plain and a blinking blue tab.
The thought tugged at the corner of his mouth.
’She’s fine.’
She had a Purple Core, an inventory full of cards, and the stubbornness of a woman who had spent a lifetime proving she belonged at tables that didn’t want her.
Still, he made a note to check on her the moment he could slip away, and went back to the soap.

At the dining table, Lia’s pencil paused mid-equation as she tilted her head, her dark eyes narrowing through the gap between her geography folio and the salt shaker, glaring across the room at the couch.
Silas was still grinning at his screen with his shoulders twitching with quiet muffled chuckles as he swiped through another luxury listing.
’Why is he smiling like that?’ Lia’s thoughts churned with dark suspicion. ’That’s the face people make in the cinema when they’re hiding something scandalous.’
Her mind flashed back to the ruined skyscraper in Iunu.
To the beautiful, green-haired goddess who had knelt beside her in the grass, smiling with that divine radiance.
’I belong to Lord Silas.
In the sovereign realm, our souls are bound beneath the branches.
In your mortal terms... you might consider us husband and wife.’
Lia’s eyes widened slightly.
’Is he... is he cheating on Miss Eluned?!’
The staggering scandal of the thought made her grip her pencil so hard the graphite snapped with a sharp crack.
Who was on that phone?
Was it that wealthy, scary woman with the gold carriages who had visited the school?
Or—
WHACK!
A heavy leather-bound volume of Classical Shogunate Prose and Grammar descended from above, smacking squarely against the top of Lia’s skull.
"Ow!" Lia yelped, clutching her head and glaring to her left.
Kaede was standing over her, holding the textbook like a club as her dark eyes burned with no-nonsense discipline.
"Focus, Lia," Kaede hissed in a fierce whisper, pointing a sharp finger at the half-finished quadratic formula on the notebook page.
"If you don’t finish the third module before four o’clock, Miss Martha will not allow us to clear the carpet...
The box has eleven figurines, Lia!
Eleven!
If we don’t start the setup now, we won’t finish anything before the sun goes down!"

chapters.title: Chapter 642: Minamoto
paragraphs: Lia rubbed her scalp, shooting a dirty look toward the couch before sighing heavily.
"Fine, fine... The third module. Whatever."

Across the room, Silas didn’t even notice. He had just discovered a limited-run bath linen set woven from spun silkworm threads, and was currently debating whether buying six dozen was excessive or merely prudent.
’Meh, I feel like it’s okay... I want to bathe like a King.’
Forty minutes later, the dining table had been abandoned as the homework was tucked into bags lined up neatly by the front door.
The expansive Persian rug in the center of the living room had been officially declared a war zone.
Penelope sat cross-legged near the coffee table wth her knees tucked beneath her pleated skirt and her violet eyes scanning the arrangement of plastic heroes with a dissatisfied pout.

"This makes no sense," Penelope said, picking up the miniature of Vala by her base and holding her between two fingers. "Why are there only eleven of them? Where are the opposing units? What are we supposed to do with an entire crew of champions if the manufacturers didn’t include a single beast or a hostile enemy for them to butcher?"
Silas stretched lazily on the couch, folding his arms behind his head and looking down at the carpet over the edge of the cushions.

"They’re display figures, Penelope," Silas said, amused. "They’re meant for display cabinets and collector shelves so wealthy people can show their guests how much disposable income they have... They aren’t meant for backyard wrestling matches."
"A warrior without an enemy is merely an ornament," Penelope recited with the dry solemnity she had clearly absorbed from her older sister. "It is an incomplete aesthetic."
Silas snorted.

"If you really want to see them fight, you don’t need monsters... Just put Eluned and Morwenna within ten paces of each other. They spend forty percent of their time in the territory actively trying to drown or strangle one another."
Penelope blinked, looking up at him with wide, startled eyes. "L-Lady Eluned fights with Lady Morwenna?"
"Constantly," Silas said, rolling his shoulder. "It’s a lot and don’t get me started on Tasmin and Brida. They’re fighting most of the time though it’s Brida that starts it..."

"That’s a lie," Lia declared loudly, clutching the Eluned figurine to her chest like a protective shield. "Miss Eluned is gentle! She’s peaceful! She doesn’t fight people! She told me herself that all living things deserve to grow toward the sunlight!"
Silas looked down at his sister with weary pity.

"Lia," Silas sighed, "live with her for three weeks first then tell me about the sunlight. The only reason she was that nice to you is because you are my sister... If you were a stray mercenary who stepped on one of her wild lilies, she would have turned your nervous system into compost before you could say hello."
Lia puffed her cheeks out, turning her back on him completely. "I don’t care... She’s still the best!"
’What is this Eluned propaganda...?’
Before Silas could offer another unhelpful reality check, Martha emerged from the hallway, carrying three freshly ironed light jackets over her arm.

"Girls," Martha announced gently, her voice cutting through the banter with effortless authority. "It is quarter to five... Your siblings’ transports have already cleared the outer security gates of the complex so please begin gathering your parcels and checking your shoes."
Penelope and Kaede rose immediately, their posture shifting back into the disciplined manners of their respective houses.
They carefully packed their newly inspected figurines back into their custom foam trays, securing the collector’s cartons with their heavy gold ribbons.
DING-DONG!
The electronic chime of the front entrance rang through the apartment with two clear chimes.
Through the intercom speaker beside the archway, a young man’s voice sounded.
"It’s Minamoto and I arrived for Kaede."
Kaede jumped slightly, smoothing down the front of her uniform blazer.
She hurried over to the foyer, slipping her feet into her black loafers before turning around and looking toward the living room.
Silas had already sat up on the edge of the couch, slipping his feet back into his leather slippers.
Kaede looked at him with her fingers fidgeting with the strap of her bag.
"Master Silas," she murmured, her voice small. "Thank you for the food and for everything."
Silas smiled, standing up from the cushions and tying the terrycloth belt of his bathrobe a bit tighter around his waist.
"Anytime. Come on, let’s go see your brother."
He walked over to the foyer, stepping onto the polished limestone floor beside her, and pulled the heavy cedar door open.
Standing on the exterior landing, framed by the late-afternoon sun filtering through the ornamental maples, was Minamoto.
The young coastal Lord was dressed in a razor-sharp double-breasted coat of midnight-navy wool over a high-collared charcoal vest.
His long black hair was tied back in a strict traditional warrior’s queue, a dark leather scabbard carrying his ancestral katana resting at his left hip.
’Why does he always carry this around...?’
His sharp hawk-like eyes were cold, assessing the stone steps with relentless vigilance and then the door opened as Minamoto’s eyes snapped up.
Immediately they locked squarely onto Silas.
For half a second, the air between them went entirely rigid.
Minamoto saw the damp hair, the VIP hotel bathrobe, the total absence of armor, and his younger sister standing right at that man’s elbow.
"Y-you..."
SWOOSH!

In a single terrifyingly fluid burst of footwork, Minamoto’s frame blurred forward across the threshold as his right arm shot out like a striking serpent, his fingers hooking under Kaede’s armpits, violently plucking his sister off the limestone floor.
YANK!

His shoulder clipped Silas on the way through in a casual perfectly aimed nudge that sent Silas stumbling half a step sideways with his slippers catching on the doormat and his hand slapping against the cedar doorframe.
"Whoa—!" Silas grunted, catching his balance against the jamb.
Minamoto had already completed the rotation.

Without breaking stride, the young Yamato lord had tucked Kaede firmly under his left arm like a long roll of imported carpet with his long coat swirling behind him as he marched down the flagstone walkway toward a sleek black sedan idling at the curb.
"Brother! Put me down! This is a bit disgraceful!" Kaede shrieked with her legs kicking uselessly in the air and her face bright crimson as she flailed against his ribs.
She twisted her neck around, waving frantically back toward the open doorway with her free hand.
"Goodbye, Big Brother Silas! Goodbye, Lia! Thank you for the food!"
Silas stood in the doorway, his bathrobe slightly askew with one hand still braced on the doorframe.
Beside him, Lia walked up to the threshold with her hands tucked into her pockets, watching the black car peel smoothly away from the curb.
Lia looked up at Silas. "He really doesn’t like you, does he?"

"He’s overprotective," Silas sighed, rubbing the bridge of his nose with an amused snort. "Though honestly, snatching a child out of someone’s living room like a bag of groceries is a bit much, even for him..."
Lia snorted into her sleeve.
"He looked at your bathrobe like it had personally insulted him."
"It’s a very nice bathrobe."
"It has a sun on it, Big Brother."
"So?"
Lia raised her hand, offering a lazy wave toward the dust kicked up by the sedan’s tires.
Silas echoed the gesture with the two of them standing side by side on the threshold as the late afternoon wind rustled the maples.
For a moment neither of them said anything.
’Big Brother... You’re really cool but I won’t tell you that.’
VROOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The heavy rumble of a high-displacement turbine engine suddenly echoed from the complex’s private driveway and cutting through the shadows of the maple trees, a car glided into the courtyard.
It was a low-slung ultra-performance car, a matte-violet Valkyrie-9... Its chassis was forged from lightweight carbon-chitin that gleamed with iridescent purple undertones in the dying sunlight.

The engine snarled with the compressed violence of an overcharged mana turbine as the interceptor came to a halt behind Silas’s Zenith IVR with the gull-wing driver’s door hissing upward with a sharp release of steam.
’There are a lot of supercars in this world though...’

A long slender leg encased in dark tailored slacks and a four-inch stiletto boot stepped out onto the cobblestones and Silas’s face instantly relaxed with a wide genuine smile breaking across his lips.
"Harp—"
The syllable died in his throat.
Harper stepped out of the vehicle, but she didn’t rush forward.
She wore a sharp bespoke three-piece charcoal suit cut to perfection, her tailored suit jacket draped casually over her shoulders like a commander’s cape.
Her long magnificent violet hair whipped gracefully in the evening draft, catching the amber light as she reached up, smoothing a stray lock behind her ear.
Dark crescents sat beneath her eyes, carefully powdered over but not quite gone, and the hand she used to smooth her hair was not steady.
She stopped at the foot of the flagstone steps, about three paces from Silas.
Then, with agonizing slowness, she tucked her right hand over her heart, bent her waist, and offered a deep flawless ninety-degree bow.
"Good evening, Lord Vespera," Harper said. "Welcome back..."
Silas stared at her. "Harper... what the hell are you doing?"
Harper straightened up.
Her violet eyes drifted over his damp hair, his oversized bathrobe, and the bare calloused toes poking out of his leather slippers.
"Is it possible," she asked. "for me to sleep over tonight?"
Silas blinked twice.
"Uh... sure," Silas said, scratching his temple. "There’s plenty of room in the guest wing. Martha, go ahead and cycle the front gate wards, will you?"
"Right away, Master," Martha called back, stepping toward the security panel.
Silas turned his eyes back to the purple-haired woman standing on the flagstones.
"Harper, are you feeling alright? You’re acting very wei—"
BOOM!
The flagstone beneath her heels didn’t crack, but the displacement of air was explosive as Harper skipped the steps and any announcement, and launched herself forward.
’Good... she’s fine.’
SLAM!
Her entire body crashed into Silas’s chest with the concussive force of an armored battering ram!
"Oof—!"
Silas let out a sudden gasp of air that he hadn’t even realized he was holding as her momentum drove him back three paces into the foyer.
Her arms weren’t gentle.

They wrapped around his neck like two bands of forged tungsten, pulling her body flush against his with such suffocating intensity that Silas felt the hard buttons of her waistcoat digging directly through the thick terrycloth of his robe into his sternum.
Her face buried itself deep into the crook of his neck with her nose pressing hard against his skin, inhaling the scent of his soap with rapid breaths that trembled against his collarbone.
She was shaking.
Beneath the flawless wool and the cold corporate perfume, her entire frame was shivering with a bone-deep terror that had finally found a wall it couldn’t break.
Silas stood still in the center of the foyer with his feet planted wide on the limestone.
His initial shock faded in a single heartbeat and slowly, his arms came up.

His right hand flattened firmly against the center of her back, pressing through the wool of her suit jacket, holding her securely against his frame, while his left arm wrapped around her waist, taking her full weight without yielding an inch.
"Welcome back," Harper whispered into his throat. "Welcome back, Silas..."
Silas let out a soft steady breath, resting his chin lightly against the top of her violet head.
"I’m back, Harper," he murmured softly. "I’m right here so you really don’t have to worry though why did you talk like that?"
"Tch, I wanted to make you worried."
"...I’ll slam you into the ground right now."
"Hey~! I’m just a girl, okay?!"
Beside the shoe cubbies, Penelope stood frozen.
The eleven-year-old girl stared at her older sister currently clinging to Silas Graves like a drowning sailor clutching a floating spar and Penelope’s face turned bright red.
She violently snapped her head away, staring resolutely at the baseboard molding with second-hand embarrassment.

’Does my sister possess zero shame?’ Penelope screamed internally, her fingers clawing into the fabric of her skirt pockets. ’NONE AT ALL?! In front of Martha?! In front of his little sister?! She’s the Head of House Whitmore and she’s hanging off him like a koala bear!’

"Hey~!
I’m just a girl, okay?!"
Beside the shoe cubbies, Penelope stood frozen.
The eleven-year-old girl stared at her older sister currently clinging to Silas Graves like a drowning sailor clutching a floating spar and Penelope’s face turned bright red.
She violently snapped her head away, staring resolutely at the baseboard molding with second-hand embarrassment.
’Does my sister possess zero shame?’ Penelope screamed internally, her fingers clawing into the fabric of her skirt pockets. ’NONE AT ALL?!
In front of Martha?!
In front of his little sister?!
She’s the Head of House Whitmore and she’s hanging off him like a koala bear!’

chapters.title: Chapter 643: A Strange Power
paragraphs: Martha stepped into the foyer from the living room, wiping her hands on a dry tea towel.
She stopped, taking in the sight with a soft knowing crinkle around her eyes, unbothered by the sudden influx of drama.

"Welcome, Lady Harper," Martha said, her voice sounding smooth and welcoming. "It is wonderful to see you well and... I must thank you once more for the automobile... It drives like a dream, though the maintenance manual is nearly three inches thick."
Harper didn’t immediately let go.
She lingered for two more heartbeats with her fingers tightening into the fabric of Silas’s shoulders, before she reluctantly released him.

She stepped back, though her hand lingered on Silas’s forearm and her fingers lightly tracing the cuff of his robe. Her composure reassembled itself with astonishing speed with her chin lifting as she looked at the housekeeper.

"You are very welcome, Martha," Harper said, her voice turning smooth again though the flush on her high cheekbones remained. "And frankly... I would willingly purchase five more of those cruisers if it meant seeing that smile on your face every afternoon."
Martha paused mid-step with her eyebrows lifting slightly as a dry smirk touched her lips.
’Good heavens,’ Martha thought, amused. ’Aren’t you supposed to be flirting with Master Silas? Why are you trying to charm the domestic help?’
’What’s going on here...?!’

"The vehicle was intended for the household," Harper added, turning her violet eyes back to Silas with her gaze softening. "I wanted Silas to have something secure and comfortable to transport the entire family... The Zenith IVR is a fine car, but it’s a bit unsuitable for grocery runs with three children."
Silas let out a low chuckle, stepping past her into the living room and sinking heavily back into the corner of the sectional couch.
"Fair point," Silas said, resting his arm along the backrest.
Harper followed him, slipping naturally onto the cushion beside him, tucking her legs beneath her with effortless grace.
Silas looked at her tired pale profile.
Without thinking, his right hand rose with his fingers gently threading through the silky cool violet strands of her hair, brushing them back from her temple.
A tiny involuntary sound escaped the back of Harper’s throat.
Her eyes fluttered half-closed as her head leaned instinctively into the warmth of his palm with her shoulders dropping two inches as the lingering tension drained from her spine.
"How are you holding up, Harper?" Silas asked quietly, his thumb tracing the soft line of her cheekbone. "Really..."
The question seemed to pull her back to the room.
Harper opened her eyes, looking around the living room before her gaze locked onto Penelope standing in the archway.
"Penelope," Harper called out, reaching into her inner coat pocket and withdrawing a sleek titanium transponder key.
She tossed it with a light flick of her wrist and Penelope caught it cleanly with one hand.

"Take the cargo from the boot of the Valkyrie," Harper instructed her sister. "There are three garment boxes containing sleepwear for everyone in the house... I had the tailors use imported silk-cotton blends and there are four insulated containers of prepared dinner dishes. Martha has spent the entire day cooking, she doesn’t need to spend her evening over a stove hehe~"
Penelope looked at the key, then looked at Silas with her expression deadpan.
"Understood, Sister."
"I’ll help!" Lia offered, bounding toward the front door. "I want to see the fancy pajamas!"
"I will accompany them to manage the containers," Martha nodded, following the two girls out the heavy cedar door, pulling it shut behind them with a soft final click.
The front door sealed and the room fell into heavy silence.
The amber light from the windows had faded into deep twilight blue, casting long cool shadows across the Persian rug and the scattered boxes of figurines.
Harper waited until the crunch of the girls’ footsteps on the gravel driveway faded completely then, she shifted.
She pulled her legs out from beneath her, sliding across the cushions until she was sitting directly beside Silas with her thigh pressing firmly against his linen robe.
Her hands rested on her knees and her fingers curled tightly into the dark wool of her trousers.
"Silas," she said, her voice dropping into a tense tone that made the hair on his arms stand up.
Silas turned to her, his hand falling from her hair to rest on the cushion between them. "What is it?"
"My body..." Harper swallowed hard, her throat working with a dry click. "...it feels weird."
Silas’s expression sharpened instantly, the relaxed sleepy expression vanishing as it was replaced by a sharp one.
"Weird how? Are your meridians rejecting mana or something? Did something else happen...? Talk to me."
Was this possibly why she was acting so weird? If so, Silas wanted to know.

He didn’t expect her to be back to normal especially since Ititius had taken over her body and used her to kill off the Royal Family of Khemet in one go, it was a surprise or perhaps a miracle that Harper herself wasn’t vindicated of the whole thing.
’I guess I should thank Ititius for ending all the possible witnesses...?’
He still hated that guy, that much was for certain and Silas really hoped he killed him that time because if he didn’t... He would have a field day when next he saw the bastard.
"No," Harper shook her head, her violet hair swaying. "It’s not damage, well it’s... something else."
She hesitated, and for a moment the polished expression she had been giving slipped, leaving only a tired young woman who had not slept properly at all.
"I haven’t told anyone... Not Penelope and not the clinic... Every night I lie there and feel it moving under my ribs like a second pulse, and every night it feels very weird but I know what it is."
She took a slow deep breath, staring down at her own manicured hands.
"When I was trapped..." She began. "...my body was taken. First by Nitocris..."
Silas’s brow furrowed. "Nitocris? I thought the entity orchestrating the engine blowout was Ititius."

"They were... essentially the same entity," Harper murmured, her fingers tightening against her fabric. "It’s a bit complicated, I really can’t explain without confusing you but essentially Ititius is Nitocris’s main body while Nitocris is a split part of her consciousness, Ititius is a woman too so..."
"Eh?"
Silas was confused and Harper pouted as well, was it her fault that her ancestor was that crazy.
"U-um... anyway... Nitocris occupied my vessel, she suppressed my consciousness, and before she was purged, she kept her promise."
Harper looked up with her violet eyes dark, swirling with an intense unreadable depth.
"She engraved the ancient techniques of the Black Sand directly into my soul, Silas... Deep into the spiritual marrow where the human meridians are born."
She raised her right hand into the empty space between them.
FSSSSSSSSSSSS!
Her eyes didn’t flare with purple mana.
From the pores of her palm, a fine light-devouring mist of pitch-black sand began to seep outward.
Ordinary mineral dust would have fallen, but this defied gravity, swirling in a tight perfectly controlled miniature whirlpool that hovered two inches above her skin.
The sand was so black it seemed to drink the twilight in the room, radiating a cold aura of desolation.
’What a weird spell...’
CRACKLE!
Without a word, Harper’s core shifted.
Thin violent arcs of purple lightning, her native elemental affinity, erupted from her fingertips, coiling tightly around the black sand vortex like hunting vipers.
WHOOSH!

The lightning didn’t scatter the sand at all, instead it fused with it, turning the swirling vortex into a shrieking cyclone of electrified obsidian particles that made the air smell of scorched ozone as Silas watched the miniature storm hover between them.
His dark eyes tracked the movement of each individual grain with his instincts analyzing the density packed into that three-inch sphere.
...This was very impressive.

"You’ve become stronger, Harper," Silas said softly, real respect coloring his tone. "A lot stronger... The control required to braid lightning through a mineral like this black sand... most high-tier lords would spend ten years in a seclusion chamber just to balance it out given that you just awakened."
A fragile smile touched Harper’s lips, though it carried none of its usual pride.

"I did," she whispered. "My mana capacity expanded during the whole thing. The hospital diagnostic scanners nearly shattered when they ran the initial scan so right now... my total mana reserves are resting comfortably above ten thousand points... I checked my Status too."
Silas’s breath hitched.
’Ten thousand?’ he thought with his pulse spiking. ’For an Awakened who hasn’t even completed her Second Stage Advancement? That’s an absurd mana pool too.’
"That should be impossible for your current level," Silas said seriously, was there something Ititius had done? She needed to tell him.
"I know," Harper said.
She closed her fingers, snuffing out the black sand and the purple lightning in a single clean fist.
"And that isn’t even the part that scares me," she murmured.
Harper closed her eyes.
She drew a long slow breath through her nose, holding it deep in her diaphragm.
HUMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMM!
A sound began to rise in the living room...
A pressure settled directly against Silas’s skull with a frequency that made the hairs on the back of his neck rise like quills as Harper slowly opened her hand once more.
From the center of her palm, an energy began to bleed into the air.
It wasn’t purple nor was it black either, this time, It was a brilliant, blinding pure white light.
WHOOOOOOOOOOOOSH!
The miniature torrent of sand erupted once more, but it had completely shed its dark corrupted form.
The light-devouring black sand had transformed into fine crystalline white particles that spun with terrifying speed and the lightning coiling around it...
The violet arcs had inverted entirely, bleached into pure, blinding white plasma that let off a quiet vibration.
’This...’
The coffee table groaned, and one of the plastic heroes tipped over on the rug with an accusing click.
The carpet beneath their boots flattened under a sudden invisible gravity that Silas had only ever felt in one other place as Silas’s eyes widened to their limits and his body went rigid on the sofa.
’This energy...’
His mind raced, slamming through the memories of the Keep of Blessed Land.

No element carried that weight, and neither did high-tier mana from his other women, nor even the refined Gold Core output he wielded through his own meridians... apart from two beings that he knew very well.

"I don’t know what this is, Silas," Harper whispered, her face pale in the blinding white glare, looking at the swirling torrent with wide frightened eyes. "Every time I call upon it... my attacks don’t just hit harder, They erase whatever they touch very easily. It feels... foreign, like something that doesn’t belong to mortals you know. Similar to those novels..."
Snuff!
With a sharp jerk of her wrist, she dispelled the light and the living room fell back into the cool dark twilight.
Harper slowly turned her body with her knees shifting on the cushions until she was facing him directly.
She reached out, her cool trembling fingers gently resting over the top of his calloused hand with her grip tight.
’I love holding your hand...’
"Does it hurt when you use it?" Silas asked, keeping his voice level.

"No." She shook her head slowly. "That’s a bit good. The Black Sand burns a little, like a stretched muscle... This doesn’t burn at all, It feels like breathing, like something I was always meant to do in a way if that makes sense, I know it can feel like I’m blabbing a lot but I’m being serious."
"What do you think, Silas?" she asked, her voice trembling in the quiet room. "I need your opinion so please... tell me the truth."
Silas sat motionless.
He looked down at her small hand resting over his as he looked back up into her wide searching violet eyes with his heart hammering against his ribs like a war drum.
He was sure of it... There was zero doubt left in his mind...
He turned his hand over beneath hers and closed his fingers around her cold ones.

That feeling she was describing... He knew it very well since it was the same feeling that both Eluned and Thor gave to him, how would he not know it that well, he was being graced by it every single day.
Harper Whitmore... was using Divinity.

chapters.title: Chapter 644: PJs [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The living room stayed quiet for a long moment with the pale twilight from the terrace doors catching the microscopic swirl of dust where the white torrent had just evaporated.
Harper sat with her knees drawn tight against her chest, both hands clamped over the charcoal wool of her trousers.
The blinding glare was gone, but her knuckles remained stark white and trembled against the fabric and her chest rose and fell in short drafts.
’The silence is good...’ Both of them thought at the same time but Silas didn’t withdraw his hand.
He kept his calloused palm planted flat against the back of hers, letting the warmth of his Gold Core seep through her skin and anchor her erratic pulse.
"Divinity," Silas said, breaking the silence in a dry voice. All of a sudden... he sounded unimpressed, was it because he was a bit jealous?
Harper blinked.
The dark violet of her eyes fluttered with her brows knitting together as she tilted her chin up to stare at him.
"Divinity? As in divine authority? The kind spoken of in the ancient scrolls of the first era or something?"

"Drop the liturgical nonsense," Silas replied, shaking his head slightly. "You aren’t reading from an altar... You took a hit from a god after all. Nitocris, Ititius... It doesn’t matter... The entity was a deity of sand and when its consciousness occupied your body beneath the White Citadel, your soul wasn’t just crushed under foreign mana... Its power was branded directly onto your spiritual conduits. I’m sure of it..."
He tapped the back of her hand lightly with his index finger.

"Before that thing came apart under the blade, its authority washed over your meridians so that means a fraction of that divine ether stuck to your marrow... What you just sparked isn’t an element, it isn’t high-order purple lightning, and it sure as hell isn’t black sand, It’s residual divinity."
Harper remained motionless with her lips slightly parted as she stared at the empty space above her lap.
She lifted her right palm and flexed her manicured fingers one by one.
The skin was smooth and unblemished, but beneath the pale surface an elusive frightening current seemed to hum just out of reach of her pulse.
"Residual," she murmured, with a dry self-deprecating chuckle. "A few dregs, then... Scraps left on the floor after an ancient god choked on my body..."
"Any amount of divine power in a mortal vessel is certainly special," Silas said firmly, shifting on the cushions so he faced her squarely.
He placed his heavy right hand on the curve of her shoulder, his fingers pressing into the tailored wool of her jacket with an unshakeable grip.

"Don’t sell it short, trust me, most Awakened would already be dead but your core held... You kept your identity intact, you maintained your native elemental affinity, and you fused the sand with your lightning too. You’re very lucky and stronger because of it."
He looked straight into her eyes.

"So you don’t need to fear it, Harper... It’s fuel... Train the energy, refine the compression ratios during your morning training and run the circuits through your central nervous system until the white spark stops biting your nerves... Keep at it, and one day you might actually forge yourself into a full-fledged deity."
Harper stared at him.
The rigid posture that usually defined the Head of House Whitmore slowly melted.
Her violet eyes widened, catching the amber gleam of the distant streetlights, shimmering with a sudden breathless brilliance that had nothing to do with calculations.
"A deity," she whispered then, without a shred of warning, the woman lunged forward at him.
LUNGE!
Harper threw both arms around Silas’s right bicep and pressed her cheek against his shoulder with a dramatic exaggerated whimper.

"Being a deity sounds absolutely terrifying!" Harper cried, her voice pitching up into a delightful whine as she clung to his arm like a child refusing to leave a toy shop. "All those rituals! The endless prayers from dusty cultists! Having to float around on a cloud looking miserable! No, thank you, Silas! That sounds like far too much paperwork!"
She squeezed his arm tighter against her ribs, tilting her face up to gaze at his profile with a wicked twinkle in her violet eyes.
"I’d much rather retire from everything and become your wife~"
Silas choked on his own breath with a bark of laughter tearing from his throat as he tried to pry her fingers off his bicep, though his effort was completely in vain.
"My wife?" Silas snorted, looking down at her clinging frame with an amused exasperated grin. "You’re the Head of House Whitmore, and your grand life ambition is to sit on my couch and steal my tea?"

"Precisely!" Harper beamed, rubbing her cheek against his sleeve with satisfaction. "Think of the tax exemptions! Think of the strategic merger! And besides, I make excellent homemade pastries when I’m not blowing up monsters like Arachnids."
Silas’s laughter faltered for half a second.
’Arachnids, huh?’
His thoughts drifted to the cluster of spider eggs sitting in the incubators back in Blessed Land, and he wondered idly whether they had hatched yet.
’I’ll check them out when I get back to the Beast Pavillion.’ Silas thought as the heavy cedar front door clicked open.
THUD-CLATTER!
Footsteps scuffled across the limestone tiles of the foyer, accompanied by the loud crinkling rustle of heavy cardboard cartons and plastic packaging.

"Penelope, watch your step with the third box!" Lia’s voice carried through the archway sounding breathless and bossy. "If you drop the silk sets, Miss Martha will make us polish the banister until midnight!"
"I am carrying the soup containers, Lia," Penelope retorted in her flat immaculate voice. "You are carrying three empty garment bags... Do not lecture me on balance."
Harper’s grip loosened, but she didn’t jump back with guilty haste.

Instead, she smoothly transitioned from clinging to his arm into a relaxed recline on the cushions, crossing one tailored trouser-leg over the other with the untouchable poise of an empress who owned every square inch of the living room.
’Eh... It’s my living room though.’
Lia, Penelope, and Martha trooped into the room like a miniature supply caravan.

Penelope set two heavy insulated thermal food flasks onto the dining table, while Lia dumped a towering stack of midnight-blue and ivory garment boxes onto the coffee table, scattering Silas’s discarded magazines.
Martha followed close behind, carrying a wooden tray lined with ceramic soup bowls and clean silver spoons.

"Mission accomplished," Lia announced, wiping a nonexistent bead of sweat from her brow with the back of her wrist. "The trunk of Lady Harper’s interceptor is essentially a mobile department store..."
Harper let out a melodic amused chuckle, leaning forward and resting her elbows on her knees as she tapped the topmost garment box with a polished fingernail.

"Not a department store, little one," Harper purred, her eyes scanning the three of them with playful pride. "Custom-tailored loungewear from the House of Valois from Australis... Imported silk-cotton blends woven with micro-temperature wards... Forty-five thousand credits per set."
She slid the lids off the boxes, revealing the pristine sets folded inside tissue paper.

"This midnight-blue set with the silver piping is for Miss Martha," Harper said, gesturing gracefully toward the housekeeper. "The pale lavender with the lace collar belongs to Penelope. The forest green with the embroidered rabbit crest is for Lia and this one..."
She lifted a deep violet set from the last box, the silk scattered with tiny embroidered golden stars that caught the lamplight like a night sky, and her lips curved into a slow devastating smirk.
"...is for a certain brooding lord who refuses to buy his own clothes. Mine matches his, of course."
Martha raised a polite hand to her cheek with her eyes widening slightly. "Forty-five thousand credits for sleepwear? Heavens, Lady Harper, that is far too extravagant for domestic duties..."
"Take the clothes, Martha," Silas interrupted with a dry smirk, waving his hand toward the box. "If you argue with her, she’ll buy thirty more sets just to prove a point about her liquidity."
Silas was very sure she was capable of it...
Lia didn’t need to be told twice as she snatched her forest-green box by the ribbon, let out a triumphant cheer, and bolted down the hallway toward her bedroom like a startled deer.
Penelope offered a stiff dignified nod of thanks to her older sister, picked up her lavender parcel, and followed with swift silent steps.
Martha, shaking her head with a faint sigh of surrender, gathered her set and retreated to the ground-floor guest quarters to change.
Silas stretched his arms above his head, letting his knuckles pop, and made to rise from the sofa.
"Right. I’ll go throw on the stars before the food goes cold."
"Sit down," Harper commanded softly.
Silas paused, his eyebrows lifting. "What?"
"I said, sit down," she repeated, her voice dropping into a purring voice that made the air in the room feel two degrees warmer.
"Whoo~"
Harper stood up from the sectional and reached for the lapels of her bespoke three-piece suit jacket.
With a slow deliberate shrug of her shoulders, she let the charcoal wool slide down her arms and drop across the back of an armchair.
Her slender fingers moved to the mother-of-pearl buttons of her high-collared white silk waistcoat, undoing them one by one with unhurried precision.
Silas sat back down on the cushions.
His posture stayed relaxed, but his dark eyes narrowed slightly as he watched her.
"Harper," Silas murmured, his voice dry as tinder. "The children are literally fifteen feet down the corridor."
"The children are currently arguing over who gets the top drawer in Lia’s wardrobe," Harper dismissed casually, sliding the waistcoat off and tossing it onto the table.
Her fingers moved to the collar of her silk shirt and undid the top three buttons, revealing the pale porcelain of her throat and the sharp, elegant dip of her collarbones.
Beneath the tailored fabric, the athletic lines of her frame were unmistakable... the narrow waist, the flare of her hips, the subtle corded muscle along her shoulders forged through years of combat.
She turned slightly, catching his gaze in the dim light with a wicked teasing glint dancing in her violet pupils.
"Tell me, Syyyy," she whispered, stepping half an inch closer to the edge of the coffee table. "Do you like what you see?"
Silas didn’t look away.
He leaned back against the cushions, crossing his arms over his chest with his jaw setting into a calm immovable line.
’If I look away, she’ll tease me more.’
For that reason, he let his gaze sweep slowly over the bare curve of her neck and down to the exposed dip of her ribs before meeting her eyes with a arrogant smirk.
"So what if I do?" Silas countered, his voice dropping into a low voice designed to rattle her composure. "You think you’re the first dangerous woman to take off her jacket in front of me?"
Harper’s violet eyes dilated slightly.
A microscopic prickle of pink heat dusted the high ridges of her cheekbones, catching her completely off-guard.
She opened her mouth, stepping forward with a defiant tilt of her chin, her voice dropping into a breathless rasp.
"Well, then... if you like it so much, Silas... you can just come over here and take i—"
SLAM!
The hallway door flew open with the force of a breaching charge.
"LOOK AT THE SLEEVES!" Lia shrieked, skidding onto the living room rug on her stockinged heels, holding her arms out like an airplane.
The forest-green silk set was two sizes too large, the cuffs swallowing her hands like floppy green mittens.
"PENELOPE SAID I LOOK LIKE A CABBAGE, BUT SHE’S JUST JEALOUS BECAUSE MINE HAS POCKETS!"
Penelope walked out behind her, adjusting the neat lace collar of her lavender set with long-suffering dignity.
"You do look like a cabbage, Lia... A very expensive, organic cabbage..."
Harper’s entire body went rigid.

In a fraction of a second that would have made an elite shinobi weep with envy, Harper snatched her matching violet set from the box, whipped her arms through the pajama shirt, and buttoned it up to her chin with frantic blurred fingers.
She spun around to face the girls with a smile so stiff it looked painted on.
Silas buried his face in his hands on the couch with his shoulders shaking with silent breathless laughter.
’Take it, huh?’ he thought, coughing into his palms. ’Almost had her.’
Martha emerged from the kitchen archway a moment later, wearing her midnight-blue set beneath a clean cotton apron.
She paused, taking in the scene which was Harper aggressively smoothing down her silk lapels, Silas grinning like an idiot on the sofa, and the two little girls inspecting the hem of the rug.
Her sharp eyes darted between Harper’s flushed cheeks and Silas’s messy hair though her lips were twitching with a knowing smirk that carried a hint of wry amusement.
’I’m a bit jealous...’
"I see the evening dress code has been established," Martha remarked with her tone sweet as honey.
Harper cleared her throat, stepping gracefully toward the dining table, her composure snapping back into place like a steel bear trap.
"Indeed! And now, dinner... Real food!"
She unlatched the heavy thermal flasks, releasing a rich intoxicating aroma that instantly conquered the living room.
It was a dark velvety beef and oxtail stew, simmered with roasted root vegetables, wild thyme, and dark red wine until the meat had dissolved into tender ribbons.
Beside it was a ceramic crock of crusty sourdough rolls, still warm to the touch, and a chilled glass dish of pickled cucumber spears.
The five of them gathered around the low table, sitting on the thick floor cushions.
Lia and Penelope dug in with zero hesitation, their eyes lighting up as they tore into the bread.
"This is amazing," Penelope admitted, closing her eyes as she chewed. "Sister, your training in cooking was not an entire waste of resources after all..."
"High praise from my own flesh and blood," Harper chuckled, ladling a generous portion into Silas’s bowl.
Silas picked up a ceramic soup spoon, dipped it into the dark broth, blew on the steam, and took a slow deliberate sip.
He chewed a piece of tender carrot with deadpan contemplation, then set the spoon down and looked at Harper.
"The broth is flat," Silas stated with unblinking seriousness. "It lacks sweetness... Honestly, I think the bone marrow they served us in the Khemet refugee camps had more flavor."
Ah, was Silas trying to court death?!

sentences.text: The living room stayed quiet for a long moment with the pale twilight from the terrace doors catching the microscopic swirl of dust where the white torrent had just evaporated.
Harper sat with her knees drawn tight against her chest, both hands clamped over the charcoal wool of her trousers.
The blinding glare was gone, but her knuckles remained stark white and trembled against the fabric and her chest rose and fell in short drafts.
’The silence is good...’ Both of them thought at the same time but Silas didn’t withdraw his hand.
He kept his calloused palm planted flat against the back of hers, letting the warmth of his Gold Core seep through her skin and anchor her erratic pulse.
"Divinity," Silas said, breaking the silence in a dry voice.
All of a sudden... he sounded unimpressed, was it because he was a bit jealous?
Harper blinked.
The dark violet of her eyes fluttered with her brows knitting together as she tilted her chin up to stare at him.
"Divinity?
As in divine authority?
The kind spoken of in the ancient scrolls of the first era or something?"
"Drop the liturgical nonsense," Silas replied, shaking his head slightly.
"You aren’t reading from an altar...
You took a hit from a god after all.
Nitocris, Ititius...
It doesn’t matter...
The entity was a deity of sand and when its consciousness occupied your body beneath the White Citadel, your soul wasn’t just crushed under foreign mana...
Its power was branded directly onto your spiritual conduits.
I’m sure of it..."
He tapped the back of her hand lightly with his index finger.
"Before that thing came apart under the blade, its authority washed over your meridians so that means a fraction of that divine ether stuck to your marrow...
What you just sparked isn’t an element, it isn’t high-order purple lightning, and it sure as hell isn’t black sand, It’s residual divinity."
Harper remained motionless with her lips slightly parted as she stared at the empty space above her lap.
She lifted her right palm and flexed her manicured fingers one by one.
The skin was smooth and unblemished, but beneath the pale surface an elusive frightening current seemed to hum just out of reach of her pulse.
"Residual," she murmured, with a dry self-deprecating chuckle.
"A few dregs, then...
Scraps left on the floor after an ancient god choked on my body..."
"Any amount of divine power in a mortal vessel is certainly special," Silas said firmly, shifting on the cushions so he faced her squarely.

You kept your identity intact, you maintained your native elemental affinity, and you fused the sand with your lightning too.
You’re very lucky and stronger because of it."
He looked straight into her eyes.

It’s fuel...
Train the energy, refine the compression ratios during your morning training and run the circuits through your central nervous system until the white spark stops biting your nerves...
Keep at it, and one day you might actually forge yourself into a full-fledged deity."
Harper stared at him.
The rigid posture that usually defined the Head of House Whitmore slowly melted.
Her violet eyes widened, catching the amber gleam of the distant streetlights, shimmering with a sudden breathless brilliance that had nothing to do with calculations.
"A deity," she whispered then, without a shred of warning, the woman lunged forward at him.
LUNGE!
Harper threw both arms around Silas’s right bicep and pressed her cheek against his shoulder with a dramatic exaggerated whimper.
"Being a deity sounds absolutely terrifying!" Harper cried, her voice pitching up into a delightful whine as she clung to his arm like a child refusing to leave a toy shop.
"All those rituals!
The endless prayers from dusty cultists!
Having to float around on a cloud looking miserable!
No, thank you, Silas!
That sounds like far too much paperwork!"
She squeezed his arm tighter against her ribs, tilting her face up to gaze at his profile with a wicked twinkle in her violet eyes.
"I’d much rather retire from everything and become your wife~"
Silas choked on his own breath with a bark of laughter tearing from his throat as he tried to pry her fingers off his bicep, though his effort was completely in vain.
"My wife?" Silas snorted, looking down at her clinging frame with an amused exasperated grin.
"You’re the Head of House Whitmore, and your grand life ambition is to sit on my couch and steal my tea?"
"Precisely!" Harper beamed, rubbing her cheek against his sleeve with satisfaction.
"Think of the tax exemptions!
Think of the strategic merger!
And besides, I make excellent homemade pastries when I’m not blowing up monsters like Arachnids."
Silas’s laughter faltered for half a second.
’Arachnids, huh?’
His thoughts drifted to the cluster of spider eggs sitting in the incubators back in Blessed Land, and he wondered idly whether they had hatched yet.
’I’ll check them out when I get back to the Beast Pavillion.’ Silas thought as the heavy cedar front door clicked open.
THUD-CLATTER!
Footsteps scuffled across the limestone tiles of the foyer, accompanied by the loud crinkling rustle of heavy cardboard cartons and plastic packaging.
"Penelope, watch your step with the third box!" Lia’s voice carried through the archway sounding breathless and bossy.
"If you drop the silk sets, Miss Martha will make us polish the banister until midnight!"
"I am carrying the soup containers, Lia," Penelope retorted in her flat immaculate voice.
"You are carrying three empty garment bags...
Do not lecture me on balance."
Harper’s grip loosened, but she didn’t jump back with guilty haste.

Instead, she smoothly transitioned from clinging to his arm into a relaxed recline on the cushions, crossing one tailored trouser-leg over the other with the untouchable poise of an empress who owned every square inch of the living room.
It’s my living room though.’
Lia, Penelope, and Martha trooped into the room like a miniature supply caravan.

Penelope set two heavy insulated thermal food flasks onto the dining table, while Lia dumped a towering stack of midnight-blue and ivory garment boxes onto the coffee table, scattering Silas’s discarded magazines.
Martha followed close behind, carrying a wooden tray lined with ceramic soup bowls and clean silver spoons.
"Mission accomplished," Lia announced, wiping a nonexistent bead of sweat from her brow with the back of her wrist.
"The trunk of Lady Harper’s interceptor is essentially a mobile department store..."
Harper let out a melodic amused chuckle, leaning forward and resting her elbows on her knees as she tapped the topmost garment box with a polished fingernail.
"Not a department store, little one," Harper purred, her eyes scanning the three of them with playful pride.
"Custom-tailored loungewear from the House of Valois from Australis...
Imported silk-cotton blends woven with micro-temperature wards...
Forty-five thousand credits per set."

chapters.title: Chapter 645: A Deceptive Territory [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Harper froze with her spoon suspended halfway to her mouth.
Her violet eyes blinked twice as the teasing smirk dissolved from her face, and her lower lip began to tremble with tiny tears welling along her dark lashes.
"F-Flat?" she choked out, her voice cracking in agonized devastation. "I spent four hours roasting the marrow bones... I harvested the thyme from the estate’s private conservatory myself and I—"
A stray tear spilled over her cheek and dripped onto the silk of her sleeve.
"SILAS GRAVES!" Lia screamed, slamming her spoon onto the table hard enough to rattle the bowls. "You are a MONSTER!"
"An uncultured barbarian," Penelope chimed in, glaring at Silas with icy contempt. "My sister bled over that stove... Apologize to her this instant or I will salt your tea for a month."
’You don’t even handle my tea though...’
Martha crossed her arms, shaking her head in solemn disapproval.
"Master Silas, that was remarkably unkind. Lady Harper’s efforts were magnificent."
Silas blinked, the smirk vanishing as cold panic seized his chest.

"Wait, Harper, no," Silas stammered, his hands coming up in a frantic wave. "I was joking! I was joking! It’s incredible! It’s the one of the best stews I’ve had in six months, I swear to my ancestors! The wine reduction is perfect! Don’t cry, please—"
SNICKER!
The weeping ceased as Harper lifted her head, wiping the stray tear with her thumb, and her face split into a triumphant wild grin.
"Aha!" she cheered, her eyes sparkling with wicked delight. "Got you! The invincible Lord Vespera, brought to his knees by a single teardrop! You really are the sweetest boy, Silas!"
Silas sat frozen with his mouth hanging slightly open.
Lia and Penelope let out matching, disgusted groans and returned to their bowls, while Silas’s eye twitched with homicidal intent.
’I am going to throw her off the balcony,’ Silas thought, his fingers itching to summon a gust of wind-mana just to blow her soup into her lap.
Before he could retaliate, Harper leaned across the cushions, broke off a piece of the warm sourdough, dipped it into the rich stew, and held it against his lips.
"Say ah, My Lord," she purred, batting her eyelashes with exaggerated innocence. "Open wide, or I might shed another tragic tear~"
Silas glared at her for three long seconds, but the smell of roasted garlic and rich beef was undeniable.
He leaned forward and snapped the bread from her fingers, chewing with stubborn enthusiasm while she laughed like a chime in the quiet house.
By ten o’clock, the apartment had settled into the deep stillness of late night.
The dishes had been washed, dried, and stacked in the cedar cupboards.
Penelope had dragged her pillow and extra quilt into Lia’s room, where the muffled sounds of the two girls bickering over a history documentary could still be heard through the door.
’It can’t be helped...’
Silas stood at the base of the staircase in his violet pajamas with the little golden stars winking across the silk and his hands tucked into his pockets.
Beside him, Harper stretched her arms with her knuckles cracking softly in a set that matched his exactly.
On her it looked unfairly cute but on him, he suspected, it looked like a constellation had lost an argument.
"I’m taking the master suite," Harper announced with airy certainty. "I need a large bed to accommodate my newly acquired meridians."
"You have a guest room with a queen mattress right down the hall," Silas countered dryly.
"The guest room faces the western alleyway," she retorted. "The street lamps buzz and it disrupts my mana cultivation... I require executive accommodations."
"The master suite or like we call it," said a calm voice from the kitchen pantry, "has belonged to Master Silas since the day he signed the lease."
Martha stepped out with silent efficiency and came to a halt beside them with her chin held high.

"The guest room has been aired, the sheets have been changed, and I have personally closed the western shutters against the street lamps." She handed Silas his clean laundry basket and, as she did, her fingers subtly flicked as a small tin was pressed discreetly into his palm.
Silas looked down.
[CHAMOMILE AND VALERIAN, FOR PERSONS WHO HAVE CARRIED ENOUGH IRON FOR ONE SEASON!]
A muffled hysterical snort escaped Harper’s nose as she clapped both hands over her mouth with her shoulders shaking.
"Rest is of paramount importance to the household," Martha stated with deadpan gravity, not a single muscle in her face twitching. "Good night, Master Silas... Good night, Lady Harper..."
With that, the older woman turned on her heel and began methodically checking the deadbolts on the front entrance.
At the first bolt she paused with her hand resting on the cold brass.
For a moment her composure slipped, and she pressed her palm to her warm cheek and let out a small startled breath.
’Good heavens, Martha,’ she scolded herself silently. ’You are a grown woman and the head housekeeper.’
She straightened her apron, smoothed her expression back into perfect neutrality, and moved to the second bolt as though nothing had happened.
Silas stared at the tin in his hand, then at the spot where she had been standing, then at Harper, who was biting her lower lip to keep from laughing aloud.
"Unbelievable," Silas muttered, shaking his head. "I am surrounded by lunatics... a bit..."
He walked Harper down the hallway to the guest room anyway.
At the door she stopped, and the teasing faded from her face.
The light from the corridor sconce picked out the dark crescents under her eyes, and she looked suddenly much smaller than the woman who had bowed to him on the doorstep.
"Silas," she said quietly. "Thank you. For today."
"Are you really okay?" Silas asked. "With the white sand? With the changes?"
She was quiet for a moment.

"I am," she murmured, and her voice was steady, stripped of all theatrics. "Truly... When I was trapped within Ititus, I thought I was going to be erased... I thought House Whitmore would receive a sealed urn, and Penelope would be left alone in this world... Today, being here with you, with the girls, with Martha, is the first time in a while my chest hasn’t felt like an open wound... I enjoyed today more than I have words for."
A faint smirk tugged at her lips.
"And besides, we’re wearing matching pajamas. That practically makes us a crew under common maritime law."
"Captain Harper," Silas said, bowing slightly. "I’ll try to be worthy."
She laughed, then stepped forward and wrapped her arms around his neck in a brief tight hug.
"Protocol requires physical anchoring for optimal rest," she mumbled against his shoulder.
"Granted," Silas said, and hugged her back until the last tension drained out of her spine then she slipped inside, and the door clicked softly shut.
Down the hall, in Lia’s room, two small lamps burned low.

Lia lay on her stomach across the quilt in her oversized green pajamas, a sheet of heavy calligraphy paper spread in front of her, a pot of lavender ink at her elbow and her tongue poking out the corner of her mouth.
She had crossed out the first line four times.
"What are you writing?" Penelope asked from the pillow beside her, though she plainly already knew.
"A letter to Miss Eluned." Lia did not look up. "Dear Miss Eluned, thank you for catching the building... Also, I am sorry about the part where I was rude to you in the grass."
She scowled at the page. "I wasn’t rude. I just asked a lot of questions. Is that rude?"
"It is thorough," Penelope said diplomatically. She rolled onto her back and stared at the ceiling.
After a while her voice went smaller. "Lia. Do you think my sister is going to be all right?"
Lia put the brush down.
She was eleven, and she had spent a long time being the one who held the family apart so she knew exactly what a question like that sounded like when it was really asking for something else.

"She hugged my brother on the doorstep like she’d been holding her breath for two weeks," Lia said. "And then she tried to make him eat flat soup, I think people who do both of those things are going to be fine..."
Penelope let out a shaky little laugh. "The soup was not flat."
"The soup was perfect. He’s a liar." Lia picked the brush back up, then paused. "Write your own letter, if you want... I’ll share the ink."
The two of them bent over the paper together with the lavender ink drying in long careful strokes, while the house settled and the lamps burned low.
In the master bedroom, Silas set the tin of tea on the nightstand and plugged his phone into the charging dock.
He lay on top of the covers, staring up at the shadowy molding of the ceiling.
’I’m not even that exhausted...’
On a whim he swiped open his territory ledger and tried to query the incubator bay, picturing the cluster of spider eggs sitting in their warm stone cradles.
The interface blinked back at him.
[Remote Territorial Inspection Unavailable Outside The Sovereign Realm... Please Return In Person.]
He sighed and swiped it away.
Whatever had hatched or not hatched would have to wait for morning, and he made a mental note to warn the girls to knock before opening any door in the west wing.
’Tomorrow morning I’ll slip through the spatial coordinates and return to Blessed Land,’ he decided. ’Hopefully Thor hasn’t burnt down the brewery while I’ve been gone.’
His thoughts drifted outward.
’I wonder how Aki’s doing.’
However, the next moment, the door opened and Silas looked to it as he blinked.
"Harper, why are you here?"
In the Sovereign Realm, the wind that blew across the rolling hills didn’t carry the necrotic chill of the Umbral Basin.
It didn’t reek of rot, petrified bone, or anything at all... Instead the air was crisp and clean, with the sharp invigorating fragrance of crushed wild mint and blooming mountain laurel.
Princess Aki stood at the crest of a low grass-covered knoll, the hem of her loose white traveler’s tunic snapping gently in the breeze.
Her long crystalline lapis-lazuli hair whipped around her shoulders like strands of liquid sapphire, catching the pale golden sunlight of an afternoon sky that looked deceptively peaceful.
This was an Unknown Zone.
In the brutal geography of the Sovereign Realm, an Unknown Zone was a double-edged sword.

It meant her territory was isolated, separated from the established borders of rival lords by hundreds of leagues of untamed wilderness. There were no foreign scouts watching her perimeter and no tax assessors drafting liens against her hall.

Vast undulating meadows of vibrant emerald grass stretched toward a dense ancient forest of broad-leafed oaks and silver-barked willows.

In the distance, a crystal-clear river cut through the valley floor, sparkling under the golden sun like a ribbon of diamonds yet as Aki looked out from behind the shimmering translucent dome of her territorial barrier, her sapphire eyes were narrow and intensely vigilant.

Their whip-like tails ended in heavy jagged bone-clubs that twitched with restless mana.

sentences.text: Harper froze with her spoon suspended halfway to her mouth.
Her violet eyes blinked twice as the teasing smirk dissolved from her face, and her lower lip began to tremble with tiny tears welling along her dark lashes.
"F-Flat?" she choked out, her voice cracking in agonized devastation.
"I spent four hours roasting the marrow bones...
I harvested the thyme from the estate’s private conservatory myself and I—"
A stray tear spilled over her cheek and dripped onto the silk of her sleeve.
"SILAS GRAVES!" Lia screamed, slamming her spoon onto the table hard enough to rattle the bowls.
"You are a MONSTER!"
"An uncultured barbarian," Penelope chimed in, glaring at Silas with icy contempt.
"My sister bled over that stove...
Apologize to her this instant or I will salt your tea for a month."
’You don’t even handle my tea though...’
Martha crossed her arms, shaking her head in solemn disapproval.
"Master Silas, that was remarkably unkind.
Lady Harper’s efforts were magnificent."
Silas blinked, the smirk vanishing as cold panic seized his chest.
"Wait, Harper, no," Silas stammered, his hands coming up in a frantic wave.
"I was joking!
I was joking!
It’s incredible!
It’s the one of the best stews I’ve had in six months, I swear to my ancestors!
The wine reduction is perfect!
Don’t cry, please—"
SNICKER!
The weeping ceased as Harper lifted her head, wiping the stray tear with her thumb, and her face split into a triumphant wild grin.
"Aha!" she cheered, her eyes sparkling with wicked delight.
"Got you!
The invincible Lord Vespera, brought to his knees by a single teardrop!
You really are the sweetest boy, Silas!"
Silas sat frozen with his mouth hanging slightly open.
Lia and Penelope let out matching, disgusted groans and returned to their bowls, while Silas’s eye twitched with homicidal intent.
’I am going to throw her off the balcony,’ Silas thought, his fingers itching to summon a gust of wind-mana just to blow her soup into her lap.
Before he could retaliate, Harper leaned across the cushions, broke off a piece of the warm sourdough, dipped it into the rich stew, and held it against his lips.
"Say ah, My Lord," she purred, batting her eyelashes with exaggerated innocence.
"Open wide, or I might shed another tragic tear~"
Silas glared at her for three long seconds, but the smell of roasted garlic and rich beef was undeniable.
He leaned forward and snapped the bread from her fingers, chewing with stubborn enthusiasm while she laughed like a chime in the quiet house.
By ten o’clock, the apartment had settled into the deep stillness of late night.
The dishes had been washed, dried, and stacked in the cedar cupboards.
Penelope had dragged her pillow and extra quilt into Lia’s room, where the muffled sounds of the two girls bickering over a history documentary could still be heard through the door.
’It can’t be helped...’
Silas stood at the base of the staircase in his violet pajamas with the little golden stars winking across the silk and his hands tucked into his pockets.
Beside him, Harper stretched her arms with her knuckles cracking softly in a set that matched his exactly.
On her it looked unfairly cute but on him, he suspected, it looked like a constellation had lost an argument.
"I’m taking the master suite," Harper announced with airy certainty.
"I need a large bed to accommodate my newly acquired meridians."
"You have a guest room with a queen mattress right down the hall," Silas countered dryly.
"The guest room faces the western alleyway," she retorted.
"The street lamps buzz and it disrupts my mana cultivation...
I require executive accommodations."
"The master suite or like we call it," said a calm voice from the kitchen pantry, "has belonged to Master Silas since the day he signed the lease."
Martha stepped out with silent efficiency and came to a halt beside them with her chin held high.

"The guest room has been aired, the sheets have been changed, and I have personally closed the western shutters against the street lamps." She handed Silas his clean laundry basket and, as she did, her fingers subtly flicked as a small tin was pressed discreetly into his palm.
Silas looked down.
[CHAMOMILE AND VALERIAN, FOR PERSONS WHO HAVE CARRIED ENOUGH IRON FOR ONE SEASON!]
A muffled hysterical snort escaped Harper’s nose as she clapped both hands over her mouth with her shoulders shaking.
"Rest is of paramount importance to the household," Martha stated with deadpan gravity, not a single muscle in her face twitching.
"Good night, Master Silas...
Good night, Lady Harper..."
With that, the older woman turned on her heel and began methodically checking the deadbolts on the front entrance.
At the first bolt she paused with her hand resting on the cold brass.
For a moment her composure slipped, and she pressed her palm to her warm cheek and let out a small startled breath.
’Good heavens, Martha,’ she scolded herself silently. ’You are a grown woman and the head housekeeper.’
She straightened her apron, smoothed her expression back into perfect neutrality, and moved to the second bolt as though nothing had happened.
Silas stared at the tin in his hand, then at the spot where she had been standing, then at Harper, who was biting her lower lip to keep from laughing aloud.
"Unbelievable," Silas muttered, shaking his head.
"I am surrounded by lunatics... a bit..."
He walked Harper down the hallway to the guest room anyway.
At the door she stopped, and the teasing faded from her face.
The light from the corridor sconce picked out the dark crescents under her eyes, and she looked suddenly much smaller than the woman who had bowed to him on the doorstep.
"Silas," she said quietly.
"Thank you.
For today."
"Are you really okay?" Silas asked.
"With the white sand?
With the changes?"
She was quiet for a moment.
"I am," she murmured, and her voice was steady, stripped of all theatrics.
"Truly...
When I was trapped within Ititus, I thought I was going to be erased...
I thought House Whitmore would receive a sealed urn, and Penelope would be left alone in this world...
Today, being here with you, with the girls, with Martha, is the first time in a while my chest hasn’t felt like an open wound...
I enjoyed today more than I have words for."
A faint smirk tugged at her lips.
"And besides, we’re wearing matching pajamas.
That practically makes us a crew under common maritime law."
"Captain Harper," Silas said, bowing slightly.
"I’ll try to be worthy."
She laughed, then stepped forward and wrapped her arms around his neck in a brief tight hug.
"Protocol requires physical anchoring for optimal rest," she mumbled against his shoulder.
"Granted," Silas said, and hugged her back until the last tension drained out of her spine then she slipped inside, and the door clicked softly shut.
Down the hall, in Lia’s room, two small lamps burned low.

Lia lay on her stomach across the quilt in her oversized green pajamas, a sheet of heavy calligraphy paper spread in front of her, a pot of lavender ink at her elbow and her tongue poking out the corner of her mouth.
She had crossed out the first line four times.
"What are you writing?" Penelope asked from the pillow beside her, though she plainly already knew.
"A letter to Miss Eluned." Lia did not look up.
"Dear Miss Eluned, thank you for catching the building...
Also, I am sorry about the part where I was rude to you in the grass."
She scowled at the page.
"I wasn’t rude.
I just asked a lot of questions.
Is that rude?"
"It is thorough," Penelope said diplomatically.
She rolled onto her back and stared at the ceiling.
After a while her voice went smaller.
"Lia.
Do you think my sister is going to be all right?"
Lia put the brush down.
She was eleven, and she had spent a long time being the one who held the family apart so she knew exactly what a question like that sounded like when it was really asking for something else.
"She hugged my brother on the doorstep like she’d been holding her breath for two weeks," Lia said.
"And then she tried to make him eat flat soup, I think people who do both of those things are going to be fine..."
Penelope let out a shaky little laugh.
"The soup was not flat."
"The soup was perfect.
He’s a liar." Lia picked the brush back up, then paused.
"Write your own letter, if you want...
I’ll share the ink."
The two of them bent over the paper together with the lavender ink drying in long careful strokes, while the house settled and the lamps burned low.
In the master bedroom, Silas set the tin of tea on the nightstand and plugged his phone into the charging dock.
He lay on top of the covers, staring up at the shadowy molding of the ceiling.
’I’m not even that exhausted...’
On a whim he swiped open his territory ledger and tried to query the incubator bay, picturing the cluster of spider eggs sitting in their warm stone cradles.
The interface blinked back at him.
[Remote Territorial Inspection Unavailable Outside The Sovereign Realm...
Please Return In Person.]
He sighed and swiped it away.
Whatever had hatched or not hatched would have to wait for morning, and he made a mental note to warn the girls to knock before opening any door in the west wing.
’Tomorrow morning I’ll slip through the spatial coordinates and return to Blessed Land,’ he decided. ’Hopefully Thor hasn’t burnt down the brewery while I’ve been gone.’
His thoughts drifted outward.
’I wonder how Aki’s doing.’
However, the next moment, the door opened and Silas looked to it as he blinked.
"Harper, why are you here?"
In the Sovereign Realm, the wind that blew across the rolling hills didn’t carry the necrotic chill of the Umbral Basin.
It didn’t reek of rot, petrified bone, or anything at all...
Instead the air was crisp and clean, with the sharp invigorating fragrance of crushed wild mint and blooming mountain laurel.
Princess Aki stood at the crest of a low grass-covered knoll, the hem of her loose white traveler’s tunic snapping gently in the breeze.
