chapters.title: Chapter 646: Lady Eluned’s Smell [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: "GWAHAHAHAHAHAHA!"
A booming roar of laughter shattered the tranquil mountain air, followed immediately by a belch that shook the leaves of the nearby birch trees.
BURRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRP!
"Hell of a view!" Thor declared, floating casually down from the sky above the knoll.
The Norse champion drifted weightlessly through the air with her muscular sun-tanned arms bare and her celestial bronze armor gleaming under the golden sunlight.
In her left hand, balanced effortlessly on her palm, was a massive two-gallon wooden cask of frothing dwarven ale, while her right hand idly spun Mjolnir by its leather strap.
She landed on the grass beside Aki with a soft thud, took a massive foaming gulp from the cask, and wiped her mouth with the back of her wrist.

"Looks like a proper kingdom!" Thor boomed, gesturing with the cask toward the tidy newly erected white-stone perimeter wall encircling the three-acre territory. "Clean grass! Fresh air! None of that miserable sulfurous dust Silas keeps making us dig through down in the south! Truly, a domain fit for a proper royal maiden!"
Aki let out a long sigh, rolling her large sapphire eyes as she turned to look at the floating goddess.

"Do you really have to belch like an artillery piece every time you cross my airspace, Thor?" Aki groaned, resting her hands on her hips. "Are you trying to intimidate my first summoned Hero before she even steps through the archway?"
The wall itself had gone up in the first twenty minutes, a ring of neat white stone twelve feet high with a single iron-banded gate, built from the material caches Silas had made her keep.
Inside it sat her boundary stone, a small unfinished hall of timber and pale granite, and a surprisingly cheerful vegetable plot that Mira would have wept to see.
It was not much but it was hers, down to the last carefully measured foundation stone.
’And I’m satisfied... I can always borrow from the main territory.’
Aki glanced to her right.
Carved into the flat bedrock near the eastern gate of her territory was a massive twenty-foot circular array of glowing gold and violet runes.
It was the Territorial Anchor Gate, the direct spatial bridge linking her vassal domain to Blessed Land.
Because Silas had used his own Gold Core to awaken her and she was his vassal, the Sovereign Realm had bound them together permanently.
The champions of Blessed Land were free to step across the threshold into her borders whenever they pleased, and Aki could stroll into Silas’s orchards as easily as walking into an adjacent room.
Thor took another massive swig of ale and let out a satisfied smack of her lips.

"Intimidate them?" Thor scoffed, her bright blue eyes twinkling with boisterous amusement. "If a warrior is intimidated by a woman enjoying a tankard of cold brew, then they are either a fragile mortal or some pathetic limp-wristed weakling who hates women! And we don’t need those kinds of cowards in this place anyway!"
Aki offered a wry, knowing smile. "Well, you won’t have to worry about fragile men, Thor."
She pointed a delicate finger toward the glowing boundary stone at the center of the camp.

"Because my domain is registered as a Vassal Territory under Blessed Land," Aki explained, her voice carrying a note of quiet pride, "my place automatically inherited Silas’s passive territory trait... Divine Sanctum."
Thor froze mid-gulp and lowered the wooden cask from her lips. "Divine Sanctum?"
"Yes," Aki nodded, a cheerful giggle escaping her. "I can only summon female troops and female champions... The territorial field outright rejects male summoning frequencies."

Thor stared at her for a single stunned second then she threw her head back and let out a laugh so loud and concussive that two birds in the distant trees plummeted three feet before catching their wings.

"GWAHAHAHAHAHAHAHA!" Thor roared, slapping her armored thigh with a metallic clang. "GLORIOUS! MAGNIFICENT! Silas truly is a genius! An entire army composed purely of fierce, battle-hungry maidens! I’m going to challenge every single one of them to an arm-wrestling match before sunset!"

"Besides," Aki added, ticking points off on her fingers, "a hall full of undisciplined knights would eat three times the rations and argue with every order... The Sanctum solves two problems at once."
"And a third!" Thor boomed. "No one to ruin my arm-wrestling record!"
Aki smiled, crossing her arms beneath her chest.
She was a bit happy about the restriction.
In the high courts of Rhyx City, she had spent years reading private complaints from female lords.

The summoning pools were filled with arrogant undisciplined male knights who constantly questioned female commanders, undermined orders, and spent half their watches inappropriately ogling their mistresses.
Aki had zero interest in managing that kind of rot.

’And besides,’ a secret, warm thought brushed against her mind, ’if someone is going to be ogling my body, I would much rather it be Silas than some random greasy mercenary lord from the central plains.’
The thought hit her with sudden clarity, and her cheeks erupted into a blinding crimson.
’WAIT! WHAT AM I THINKING?!’
SLAP! SLAP!
Aki brought both hands up and smacked her own cheeks with two loud, sharp cracks.

’Stop it! Stop it, you shameless royal degenerate!’ Aki scolded herself frantically, shaking her blue head until her hair thrashed wildly. ’Silas has Lady Eluned! He has Lady Aeliana! He’s surrounded by breathtaking goddesses with legs that reach their chins and figures like sculpted marble! My body isn’t even developed like that! I’m petite! I look like a scholar who hasn’t seen the sun in three years!... Why would he ever look at me like that?!’
Thor lowered her ale cask, tilting her head as she watched the young princess slap herself like an wild marionette.

"What in Odin’s name are you doing, girl?" Thor asked, her brow furrowing in bewildered concern. "Did a wasp sting your nose? You’ve slapped yourself three times in forty seconds. If your brain is malfunctioning, drink some ale... it resets the humors."
Aki stopped, panting slightly with her cheeks stinging with bright red handprints.

She looked at Thor’s towering seven-foot frame, at the celestial bronze cuirass straining against a chest the size of two heavy war-shields, framed by thick sculpted pectorals and steel-hard deltoids.
A sudden wave of petty feminine frustration boiled over in her chest.
"You," Aki muttered, narrowing her sapphire eyes.
"Me?" Thor blinked.
THWACK!
Aki stepped forward and slapped her open palm straight against Thor’s right breast.
CLANK!
A sound like a blacksmith’s hammer striking an anvil echoed across the grass and Aki froze with her eyes snapping wide.

"OWWWWWWWWWWWWWWW!" Aki shrieked, clutching her right hand to her chest and hopping on one foot across the lawn in blinding agony. "WHAT IN THE HEAVENS IS THAT?! YOUR BREASTS ARE SOLID MUSCLE! IT FEELS LIKE HITTING A REINFORCED GRANITE SLAB!"
Thor didn’t even flinch.
She looked down at her chest, looked back at the hopping princess, and let out a boisterous delighted chuckle.
She took a deep breath and flexed her upper torso, her pectorals contracting with such concussive force beneath her armor that the bronze plates groaned.

"Of course they’re muscle!" Thor declared proudly, pounding her own chest with a heavy fist that would have cracked Silas’s ribs. "I swing Mjolnir eight thousand times a day! Do you think thunder generates itself from fat deposits?! These are forged from pure celestial iron and roasted boar meat!"
Aki blew on her throbbing knuckles, pouting with enough intensity to crack porcelain. "Unfair... Absolutely unfair... The gods play favorites."
"Gwahaha! Drink more milk, little princess!" Thor laughed, reaching into a leather pouch at her belt and tearing off a massive, greasy leg of roasted wild boar with her teeth.
"Stop laughing," Aki muttered, though the corner of her mouth twitched. "Shouldn’t you be doing something useful? Like explaining why Tier 2 Peak is so common out here?"

"Because the Sovereign Realm likes watching new lords panic," Thor said cheerfully through a mouthful of boar. "Give them a pretty view and a thousand hungry teeth... Don’t worry, I’ll clear the Thorn-Stalkers myself if they get bold but a lord ought to see her first Hero fight, so I’ll hold off until the lady’s had her turn."
Aki shook her stinging hand, took a deep steadying breath to clear her head, and turned her back on the noisy thunder-goddess.
She walked with firm determined steps toward the center of her camp.
Rising from the grassy clearing was her Summoning Portal.
It wasn’t the plain white stone arch of an ordinary novice lord.

It was a single soaring archway of pale rose-veined white marble, its twin pillars inlaid with spiraling threads of beaten gold and wrapped in dormant crystalline vines, its crown carved into a pair of sea-drakes curling around a sun of star-silver.
Between the pillars hung a shimmering, empty space, and at the base of the right pillar stood a slender pedestal topped with a circular holder of polished star-silver.
It looked like the gate to a queen’s palace, which Aki thought was only appropriate.
"Thor," Aki called over her shoulder, pausing with one hand on the cool marble of the pillar.
"Thor," she repeated, softer, "thank you for coming. I know you have a hundred better things to do than watch a novice lord pick her first card."
Thor blinked, the ale cask halfway to her mouth, and for once she had no boast ready.
"Silas asked me to look after you," she said, with surprising gentleness. "But I would have come anyway... You are the first lord in an age who read the manual before the monsters."
Aki flushed, then squared her shoulders.
For a moment, though, her fingers tightened on the cold marble, and the bravado slipped enough for Thor to see it.

"I’m frightened," Aki admitted quietly. "Not of the monsters... I read about them all my life. I’m frightened that I’ll summon someone and she’ll look at me and see a princess who could never lift a sword... All those years in the archives, people told me I was clever for someone with no core so I’ve never had to be anything but clever."
Thor was silent for a heartbeat, which for Thor was a very long time then she dropped to the ground beside Aki with her armor clanging and set her ale cask down on the grass.

"Well, Silas looked at a pile of cards and a girl who had never held a sword," Thor said, "and he gave her this power without blinking. Does that sound like a man who is worried about your usefulness?"
Aki let out a tiny wet laugh. "I’m glad..."
"Of course you should be glad." Thor grinned and ruffled her hair with a hand the size of a dinner plate. "Now go and summon your first friend, little princess. I’ll stand behind you."
Aki turned back to the pedestal.
Her voice regained its crisp authority.
"Now pay attention. Under standard deployment protocols, a newly initialized lord must summon their primary Hero before initiating troop formations..."
Thor drifted over, chewing on her boar meat, hovering four feet above the grass with her tankard cradled in the crook of her arm.

"Aye, aye, commander. I’m watching. Summon someone who likes a good brawl!" She jabbed her ale cask toward the Thorn-Stalkers at the treeline. "And if she’s any good, I want first pick of their carapaces... Chitin that thick makes excellent mugs..."
"Their carapaces belong to the treasury," Aki said primly. "But I will consider a commission."
Aki reached into her newly acquired Lord’s tab.
SHING!
With a delicate flick of her wrist, a single glowing card materialized between her slender fingers.
It was a pristine gold-bordered Hero Summoning Ticket, its surface pulsing with a soft luminescence that caught the golden afternoon sun.
Aki held the ticket close to her chest and closed her sapphire eyes, her eyelashes fluttering against her pale skin and Aki brought the card to her lips.
CHOO!
She planted a soft, reverent kiss against the golden parchment.
"Please," Aki whispered into the mountain breeze, her voice trembling with earnest hope. "Summon me someone as cool as Lady Eluned... someone who can protect this land with gentle strength."
She stepped up to the pedestal, leaned forward, and slid the glowing card into the star-silver holder.
CLICK!
The card seated perfectly.
For a single heartbeat, the world held its breath as the wind over the meadow died completely and the chirping of the distant birds cut off as if severed by a blade.
The Iron-Spined Thorn-Stalkers at the forest edge froze, their tails dropping flat against the soil in sudden instinctive terror.
Then a deep tone rose from the marble... a sound that was felt in the bones more than heard, reverberating straight through the bedrock of the Sovereign Realm.
HUMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMM!
The dormant runes carved into the soaring archway flared from dull stone to an incandescent, blinding gold.
It began as a soft, pulsing ring around the pedestal then....
CRACK-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A colossal vertical pillar of celestial gold radiance erupted from the archway and tore straight through the clouds like an lance.
The light was so pure that Thor instinctively threw her arm over her eyes, her boisterous laugh dying in her throat as the atmospheric pressure over the territory spiked.

The golden beam punched through the shimmering barrier covering Aki’s territory, shattering the dome into millions of sparkling motes, and then, a single heartbeat later, the motes drew back together and the barrier knit itself whole again looking seamless and unharmed.
The light churned, weaving itself into a tight, dense cyclone of starlight.
Silver motes rained down through the golden glare like falling snow, carrying a fragrance of cold night ai.
Aki stood at the edge of the platform with her hands raised against the gale, her sapphire hair whipping wildly as her breath caught in her throat.
’Who?’ she thought, her heart hammering against her ribs like a war drum. ’Who could carry mana this heavy?!’
She was not as strong as Eluned and the others but strong regardless...
The pillar of light slowly began to contract, pulling inward toward the center of the archway and condensing into the tall powerful silhouette of a woman standing between the pillars.
The glare faded into a soft shimmer of golden motes.
She was an elf, and she was nothing like the delicate elves of the storybooks.

She stood six feet and one inch tall, almost level with Silas himself, and her frame was a warrior’s, broad through the shoulders and corded with lean hard muscle beneath the fitted gunmetal-and-white battle leathers that bared her forearms.

Her silver hair fell down her back in a heavy gleaming sheet that glowed with the pale cool color of a night moon, and small stellar marks... tiny pinpricks of faint silver light, were scattered across her cheekbones and the bridge of her nose like a constellation.
She slowly opened her eyes.
They were a piercing blue, sharp as glacial ice, and as the last of the starlight flared across her skin the blue deepened and bled into a luminous lilac purple like the way twilight bled into night.
She lifted her head and took a slow deep breath of the mountain breeze.
Her eyes drifted toward the eastern gate, locking onto the glowing anchor that led straight into the heart of Blessed Land.
Her lips parted.
"...Lady Eluned’s scent..."

Fresh air!
None of that miserable sulfurous dust Silas keeps making us dig through down in the south!
Truly, a domain fit for a proper royal maiden!"
Aki let out a long sigh, rolling her large sapphire eyes as she turned to look at the floating goddess.
"Do you really have to belch like an artillery piece every time you cross my airspace, Thor?" Aki groaned, resting her hands on her hips.
"Are you trying to intimidate my first summoned Hero before she even steps through the archway?"
The wall itself had gone up in the first twenty minutes, a ring of neat white stone twelve feet high with a single iron-banded gate, built from the material caches Silas had made her keep.
Inside it sat her boundary stone, a small unfinished hall of timber and pale granite, and a surprisingly cheerful vegetable plot that Mira would have wept to see.
It was not much but it was hers, down to the last carefully measured foundation stone.
’And I’m satisfied...
I can always borrow from the main territory.’
Aki glanced to her right.
Carved into the flat bedrock near the eastern gate of her territory was a massive twenty-foot circular array of glowing gold and violet runes.
It was the Territorial Anchor Gate, the direct spatial bridge linking her vassal domain to Blessed Land.
Because Silas had used his own Gold Core to awaken her and she was his vassal, the Sovereign Realm had bound them together permanently.
The champions of Blessed Land were free to step across the threshold into her borders whenever they pleased, and Aki could stroll into Silas’s orchards as easily as walking into an adjacent room.
Thor took another massive swig of ale and let out a satisfied smack of her lips.
"Intimidate them?" Thor scoffed, her bright blue eyes twinkling with boisterous amusement.
"If a warrior is intimidated by a woman enjoying a tankard of cold brew, then they are either a fragile mortal or some pathetic limp-wristed weakling who hates women!
And we don’t need those kinds of cowards in this place anyway!"
Aki offered a wry, knowing smile.
"Well, you won’t have to worry about fragile men, Thor."
She pointed a delicate finger toward the glowing boundary stone at the center of the camp.

"Because my domain is registered as a Vassal Territory under Blessed Land," Aki explained, her voice carrying a note of quiet pride, "my place automatically inherited Silas’s passive territory trait...
Divine Sanctum."
Thor froze mid-gulp and lowered the wooden cask from her lips.
"Divine Sanctum?"
"Yes," Aki nodded, a cheerful giggle escaping her.
"I can only summon female troops and female champions...
The territorial field outright rejects male summoning frequencies."

Thor stared at her for a single stunned second then she threw her head back and let out a laugh so loud and concussive that two birds in the distant trees plummeted three feet before catching their wings.
"GWAHAHAHAHAHAHAHA!" Thor roared, slapping her armored thigh with a metallic clang.
"GLORIOUS!
MAGNIFICENT!
Silas truly is a genius!
An entire army composed purely of fierce, battle-hungry maidens!
I’m going to challenge every single one of them to an arm-wrestling match before sunset!"
"Besides," Aki added, ticking points off on her fingers, "a hall full of undisciplined knights would eat three times the rations and argue with every order...
The Sanctum solves two problems at once."
"And a third!" Thor boomed.
"No one to ruin my arm-wrestling record!"
Aki smiled, crossing her arms beneath her chest.
She was a bit happy about the restriction.
In the high courts of Rhyx City, she had spent years reading private complaints from female lords.

The summoning pools were filled with arrogant undisciplined male knights who constantly questioned female commanders, undermined orders, and spent half their watches inappropriately ogling their mistresses.
Aki had zero interest in managing that kind of rot.

’And besides,’ a secret, warm thought brushed against her mind, ’if someone is going to be ogling my body, I would much rather it be Silas than some random greasy mercenary lord from the central plains.’
The thought hit her with sudden clarity, and her cheeks erupted into a blinding crimson.
’WAIT!
WHAT AM I THINKING?!’
SLAP!
SLAP!
Aki brought both hands up and smacked her own cheeks with two loud, sharp cracks.
’Stop it!
Stop it, you shameless royal degenerate!’ Aki scolded herself frantically, shaking her blue head until her hair thrashed wildly. ’Silas has Lady Eluned!
He has Lady Aeliana!
He’s surrounded by breathtaking goddesses with legs that reach their chins and figures like sculpted marble!
My body isn’t even developed like that!
I’m petite!
I look like a scholar who hasn’t seen the sun in three years!...
Why would he ever look at me like that?!’
Thor lowered her ale cask, tilting her head as she watched the young princess slap herself like an wild marionette.
"What in Odin’s name are you doing, girl?" Thor asked, her brow furrowing in bewildered concern.
"Did a wasp sting your nose?
You’ve slapped yourself three times in forty seconds.
If your brain is malfunctioning, drink some ale... it resets the humors."
Aki stopped, panting slightly with her cheeks stinging with bright red handprints.

She looked at Thor’s towering seven-foot frame, at the celestial bronze cuirass straining against a chest the size of two heavy war-shields, framed by thick sculpted pectorals and steel-hard deltoids.
A sudden wave of petty feminine frustration boiled over in her chest.
"You," Aki muttered, narrowing her sapphire eyes.
"Me?" Thor blinked.
THWACK!
Aki stepped forward and slapped her open palm straight against Thor’s right breast.
CLANK!
A sound like a blacksmith’s hammer striking an anvil echoed across the grass and Aki froze with her eyes snapping wide.
"OWWWWWWWWWWWWWWW!" Aki shrieked, clutching her right hand to her chest and hopping on one foot across the lawn in blinding agony.
"WHAT IN THE HEAVENS IS THAT?!
YOUR BREASTS ARE SOLID MUSCLE!
IT FEELS LIKE HITTING A REINFORCED GRANITE SLAB!"
Thor didn’t even flinch.
She looked down at her chest, looked back at the hopping princess, and let out a boisterous delighted chuckle.
She took a deep breath and flexed her upper torso, her pectorals contracting with such concussive force beneath her armor that the bronze plates groaned.
"Of course they’re muscle!" Thor declared proudly, pounding her own chest with a heavy fist that would have cracked Silas’s ribs.
"I swing Mjolnir eight thousand times a day!
Do you think thunder generates itself from fat deposits?!
These are forged from pure celestial iron and roasted boar meat!"
Aki blew on her throbbing knuckles, pouting with enough intensity to crack porcelain.
"Unfair...
Absolutely unfair...
The gods play favorites."
"Gwahaha!
Drink more milk, little princess!" Thor laughed, reaching into a leather pouch at her belt and tearing off a massive, greasy leg of roasted wild boar with her teeth.
"Stop laughing," Aki muttered, though the corner of her mouth twitched.
"Shouldn’t you be doing something useful?
Like explaining why Tier 2 Peak is so common out here?"
"Because the Sovereign Realm likes watching new lords panic," Thor said cheerfully through a mouthful of boar.
"Give them a pretty view and a thousand hungry teeth...
Don’t worry, I’ll clear the Thorn-Stalkers myself if they get bold but a lord ought to see her first Hero fight, so I’ll hold off until the lady’s had her turn."
Aki shook her stinging hand, took a deep steadying breath to clear her head, and turned her back on the noisy thunder-goddess.
She walked with firm determined steps toward the center of her camp.
Rising from the grassy clearing was her Summoning Portal.
It wasn’t the plain white stone arch of an ordinary novice lord.

It was a single soaring archway of pale rose-veined white marble, its twin pillars inlaid with spiraling threads of beaten gold and wrapped in dormant crystalline vines, its crown carved into a pair of sea-drakes curling around a sun of star-silver.
Between the pillars hung a shimmering, empty space, and at the base of the right pillar stood a slender pedestal topped with a circular holder of polished star-silver.
It looked like the gate to a queen’s palace, which Aki thought was only appropriate.
"Thor," Aki called over her shoulder, pausing with one hand on the cool marble of the pillar.
"Thor," she repeated, softer, "thank you for coming.
I know you have a hundred better things to do than watch a novice lord pick her first card."
Thor blinked, the ale cask halfway to her mouth, and for once she had no boast ready.
"Silas asked me to look after you," she said, with surprising gentleness.
"But I would have come anyway...
You are the first lord in an age who read the manual before the monsters."
Aki flushed, then squared her shoulders.
For a moment, though, her fingers tightened on the cold marble, and the bravado slipped enough for Thor to see it.
"I’m frightened," Aki admitted quietly.
"Not of the monsters...
I read about them all my life.
I’m frightened that I’ll summon someone and she’ll look at me and see a princess who could never lift a sword...
All those years in the archives, people told me I was clever for someone with no core so I’ve never had to be anything but clever."
Thor was silent for a heartbeat, which for Thor was a very long time then she dropped to the ground beside Aki with her armor clanging and set her ale cask down on the grass.
"Well, Silas looked at a pile of cards and a girl who had never held a sword," Thor said, "and he gave her this power without blinking.
Does that sound like a man who is worried about your usefulness?"
Aki let out a tiny wet laugh.
"I’m glad..."
"Of course you should be glad." Thor grinned and ruffled her hair with a hand the size of a dinner plate.
"Now go and summon your first friend, little princess.
I’ll stand behind you."
Aki turned back to the pedestal.
Her voice regained its crisp authority.
"Now pay attention.
Under standard deployment protocols, a newly initialized lord must summon their primary Hero before initiating troop formations..."
Thor drifted over, chewing on her boar meat, hovering four feet above the grass with her tankard cradled in the crook of her arm.
"Aye, aye, commander.
I’m watching.
Summon someone who likes a good brawl!" She jabbed her ale cask toward the Thorn-Stalkers at the treeline.
"And if she’s any good, I want first pick of their carapaces...
Chitin that thick makes excellent mugs..."
"Their carapaces belong to the treasury," Aki said primly.
"But I will consider a commission."
Aki reached into her newly acquired Lord’s tab.
SHING!
With a delicate flick of her wrist, a single glowing card materialized between her slender fingers.
It was a pristine gold-bordered Hero Summoning Ticket, its surface pulsing with a soft luminescence that caught the golden afternoon sun.
Aki held the ticket close to her chest and closed her sapphire eyes, her eyelashes fluttering against her pale skin and Aki brought the card to her lips.
CHOO!
She planted a soft, reverent kiss against the golden parchment.
"Please," Aki whispered into the mountain breeze, her voice trembling with earnest hope.
"Summon me someone as cool as Lady Eluned... someone who can protect this land with gentle strength."
She stepped up to the pedestal, leaned forward, and slid the glowing card into the star-silver holder.
CLICK!
The card seated perfectly.
For a single heartbeat, the world held its breath as the wind over the meadow died completely and the chirping of the distant birds cut off as if severed by a blade.
The Iron-Spined Thorn-Stalkers at the forest edge froze, their tails dropping flat against the soil in sudden instinctive terror.
Then a deep tone rose from the marble... a sound that was felt in the bones more than heard, reverberating straight through the bedrock of the Sovereign Realm.
HUMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMM!
The dormant runes carved into the soaring archway flared from dull stone to an incandescent, blinding gold.
It began as a soft, pulsing ring around the pedestal then....
CRACK-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A colossal vertical pillar of celestial gold radiance erupted from the archway and tore straight through the clouds like an lance.
The light was so pure that Thor instinctively threw her arm over her eyes, her boisterous laugh dying in her throat as the atmospheric pressure over the territory spiked.

The golden beam punched through the shimmering barrier covering Aki’s territory, shattering the dome into millions of sparkling motes, and then, a single heartbeat later, the motes drew back together and the barrier knit itself whole again looking seamless and unharmed.
The light churned, weaving itself into a tight, dense cyclone of starlight.
Silver motes rained down through the golden glare like falling snow, carrying a fragrance of cold night ai.
Aki stood at the edge of the platform with her hands raised against the gale, her sapphire hair whipping wildly as her breath caught in her throat.
’Who?’ she thought, her heart hammering against her ribs like a war drum. ’Who could carry mana this heavy?!’
She was not as strong as Eluned and the others but strong regardless...
The pillar of light slowly began to contract, pulling inward toward the center of the archway and condensing into the tall powerful silhouette of a woman standing between the pillars.
The glare faded into a soft shimmer of golden motes.
She was an elf, and she was nothing like the delicate elves of the storybooks.

She stood six feet and one inch tall, almost level with Silas himself, and her frame was a warrior’s, broad through the shoulders and corded with lean hard muscle beneath the fitted gunmetal-and-white battle leathers that bared her forearms.

Her silver hair fell down her back in a heavy gleaming sheet that glowed with the pale cool color of a night moon, and small stellar marks... tiny pinpricks of faint silver light, were scattered across her cheekbones and the bridge of her nose like a constellation.
She slowly opened her eyes.
They were a piercing blue, sharp as glacial ice, and as the last of the starlight flared across her skin the blue deepened and bled into a luminous lilac purple like the way twilight bled into night.
She lifted her head and took a slow deep breath of the mountain breeze.
Her eyes drifted toward the eastern gate, locking onto the glowing anchor that led straight into the heart of Blessed Land.
Her lips parted.
"...Lady Eluned’s scent..."

chapters.title: Chapter 647: Emotions
paragraphs: Ther’Abella turned in three slow circles with her palms empty and her eyes darting across the moss-slick terraces.
The sun beat down broad and clean through the upper branches, casting shadows that shifted with every breath of wind through Yggdrasil.
The canopy was alive, noisy, and full of moving bodies.

Down in the lower rings of the Sovereign Realm, wandering vagrants and provincial lords spoke of Yggdrasil as a monument, a solitary silent spire of petrified timber that simply bled raw vitality into the planetary soil.
They wrote hymns about a dead pillar of life.
To those who drew breath upon its vast ribs, the World Tree was an empire.

Entire stone-paved districts rested upon the primary boughs. Aqueducts fed by clear celestial springs cut through living wood without rotting it, cascading into ornamental cisterns where juvenile spirits dipped their heels.
The bark was thick and warm underfoot, and it vibrated with a low thrum like the pulse of an ancient sleeping sovereign.
Its people were hers, too.

The elves of Yggdrasil did not follow Lady Eluned the way subjects follow a queen... They worshipped her as every house, every guild, and every child who left a white lotus on the edge of a cistern belonged to her pantheon, a congregation of tens of thousands who had built their temples and their whole lives around the goddess who held up the sky above them.
"Ther’Abella!"
The shouting echoed from the tiered walkways above the courtyard.
"Ther’Abella, if Captain Kaelith catches you without your polearm on morning inspection, she’s going to make you scrub the resin vats until your fingernails turn amber!"
Ther’Abella winced, tossing her head so her long silver hair spilled over her shoulder.
She recognized the voice immediately... It was Evandra, who was likely pacing by the training yard with her hand already clamped to her scabbard.
The Viridian Guard was assembling for the third rotation of the watch.
They were the sworn protectors of the World Tree and Lady Eluned, eight elite elven maidens chosen from nine thousand applicants, tasked with guarding the sanctum day and night.
Any one of them could hold a bridge alone against a Tier 4 horde, and together they had never lost a drill, a duel, or a wager.
Ther’Abella was the youngest, and the only one still afraid of Captain Kaelith’s resin vats.
In truth, every woman in the squad knew the assignment was an honorable redundancy.

Lady Eluned did not need a guard... If Ther’Abella were forced to measure the Lady against every crowned sovereign, ancestral spirit, and high conqueror who walked the Sovereign Realm, Eluned stood above them all.

She had not crawled through the mud of mortal cultivation, no, the woman had been born from the former Tree Spirit, her mother, who had chosen to become ether itself, dissolving her own primordial essence into the air of the sanctum so that two daughters could be born from the vapor.
The instant Eluned drew her first breath within the heartwood hollow, the foundations of the world had cracked as she had stepped out of the womb as an ascended deity.
Because of that instantaneous, terrifying leap into godhood, there were things she had simply never touched.
The ordinary experiences of an elf, the clumsy adolescent years, the scraped knees, the slow gathering of mortal attachments, had been bypassed entirely.
She had begun at the peak, watching the world crawl beneath her canopy.
"Your weapon is here."
The voice was cool and carried no weight at all... It sounded like dry leaves drifting over polished stone.
Ther’Abella stopped in her tracks.
She had reached the arched entryway of the Grand Library, where thousands of leather-bound folios and bark-skin scrolls were nestled into the living grain of the hollow trunk.
Standing by a low cedar table was Lady Eluned.
The Spirit of the World Tree was breathtaking, though she was noticeably petite beside the towering wide-shouldered frame of her late mother.
What she lacked in height she made up for with an effortless sculpted perfection that seemed entirely at odds with the mortal world.

Her jade-tinted robes brushed against the moss on the flagstones and her emerald hair fell in loose fragrant waves down to her waist, crowned with white star-lotuses that never withered and never bloomed beyond half-parted petals.
It was nearly impossible to picture Lady Eluned with anyone.
She seemed genuinely oblivious to the posturing of the high elven lords who frequented the court, and she showed zero interest in the theatrics of romance...
Yet, as Ther’Abella looked at her, a small, quiet thought that had nagged at her for decades surfaced again.
’She acts so robotic sometimes.’
Was it because she couldn’t understand?
She had lived for over a thousand years upon the highest bough, and her reactions often lacked the natural messiness of living creatures.
Rustle!

A thin emerald vine uncoiled smoothly from the vaulted ceiling above, wrapped around the shaft of Ther’Abella’s silver polearm, and lowered it through the air with precision until the iron butt clicked against the floorboards.
"Thank you, Lady Eluned," Ther’Abella breathed, catching the haft with both hands.
As she stepped forward, Eluned tossed the text she had been holding onto the table.
The paper fell open, and Ther’Abella’s blue eyes instantly caught the gilded lettering across the cover.
[Guides to Romance: A Comprehensive Survey of Mortal Longing.]
Ther’Abella’s mouth opened slightly. She blinked.
"Guides to Romance?" she read aloud with her voice trembling slightly.
She snapped her gaze up to Eluned’s face.
Eluned stared back at her with a completely blank expression.
Her porcelain brow did not knit, her eyes did not narrow, and not a single muscle twitched around her mouth.
’Aren’t people supposed to act flustered when someone catches them reading something like that?’ Ther’Abella wondered with an awkward sweat breaking out beneath her silver bangs.
"Sit down," Eluned said flatly, pointing toward a woven wicker chair beside the table.
Ther’Abella propped her polearm against the carved bookshelf and slid into the chair, her knees together and her posture rigid.
"My Lady?"
A slow faint dusting of pink began to spread over the pale skin of Eluned’s cheeks.
It was subtle, like a drop of pomegranate juice sinking into milk, but it was unmistakably there.
"Tell me," Eluned said, leaning forward slightly, her green eyes fixed on Ther’Abella’s pupils. "What is romance?"
Ther’Abella’s face ignited in an instant. A violent heat rushed to her pointed ears, turning the tips dark red.

"R-Romance?" Ther’Abella stammered, her fingers clutching her knees. "Well, it’s when two people find an affinity that goes beyond duty.. You care for someone’s happiness more than your own comfort... Your chest tightens when you see them approach, your thoughts return to them when you’re alone in the dark, and you want to hold their hand, share their meals, and stand between them and harm."
Eluned listened without blinking, her fingers flat on the cedar table.
"I still find it confusing," Eluned murmured, shaking her head. "Even after a thousand years of watching the lower districts from the canopy, the mechanics make very little sense."
She looked down at her own pale hands and flexed her fingers slowly.

"I am a spirit of pure nature," she explained, her voice carrying a rare, quiet wistfulness. "I can detect the currents of sorrow. I can feel the sharpness of anger... it moves like lightning scorching dry timber but because I was born complete, because my mother passed her divine mantle to me the instant I opened my eyes, I cannot embody these things naturally... It is a wall, like a limitation placed upon my very divinity."
She poked the open page of the romance guide with one fingernail.
SNAP!
A burst of green life flared from the tip of her nail. The book shuddered as thick, pale-wood roots exploded from the spine, splitting the leather in two.
Within three seconds the manual had transformed into a small leafy dogwood sapling that sat upright on the table with its branches trembling in the draft.
Eluned looked at the little tree.
Her lower lip pushed out slightly and she pouted.
It was a small genuinely frustrated pout that looked utterly bizarre on an immortal goddess.
"When am I going to fall in love at this rate?" she grumbled softly, crossing her arms beneath her chest.
Ther’Abella stared, dumbfounded.
In every ceremonial gathering, in every assembly of the high houses, Lady Eluned was a monument of serene majesty.
She commanded the sky, she dictated the harvest, and she looked down on kings without blinking.
Who could possibly guess that she sat alone in the library, stewing over her inability to feel a flutter in her stomach?

"Lady Eluned," Ther’Abella ventured carefully, leaning across the table. "Have you considered looking among the high lords? An elven arch-magus from the western terraces? Or perhaps an immortal from one of the outer pantheons? There are dozens of princes who would throw their armies into an abyss just to receive an audience..."

"No," Eluned said instantly with her tone flat and dismissive. "They are predictable... They look at me and they see the World Tree’s territory under their control. I doubt they can understand what love is..."
She lifted her chin, and her green eyes softened until they seemed to look straight through the ceiling of the library, staring into some distant unfathomable void beyond the Sovereign Realm itself.

"I know there is someone special for me," Eluned murmured. Her voice drifted, taking on a slow tone cadence that made Ther’Abella hold her breath. "I can feel the feeling in the deep roots... It is faint, like a bell ringing beneath deep water. I cannot see his face, and I cannot pinpoint his coordinates, but I know he does not walk within the Sovereign Realm. He is somewhere out there, beyond the veil in a way."
’Can deities actually sense their soulmates like that?’ Ther’Abella thought, her eyes widening.
A sudden sharp protectiveness flared in the young shieldmaiden’s chest.
If there truly was some unknown man out there destined to stand beside Lady Eluned, Ther’Abella would find him first.
She would test his steel, evaluate his manners, and make sure he wasn’t some arrogant loud-mouthed commoner before he was ever allowed within ten yards of the Goddess.

"Lady Eluned," Ther’Abella asked, tilting her head, "why do you even want this? Isn’t romantic longing a weakness? For an immortal guardian, an emotional anchor only gives your enemies something to target..."
"I am curious," Eluned answered simply.
Ther’Abella opened her mouth to argue, but Eluned kept speaking, her words flowing in a quiet breathless rhythm that carried an astonishing amount of buried emotion.

"As a primordial spirit, it is nearly impossible for me to produce offspring though I can but I’ll have to do it naturally... and it’ll be much harder since I can’t even alter the nature of my body that far," Eluned said, her jade eyes fixed on the miniature tree on the table. "My mother had to become ether itself just to bring forth Ellvi and myself... I do not want that. I want to know what it feels like to love someone so deeply that your chest aches. I want to walk through an orchard in the evening, leaning against his shoulder while the sun sets. I want to carry his children beneath my heart, not out of some necessity to preserve the World Tree, but because we chose each other... I want to hear little voices running across the floorboards... I want to cook a simple meal for someone who doesn’t bow when I hand them a bowl."
Ther’Abella sat completely still.
The longing in the Goddess’s voice was so thick that she felt a lump rise in her throat.
She had never heard Eluned speak like this, not in a thousand years of royal service.
Eluned paused as she blinked, and the soft dreamy glow faded from her eyes, replaced once more by that cool unreadable calm.

"It might just be my imagination," Eluned said, with a faint, self-deprecating shrug. "A stray thought caused by reading foolish books... In the end, it does not matter. I do not mind staying here with all of you as you are enough."
Ther’Abella felt a rush of heat in her chest, her hands clenching into fists on her knees.
"I like being with you too, Lady Eluned! We all do! We would never leave your side!"
Eluned let out a soft genuine laugh, sounding like a rare musical chime that brightened the entire library.
She stood up, her jade robes sweeping over the flagstones and pooling gracefully around her ankles.
"You are my family," Eluned said, reaching out to pat Ther’Abella’s silver head with a cool, gentle hand. "You, the Guard, and my sister Ellvi. I am grateful for your service..."
She withdrew her hand, her expression turning serious.
"However, I have a request for you, Ther’Abella."
Ther’Abella scrambled to her feet, instinctively saluting with her right hand over her collarbone. "Name it, My Lady."

"Tomorrow," Eluned said, her voice dropping into a quiet, firm register, "do not come to the World Tree... Tell Captain Kaelith and the others to stand down. None of you are to enter the inner sanctum until the day after tomorrow."
Ther’Abella blinked, her brow furrowing in confusion. "Do not come? But My Lady, the daily patrol schedule—"

"I know what I am saying," Eluned interrupted gently. "It will be a rest day for the entire guard... You have trained hard for three centuries without a single leave so go into the lower city, drink sweet wine and rest. I do not need protection every hour of the day."
Ther’Abella stared at her for a moment before the realization clicked into place.
Tomorrow was the first anniversary of the Elven Overlord’s death.
A year ago, the great warrior who had united the northern reaches had fallen in battle, swallowed by an abyssal rift.
Lady Eluned had regarded him as a true brother, one of the few people whose presence she had actively enjoyed.

Every year she planned to spend that day in total isolation within the core sanctum, fasting and communing with the deep roots, and the grief of this first anniversary had hung over her for weeks like a bruise.
Ther’Abella was also aware of the rumors, which had grown louder in recent weeks.
A few bitter, disgraced elves in the outer rings whispered that Eluned had orchestrated his death using black magic to consolidate her reign over Yggdrasil.
Ther’Abella had always laughed at those tales.
Who could possibly believe that Lady Eluned, who couldn’t bring herself to crush a caterpillar, would kill her own kin with dark arts?
It did strike her as odd that the whispers had started so suddenly, all at once, in the same polished phrases, as if someone had written them out and handed them round.
"I understand, Lady Eluned," she said, bowing low. "I will inform the Captain and the squad. We will leave you to your peace..."
"Thank you, Ther’Abella," Eluned murmured, turning her back to look out through the library’s living archway.
"Ther’Abella! Move your legs, the drill is starting!" Evandra’s voice boomed from the courtyard outside.
"I’m coming!" Ther’Abella shouted back.
She grabbed her silver polearm, offered one last respectful bow to the Goddess, and walked toward the exit.
In the corridor she passed a woman coming the other way, tall and curvaceous in a corset of dark thorn-bark, her emerald hair so dark it was almost black.
Lady Ellvi paused with a warm smile and a languid wave, though her eyes lingered on Ther’Abella like the way a chess player studied a piece.
"A rest day?" Ellvi said pleasantly, in the voice of a woman who had somehow already heard. "How thoughtful of my sister."
Ther’Abella bowed, uneasy for a reason she couldn’t name, and hurried into the sunlight.
At the threshold she glanced back over her shoulder and waved with a bright youthful grin.
Eluned offered a small quiet wave in return.
’I want to be like her one day,’ Ther’Abella thought, gripping her weapon with pride as she sprinted toward the courtyard. ’Strong, kind, and untouchable...’
’Maybe I should have listened to Lady Eluned.’

She recognized the voice immediately...
It was Evandra, who was likely pacing by the training yard with her hand already clamped to her scabbard.
The Viridian Guard was assembling for the third rotation of the watch.
They were the sworn protectors of the World Tree and Lady Eluned, eight elite elven maidens chosen from nine thousand applicants, tasked with guarding the sanctum day and night.
Any one of them could hold a bridge alone against a Tier 4 horde, and together they had never lost a drill, a duel, or a wager.
Ther’Abella was the youngest, and the only one still afraid of Captain Kaelith’s resin vats.
In truth, every woman in the squad knew the assignment was an honorable redundancy.
Lady Eluned did not need a guard...
If Ther’Abella were forced to measure the Lady against every crowned sovereign, ancestral spirit, and high conqueror who walked the Sovereign Realm, Eluned stood above them all.

She had not crawled through the mud of mortal cultivation, no, the woman had been born from the former Tree Spirit, her mother, who had chosen to become ether itself, dissolving her own primordial essence into the air of the sanctum so that two daughters could be born from the vapor.
The instant Eluned drew her first breath within the heartwood hollow, the foundations of the world had cracked as she had stepped out of the womb as an ascended deity.
Because of that instantaneous, terrifying leap into godhood, there were things she had simply never touched.
The ordinary experiences of an elf, the clumsy adolescent years, the scraped knees, the slow gathering of mortal attachments, had been bypassed entirely.
She had begun at the peak, watching the world crawl beneath her canopy.
"Your weapon is here."
The voice was cool and carried no weight at all...
It sounded like dry leaves drifting over polished stone.
Ther’Abella stopped in her tracks.
She had reached the arched entryway of the Grand Library, where thousands of leather-bound folios and bark-skin scrolls were nestled into the living grain of the hollow trunk.
Standing by a low cedar table was Lady Eluned.
The Spirit of the World Tree was breathtaking, though she was noticeably petite beside the towering wide-shouldered frame of her late mother.
What she lacked in height she made up for with an effortless sculpted perfection that seemed entirely at odds with the mortal world.

Her jade-tinted robes brushed against the moss on the flagstones and her emerald hair fell in loose fragrant waves down to her waist, crowned with white star-lotuses that never withered and never bloomed beyond half-parted petals.
It was nearly impossible to picture Lady Eluned with anyone.
She seemed genuinely oblivious to the posturing of the high elven lords who frequented the court, and she showed zero interest in the theatrics of romance...
Yet, as Ther’Abella looked at her, a small, quiet thought that had nagged at her for decades surfaced again.
’She acts so robotic sometimes.’
Was it because she couldn’t understand?
She had lived for over a thousand years upon the highest bough, and her reactions often lacked the natural messiness of living creatures.
Rustle!

A thin emerald vine uncoiled smoothly from the vaulted ceiling above, wrapped around the shaft of Ther’Abella’s silver polearm, and lowered it through the air with precision until the iron butt clicked against the floorboards.
"Thank you, Lady Eluned," Ther’Abella breathed, catching the haft with both hands.
As she stepped forward, Eluned tossed the text she had been holding onto the table.
The paper fell open, and Ther’Abella’s blue eyes instantly caught the gilded lettering across the cover.
[Guides to Romance: A Comprehensive Survey of Mortal Longing.]
Ther’Abella’s mouth opened slightly.
She blinked.
"Guides to Romance?" she read aloud with her voice trembling slightly.
She snapped her gaze up to Eluned’s face.
Eluned stared back at her with a completely blank expression.
Her porcelain brow did not knit, her eyes did not narrow, and not a single muscle twitched around her mouth.
’Aren’t people supposed to act flustered when someone catches them reading something like that?’ Ther’Abella wondered with an awkward sweat breaking out beneath her silver bangs.
"Sit down," Eluned said flatly, pointing toward a woven wicker chair beside the table.
Ther’Abella propped her polearm against the carved bookshelf and slid into the chair, her knees together and her posture rigid.
"My Lady?"
A slow faint dusting of pink began to spread over the pale skin of Eluned’s cheeks.
It was subtle, like a drop of pomegranate juice sinking into milk, but it was unmistakably there.
"Tell me," Eluned said, leaning forward slightly, her green eyes fixed on Ther’Abella’s pupils.
"What is romance?"
Ther’Abella’s face ignited in an instant.
A violent heat rushed to her pointed ears, turning the tips dark red.
"R-Romance?" Ther’Abella stammered, her fingers clutching her knees.
"Well, it’s when two people find an affinity that goes beyond duty..
You care for someone’s happiness more than your own comfort...
Your chest tightens when you see them approach, your thoughts return to them when you’re alone in the dark, and you want to hold their hand, share their meals, and stand between them and harm."
Eluned listened without blinking, her fingers flat on the cedar table.
"I still find it confusing," Eluned murmured, shaking her head.
"Even after a thousand years of watching the lower districts from the canopy, the mechanics make very little sense."
She looked down at her own pale hands and flexed her fingers slowly.
"I am a spirit of pure nature," she explained, her voice carrying a rare, quiet wistfulness.
"I can detect the currents of sorrow.

I can feel the sharpness of anger... it moves like lightning scorching dry timber but because I was born complete, because my mother passed her divine mantle to me the instant I opened my eyes, I cannot embody these things naturally...
It is a wall, like a limitation placed upon my very divinity."
She poked the open page of the romance guide with one fingernail.
SNAP!
A burst of green life flared from the tip of her nail.
The book shuddered as thick, pale-wood roots exploded from the spine, splitting the leather in two.
Within three seconds the manual had transformed into a small leafy dogwood sapling that sat upright on the table with its branches trembling in the draft.
Eluned looked at the little tree.
Her lower lip pushed out slightly and she pouted.
It was a small genuinely frustrated pout that looked utterly bizarre on an immortal goddess.
"When am I going to fall in love at this rate?" she grumbled softly, crossing her arms beneath her chest.
Ther’Abella stared, dumbfounded.
In every ceremonial gathering, in every assembly of the high houses, Lady Eluned was a monument of serene majesty.
She commanded the sky, she dictated the harvest, and she looked down on kings without blinking.
Who could possibly guess that she sat alone in the library, stewing over her inability to feel a flutter in her stomach?
"Lady Eluned," Ther’Abella ventured carefully, leaning across the table.
"Have you considered looking among the high lords?
An elven arch-magus from the western terraces?
Or perhaps an immortal from one of the outer pantheons?
There are dozens of princes who would throw their armies into an abyss just to receive an audience..."
"No," Eluned said instantly with her tone flat and dismissive.
"They are predictable...
They look at me and they see the World Tree’s territory under their control.
I doubt they can understand what love is..."
She lifted her chin, and her green eyes softened until they seemed to look straight through the ceiling of the library, staring into some distant unfathomable void beyond the Sovereign Realm itself.
"I know there is someone special for me," Eluned murmured.
Her voice drifted, taking on a slow tone cadence that made Ther’Abella hold her breath.
"I can feel the feeling in the deep roots...
It is faint, like a bell ringing beneath deep water.
I cannot see his face, and I cannot pinpoint his coordinates, but I know he does not walk within the Sovereign Realm.
He is somewhere out there, beyond the veil in a way."
’Can deities actually sense their soulmates like that?’ Ther’Abella thought, her eyes widening.
A sudden sharp protectiveness flared in the young shieldmaiden’s chest.
If there truly was some unknown man out there destined to stand beside Lady Eluned, Ther’Abella would find him first.
She would test his steel, evaluate his manners, and make sure he wasn’t some arrogant loud-mouthed commoner before he was ever allowed within ten yards of the Goddess.
"Lady Eluned," Ther’Abella asked, tilting her head, "why do you even want this?
Isn’t romantic longing a weakness?
For an immortal guardian, an emotional anchor only gives your enemies something to target..."
"I am curious," Eluned answered simply.
Ther’Abella opened her mouth to argue, but Eluned kept speaking, her words flowing in a quiet breathless rhythm that carried an astonishing amount of buried emotion.

"As a primordial spirit, it is nearly impossible for me to produce offspring though I can but I’ll have to do it naturally... and it’ll be much harder since I can’t even alter the nature of my body that far," Eluned said, her jade eyes fixed on the miniature tree on the table.
"My mother had to become ether itself just to bring forth Ellvi and myself...
I do not want that.
I want to know what it feels like to love someone so deeply that your chest aches.
I want to walk through an orchard in the evening, leaning against his shoulder while the sun sets.
I want to carry his children beneath my heart, not out of some necessity to preserve the World Tree, but because we chose each other...
I want to hear little voices running across the floorboards...
I want to cook a simple meal for someone who doesn’t bow when I hand them a bowl."
Ther’Abella sat completely still.
The longing in the Goddess’s voice was so thick that she felt a lump rise in her throat.
She had never heard Eluned speak like this, not in a thousand years of royal service.
Eluned paused as she blinked, and the soft dreamy glow faded from her eyes, replaced once more by that cool unreadable calm.
"It might just be my imagination," Eluned said, with a faint, self-deprecating shrug.
"A stray thought caused by reading foolish books...
In the end, it does not matter.
I do not mind staying here with all of you as you are enough."
Ther’Abella felt a rush of heat in her chest, her hands clenching into fists on her knees.
"I like being with you too, Lady Eluned!
We all do!
We would never leave your side!"
Eluned let out a soft genuine laugh, sounding like a rare musical chime that brightened the entire library.
She stood up, her jade robes sweeping over the flagstones and pooling gracefully around her ankles.
"You are my family," Eluned said, reaching out to pat Ther’Abella’s silver head with a cool, gentle hand.
"You, the Guard, and my sister Ellvi.
I am grateful for your service..."
She withdrew her hand, her expression turning serious.
"However, I have a request for you, Ther’Abella."
Ther’Abella scrambled to her feet, instinctively saluting with her right hand over her collarbone.
"Name it, My Lady."
"Tomorrow," Eluned said, her voice dropping into a quiet, firm register, "do not come to the World Tree...
Tell Captain Kaelith and the others to stand down.
None of you are to enter the inner sanctum until the day after tomorrow."
Ther’Abella blinked, her brow furrowing in confusion.
"Do not come?
But My Lady, the daily patrol schedule—"
"I know what I am saying," Eluned interrupted gently.
"It will be a rest day for the entire guard...
You have trained hard for three centuries without a single leave so go into the lower city, drink sweet wine and rest.
I do not need protection every hour of the day."
Ther’Abella stared at her for a moment before the realization clicked into place.
Tomorrow was the first anniversary of the Elven Overlord’s death.
A year ago, the great warrior who had united the northern reaches had fallen in battle, swallowed by an abyssal rift.
Lady Eluned had regarded him as a true brother, one of the few people whose presence she had actively enjoyed.

Every year she planned to spend that day in total isolation within the core sanctum, fasting and communing with the deep roots, and the grief of this first anniversary had hung over her for weeks like a bruise.
Ther’Abella was also aware of the rumors, which had grown louder in recent weeks.
A few bitter, disgraced elves in the outer rings whispered that Eluned had orchestrated his death using black magic to consolidate her reign over Yggdrasil.
Ther’Abella had always laughed at those tales.
Who could possibly believe that Lady Eluned, who couldn’t bring herself to crush a caterpillar, would kill her own kin with dark arts?
It did strike her as odd that the whispers had started so suddenly, all at once, in the same polished phrases, as if someone had written them out and handed them round.
"I understand, Lady Eluned," she said, bowing low.
"I will inform the Captain and the squad.
We will leave you to your peace..."
"Thank you, Ther’Abella," Eluned murmured, turning her back to look out through the library’s living archway.
"Ther’Abella!
Move your legs, the drill is starting!" Evandra’s voice boomed from the courtyard outside.
"I’m coming!" Ther’Abella shouted back.
She grabbed her silver polearm, offered one last respectful bow to the Goddess, and walked toward the exit.
In the corridor she passed a woman coming the other way, tall and curvaceous in a corset of dark thorn-bark, her emerald hair so dark it was almost black.
Lady Ellvi paused with a warm smile and a languid wave, though her eyes lingered on Ther’Abella like the way a chess player studied a piece.
"A rest day?" Ellvi said pleasantly, in the voice of a woman who had somehow already heard.
"How thoughtful of my sister."
Ther’Abella bowed, uneasy for a reason she couldn’t name, and hurried into the sunlight.
At the threshold she glanced back over her shoulder and waved with a bright youthful grin.
Eluned offered a small quiet wave in return.
’I want to be like her one day,’ Ther’Abella thought, gripping her weapon with pride as she sprinted toward the courtyard. ’Strong, kind, and untouchable...’
’Maybe I should have listened to Lady Eluned.’

chapters.title: Chapter 648: A Ploy
paragraphs: The thought clawed at Ther’Abella’s mind like rusted iron.
The Guard had not stayed away.
Captain Kaelith had felt it first, a wrongness in the mana of the roots that no amount of sweet wine could drown out.
By dusk she had gathered the squad at the foot of the great stairs.
"We are going back early. If I am wrong, I will scrub the vats myself."
None of them had argued.
...It was the best decision any of them had made in three centuries, and it had come exactly one hour too late.
’We shouldn’t have come back early,’ Ther’Abella thought. ’We shouldn’t be here.’
The sky above the World Tree was not blue.
It was a churning bruise of charcoal purple, weeping heavy, freezing rain that drummed against the bark with a relentless roar.
The rain was cold, but the liquid pooling around Ther’Abella’s boots was hot.
Drip! Drip! Splat!
Golden luminescent blood splattered against the pale stones of the central sanctum and hissed as it corroded the pristine masonry.
In the center of the terrace, Lady Eluned was on her knees.
Her green robes were torn to ribbons and soaked in her own radiant blood as a long blade of blackened ironwood protruded through the center of her chest, slick with gold.
A hand reached out and wrenched the sword free with a sickening wet slide.
Shlick!
Eluned gasped with a thin stream of golden ichor trailing down her chin.

She tried to raise her hand toward the Viridian Guard, who stood paralyzed fifty yards away, but thick thorned roots dripping with purple miasma surged up from the fractured floorboards and coiled around her arms, her throat, and her waist, pinning her down.
Standing directly behind her, holding the dripping black sword, was Ellvi.
She was taller than her sister and far more heavily curved with her waist cinched in a corset of dark petrified thorn-bark.
Her emerald hair was almost black in the rain, and her eyes held a sharp malice that made Ther’Abella’s skin crawl.
She did not look like a woman acting in anger at all, to Ther’Abella, she looked like a woman who had rehearsed something for so long and was pleased to find that it fit.
In her left hand she held a scroll sealed with the World Tree’s own wax.
Behind her, a ring of grey-robed elders stood in a half-circle under the eaves, sheltered from the rain with their faces carefully composed.
Ther’Abella understood then that the elders were meant to be witnesses as Ellvi had not simply seized a throne... She had arranged a trial!

"By the authority of the World Tree," Ellvi’s voice rang out, carrying across the storm like a brass horn, "I hereby rescind your position as Spirit of the World Tree! For the murder of the Elven Overlord, a man we both called brother, committed through vile collusion with the dark rifts, your divinity is forfeit!"
She unrolled the scroll with a flick of her wrist and held it up so the elders could see the careful black script.

"Your own hand, sister... Your own seal... An order to open the rift beneath his war-camp." Her smile turned wistful. "It took me three weeks to master your penmanship! Your loops are atrocious, by the way... A goddess ought to take more care."
"Ellvi," Eluned choked out, her fingers weakly clawing at the black roots. "The roots. You have unsealed the—"
CRUNCH!
The massive roots twisted violently and pulled Eluned down into the gaping lightless chasm that had opened in the heartwood floor.
Ellvi leaned over the edge to watch her sister go, and then, with the tip of a polished boot, nudged a fallen star-lotus crown in after her.
"You won’t be needing that," she said. "I’m redecorating."
The World Tree shuddered with a colossal groan echoing from deep within its core as Lady Eluned was absorbed into the wood.
The instant she vanished, a tidal wave of golden-green mana erupted from the chasm and rushed straight into Ellvi’s chest.
Ellvi arched her back, throwing her head toward the stormy sky as the stolen power flooded her veins.
"Lady Ellvi!" Captain Kaelith shouted, stepping forward with her tower shield raised and her voice shaking with disbelief. "What is this?! How is this possible?! Release the Lady!"
Ellvi slowly lowered her head and looked at the eight shieldmaidens with venomous disdain.
She wiped a drop of golden blood from her cheek with her thumb, regarded it with distaste, and wiped it on the elder’s sleeve beside her.

"Good riddance," she sneered, in a cold purr. "For a thousand years her timid, saintly presence has been a thorn in my side... She held all this authority, yet she wept over dead leaves and refused to conquer the outer rings and you, Captain. I knew you would come back early... I planned for eight guards the way a gardener plans for weeds... A rest day was never going to hold you."
She smiled at the squad.
"Now. Why don’t you all die for me?"
She snapped her fingers.
BOOM!
A colossal dome of pressurized green mana exploded from Ellvi’s palm.
The shockwave hit the guards like a falling mountain, and Ther’Abella didn’t even have time to raise her polearm before the blast wave crushed her chest.
SNAP! CRACK! WHOOSH!
The force tore her arms from their sockets, shattered the bones in her forearms, and snapped her legs like brittle twigs.
The violent pressure ripped her off the sanctum platform and launched her body into the open sky above the canopy.
Spinning in the air, she caught one last glimpse of the terrace as her sisters were lifting their heads in the rain, and in their eyes, a sickly green light beginning to kindle...
Wind screamed in her ears and rain whipped across her face as she hurtled through the air toward the sprawling metropolis of the lower rings.
’Heal!’ her mind screamed through the blinding red haze. ’Circulate the mana!’
With a desperate ragged gasp, Ther’Abella forced her sluggish core to turn.
Green healing mana surged through her crushed limbs and dragged broken bone fragments back into place with sickening crunches.
She gritted her teeth until her gums bled, twisting her torso in mid-air to orient her boots toward the ground.
KABOOM!
Ther’Abella slammed into the center of a wide commercial plaza and blew a smoking crater into the granite pavers.

Stone fragments sprayed in all directions, shattering shop windows and tearing through awnings and Ther’Abella lay in the middle of the depression, vomiting blood onto the wet stone with her chest heaving as she struggled to push herself upright.
"Ug... Ugh... Help..."
’Lady Eluned,’ she thought with her vision blurring. ’Ellvi took her.’
The rain continued to hammer the plaza.
An amplified thunderous voice rolled across the entire district, echoing from the high towers along the bough.

"Citizens of Yggdrasil! The traitor Ther’Abella of the Viridian Guard has struck down our Lady! She conspired in secret with the dark forces that took our beloved Overlord a year ago! She is armed, dangerous, and carries silver hair and a moonlight spear! Find her! Bring her head to the roots!"
Ther’Abella pushed herself onto her knees with horror clamping around her throat.
’That will never work,’ she reasoned frantically, coughing up another clot of red. ’The people know us... They know Lady Eluned’s gentleness... They would never—’
"Officer?"
A soft hesitant voice spoke from the edge of the crater.
An elderly elven merchant in a leather apron stood at the rim and she recognized his kind face from her morning patrols.
He reached out a weathered hand and stepped down the slope of the rubble toward her.
"Are you hurt, child? Let me help you up."
Ther’Abella felt a surge of relief. "Sir, please, you have to hear me. Lady Ellvi is lying—"
The old man froze mid-step as his eyes went wide.
FZZZZT!
A sickly bright green glare ignited within his pupils and the welcoming hand did not grasp her fingers.
His fingernails lengthened into rigid wooden talons that stabbed straight for her jugular.
’No!’
Years of drills fired on instinct.
Ther’Abella threw her upper body backward and pressed her palms into the wet rock, and the wooden claws sliced through the air an inch above her nose, tearing the silver collar of her tunic.
Above the plaza, Ellvi’s voice roared from the towers, dripping with toxic command.
"IF YOU WISH TO LIVE, KILL HER! SHE KILLED YOUR OVERLORD! TEAR HER APART!"
Around the crater, dozens of elves, guards, merchants, and women carrying market baskets, turned their heads at the same moment.
Every pair of eyes ignited with the same unnatural green light.
"DIE!"
"TRAITOR!"
"AVENGE THE OVERLORD!"
They surged down the crater like a pack of rabid animals, pulling cleavers, iron ladles, and ornamental daggers from their belts.
A blast of wind-mana erupted from an incoming city guard and hurled a cluster of jagged stone spikes straight at her face.
Ther’Abella rolled aside, snatched her polearm from the mud, and watched the spikes obliterate the flagstones where she had been lying.
’They’re insane,’ she thought, scrambling to her feet. ’I have to run.’

She channeled wind-mana into her calves as a concentrated updraft blasted from the soles of her boots and launched her straight up out of the crater, over the grasping hands and onto the tiled roof of a three-story tea house.
Three enchanted arrows whistled through the downpour with their tips glowing with acidic green venom however she spun her polearm in a tight vertical circle.
CLANG! CLANG! TING!
The silver blade knocked two arrows into the rain gutters, and the third clipped her shoulder pauldron, hissing as it dissolved a layer of lacquer.
Down in the streets, hundreds of green-eyed elves poured out of alleyways and climbed the trellises and drainpipes with inhuman agility.
Spells of fire, pressurized water, and earth-spikes began bombarding the rooftops, blowing timber and ceramic shingles into flying shrapnel.
She sprinted.
WHOOSH!
Her boots slapped wet clay tiles as she leaped across narrow alleys, using small precise pulses of wind beneath her feet to glide between rooftops.
BOOM!
A bolt of lightning vaporized a brick chimney behind her.

She ducked under a sweeping wave of flame, cut a thrown cleaver out of the air with the flat of her blade, and vaulted a bunch of earth-spikes with a Gale Step that left a ring of shattered tile in her wake.
Behind her the mob grew by the minute, because the towers kept calling and the whole city kept answering.

Ahead stood an elite squad of the royal palace guard, blocking the massive suspension bridge that led toward the city limits was an officer in a shimmering mantle that warped the light around his shoulders, with the crest of Princess Selvanie embroidered along the hem.
’The Spatial Cloak,’ Ther’Abella realized. ’It belongs to Princess Selvanie’s private retinue...’
That cloak was an enchanted relic capable of short-range spatial translocation. If she could take it, she could bypass the city walls.
"STOP HER!" the officer shouted, drawing his rapier as his eyes flared green.
Ther’Abella didn’t slow down.
She leaped from the edge of the roof, wrapping her wind-mana around her body like a descending cyclone, and slammed into the center of the bridge.
Her polearm swept low with the haft catching two guards behind their knees and dropping them.
The officer’s rapier flickered toward her throat in three thrusts too fast to follow.
WHOOSH! WHOOSH! WHOOSH!

Ther’Abella turned the first with her haft, took the second across her cheek, and bent beneath the third, and before he could trigger the blade’s enchantment she closed the distance in one step, drove her shoulder into his sternum, and ripped the silver clasp of the Spatial Cloak clean off his collar.
"Traitor!" the officer choked out.
She threw the shimmering cloak around her shoulders, channeled raw mana into the hem, and pulled the hood forward.
VRRRRR-POP!
Space folded as the bridge, the screaming guards, and the rain-slicked roofs vanished into a silent blur of violet light.
’Take me out of here please...’
THUD!
Ther’Abella tumbled out of the spatial rift with her knees in muddy grass.
She was outside the city and ahead of her, rising against the dark, stormy horizon, were the colossal Outer Boundary Gates of Yggdrasil.

These were the dimensional portals at the very edge of the World Tree’s territory massive arched structures of ancient petrified wood intertwined with crystalline vines that hummed with a deep blue light.
They led outward, connecting the secluded realm of the elves to the wild sectors of the Sovereign Realm beyond and they were dying.

Because Lady Eluned had been torn from the tree’s core, the energy sustaining the gates was failing as the blue light sputtered, fading into a dull ash-gray, and the portals shrank and their edges contracting inward like burning paper.

’I have to cross,’ she thought, staggering to her feet and dragging her polearm through the mud. ’If I stay here, they will butcher me... I have to reach the Sovereign Realm, get stronger, and come back for Lady Eluned...’
She took three running steps toward the nearest archway.
THWIP-BOOM!
An explosive arrow struck the ground five feet in front of her.
The concussive force hurled Ther’Abella backward, and she planted her blade into the soil to stop her momentum, panting as she wiped the rain from her eyes.
Through the mist, seven armored figures walked forward and cut off the path to the gates.
Ther’Abella’s heart stopped.
Standing in a loose semicircle were the surviving members of the Viridian Guard.
’Why... why are they here...?’
Captain Kaelith stood in the center with her tower shield on her left arm and her two-handed battleaxe in her right with the stance she called the Hollow Oak.
Flanking her were Caelia and Evandra, the twin blade-dancers, their curved scimitars drawn and humming with pressurized wind.
Behind them stood the three elite archers, Althea, Nim, and Cheryl with their composite bows fully drawn, holding explosive arrowheads trained on Ther’Abella’s chest.
To the far right stood Moriel, the spear-master, her long crystalline lance held in a relaxed low guard.
It was the formation they had drilled ten thousand times.
Ther’Abella knew every angle of it, which was exactly why she knew she could not win.

Kaelith’s shield denied the center, the twins covered both flanks with overlapping arcs, Moriel’s lance owned the long middle distance, and the archers sat behind them like three patient stones, covering every gap the others left.
In drills, the youngest member had never once broken it because in those same drills, they had always held back.
