And this damn system wanted to wipe it clean in a single stroke?
Strip her priority skills?
Reduce her to the strength of a newly awakened child?
’Why the hell would I throw four centuries of agony down the drain?!’
Her teeth ground together so hard her jaw ached.
To lose her level was to become weak again...
It was to become that helpless squire who stood on the terrace while her Lady was dragged into the dirt...
She stared at the pulsing crimson prompt, and then, slowly, she swallowed the dry lump in her throat.
’Wait.’
A dark calculating thought flickered behind her piercing blue eyes.
’Where is this Lord summoning me?’

If the summoning was taking place in one of the high-tier outer rings, an Unknown Zone or an active sovereign battlefield crawling with high-rank monsters, she wouldn’t need four hundred years to rebuild her stats.

Her martial mastery wasn’t gone, her combat instincts, her blade katas, and her stellar control were carved into her soul so a Level 1 warrior with the reflexes of an apex killer could slaughter high-tier beasts and skyrocket her level in weeks.
’And the Lord,’ she thought, her jaw hardening into stone. ’If this Lord is weak...
If this Lord tries to hold me back, tries to use me as an ornamental guard or dictate my path.’
She could kill the Lord.
Break the boundary stone, reclaim her rogue status, and use the territory’s carcass as a launching pad to wage war on Yggdrasil.
"Fine," Ther’Abella growled through her teeth.
"Take the levels."
She jabbed her index finger straight into the glowing [ Y ].
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A colossal vortex of golden light swallowed the tavern room whole.

chapters.title: Chapter 652: Reuniting With Eluned [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The transition was instantaneous.
Unlike the first time there was no falling feeling as space simply folded, and Ther’Abella felt cool smooth marble beneath her boots.

The weight in her limbs was gone and the golden glare washed out of her vision, replaced by the sweet clean scent of mountain air however beneath it... so faint she thought she had imagined it was something else.
...There was sap and moss, it was an area thriving in nature, but there was something very familiar about this place, specifically a smell.
"...Lady Eluned’s scent..." she breathed.
She stood between two soaring pillars of rose-veined white marble, inlaid with spiraling threads of beaten gold with a pair of carved sea-drakes curling around a star-silver sun above her head.

Beyond the arch lay a grassy knoll under an afternoon sky and standing three paces in front of her with her hands clasped nervously over the hem of her loose white traveler’s tunic, was a young woman with long crystalline lapis-lazuli hair and wide sapphire eyes, staring up at her with innocent breathless awe.
Beyond the arch, she saw a modest wall of neat white stone, a half-built hall of timber and pale granite, and a surprisingly cheerful vegetable plot.
At the far edge of the meadow, a pack of iron-spined stalkers crouched at the treeline beyond the barrier, frozen in place and staring at the archway as though it had grown teeth.
Princess Aki’s breath hitched in her throat.
’She’s so tall,’ She thought frantically, her mind spinning as she struggled to form words.
’What do I say? "Welcome to my territory, I am your Lord"? No, that sounds too arrogant! "Hello, please protect me"? That sounds pathetic! What do I—’
On the Lord’s tab in front of her face, a line of golden letters blinked.
[Your Hero has been summoned!]

Aki had spent years memorizing every variable of the summoning protocol, and not one of them had said anything about the Hero looking as though she had walked out of a siege... well it depended on how you summoned them though.
WHOOSH!
Aki didn’t even get to finish the thought as Ther’Abella ignored her.

Her senses, stripped down to a Level 1 registered a thunderous vibration from the grass beyond the archway... it was a loud booming belch, and the thick unmistakable reek of fermented dwarf ale and roasted boar meat.
Her head snapped to the right.

Floating three feet above the emerald grass, idly spinning a heavy warhammer by its strap while wiping froth from her lips with the back of a bronze-clad forearm, was a towering seven-foot woman with golden hair and a celestial bronze cuirass.
...Thor.
’Eh... Eh... She’s here...?’
Ther’Abella’s vision turned a violent purple.
The blood in her veins roared, and four hundred years of buried agony and hatred erupted through her skull in a single second.
’THOR!’
She was Thor the Thunderer...
A friend of Lady Eluned’s from before the sky had cracked, the one who had feasted at the sanctum table and sworn, with a tankard raised, that anyone who touched the Tree Spirit would answer for it.

Ther’Abella remembered the night Thor had arrived at the sanctum gates with a barrel of mead on each shoulder, laughing so loudly that three lanterns burst, and Lady Eluned, who never laughed, had pressed a hand to her mouth and giggled like a girl while the whole Guard stood frozen in shock.
Ther’Abella remembered the laugh that had rattled the library shelves.
When the roots split, when Ellvi marched her traitors into the heartwood and Lady Eluned bled out on the stone, where was the friend who had promised?
Where were the great war-horns of the north? They had sat in their golden halls, drinking their casks, while Eluned choked on her own blood.
"YOU TRAITOROUS WHORE!" Ther’Abella shrieked, her voice tearing raw fury.
SWOOSH!
She blurred forward, launching herself off the marble base like an uncoiled viper.
She had no silver weapon since the system reset had stripped her gear, and it didn’t matter.
She reached into her soul, and her piercing blue eyes ignited into deep radiant lilac starlight.
SHING!
A five-foot lance of white concentrated starlight condensed between her palms, its edge humming with freezing plasma.
WHOOSH!
Ther’Abella drove it straight at Thor’s throat in a blinding thrust aimed to pierce the jugular.

Some part of her, perhaps the part that had been a squire of the Viridian Guard before she was anything else, was reading the woman in front of her the way Captain Kaelith had taught her to read a field...
’I can’t hope to match...’

This was a woman on Lady Eluned’s level at least, standing in the open with her guard down with a drink in her left hand and a hammer in her right, and she was still the most dangerous thing within a hundred miles.
Thor’s bright blue eyes narrowed slightly.
The lazy drunken smile vanished from her lips, replaced by the razor-sharp reflexes of a warrior who had fought in more than ten thousand wars.
"Who are you again?"
WHAM!
Thor’s heavy bronze-plated war-boot snapped up in a short brutal front-kick and caught Ther’Abella squarely in the center of her sternum before the starlight lance could cross the final foot.
CRACK!
The concussive force was like hitting an iron rampart.
Even with Thor holding back ninety-nine percent of her output, the mass behind the kick blew Ther’Abella backward through the air and into the grass.
She tumbled across the lawn, tearing up patches of emerald clover, sliding violently across the stone flagstones until her back slammed against the carved border of the Anchor Gate.
"Ugh—!"
She coughed, spitting a mouthful of blood onto the carved runes beneath her hands.
Her freshly reset Level 1 frame screamed in protest, with three ribs fractured by the single strike.

"Oi!" Thor barked, planting her boots on the grass and glaring down at the silver-haired elf with deep annoyance. "What in Odin’s name is wrong with you, girl?! You step out of the portal and immediately aim a spear at my throat?!"
"SILENCE!" Ther’Abella roared, pushing herself up with trembling arms with her lilac starlight flaring around her fists.
Her face was twisted in grief and rage as tears began to cut tracks through the dust on her cheeks.

"You were her friend!" she screamed at Thor, her voice breaking. "You sat at her table! You drank her wine! You promised, and when Lady Eluned screamed for help beneath the roots, not one of you came! You left her to die! She is DEAD because of cowards like you!"
The grin had gone out of Thor’s face and her hand tightened on the strap of her hammer.
"Dead?" she said slowly. "Girl, who in hell told you Eluned is—"
HUMMMMMM!
Starlight coalesced around her hands again, forming two curved, jagged daggers of freezing white plasma.
Her stats were gutter-tier right now and her mana reserves were practically nonexistent but she didn’t care.
WHOOSH!
The daggers went in low and fast as Thor tilted a hip and let the first pass her ribs.
She caught the second wrist in one broad hand without spilling a drop of ale, and held it there as easily as she might have held a fussing cat.
’Fuck you!’
Ther’Abella drove her forehead into Thor’s nose.
BANG!
The goddess blinked, touched her own lip with her thumb, and found a thread of blood as a slow delighted grin spread across her face.
"Ha! That was good," Thor said with real appreciation. "I could kick you again, but it would be rude..."
"Wait! STOP!" Princess Aki yelled, waving her arms in panic as she sprinted between them. "Both of you, calm down! Thor, put the hammer away! Ther’Abella, stand down! That’s an ally—"
She planted herself between them with her arms spread wide looking small and quite visibly terrified then she lifted her right hand, and a ripple of royal-purple mana rolled out across the clover.
A clump of grass at her feet shivered and began to come apart, blade by blade, into fine violet dust.

"I am Aki," she said, in the clearest voice she could manage. "I am the Lord of this territory, and you are my Hero... I do not know what Thor has done to you, but I promise that nothing in this meadow is your enemy..."
’That sounded much better in my head,’ Aki thought, her heart hammering in her ears. ’Please do not let her kill me... I have only just gotten my wall finished...’
Behind her, Thor lowered the hammer a few inches and muttered out of the corner of her mouth.
"Aki, I swear on Odin’s beard I have never seen this woman in my life."
Ther’Abella stared at the slight girl in the white tunic, at the purple light and the trembling chin.
’A child...?’
She was a child with the courage of a woman twice her size... It was a bit different from what she was used to.
VUUUUUUUUUUUM.
Behind Ther’Abella’s back, the massive twenty-foot runic circle carved into the bedrock as the Territorial Anchor Gate leading to Blessed Land, suddenly flared to life.
A gentle pulse of verdant green mana rippled across the grass as a cheerful melodious voice called out from the portal threshold.
"Aki, dear! I baked a fresh tray of honeyed lotus pastries for your new summon! I wanted to make sure she felt welcome, you see—"
The voice paused, and a soft scolding chuckle drifted through the air.

"—because you know how Lord Silas is! On his very first day in the territory, he was so terribly excited about summoning the girls that he actually forgot to feed the girls until the following morning..."
Ther’Abella froze as every muscle in her body locked into solid stone and the starlight daggers in her hands sputtered and died.
That voice... That rhythm... That gentle unhurried tone that sounded like a spring breeze rustling through dry willow leaves...
Slowly, Ther’Abella turned her neck.
Standing on the edge of the runic circle, barely three paces behind her, was a woman dressed in simple flowing robes of translucent jade silk that brushed against the clover.
Her hair, a magnificent cascade of luminous pale emerald, fell past her waist, adorned with half-bloomed white star-lotuses.
In her hands she carefully balanced a steaming ceramic baking dish filled with golden, honey-glazed pastries, and the dish tilted a worrying degree as her fingers loosened in surprise.
Eluned stopped.
She had flour on her cheek, and her sleeves were rolled to the elbow like a woman who had been in a kitchen all afternoon.
"Ah... An Elf...?"
Ther’Abella swallowed.
’...Alive.’
She was not entombed in the lightless dark... not reduced to petrified ash beneath a stolen tree?
Lady Eluned was alive and standing in the sun in front of her, smelling of honey and warm bread, with a pastry dish in her hands and a faintly worried line between her brows.
Ther’Abella’s throat closed.

Four hundred years of loneliness could do things to a mind, and for one terrifying second she was certain it was a hallucination, maybe the last kind trick of a dying brain... after all, she was about to die.
"Umph..."
Her knees gave out as her fingers closed around the polearm she no longer had.
"Lady," she tried to say, and the word came out as a broken wet sound she hadn’t made in so long.
Thor, who had been dabbing at her split lip, froze with the back of her hand halfway to her mouth.
She looked from the elf to Eluned and back again, slowly assembling a picture she did not like at all.
Her large brilliant jade eyes blinked as she tilted her head, looking down at the tall silver-haired elf kneeling in the dirt at her feet.
In the hush, even the iron-spined stalkers at the treeline had gone silent, as though the whole meadow were holding its breath.
A single honeyed pastry slid off the tray and landed in the clover without anyone noticing.
"O-Oh," Eluned murmured, her porcelain brow creasing into a tiny bewildered furrow.
A strand of emerald hair slid over her shoulder, and she brushed it back with the flour-dusted heel of her hand.
’It’s really her...’
This was the same absent gesture Ther’Abella had watched on ten thousand mornings, and every cell in her body recognized it before her mind could argue with it too.
At the edge of the circle, Aki pressed both hands over her mouth.
Eluned stared at the elf’s face as she looked at the silver constellations on her cheekbones.
’Where have I seen her before...?’
She tapped her chin with one finger, clearly struggling with immense effort to dredge a specific memory out of the thousand years of clutter in her head.
’I’m not that old so why is it hard to remember— Oh right! It’s Ther’Abella!’

She was the youngest... The one who always saluted too fast, whose ears turned red when she was embarrassed, who had carried her polearm into the library every morning for three hundred years as though it were a spoon she had been told not to drop.
Eluned had never once told her how much she looked forward to the sound of those hurried boots on the flagstones.
A sudden bright spark of recognition lit up the Goddess’s eyes as Eluned beamed... it was a radiant breathtaking smile that made the grass around her boots instantly sprout tiny yellow buttercups.
"Ther’Abella!" Eluned chimed happily, her voice ringing clear across the meadow. "Goodness, look at you! Welcome to Blessed Land!"

chapters.title: Chapter 653: Reuniting With Eluned [II / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The meadow smelled of Lady Eluned... there were so many beautiful scents wafting out that overwhelmed her senses however...
Ther’Abella didn’t speak.
Her knees were sunk into the damp loam, her shins grinding against the runic border where the boundary array met the grass.
Blood still dripped from the corner of her lip looking thin and pinkish from the ribs Thor’s boot had broken, and it spattered the white clover in slow drops.
Her fingers were clawed into the soil so hard that dirt had packed under her split nails and she stared up.
The green robes didn’t billow in some great terrible gale the way a goddess’s robes were supposed to, instead they just hung there.
It was made of unbleached jade silk, soft at the hem where it touched the moss and dusted with white flour around the left pocket.
’A phantom,’ she thought, cold and brittle as winter glass. ’The desert finally broke something in my head, and this is what it made out of the pieces...’
Her breath hitched.
A dry ugly sound scraped the back of her throat, and then the tears came...
"Mmm... Mm... Mmm... I’m sorry..."
Eluned looked down at her.

The small crease between the Goddess’s brows smoothed out a the distant calm that had always made the elves tread softly around her seemed to melt off her face a layer at a time, like frost under noon sun.
...And she remembered.
She remembered lying pinned in the sap-dark beneath Ellvi’s boots, with the roots drinking her light, while seven small flames went out one after another in the great loom of the Tree.
Kaelith’s heavy heart had burst open, the twins’ breath going to salt and the archers’ fingers freezing on their strings while Moriel was last.
She had counted all seven in the dark however one thread hadn’t snapped.
It had stretched thin and kept humming like a wounded note drifting farther and farther out into the lawless wastes until Eluned lost it in the dark.
’So many memories of the past...’

She remembered the training yard in the grey hour before dawn, the clang of practice scimitars, Captain Kaelith pacing the line with a mug of tea she never finished and one skinny squire in the back rank who always arrived late, always had resin on her sleeves, and always saluted a half-second too fast...
It was too cute.
Eluned had watched them from the library window every morning for three centuries without once letting them see her do it.
’You survived,’ she thought, and small gold flecks in her jade eyes flared and trembled. ’The smallest one... The one who never managed to keep her sleeves clean during the resin harvest...’

She set the baking dish down on the flat stone of the boundary marker then she walked forward with her barefoot sounding silent on the clover as she knelt in front of the kneeling elf with her robes spreading around them both like a pool of living moss.
The smell of star-lotus and warm honey washed over Ther’Abella, so thick and so real that the silver constellations on her cheekbones began to prickle with heat.
Eluned raised her right hand.
The palm was pale and floury at the heel as she laid it on the crown of Ther’Abella’s head and curled her fingers into silver hair that hadn’t seen a brush in a long time.
"Welcome," she said, in that clear sweet voice that had once made the willow boughs lean down just to hear it. "Welcome home, Ther’Abella... Welcome to Blessed Land..."
A shudder ran down the elf’s spine.
Her hands came up out of the mud, shaking so badly that her knuckles clacked together like wooden dice.
She reached for Eluned’s waist and stopped with her arms hovering an inch from the jade silk.
Four hundred years in the desert hadn’t changed her very old habits...
The old law still held her by the throat as no one, not even a knight of the Viridian Guard, touched the hem of the World Tree’s daughter without permission.
Eluned didn’t wait for the protocol.
She leaned in, wrapped both arms around Ther’Abella’s neck, and pulled that broad armored frame down into her lap.
"You may," she whispered in her ear.
SNAP!
Whatever iron rod had held Ther’Abella upright through four hundred years of slaughter, through the stink of butcher’s stalls and the mockery of caravan masters, simply broke...
She buried her face in the curve of Eluned’s neck.
Her arms locked around the Goddess’s back hard enough to crush the ribs of an unawakened man, and she wept with her whole body with great gasping sobs that tore out of her like broken glass.
Blood, road dust and salt soaked into the jade silk but she didn’t care and Eluned didn’t either. They were just happy to see the other was alive.
"My Lady," she choked. "My Lady, my Lady, you’re... you’re..."

"Hush." Eluned stroked her silver hair, her nails scratching lightly at the scalp the exact way she used to calm the young tree-cats when summer gales shook the high nests. "I’m here... It’s over... No one is hunting you through the boughs anymore..."
"I killed them."
It came out muffled and cracked against her shoulder sounding ugly and small.
She could still feel the weight of it in her wrists, Moriel’s breath on her face, Kaelith’s hand closing over hers on the axe haft and trying, with the last of her will, to point it the right way.

"Kaelith... Caelia... Evandra... they had the rot in their eyes... They were fighting it... They asked me to do it... I put the blade through Moriel’s sternum and I held on until she stopped breathing... I couldn’t reach the sanctum... I couldn’t reach you... I was too slow, and I was too weak, and—"
"I know."
A single clear drop slid off Eluned’s lower lash, ran down her porcelain cheek, and landed on the tip of Ther’Abella’s ear.

"I felt each of them go... They didn’t die in hatred, little one, they died looking toward the sun. It wasn’t your hand that did that. It was my sister’s spell, and whatever she twisted in them, they were still fighting her at the end. You carried their weight a very long way but you don’t have to carry it by yourself anymore."
Ther’Abella’s fingers twisted in the jade silk.

"Every morning," she said into Eluned’s collar. "I saluted the horizon. Every morning, four hundred years... I didn’t know who I was saluting anymore. I just... I couldn’t stop. Good morning, Lady... Nobody ever answered..."
Something in Eluned’s face cracked wide open.
"I couldn’t hear you," she whispered. "I would have answered every single one. I would have answered before you finished."
She pressed her cheek against the top of the silver head. "Say it again."
A wet broken laugh followed.
"Good morning, My Lady."
"Good morning, Ther’Abella."
They stayed like that as Eluned rocked her slowly, and the grass around them, without being asked, began to sprout small yellow buttercups in a ring.
"There’s a lotus," Ther’Abella said quietly. "Every year, on my birthday... I never thanked you my Lady."

"You didn’t have to." Eluned’s voice shook. "It was the one day of the year I could be sure that somebody was happy because of something I did... I wanted to leave you one every year of those four hundred so I’m sorry I couldn’t."
From the edge of the knoll came a loud wet sniff.
Thor had turned her back and was staring very hard at the horizon, scrubbing at her face with her bronze forearm.
"Dust," she announced to nobody in particular. "Terrible dust in this meadow."
What would Aki say if she saw her crying...?
Ten paces back, Princess Aki stood frozen on the lawn with her fingers knotted into the white linen of her tunic.
Her sapphire eyes went back and forth between the silver-haired giant sobbing in the grass and the flour-dusted Goddess holding her like a child.
She’d been raised in the royal pavilions of Rhyx City, where grief was a rehearsed affair but this looked like two halves of a continent drifting back together after the flood... if that made sense.
"Thor," she whispered out of the side of her mouth.
Her voice wobbled. "What happened to them?"
Thor stood with her arms crossed and Mjolnir’s strap dangling from her wrist with her thumb absently tracing the split in her lower lip where the elf’s forehead had landed.
The grin was gone as her blue eyes were narrow and cold as fjord ice, fixed on the scars crossing Ther’Abella’s back.
"You don’t really need to know..."
Aki swallowed and she nodded once.
The sobbing in the grass slowly thinned out into wet, ragged hiccups.
Ther’Abella pulled back with her hands lingering on Eluned’s forearms like she was afraid the Goddess would turn to dandelion seeds if she let go.
She dragged the heel of her palm across her eyes and smeared grit and tears into one long streak.
Eluned didn’t answer right away.
She laid her palm flat against the elf’s broken ribs, and a soft green glow bloomed under her fingers.
Thin vines uncurled from her sleeve, small as thread, and slid beneath the torn cuirass to knit the cracked bone one careful stitch at a time.
"Hngh..."
Ther’Abella hissed then went still.
The ache she had carried for four centuries eased by a degree and she realized that she had forgotten what it felt like to be touched by something that meant her no harm.
"There," Eluned murmured, tucking a loose strand of hair behind her pointed ear. "That’s the ribs... The rest will take a few days and a lot of soup..."
"My Lady, I don’t need—"
"Hush."

"How?" she rasped. Her blue eyes searched every line of Eluned’s face. "My Lady, Ellvi dragged you into the roots. I watched the heartwood close over you... How are you kneeling in a field with flour on your cheek?"
Eluned gave her a small crooked smile and brushed a clump of dirt off the elf’s brow.

"It’s not a dream... I was sealed inside the marrow for a very long time... There was only the dark, the taste of bitter sap, and the slow grinding sound of my sister turning the branches into war-forges. I thought it would simply end there until the soil forgot my name."
Her eyes tipped toward the huge runic circle behind them with the Anchor Gate that tied this meadow to the main realm of Blessed Land.
"A while ago, a lord from the outer world brought me through the gray mist... He became my Lord."
A long breath shuddered out of Ther’Abella.
"And I am his Hero... you see, I joined his Territory."
"I see..."
Everything in her chest woke all at once as her shoulders squared.
The lilac starlight under her skin flickered and her voice dropped into the clipped tone of a commander drawing up an assault.

"Then we have a path... My Lady, even if the summoning contract has dimmed your core, we can use this territory as a staging bastion... Ellvi’s hold on the high boughs is shallow as she doesn’t have your feel for the world. If we rally the exiled clans of the outer rings, cut the supply aqueducts on the western terraces, and go up through the root-tunnels where the ward-anchors are thinnest, we can drag her off that throne! We can take her apart limb by limb, take back your mantle, and cleanse Yggdrasil of the rot!"
She leaned forward with her eyes wide and burning with four centuries of fire.
"We’ll make her pay for every drop of gold she drew out of your chest... Ten thousand leagues of ash, My Lady. I swear it..."
Tap!
A small cool hand settled on her left pauldron.
"Stop, Ther’Abella."
Ther’Abella froze.

chapters.title: Chapter 654: A Husband? [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Eluned looked straight into her wide bloodshot eyes.

"Because I can feel it." She lifted a hand and touched the center of Ther’Abella’s chest, right where the cracked ribs were still knitting. "That rage isn’t steel, Ther’Abella... It’s poison... It’s running out of your spiritual circuits like swamp water. You’ve carried it for so long that it has eaten everything except your blade."
She sighed with a sound following like autumn leaves crossing a pond.
"I don’t want that life anymore."
Ther’Abella’s mouth hung open.
"You don’t... want what?"

"I don’t care about Yggdrasil’s throne." Her tone was entirely calm. "I’m still a goddess... I’m smaller now than I was, much weaker than the great being who held up the canopy, but I’m here and my sister, since we were seedlings splitting off from our mother’s marrow, has looked at the light on my leaves and burned... She wanted to be the god, she wanted the councils to bow... She wanted the realm to tremble when her name crossed a border."
Her chin tipped up toward the pale-blue sky of Aki’s meadow.

"Now she has it... She has the timber, the spires, the empty marble halls, and the frightened courtiers who kiss her boots so lt her keep them... Let her choke on everything and the border wars with the frost giants, What she does with stolen power isn’t my burden."
"But the people—"

"The people cheered when she called me a murderer," Eluned said, without a trace of bitterness. "The elders who drank my sap for centuries turned their bows on my own squires inside ten seconds of her decree... Why should I bleed a second time for the ones who cheered at my execution?"
She looked back down, and the smile on her face was so clean that it seemed to burn the chill out of Ther’Abella’s bones.

"I have a family now, Ther’Abella." Tears of plain simple happiness gathered in the corners of her jade eyes. "A real one... Not courtiers measuring my yield, not high priests timing my prayers. I have a lord who minds my garden and a land where no one looks at me with fear. I’m happy here... Truly."
She took the elf’s scarred hands between her own soft ones.

"I want you to be part of it. I know Kaelith is gone... I know Caelia, Evandra, and Moriel are sleeping in the earth, and I carry the weight of being too weak to shield them every single day... But you’re here and you survived the dark so let the spear rest, little one. Come to Blessed Land... Let me look after you for once..."
Ther’Abella sat motionless while the wind dragged loose strands of silver across her mouth then Eluned’s hands slackened.
She lowered her head, and a small fragile sorrow crept into her face.

"Of course," she murmured, her voice shrinking into something shy and self-conscious, "it’s completely understandable if you refuse... I was a foolish goddess. I let myself be tricked by my own blood, I let my Guard be butchered, and I left you to starve in the wastes for four hundred years. If you look at me now and see only failure, if you despise me for being small..."
GRASP!

Ther’Abella lunged and clamped both hands around Eluned’s palms as she bowed until her silver bangs touched the Goddess’s knuckles and pressed her forehead against the cool flour-dusted skin of her wrists.

"Never." Her voice was thick and trembling. "Never say that, My Lady... If I had ten thousand lives I would spend every one of them guarding the dust under your feet. To serve you again... to sit in your garden and see you smile like this... it’s more than someone like me deserves. Please. Let me be part of your family and let me hold the shield for you again."
Eluned’s face lit up so bright it rivaled the noon sun.
"Thank you, Ther’Abella." She laughed and bent to press a kiss to the top of the silver head. "Thank you for coming back to me."
For a few heartbeats the meadow was quiet, and all that could be heard was grass, and the sniffling of a very tall woman kneeling at a goddess’s feet.
"Ahem."
A tiny high throat-clearing came from five paces to the left.
The two of them turned.
Princess Aki stood with her hands clasped in front of her tunic with her lapis hair stirring in the breeze and her cheeks bright with embarrassed pink.
She shifted from one boot to the other and held up one finger by about half an inch.
"Um. I really hate to interrupt, but technically..." She pointed her thumb at her own chest. "Ther’Abella is my Hero."
Ther’Abella’s silver brows drew together.
She rose slowly, all her height unfolding, and even with her armor dented and her clothes caked in mud she loomed over the petite princess like an old monument.
She looked down at the girl. "You’re the Lord of this territory?"
Aki’s heart hammered like a trapped bird.

’She’s terrifying,’ she thought, knees knocking under her tunic. ’She looks like she could snap an oak over her knee! What was the recruitment speech they taught at the Academy? "By the divine right of the Sovereign Realm, your deeds shall be recorded in the annals of—" No! That sounds awful!’

"Y-Yes!" She puffed out her chest and tried to make her chin look regal. "I am Princess Aki, Lord of this domain! I intend to build a territory founded on fair trade, true mutual defense, and thoughtful farming! If you pledge your steel to my banner, I swear upon Blessed Land that you will never lack for bread, shelter, or honor!"
She shut her eyes and waited for the giant to laugh in her face.
CLANG!
Ther’Abella dropped to one knee with her right fist striking the turf in front of Aki’s boots and her head bowed so low that silver hair pooled around the princess’s toes.
"I hear and obey, My Lord."
Aki’s eyes flew open.

"You pulled my soul out of the outer dark," Ther’Abella said, and her voice had no mockery left in it. "You brought me to this meadow and you put Lady Eluned in front of me again. For that alone, my life belongs to your hall... My level is reset and my greater arrays are sealed by the contract, but the memory in my hands is whole so until my core crumbles, my spear is yours."
Aki’s face turned the exact shade of an overripe strawberry.
"That is far too much! Please stand up! A nod is fine, truly!"
From the edge of the knoll came a very loud very rude snort as Ther’Abella’s ears twitched.
She turned her head, and her gaze landed on the floating thunder-goddess.
The warmth drained out of her face and what replaced it was a wall of arctic frost.
Thor met it with a wide mocking smirk and tapped Mjolnir against the bronze plate of her thigh.
Thunk-thunk!
Neither said a word.
The air between them tightened until a patch of clover between their boots withered to brown dust.
Anyone in the valley could tell those two had enough mutual contempt to run a thirty-year border dispute.
"Now, now," Eluned said smoothly, gliding between the two giants like a mother stepping between bickering hounds.
She picked the baking dish up off the boundary stone.
A tiny gust of spring wind curled out of her fingers, lifted the single pastry that had fallen in the dirt, stripped every speck of loam off it, and set it neatly back among the others.
"Ther’Abella, you must be obedient to Princess Aki... She’s young, but her heart is kind and her foundation is sound so take a honey cake. You haven’t eaten proper food in centuries, have you?"
"No, My Lady." Ther’Abella took one with trembling fingers and bit into it.
Wildflower honey and roasted lotus seed filled her mouth, and for a moment her throat closed up all over again.
She chewed slowly and looked around at the little camp: the white-stone wall, the timber hall, the vegetable plot, the huge runic circle humming at the eastern gate.
"Lady Eluned, there’s something I don’t understand... The girl said I was summoned to Blessed Land, but this hall is small. Is Princess Aki the lord who went into the root-tomb to rescue you?"
Aki jumped in, eager to show she was competent.
"This is a Vassal Territory! We’re registered as a branch of Blessed Land’s central core. I handle day-to-day defense and local building myself, but our hero registers are bound to the mother-hall."
"And I belong to the mother-hall," Eluned added cheerfully, smoothing her flour-dusted apron. "I was Lord Silas’s very first Hero."
Ther’Abella’s jaw tightened.
’Lord Silas.’
The name had been hovering over the whole conversation.
Was he some ancient northern warlord or a grizzled tactician who hoarded a being like Eluned herself... as a chess piece to climb the rankings of the world.

"Lord Silas," she said, folding her arms across her torn cuirass. "When he returns from his campaigns, I’ll have to judge his character with my own eyes... A man who commands Lady Eluned must have unshakeable discipline."
Eluned blinked, then gave a soft musical giggle with a decidedly un-martial, dreamy warmth.
"Oh, Silas doesn’t command me... He’s very gentle. He worries whether I’ve had enough food, and he brings me gifts from the mortal markets and he’s terribly cute when he tries to look serious."
"Cute?" Ther’Abella said. "A Lord?"
"Of course." Eluned pressed her hands over her heart with unashamed pride. "It’s only natural I find him charming... He’s my husband, after all."
Silence dropped over the meadow like a block of lead as Ther’Abella’s mouth opened.
SPURT!
A fine spray of bright red blood shot out between her teeth and splattered the green clover.
The shock was so violent that her damaged spiritual circuits misfired and back-blasted half a cup of blood through her mouth.
"H-H-HUSBAND?!" She wheezed with her eyes bulging, and dragged a trembling forearm across her chin.
She took two steps and loomed over the smaller Goddess with her voice dropping into a horrified rasp.
"My Lady, I beg your pardon. The desert winds must have damaged my hearing. Did you just say... husband?"
Eluned tilted her head looking utterly lost.
"Yes? I’m married. Lord Silas is my husband... Is something wrong?"
Every muscle in Ther’Abella’s face went completely blank.
The silver constellations on her cheeks stopped glowing and faded to dead slate-gray lines as her eyes became two hollow wells of frost.
’Husband.’
The word rang through her skull like a funeral bell.

’A mortal man... put his hands on Lady Eluned... wrapped his common dirt-caked arms around the daughter of the World Tree and left her in an open field with flour on her apron while he swaggers around the outer realms.’
"Where is he?"
There was no anger in her voice... There was nothing, it sounded like glacial ice grinding under a black sea.
"I wish to meet this Lord Silas... Immediately..."
Behind them, Thor had folded in half.
She was wheezing, one hand braced on her knee and the other pounding the air and tears running into her braids.
"Gwahaha! The face! Did you see her face?! Oh, I wish I had a mirror! I wish I had a mirror and a camera and a barrel of mead!"
"Thor," Aki hissed, "not helping!"
Eluned looked from the choking elf to the cackling goddess and back with a small puzzled frown.
"Did I say something wrong?"
Aki threw up both hands with sweat running down the back of her neck as the murderous radiation rolled off the elf.
"He isn’t here! He’s on Earth, in the mortal layer! He went back to his home city to see to family business and resupply our lines... He won’t be back until tomorrow morning at the earliest!"
"Earth," Ther’Abella repeated, flat as a blade. "The mortal layer."

’Good,’ she thought, and her hands curled slowly into white-knuckled fists behind her back. ’That gives me more hours to sharpen my lance... When this "cute" husband steps through that gate, I’ll evaluate the structural integrity of his collarbones.’
She forced her face to soften and gave Eluned a stiff, mechanical bow.
"I understand, My Lady. I’ll await his return with great anticipation."
Eluned beamed, completely oblivious to the assassination plot forming in her former squire’s head.
"Wonderful! You two will get along splendidly... Silas loves strong women."
Aki let out a long shuddering sigh of relief, though her gut told her the meadow was going to turn into an active war zone the second Silas set foot on the grass.

sentences.text: Eluned looked straight into her wide bloodshot eyes.
"Because I can feel it." She lifted a hand and touched the center of Ther’Abella’s chest, right where the cracked ribs were still knitting.
"That rage isn’t steel, Ther’Abella...
It’s poison...
It’s running out of your spiritual circuits like swamp water.
You’ve carried it for so long that it has eaten everything except your blade."
She sighed with a sound following like autumn leaves crossing a pond.
"I don’t want that life anymore."
Ther’Abella’s mouth hung open.
"You don’t... want what?"
"I don’t care about Yggdrasil’s throne." Her tone was entirely calm.
"I’m still a goddess...

I’m smaller now than I was, much weaker than the great being who held up the canopy, but I’m here and my sister, since we were seedlings splitting off from our mother’s marrow, has looked at the light on my leaves and burned...
She wanted to be the god, she wanted the councils to bow...
She wanted the realm to tremble when her name crossed a border."
Her chin tipped up toward the pale-blue sky of Aki’s meadow.
"Now she has it...
She has the timber, the spires, the empty marble halls, and the frightened courtiers who kiss her boots so lt her keep them...
Let her choke on everything and the border wars with the frost giants, What she does with stolen power isn’t my burden."
"But the people—"
"The people cheered when she called me a murderer," Eluned said, without a trace of bitterness.
"The elders who drank my sap for centuries turned their bows on my own squires inside ten seconds of her decree...
Why should I bleed a second time for the ones who cheered at my execution?"
She looked back down, and the smile on her face was so clean that it seemed to burn the chill out of Ther’Abella’s bones.
"I have a family now, Ther’Abella." Tears of plain simple happiness gathered in the corners of her jade eyes.
"A real one...
Not courtiers measuring my yield, not high priests timing my prayers.
I have a lord who minds my garden and a land where no one looks at me with fear.
I’m happy here...
Truly."
She took the elf’s scarred hands between her own soft ones.
"I want you to be part of it.
I know Kaelith is gone...
I know Caelia, Evandra, and Moriel are sleeping in the earth, and I carry the weight of being too weak to shield them every single day...
But you’re here and you survived the dark so let the spear rest, little one.
Come to Blessed Land...
Let me look after you for once..."
Ther’Abella sat motionless while the wind dragged loose strands of silver across her mouth then Eluned’s hands slackened.
She lowered her head, and a small fragile sorrow crept into her face.
"Of course," she murmured, her voice shrinking into something shy and self-conscious, "it’s completely understandable if you refuse...
I was a foolish goddess.
I let myself be tricked by my own blood, I let my Guard be butchered, and I left you to starve in the wastes for four hundred years.
If you look at me now and see only failure, if you despise me for being small..."
GRASP!

Ther’Abella lunged and clamped both hands around Eluned’s palms as she bowed until her silver bangs touched the Goddess’s knuckles and pressed her forehead against the cool flour-dusted skin of her wrists.
"Never." Her voice was thick and trembling.
"Never say that, My Lady...
If I had ten thousand lives I would spend every one of them guarding the dust under your feet.
To serve you again... to sit in your garden and see you smile like this... it’s more than someone like me deserves.
Please.
Let me be part of your family and let me hold the shield for you again."
Eluned’s face lit up so bright it rivaled the noon sun.
"Thank you, Ther’Abella." She laughed and bent to press a kiss to the top of the silver head.
"Thank you for coming back to me."
For a few heartbeats the meadow was quiet, and all that could be heard was grass, and the sniffling of a very tall woman kneeling at a goddess’s feet.
"Ahem."
A tiny high throat-clearing came from five paces to the left.
The two of them turned.
Princess Aki stood with her hands clasped in front of her tunic with her lapis hair stirring in the breeze and her cheeks bright with embarrassed pink.
She shifted from one boot to the other and held up one finger by about half an inch.
"Um.
I really hate to interrupt, but technically..." She pointed her thumb at her own chest.
"Ther’Abella is my Hero."
Ther’Abella’s silver brows drew together.
She rose slowly, all her height unfolding, and even with her armor dented and her clothes caked in mud she loomed over the petite princess like an old monument.
She looked down at the girl.
"You’re the Lord of this territory?"
Aki’s heart hammered like a trapped bird.
’She’s terrifying,’ she thought, knees knocking under her tunic. ’She looks like she could snap an oak over her knee!
What was the recruitment speech they taught at the Academy?
"By the divine right of the Sovereign Realm, your deeds shall be recorded in the annals of—" No!
That sounds awful!’
"Y-Yes!" She puffed out her chest and tried to make her chin look regal.
"I am Princess Aki, Lord of this domain!
I intend to build a territory founded on fair trade, true mutual defense, and thoughtful farming!
If you pledge your steel to my banner, I swear upon Blessed Land that you will never lack for bread, shelter, or honor!"
She shut her eyes and waited for the giant to laugh in her face.
CLANG!
Ther’Abella dropped to one knee with her right fist striking the turf in front of Aki’s boots and her head bowed so low that silver hair pooled around the princess’s toes.
"I hear and obey, My Lord."
Aki’s eyes flew open.
"You pulled my soul out of the outer dark," Ther’Abella said, and her voice had no mockery left in it.
"You brought me to this meadow and you put Lady Eluned in front of me again.
For that alone, my life belongs to your hall...
My level is reset and my greater arrays are sealed by the contract, but the memory in my hands is whole so until my core crumbles, my spear is yours."
Aki’s face turned the exact shade of an overripe strawberry.
"That is far too much!
Please stand up!
A nod is fine, truly!"
From the edge of the knoll came a very loud very rude snort as Ther’Abella’s ears twitched.
She turned her head, and her gaze landed on the floating thunder-goddess.
The warmth drained out of her face and what replaced it was a wall of arctic frost.
Thor met it with a wide mocking smirk and tapped Mjolnir against the bronze plate of her thigh.
Thunk-thunk!
Neither said a word.
The air between them tightened until a patch of clover between their boots withered to brown dust.
Anyone in the valley could tell those two had enough mutual contempt to run a thirty-year border dispute.
"Now, now," Eluned said smoothly, gliding between the two giants like a mother stepping between bickering hounds.
She picked the baking dish up off the boundary stone.
A tiny gust of spring wind curled out of her fingers, lifted the single pastry that had fallen in the dirt, stripped every speck of loam off it, and set it neatly back among the others.
"Ther’Abella, you must be obedient to Princess Aki...
She’s young, but her heart is kind and her foundation is sound so take a honey cake.
You haven’t eaten proper food in centuries, have you?"
"No, My Lady." Ther’Abella took one with trembling fingers and bit into it.
Wildflower honey and roasted lotus seed filled her mouth, and for a moment her throat closed up all over again.
She chewed slowly and looked around at the little camp: the white-stone wall, the timber hall, the vegetable plot, the huge runic circle humming at the eastern gate.
"Lady Eluned, there’s something I don’t understand...
The girl said I was summoned to Blessed Land, but this hall is small.
Is Princess Aki the lord who went into the root-tomb to rescue you?"
Aki jumped in, eager to show she was competent.
"This is a Vassal Territory!
We’re registered as a branch of Blessed Land’s central core.
I handle day-to-day defense and local building myself, but our hero registers are bound to the mother-hall."
"And I belong to the mother-hall," Eluned added cheerfully, smoothing her flour-dusted apron.
"I was Lord Silas’s very first Hero."
Ther’Abella’s jaw tightened.
’Lord Silas.’
The name had been hovering over the whole conversation.
Was he some ancient northern warlord or a grizzled tactician who hoarded a being like Eluned herself... as a chess piece to climb the rankings of the world.
"Lord Silas," she said, folding her arms across her torn cuirass.
"When he returns from his campaigns, I’ll have to judge his character with my own eyes...
A man who commands Lady Eluned must have unshakeable discipline."
Eluned blinked, then gave a soft musical giggle with a decidedly un-martial, dreamy warmth.
"Oh, Silas doesn’t command me...
He’s very gentle.
He worries whether I’ve had enough food, and he brings me gifts from the mortal markets and he’s terribly cute when he tries to look serious."
"Cute?" Ther’Abella said.
"A Lord?"
"Of course." Eluned pressed her hands over her heart with unashamed pride.
"It’s only natural I find him charming...
He’s my husband, after all."
Silence dropped over the meadow like a block of lead as Ther’Abella’s mouth opened.
SPURT!
A fine spray of bright red blood shot out between her teeth and splattered the green clover.
The shock was so violent that her damaged spiritual circuits misfired and back-blasted half a cup of blood through her mouth.
"H-H-HUSBAND?!" She wheezed with her eyes bulging, and dragged a trembling forearm across her chin.
She took two steps and loomed over the smaller Goddess with her voice dropping into a horrified rasp.
"My Lady, I beg your pardon.
The desert winds must have damaged my hearing.
Did you just say... husband?"
Eluned tilted her head looking utterly lost.
"Yes?
I’m married.
Lord Silas is my husband...
Is something wrong?"
Every muscle in Ther’Abella’s face went completely blank.
The silver constellations on her cheeks stopped glowing and faded to dead slate-gray lines as her eyes became two hollow wells of frost.
’Husband.’
The word rang through her skull like a funeral bell.

’A mortal man... put his hands on Lady Eluned... wrapped his common dirt-caked arms around the daughter of the World Tree and left her in an open field with flour on her apron while he swaggers around the outer realms.’
"Where is he?"
There was no anger in her voice...
There was nothing, it sounded like glacial ice grinding under a black sea.
"I wish to meet this Lord Silas...
Immediately..."
Behind them, Thor had folded in half.
She was wheezing, one hand braced on her knee and the other pounding the air and tears running into her braids.
"Gwahaha!
The face!
Did you see her face?!
Oh, I wish I had a mirror!
I wish I had a mirror and a camera and a barrel of mead!"
"Thor," Aki hissed, "not helping!"
Eluned looked from the choking elf to the cackling goddess and back with a small puzzled frown.
"Did I say something wrong?"
Aki threw up both hands with sweat running down the back of her neck as the murderous radiation rolled off the elf.
"He isn’t here!
He’s on Earth, in the mortal layer!
He went back to his home city to see to family business and resupply our lines...
He won’t be back until tomorrow morning at the earliest!"
"Earth," Ther’Abella repeated, flat as a blade.
"The mortal layer."
’Good,’ she thought, and her hands curled slowly into white-knuckled fists behind her back. ’That gives me more hours to sharpen my lance...
When this "cute" husband steps through that gate, I’ll evaluate the structural integrity of his collarbones.’
She forced her face to soften and gave Eluned a stiff, mechanical bow.
"I understand, My Lady.
I’ll await his return with great anticipation."
Eluned beamed, completely oblivious to the assassination plot forming in her former squire’s head.
"Wonderful!
You two will get along splendidly...
Silas loves strong women."
Aki let out a long shuddering sigh of relief, though her gut told her the meadow was going to turn into an active war zone the second Silas set foot on the grass.

chapters.title: Chapter 655: Face-Kissing Demon [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: She turned toward the center of the camp and waved for them to follow.
"Come on... Under standard Lord protocols, the first summoned Hero sets the tone of the territory but a lord can’t rely on one champion... The walls need standing infantry too."
They walked back to the rose-veined marble archway, with its gold-threaded pillars and the pair of carved sea-drakes curling around a star-silver sun.
The slender pedestal stood at the base of the right pillar with its circular holder gleaming.
Ther’Abella looked past it at the treeline, where iron-spined stalkers crouched beyond the barrier, which had knitted itself whole again.
"My Lord, do you want me to deploy my remaining starlight? Even at Level 1, I can project a terror-ward and suppress those beasts while you conduct the ritual."
Aki shook her head at once.
"No, Ther’Abella. Your core needs to recharge, and your ribs are broken from Thor’s kick so save your mana... Just stand there and look like a commander so the troops recognize you."
She opened her Lord’s tab.

"We’ll summon standard troops for now and maybe a second Hero when Silas comes back to check out the territory compltely... I want to do this slowly. In the Lord archives online, I read hundreds of accounts of novice lords who summoned five Heroes on their first afternoon and then suffered terrible backlash, because they didn’t understand the personalities or skill trees of their own vanguard."
She drew a stack of tickets from the satchel at her waist.
"I want to know every woman under my command. Names, weapons, home provinces... It’ll make me a slower lord than the others but I intend to build a kingdom that lasts."
She set the stack on the star-silver holder.
SHING!
All twenty tickets flared a soft uniform white as a tab appeared in front of her eyes.
[Would you like to use 20x Troop Summoning Cards?]
[Y / N]
Aki took a breath and pressed her thumb on the golden [Y].
HUMMMMMMMMM!
There was no sky-shattering pillar this time.

A warm ring of emerald light spread out from the base of the pedestal, turning slowly like a loom, and motes of white ether gathered into twenty pale pillars arranged in two neat ranks of ten across the marble base of the archway.
When the glare faded, twenty women stood there.
They were young and sturdy, with the build of frontier settlers, hunters, and village militia.
None wore heavy plate as they were dressed in plain homespun tunics, good leather boots, and canvas breeches, and they looked around the meadow with wide lost eyes.
The twenty stood in two neat ranks, blinking in the sun, and Aki felt her heart do something complicated.
’I need to get more confidence...’
She had read about this moment in a hundred chronicles, always written from a conqueror’s point of view.
None of them had mentioned how small and how human the people looked when they arrived.
Before she gave her speech, she went down the line.
"Name?" she asked the first, a tall, freckled woman with a hunter’s braid.
"B-Brynja, my Lord. Of the Eastern Marches."
"Brynja. Do you like the bow, or the spear?"
"The... spear, my Lord. I’m not very good with the bow."
"Then you’ll have a spear," Aki said, as though it were the simplest thing in the world, and moved to the next.
A stocky serious girl named Tove said she was a baker’s daughter.
A quiet bespectacled one named Ilse said she’d trained as a bonesetter.
Aki repeated each name once under her breath, like a charm, so she’d keep it.
By the end of the line she’d gotten twenty names and twenty provinces, and she hadn’t looked at her tab once.
Somewhere behind her, Thor muttered to Eluned. "She’s doing it a bit slow, you know... She does have the tabs I think."
"Of course she is," Eluned murmured. "She’s kind."
Aki heard none of it.
She walked back to the edge of the base and lifted her chin with all the natural authority of a Royal Family daughter.
"Citizens of the Sovereign Realm!"
Twenty heads snapped toward her. The murmuring stopped.

"I am Princess Aki," she said, meeting each of their faces with warm, honest eyes. "Lord of this domain, which is recorded in the Sovereign Realm as Vineworld... You’ve been pulled out of the ether into an untamed frontier, and I won’t lie to you... The woods beyond our walls are dangerous so taming this soil will take sweat and vigilance but under my banner you will never go hungry. You’ll have sturdy roofs, fair wages, and good steel to guard your hearths!"
She pointed at the huge runic circle on the eastern edge of the camp.
"And Vineworld doesn’t stand alone... We’re the recognized vassal territory of Blessed Land, a power whose shield covers our borders!"
She spread her arms toward the two women flanking her.

"Beside me is my First Hero, Commander Ther’Abella, formerly of an Elite Guard, who will teach you the spear and beside her is Lady Eluned, the Spirit of the World Tree, whose grace feeds our fields!"
The twenty looked at the tall silver-haired elf with stars on her cheeks and they looked at the gentle, green-haired goddess holding a tray of pastries.
Then they looked at the small, lapis-haired girl standing straight in front of them.
The hesitation left their faces.
THUD!
All twenty dropped to their right knees in perfect unison and put their fists over their hearts.
"We hear and obey, Lord Aki!" They rang out together across the meadow. "Long live Vineworld! Long live Blessed Land!"
A hot dizzying rush of pride rose in Aki’s chest.
...She’d done it.
’I’m... I’m good...’
She wasn’t the frail unawakened spare daughter shut away in the royal library anymore, instead she was a lord with a domain, an army, and a champion at her side.
"Rise, sisters!" Eluned chimed, stepping down from the base with the tray held high. "Come, eat! Warm pastries for everyone before we hand out the barracks!"
The new troops broke ranks with relieved cheerful smiles and clustered around her like schoolgirls, laughing and thanking her as she passed out honeyed lotus cakes.
Brynja took two and looked at them as though they were made of gold.
Thor floated over with a cask in each hand, grinned at the nearest row, and bellowed.
"Who wants to arm-wrestle?" Every one of them took a step back.
One, a broad-shouldered smith named Gudrun, took a step forward, and Thor’s grin became downright pleased.
Aki stayed at the edge, watching with a soft smile then her gaze drifted south and the smile slipped.
’Silas.’ Her fingers tapped her leather belt. ’He’s been back in Valoria City for a long time... What could be keeping him that busy?’
A sharp dangerous thought slid in as the memory of a certain red-haired Bloom heiress with a very sharp tongue came to mind.

’He had better not be spending his evening with that Sera woman,’ she grumbled inside with her lower lip pushing out into a tiny royal pout. ’If I find out he was drinking foreign wine in some fancy lounge while I was out here hauling stone for the palisades, I’m locking the Anchor Gate... and I won’t talk to him for a week! Hmph!’
The pastries went around twice.

By the time the sun had slid toward the western treeline, the new troops were laughing in clusters on the grass, Thor was winning loudly in an arm-wrestling match to a smith named Gudrun, and Ther’Abella had sat down on the marble base of the archway to rest her ribs.
She didn’t mean to fall asleep.

She sat bolt upright with a half-eaten honey cake in her lap and her chin on her chest with her free hand twitching and in under a minute her breathing went slow and deep for the first time in four hundred years.
Aki noticed first.

She slipped off her own traveler’s cloak, crossed the grass on tiptoe, and laid it over those broad scarred shoulders then she put a finger to her lips at Eluned, who was already watching with her whole heart in her eyes.
"She’s safe," Aki whispered. "Isn’t she?"
"She is," Eluned whispered back, and she sat down at the elf’s side and stayed.
The master bedroom of the Silverleaf apartment was dark and filled with the monotonous sound of the climate control unit blasting air from the ceiling vents.
Silas lay flat on his back, staring up at the white ceiling plaster with an expression of soul-weary resignation.
SMACK!
Silas winced with his eye twitching slightly.
Draped across his entire torso like an overgrown silk-clad octopus was Harper...
Her long slender legs were tangled so thoroughly between his thighs that any attempt to extract his left knee would require him to use space to teleport.
’But I already tried that...’
She would just sense his presence and lock him harder, this was the third time she had done so in fact.

Harper’s left arm was hooked securely around his neck, pinning his chin downward, while her entire upper body pressed flush against his ribs, radiating an absurd amount of heat that completely mocked the freezing air from the air conditioner.

’She said she wanted to sleep in my room because the alleyway lights disturbed her thoughts,’ Silas thought with his breathing coming in shallow careful drafts so as not to disturb the knot of limbs. ’So I allowed it...’

According to what he had heard Penelope say while doing her homework, Harper had spent the last two days complaining to anyone who would listen swearing she hadn’t slept a solid four hours since the whole incident.
Yet, the exact second her head had hit Silas’s chest, she had gone limp as a sack of wet flour and out cold before he could even finish pulling the down quilt over her shoulders.
Silas had felt a genuine quiet warmth in his chest at first.
It was nice to know that House Whitmore’s Head trusted him enough to drop her defenses completely, leaving her throat bare and her core dormant in his bed.
’...Which would be deeply touching,’ Silas reflected bitterly, ’if she didn’t have this one horrifying nocturnal habit.’
SLURP-SMACK!
Harper’s violet head shifted against his collarbone.
In the dead peaceful throes of deep sleep, her lips parted.
She leaned her chin up, pressed her mouth squarely against the side of Silas’s nose, and proceeded to vigorously lick the bridge of his snout with her tongue, letting out a soft contented mumble.
"Mmm... sweet pastry... needs more sugar..."
SMACK!
She planted a loud wet kiss directly onto his left nostril, followed by an aggressive suction-cup nuzzle against his cheekbone that sounded like an octopus detaching from a ship’s hull.
It was almost like she was a Face-Kissing Demon...
Silas lay completely paralyzed with his hands hovering awkwardly in the air beside her ribs.

’Why does she keep sucking on my face in her sleep?!’ Silas screamed silently at the dark ceiling molding with his left eyelid spasming with distress. ’Is she dreaming about fruit?! Am I an oversized peach in her subconscious?!’
He tried to gently slide his right shoulder back to gain half an inch of clearance.
"Ugh—!"

Harper’s arms and legs instantly contracted with the terrifying force securing a submission hold as her ankles locked behind his calves and her fingers dug deep into the silk of his pajama shirt, pulling his face right back down into the line of fire.
SLURP!
Another enthusiastic lick across his eyebrow.
Silas let out a long defeated breath through his teeth, letting his head sink back into the pillow.

He was a Gold Core Lord who could do many things but right now, he couldn’t even escape a woman in matching pajamas because he was terrified that using his physical strength might accidentally dislocate her shoulder while she was sleeping.
’I don’t want to wake her up... She looks so cute while she’s sleeping too.’
Resigned entirely to his sticky fate, Silas let his arms fall... gently resting his hands against the small of her back.
"Mmmph~"
Harper let out a dreamy purring sigh, burrowing her forehead deep beneath his chin with her breathing settling back into a slow hush against his throat.
Silas stared up into the dark, listening to the quiet hum of the apartment, and closed his eyes.
’I need to sleep.’
