"We hear and obey, Lord Aki!" They rang out together across the meadow.
"Long live Vineworld!
Long live Blessed Land!"
A hot dizzying rush of pride rose in Aki’s chest.
...She’d done it.
I’m good...’
She wasn’t the frail unawakened spare daughter shut away in the royal library anymore, instead she was a lord with a domain, an army, and a champion at her side.
"Rise, sisters!" Eluned chimed, stepping down from the base with the tray held high.
"Come, eat!
Warm pastries for everyone before we hand out the barracks!"
The new troops broke ranks with relieved cheerful smiles and clustered around her like schoolgirls, laughing and thanking her as she passed out honeyed lotus cakes.
Brynja took two and looked at them as though they were made of gold.
Thor floated over with a cask in each hand, grinned at the nearest row, and bellowed.
"Who wants to arm-wrestle?" Every one of them took a step back.
One, a broad-shouldered smith named Gudrun, took a step forward, and Thor’s grin became downright pleased.
Aki stayed at the edge, watching with a soft smile then her gaze drifted south and the smile slipped.
’Silas.’ Her fingers tapped her leather belt. ’He’s been back in Valoria City for a long time...
What could be keeping him that busy?’
A sharp dangerous thought slid in as the memory of a certain red-haired Bloom heiress with a very sharp tongue came to mind.

’He had better not be spending his evening with that Sera woman,’ she grumbled inside with her lower lip pushing out into a tiny royal pout. ’If I find out he was drinking foreign wine in some fancy lounge while I was out here hauling stone for the palisades, I’m locking the Anchor Gate... and I won’t talk to him for a week!
Hmph!’
The pastries went around twice.

By the time the sun had slid toward the western treeline, the new troops were laughing in clusters on the grass, Thor was winning loudly in an arm-wrestling match to a smith named Gudrun, and Ther’Abella had sat down on the marble base of the archway to rest her ribs.
She didn’t mean to fall asleep.

She sat bolt upright with a half-eaten honey cake in her lap and her chin on her chest with her free hand twitching and in under a minute her breathing went slow and deep for the first time in four hundred years.
Aki noticed first.

She slipped off her own traveler’s cloak, crossed the grass on tiptoe, and laid it over those broad scarred shoulders then she put a finger to her lips at Eluned, who was already watching with her whole heart in her eyes.
"She’s safe," Aki whispered.
"Isn’t she?"
"She is," Eluned whispered back, and she sat down at the elf’s side and stayed.
The master bedroom of the Silverleaf apartment was dark and filled with the monotonous sound of the climate control unit blasting air from the ceiling vents.
Silas lay flat on his back, staring up at the white ceiling plaster with an expression of soul-weary resignation.
SMACK!
Silas winced with his eye twitching slightly.
Draped across his entire torso like an overgrown silk-clad octopus was Harper...
Her long slender legs were tangled so thoroughly between his thighs that any attempt to extract his left knee would require him to use space to teleport.
’But I already tried that...’
She would just sense his presence and lock him harder, this was the third time she had done so in fact.

Harper’s left arm was hooked securely around his neck, pinning his chin downward, while her entire upper body pressed flush against his ribs, radiating an absurd amount of heat that completely mocked the freezing air from the air conditioner.

’She said she wanted to sleep in my room because the alleyway lights disturbed her thoughts,’ Silas thought with his breathing coming in shallow careful drafts so as not to disturb the knot of limbs. ’So I allowed it...’

According to what he had heard Penelope say while doing her homework, Harper had spent the last two days complaining to anyone who would listen swearing she hadn’t slept a solid four hours since the whole incident.
Yet, the exact second her head had hit Silas’s chest, she had gone limp as a sack of wet flour and out cold before he could even finish pulling the down quilt over her shoulders.
Silas had felt a genuine quiet warmth in his chest at first.
It was nice to know that House Whitmore’s Head trusted him enough to drop her defenses completely, leaving her throat bare and her core dormant in his bed.
’...Which would be deeply touching,’ Silas reflected bitterly, ’if she didn’t have this one horrifying nocturnal habit.’
SLURP-SMACK!
Harper’s violet head shifted against his collarbone.
In the dead peaceful throes of deep sleep, her lips parted.
She leaned her chin up, pressed her mouth squarely against the side of Silas’s nose, and proceeded to vigorously lick the bridge of his snout with her tongue, letting out a soft contented mumble.
"Mmm... sweet pastry... needs more sugar..."
SMACK!
She planted a loud wet kiss directly onto his left nostril, followed by an aggressive suction-cup nuzzle against his cheekbone that sounded like an octopus detaching from a ship’s hull.
It was almost like she was a Face-Kissing Demon...
Silas lay completely paralyzed with his hands hovering awkwardly in the air beside her ribs.
’Why does she keep sucking on my face in her sleep?!’ Silas screamed silently at the dark ceiling molding with his left eyelid spasming with distress. ’Is she dreaming about fruit?!
Am I an oversized peach in her subconscious?!’
He tried to gently slide his right shoulder back to gain half an inch of clearance.
"Ugh—!"

Harper’s arms and legs instantly contracted with the terrifying force securing a submission hold as her ankles locked behind his calves and her fingers dug deep into the silk of his pajama shirt, pulling his face right back down into the line of fire.
SLURP!
Another enthusiastic lick across his eyebrow.
Silas let out a long defeated breath through his teeth, letting his head sink back into the pillow.

He was a Gold Core Lord who could do many things but right now, he couldn’t even escape a woman in matching pajamas because he was terrified that using his physical strength might accidentally dislocate her shoulder while she was sleeping.
’I don’t want to wake her up...
She looks so cute while she’s sleeping too.’
Resigned entirely to his sticky fate, Silas let his arms fall... gently resting his hands against the small of her back.
"Mmmph~"
Harper let out a dreamy purring sigh, burrowing her forehead deep beneath his chin with her breathing settling back into a slow hush against his throat.
Silas stared up into the dark, listening to the quiet hum of the apartment, and closed his eyes.
’I need to sleep.’

chapters.title: Chapter 656: Martha’s Morning [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The grandfather clock in the ground-floor corridor gave a dull click as its brass gears engaged.
...It was four in the morning.
Outside, Valoria City was drowned in deep ink-wash blue, with the streetlamps along the lane glowing like dim amber pearls through the fog.
The Silverleaf residence was wrapped in silence as well as the rest of the Houses in the area.
In the ground-floor servants’ quarters, Martha opened her eyes.
’Good morning.’
For thirty-five years her body had answered the tick of clocks so it was easy for her to sit up with her bare feet already finding the woven rug.
She was still wearing the midnight-blue silk set Harper had handed out the evening before.
It was absurdly luxurious, slipping over her skin like cool river water, with tiny temperature wards sewn into the hems to keep the hardwood chill from biting her ankles.
"Forty-five thousand credits for sleepwear," she muttered, smoothing the collar by the dim glow of her nightstand lamp. "Young nobility throws gold around like it grows on elderberry bushes..."
She tied her hair back with a plain linen ribbon, slipped into soft velvet slippers and opened her door.
The hallway smelled of last night’s oxtail stew... Decades of experience in this had turned her footsteps into ghosts as she crossed the hallway without rattling anything.
’I need to prepare for everyone...’
It was what she was being paid as a maid to do, though in her honest opinion, she didn’t deserve to be paid as much as she did but Lord Silas was quite generous.

’He’s too generous for his own good...’ She thought, she had paid her late husband’s medical bills completely too and Martha could even remember the faces of the debtors when she had come to pay them arriving in her Master’s car. ’So I have my own money...’
The woman twiddled her thumbs a bit, what was she going to use her salary to do? She really didn’t know... maybe buy more maid wear?
The kitchen was cold when she walked in and three minutes later it was warm.
She lit the low burners and set a heavy copper kettle of spring water on the grate.

Short-grain pearl rice from the market province went into a bowl, and she rinsed it three times until the water ran clear, then settled it into the cast-iron steamer with a strip of dried kelp and a spoonful of toasted sesame oil.
The kitchen filled with a soft hush of steam.

’He likes the rice firm,’ she thought, tipping the lid a quarter inch to check. ’Not too firm... It should be just enough that it holds its shape when he lifts it with his spoon. My goal is to get Master to take a second bowl.’
Chop! Chop! Chop!
Her knife moved against the end-grain block in a quick hypnotic rhythm as scallions fell away into paper-thin emerald rings and ginger became fine needles as well.
Dried shiitake, plumped in warm broth, were sliced into soft ribbons.
In the stockpot, kelp and dried fish had begun to give up their flavor, and a thin ribbon of steam carried the smell of the sea up to the ceiling.
’I’ll be making my favorite today... I hope Master likes it.’
She knew the first sip of the dashi would land on a tired man at the head of the table.
He would hold the bowl in both hands without thinking while slurping and his shoulders would drop several inches, showing all of the muscles on that his handsome fac—
’Mmph... Don’t be foolish, Martha,’ she scolded herself, catching a small smile on her own face in the glass of the cupboard. ’You’re the housekeeper.’
She turned the heat down under the stock anyway and hummed.
The salmon came out next, thick coastal cuts packed in sea salt the day before with their silver skin ready to crisp.
She laid the best piece in the pan first with skin down, and listened to it hiss.
Shhhhhh!
’This is how my mornings pass most of the time...’

She stood watching the skin turn golden and crackling at the edges, and she was already picturing him pulling it apart with his chopsticks, the flesh flaking in pale pink curls, and his face doing the thing it did when he thought nobody was looking.
’I cook and then think of Master Silas’s face... and how he reacts.’
It was perverted... perhaps a bit but she wanted to cook the best, especially since he looked several years younger when he was eating something good.
’Is it bad that I want to be his maid for a very long time...?’
The tamago went into a rectangular pan one thin golden layer at a time, folded and pushed and folded again, with a little sugar and a splash of the dashi so the egg stayed soft.
The first one she slid onto a plate was for Lia and it was sweet.
’Lia likes a lot of sweet food...’
The second she made less sweet which was the way Penelope liked.
’Penelope on the other hand is in the middle and then there’s... me...’
The third she set aside for herself and quietly wrapped the best slice in a napkin to tuck onto his plate while another one was kept aside for Harper.
While the miso stock simmered, she didn’t sit still as she moved through the lower floor like the weather.
Fwip!
The drapes were drawn back exactly four inches so the pale pre-dawn could touch the parlor floor.
The sofa cushions, dented from yesterday’s figurine wars, got fluffed and squared at forty-five-degree angles.

She wiped the cedar tables, gathered the empty tea goblets, swept up the gravel by the shoe rack, and checked the temperature on the panel then she went back to the stove and tasted the miso with the back of a spoon, and frowned, and added a pinch more spice.
’Master should give me a big headpat!’
By five-thirty, the entire ground floor smelled like heaven.
She checked the brass watch pinned under her apron and it was five fifty-eight.
"...It’s time."
She wiped her hands on a dry towel, climbed the stairs without a sound, and stopped outside Lia’s room.
Rap, rap, rap!

"Lady Penelope. Little Mistress Lia." Her voice was gentle, but it carried the weight of an iron bell. "It is six o’clock... The washroom water is hot, and breakfast will be on the table in twenty minutes."
From inside, a muffled agonized groan rattled the wood.
"Five more minutes, Miss Martha," Lia’s voice croaked into a pillow. "The blankets trapped me... the world is in danger and Big Brother has to clear the rift."

"The only danger, Little Mistress," Martha answered with dry unshakable composure, "is the extra unfinished math worksheet on your desk... If your boots are not on the first floor by six-twenty, I shall have to tell Master Silas you require extra supervision after school."
A sudden scuffle broke out behind the door.
THUD!
"Lia, get off my arm!" Penelope’s haughty hiss came through the panels. "You knocked my glasses off the nightstand! If we are late for the academy tram, the prefect will dock our deportment marks!"
"I’m moving! I’m moving! Where’s my left sock?!"
Martha smiled to herself, folded her hands over her apron, and went back downstairs to plate the food.
At six-twenty on the dot, chaos arrived.
Penelope and Lia came tumbling down the stairs with hastily brushed hair and navy-and-gold uniforms pulled tight.
The school had other uniforms and this was a Wednesday where they had to wear the second one.
Lia was still fighting with her red necktie while Penelope was checking the brass clasps of her satchel with her posture snapping into noble stiffness the second her loafers touched the ground floor.
"Good morning, Miss Martha," Penelope said with a small, dignified nod, and slid into her seat.
"Good morning, Penelope." Martha set down a steaming bowl of rice and a piece of glazed salmon in front of her. "Mind the tea... It’s quite hot."
"It smells incredible!" Lia dropped onto her cushion like a sack of stones and grabbed her chopsticks. "I thought I was going to starve in my sleep."
"You ate four honey pastries at ten o’clock last night," Penelope noted coldly, not looking up. "Your metabolism is terrifying... You resemble a locust..."
"I’m a growing child!" Lia shot back, mouth already full. "Locusts don’t do fractions!"
The heavy floorboards of the upper landing groaned.
Two figures appeared at the top of the stairs, and the contrast between them was so absurd that Martha had to press a linen napkin to her lips to smother an unladylike snort.
Harper came down like an empress arriving to greet her court and she was radiant.
Her long violet hair spilled loose over her shoulders like crushed silk, her skin was flushed and rosy, and her eyes were wide and bright with terrifying energy.
Her violet pajama shirt with the little golden stars was unbuttoned at the collar, and she floated down the steps with both hands tucked in her pockets.

"Good morning, everyone!" she announced, in a voice like a silver bell. "What a glorious magnificent morning! The air is crisp, the birds are singing, and I feel like I could wrestle a monster into submission with my bare hands! I slept like a baby!"
Behind her, Silas was being dragged.
He looked like he’d spent eight hours strapped to the bumper of an imperial supply train.
His hair was a bird’s nest of cowlicks, his eyes were hooded and bloodshot, with deep purple shadows under them like a necromancer fresh out of a grave.
His violet silk pajama shirt had been twisted into complete ruin around his torso, and there was a suspicious damp patch on the left sleeve, ringed in teeth marks.
He came down the stairs with the stiff gait of a wooden marionette with one hand gripping the banister as though his knees might go at any moment.
"I am never," he croaked, in a voice like iron on granite, "letting you into my room again! You’re banned... Banned! Don’t come to my house again!"
Harper turned on the third step, leaned back against the banister, and looked at him with a wide unrepentant grin.

"Oh, don’t be so dramatic! You make it sound like I subjected you to some kind of torture... I was resting. Anchoring my body against your warm sturdy frame, anyway, I found the accommodations so restorative that I’ve decided to stay another four or five days."
Silas stopped on the landing, his left eye twitching with violent exhaustion.
"Go home, Harper." He dragged both hands down his face. "You have an entire house to run... Go sleep in your own bed before you dislocate my spine."

"My own bed doesn’t have an oversized Gold Core heating furnace," Harper said cheerfully, hopping down the last three steps and strutting toward the table. "And my house doesn’t have Miss Martha’s cooking... I’m a guest! Hospitality is a recognized virtue in the Sovereign Realm!"
Martha came over from the counter with two heavy stoneware trays and a serene amused smile crinkling the corners of her eyes.

"Lady Harper is welcome to stay as long as she pleases... The house has several empty suites, and a lively presence in the halls is quite refreshing." She set a steaming bowl of dashi at the empty seat beside Silas. "Please sit, Master Silas... You look as though you fought three wars before dawn."
"I fought something worse," Silas muttered, collapsing into the high-backed oak chair at the head of the table. "An Awakened koala with a vacuum attachment."
Harper stuck her tongue out at him from across the table and picked up her soup with an appreciative hum.
Silas leaned back and let out a ragged exhale that ruffled his bangs s his shoulders were knotted into iron.
Rustle!
Warm hands settled over his shoulders.
He blinked and tilted his head back.
Martha had stepped behind his chair as her face was the picture of dignified service.
’She still looks cute...’
Her chin was held high, her starched white apron was without a crease too making her look elegant then her slender experienced fingers dug into the thick muscle between his neck and collarbone.
Knead! Press! Squeeze!
His mouth fell open.
"Ngh~"
A low helpless groan of relief rumbled in his throat as the knots along his trapezius started to melt under her thumbs.
"Ah... hell. Martha, you’re an angel... A saint..."
"You carry far too much tension in your neck, Master Silas," she murmured, pitching her voice low enough that the girls bickering over the salmon didn’t catch it.
Under that calm, her heart was doing something she hadn’t given it permission to do.
Her thumbs mapped the hard muscle of his shoulders, and she nearly salivated.
’Good heavens, it’s like kneading warm bronze and that purple-haired menace chewed on his arm all night like a fruit bat... Shameless.’
Master needed to be with her and Lia... they were his family, the others could come second.
"Is the pressure acceptable, Master?"
"It’s incredible." His eyes were half closed. "If you ever leave this house, Martha, I’ll bring you back... I can’t survive without you."
She laughed and let her fingers rest on the nape of his neck for two last strokes before she withdrew.
"You exaggerate. Eat your broth while it holds the heat, Master..."

’Good heavens, it’s like kneading warm bronze and that purple-haired menace chewed on his arm all night like a fruit bat...
Shameless.’
Master needed to be with her and Lia... they were his family, the others could come second.
"Is the pressure acceptable, Master?"
"It’s incredible." His eyes were half closed.
"If you ever leave this house, Martha, I’ll bring you back...
I can’t survive without you."
She laughed and let her fingers rest on the nape of his neck for two last strokes before she withdrew.
"You exaggerate.
Eat your broth while it holds the heat, Master..."

chapters.title: Chapter 657: Jealousy Brews Best In The Morning [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: "Also... The salmon was salted with coastal sea-crust..."
Silas picked up his spoon and took a deep hot sip of the dashi.
The rich savory broth hit his palate, kelp and ginger and the velvet fat of the pork belly, and his eyes closed.
His shoulders dropped an inch and the line between his brows let go.
’It’s exactly as I thought!’
Martha looked away fast, because her face had done something foolish and if Silas saw it, he wouldn’t stop teasing her.
Silas on the other hand ate three spoonfuls before he could stop himself.
’Gods this is good...’
Nearly two weeks of ration biscuits and cold canned stew in a burning desert had left him with a hollow ache he hadn’t had the words for, and this bowl of soup filled him whole.
’I didn’t have time to cook at all, that’s how busy it was out there.’
Silas was happy though...There was a table, a warm kitchen, a little sister arguing about locusts and a rude houseguest stealing his fish.
"Incredible," Silas said, and dug into the rice with sudden, ravenous enthusiasm. "Martha, seriously..."
"The salmon skin is so crispy it sounds like potato chips!" Lia announced, holding up her empty bowl with a triumphant grin.
"The seasoning on the rolled egg is remarkably balanced," Penelope added, dabbing her mouth with a napkin. "The sugar is restrained, which lets the stock dominate... It’s an exceptional execution."

"A culinary triumph!" Harper beamed, polishing off her second piece of fish with shameless gusto. "If House Whitmore could produce a cook with half your talent, Martha, we would never have had to conquer three trade leagues just to secure decent kitchen imports!"
’Conquer trade leagues?’
Surrounded by the praise, Martha’s cheeks went a bright honest crimson.
She ducked her head and smoothed her apron with flustered fingers.
"You flatter me, all of you. It’s only a simple morning spread... I’m overjoyed it pleases the table."
Clack!
Penelope set her chopsticks down, followed instantly by Lia, who swallowed the last pickled radish nearly whole.
"Done!" Lia leaped out of her chair and grabbed her satchel. "Penelope, hurry! If we catch the early tram we can compare the Blessed Land box art before homeroom!"
Martha glanced at the antique clock and slid back into household-commander mode, crossing to the key rack.
She lifted a heavy emerald-enameled fob.
"No tram this morning, girls... I’ll drive you to the academy gates in the Vell-965 as usual. After that I have errands, and the cruiser has room for them."
"Oooooh!" Lia’s eyes turned into giant stars. "We’re taking the emerald land-yacht?! Tommy from the track team is going to explode on the sidewalk!"
’When did you get so excited about trying to impress boys...?’ Silas thought with his eye twitching, was there some specific reason Lia was doing this?
Penelope lifted her chin two inches, a faint, haughty smirk touching her lips.
"A sensible deployment of family assets. Let us proceed."
"Hold on a second, Martha," Silas called, setting his tea bowl down.
She paused at the foyer archway and turned back. "Yes, Master Silas?"
He wiped his mouth with a napkin and leaned forward on his elbows.

"Yesterday, while I was lying on the sofa, I logged into the Europa trade exchange and ordered a few crates of specialized imports... The exact cosmetic formulas, maritime lavender soaps, triple-milled saponin bars, and alabaster bath salts that a close friend of mine uses."
Martha blinked. "Soaps, Master?"

"The highest grade available." He took a folded slip of parchment with a consignment code scribbled across the top out of his pocket and held it out. "The shipment cleared customs at the southern transit hub about twenty minutes ago... After you drop the girls off, go down to Gate Four, hand this manifest to the supervisor, and they’ll load the crates into the cargo boot."
He looked right at her, and his expression softened into one that was warm and earnest.
"There are six crates, Martha. Two have silver seals... Those are for you."
Martha froze with her hand halfway to the paper.

"For me, Master?" she whispered. "No. Master Silas, that’s unnecessary, Celestial saponin and alabaster salts are priced at thousands of credits an ounce and they’re meant for consorts and high lords. A bar of tallow soap from the grocer is more than enough for a housekeeper—"
Pat!
He rose from his chair, closed the distance in two easy strides, and set his broad warm palm on top of her hair.
He ruffled it gently, exactly the way he did with Lia when she was being stubborn with his eyes crinkling.

"Stop that nonsense, Martha. You get up at four every morning to make sure my little sister eats warm rice... You wash my clothes, you run the wards, you keep this place from falling apart while I’m in my territory so no, you’re not ’just a maid.’... You’re part of this house."
He pressed the slip into her trembling fingers.
"Take the soaps and soak in the tub for an hour tonight... You’ve earned it ten times over."
Martha stood completely rigid.
A fierce wave of heat climbed her neck and flooded her cheeks, her ears as well as the bridge of her nose.
Her heart hammered like a trapped sparrow as she looked up into his relaxed, handsome face, and her dignified composure turned to dust.
She folded at the waist in a bow so deep and fast that the hem of her apron nearly brushed the floor.
"I shall see to the logistics immediately, Master Silas! Th-thank you! Thank you profoundly!"
Clutching the paper to her chest, the dignified head housekeeper spun on her velvet slippers and scurried toward the foyer like a startled rabbit with her face hot enough to fry an egg.
Silas let out a low chuckle and crossed his arms.
Lia bounded over to tug on the sleeve of his pajamas. "Bye-bye, Big Brother!"
He leaned down, and she planted a loud, sticky kiss on his right cheek.
"Be good in class," he said, tapping her nose. "Don’t use the signed figurine box to gamble for snacks..."
"No promises!" she chirped, and ran after Martha.
Penelope stopped in front of him, adjusting the strap of her satchel.
She glanced at Silas, then past him at her older sister, who was leaning against the table with an amused, feline smirk, and her sharp violet eyes narrowed.
"Goodbye, Silas," she said smoothly then she locked onto Harper with the merciless judgment of an inquisitor. "And, Sister, please do not make any babies while we are gone..."
Silence dropped over the kitchen like an anvil.
Harper’s smirk vanished as a blinding shade of magenta exploded from her collarbones to the tips of her ears.
"PENELOPE MARIE WHITMORE!" She slammed both palms onto the table, her violet hair flaring with static. "WHERE DID YOU HEAR THAT?! WHO TAUGHT YOU THAT?! YOU LITTLE BRAT, GET BACK HERE THIS INSTANT—"
"I am departing for my education," Penelope announced in a flat immaculate monotone, already turning on her heel.
The heavy cedar door swung shut behind her with a solid thud.

"I’M GROUNDING HER FOR THREE MONTHS!" Harper fumed, pacing along the hardwood and fanning her burning cheeks with both hands while Silas leaned on the counter while clutching his ribs. "No allowance! No library privileges! The audacity of that child! She doesn’t even know what she’s saying!"
’I thought she would use this as a chance to tease me but I’m glad she’s back to normal...’
"She said what she said," Silas wheezed. "Very clearly."
VROOOOOOOOM!
Outside, the Vell-965’s twin turbines purred to life with a low rumble, and the iron gates groaned open along their oiled tracks.
The big emerald land-cruiser slid down the cobblestone driveway, floating over the ruts without a single vibration reaching the cabin, and swung out into the morning lane.
Silas walked out into the foyer and pushed the front door open.
The air hit his face as he stood on the landing running a hand through his messy hair.
’Right... Martha’s helping me out, there’s barely anything I can do like this.’
He took two steps toward the wrought-iron gate and stopped.
Through the thinning fog of the private lane, two figures were walking side by side with their footsteps steady and unhurried on the asphalt.
To a lot of people, they were pretty well known and it was the same for Silas, he would have known those silhouettes anywhere on Earth.
’Why are they here?’
Walking on the left was Seraphina Bloom.
Her crimson hair tumbled in loose wild waves over her shoulders, glowing like rubies in the early light.

Instead of her tailored suits or high-collared combat silks, she wore a big oversized white button-down, the cuffs rolled carelessly up her forearms, and loose black trousers that pooled over her leather loafers.
It looked absurdly casual on a Bloom heiress, like she’d grabbed whatever was on the floor on her way out the door.
...Sera still looked good in it too.
Beside her, tall and easy and golden, walked Valerius Sterling.
His blond hair caught the sun like polished brass as he wore a charcoal vest over an open-collared cream shirt, and a warm lazy grin sat on his handsome face.
As they crossed the threshold of the open gate, Valerius spotted Silas and raised a hand.
"Yo, Silas!" His deep voice carried across the courtyard. "Looking lively as ever! I hear you’ve been busy playing house!"
Silas lifted a hand back, a faint smile touching his mouth. "Valerius."
They hadn’t spoken since the aftermath of the Ititius Secret Realm.
Silas had barely seen the idiot throughout the Tournament Of Succession, and seeing the blond man strolling around in one piece was a small welcome relief.
’Still,’ he thought, shifting into sharp focus as they walked past the iron pillars, ’why are they here at seven in the morning with no escort too.’
They should have brought the butler of last time... It would have been a lot better.
Before he could ask, Seraphina broke into a brisk purposeful stride.
She didn’t look at the garden as her red eyes went straight to Silas, to his wrecked hair, his rumpled violet pajamas and his tired face with the focus of a hawk who had spotted prey.
She closed the distance in three long steps and threw both arms around his neck.
"Oof—" Silas grunted, slippers skidding half an inch across the flagstones as her momentum hit him.

She buried her face in the curve of his neck for one greedy heartbeat, breathing him in with a small shaky shudder then she pulled back just far enough to look up at him with her red eyes looking bright and dilated.
"Good morning, handsome," Seraphina purred, low and smoky.
She reached up and threaded her fingers through his messy dark hair, brushing it back from his forehead in slow, deliberate strokes.
"Look at you... Your hair’s gotten longer since we last saw each other, It suits you, Silas. Makes you look remarkably dangerous, just like I wanted."
Silas raised an eyebrow, his hands settling lightly on her waist to steady her.
"Sera, what are you—"
"I decided," she said, her voice dropping, "that you deserve a proper reward for surviving the rifts."
He barely had time to blink.
PULL!
Her fingers tightened in the hair at the base of his skull, and she hauled his head down.
SMACK!
She kissed him.
It wasn’t a polite peck of greeting... how could anyone expect Sera to do such a thing...? When she did something, she liked doing it with all of her might and the situation didn’t change now.
The kiss was hot and a little fierce with her soft lips pressing hard against his, her tongue slipped past his teeth as her free arm locked around his neck and pulled her flush against his chest.
SMACK!
Silas froze with his eyes wide.
That lasted one heartbeat then his hand slid from her waist to the small of her back as his eyes closed and he kissed her back.
’Kissing me out of nowhere...? When did that start?’

However he would naturally lean into it, the first was to get back at Harper for not only licking his face all night but teasing him about it in the morning and as for the second, he wanted to tease Sera more.
"Mhm~"
Seraphina made a small startled sound against his mouth as her fingers curled tighter in his hair.
’Idiot...! Why are you trying to outdo me?!’
How would he not outdo her... Sera didn’t have any experience in these things at all!
Behind them, in the open doorway of the residence, Harper had just stepped out onto the threshold with a half-eaten honey roll in her fingers.
She froze.
Her jaw dropped and her violet eyes went wide as saucers as the pastry slipped out of her limp hand and landed on the limestone doormat with a soft pathetic plop.
Right in the middle of the driveway, locked in a mouth-to-mouth embrace with Silas, was Seraphina Bloom.
And without breaking the kiss, without letting go of a single millimeter of Silas’s mouth, Seraphina slowly opened her red eyes.
Her gaze slid over his shoulder and locked onto Harper’s horrified face as her lips curved against Silas’s in a victorious smirk.
’He’s mine...’ She thought as her red eyes began burning with triumph.
’...you jealous bitch.’

chapters.title: Chapter 658: A Very Important Question [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The morning breeze swept through the open gates of the Silverleaf driveway and rustled the branches, but the temperature within a five-foot radius of Silas was spiking toward combustion.
’She’s hot...’
He meant that figuratively and quite literally too... Her body was growing hotter by the second and in extension so was the air.
However Sera on the other hand could not form a single normal thought.

For the first four seconds, she had moved purely on hot-blooded momentum in an explosive assault fueled by the sight of that oversized violet-haired vulture standing in Silas’s doorway but momentum was a finite currency.
As the seconds dragged out, the stark reality of her own ignorance slammed into her nervous system like an ice-water bath.
’I’m a fool...’
She had read the courtly romance scrolls in her mother’s private study.
She had watched the theatrical holographic dramas imported from the southern empires.

In theory, Intimacy was a battlefield of leverage, subtle parted sighs, and dominance but in practice, she was eighteen, possessed zero field experience and had completely forgotten that human beings required oxygen to stay conscious.
Even someone like her...
Her breath came short and frantic through her nose.
Her tongue, which had darted forward with such predatory swagger, grew clumsy and tangled against Silas’s teeth, because it turned out she had no idea what came after the initial breach.

Her fingers, knotted with such authority into the dark hair at the base of his skull, began to tremble as a furious dizzying heat rushed into her ears and turned her vision into a kaleidoscope of dancing crimson sparks.
In the doorway, Harper knelt with her knuckles white as she collected the dropped honey roll and its wax paper.
’I’m going to kill her... One day... be sure of it.’
Finally, with her lungs burning and her balance tilting, Seraphina broke the seal.
Pop!
She pulled back with a breathless wet gasp with her chest heaving beneath the oversized white cotton shirt.
Her crimson hair was a disheveled storm around her flushed collarbones and her red eyes, normally as sharp and serious as a magistrate’s, were wide and dazed and swimming with flustered watery panic.
Silas stood frozen on the limestone tread, blinking slowly.
He reached up with the back of his violet silk sleeve and wiped his chin and mouth with a dull scraping drag then he looked down at the heiress of House Bloom.
"Sera," he said, in a dry voice like two slate shingles rubbing together. "Were you trying to greet me, or were you attempting to detach my lower mandible and eat it for breakfast?"
A violent shade of scarlet detonated across Seraphina’s porcelain cheeks, raced down her throat, and vanished beneath the broad collar of the shirt.

"I... What...?!" she stammered, her voice pitching up a bit as she took a frantic half-step backward with her hands flying to her hips in a desperate attempt to reconstruct her shattered dignity. "H-How dare you! An uncultured brute like you wouldn’t know a mark of favor if it struck you in the forehead! It was a demonstration of marking your territory! You should be on your knees thanking me!"
"Right," Silas muttered, rubbing his sore neck. "Next time send a formal dispatch... It’s safer for my teeth."
’You’re the one that kissed me and I’m the one at fault?
A few paces behind Seraphina, standing tall and broad on the driveway, Valerius cleared his throat.
"Ahem!"
The blond scion was staring at the back of Seraphina’s neck with an expression of deep bewilderment with one hand hovering over his chin and his golden brows knitted into a tight disbelieving knot.
’I still can’t believe it...’
Valerius had known Seraphina since they were toddlers, hauled to the same insufferable noble galas and guild functions and told to be polite.
Their formal names were long and exhausting to say during formal greetings, so at some point they had shortened them to "Seraph" and "Val."

He had watched her throw a flaming dagger at an ambassador’s son because the boy had stepped on her shadow so he knew exactly how rare it was to see her lose her composure and he was well aware that over the past week or two she had taken to calling Silas her "prospective husband" with all the stubborn arrogance of a girl claiming a rare drop in a dungeon.
’But they’re actually swapping spit on the driveway?!’ Valerius thought, his jaw slightly slack. ’In broad daylight?! At seven in the morning?!’
His golden eyes drifted past Silas’s shoulder and locked onto the front door, where Harper Whitmore had just risen to her feet.
She was wearing a violet silk pajama shirt dotted with tiny golden stars.
Silas was wearing the exact same violet silk pajama shirt, with the exact same golden stars.
A sudden sharp pang of bitter injustice pierced Valerius’s chest like a wind-lance.
He was the heir to the Sterling Conglomerate... He stood six-foot-two, the same height as Silas, with thick golden hair that practically sparkled in the dawn sun.
...And what did his social life look like? Zero girlfriends.

The only women who ever approached him at society galas were third-tier socialites trying to extract corporate contracts for their fathers’ logistics guilds, or his father Lohan barking at him to review shipping margins.

’Why does Silas get all the luck?!’ Valerius lamented silently, kicking a piece of loose gravel with his leather boot. ’He wears unbrushed hair, lives like a hermit, spends ninety percent of his time in rifts, and he’s out here juggling the heiress of House Bloom and the Head of House Whitmore in matching sleepwear! What kind of forbidden cultivation manual is this?!’
Silas, blissfully unaware of the existential crisis rotting his friend’s brain, let out a quiet sigh and gestured toward the open front door.
"Whatever," he said, rolling his stiff shoulders. "You’re already here. Come inside before the neighbors start calling the police about a public disturbance."
Harper stood in the doorway with the crushed wax paper clenched in her palm.
Her violet eyes were narrowed into two icy slits as she puffed out her pale cheeks and aimed a venomous unblinking pout straight at Seraphina.
Seraphina’s chin snapped up, and her red eyes narrowed right back, throwing off enough invisible heat to ignite dry tinder.
The two women stood five feet apart, glaring at each other with open hostility... It was a silent standoff between purple lightning and crimson flame that made the air hum with static.

"Much obliged, Silas," Valerius broke in cheerfully, stepping past the line of fire and wiping his boots on the mat. "The breeze off the eastern bay is brisk this morning, it smells like someone’s roasting fish in here!"
Silas ushered them inside and pulled the heavy cedar door shut, engaging the interior lock with a solid click.
The front hall was warm and quiet and filled with the lingering aroma of Martha’s glazed salmon and roasted dashi broth.
The hardwood floor gleamed with fresh lemon wax, reflecting the pale morning light that filtered through the sheer drapes.

Seraphina stepped into the open-plan parlor with her arms crossed, the oversized sleeves of her white shirt swallowing her wrists, and cast a slow hyper-critical gaze around the vaulted living room, scanning the leather sectionals and the polished staircase leading to the upper gallery.
Her nose wrinkled with a bit of distaste.

"Honestly, Silas," she scoffed, tapping one loafer against the parquet. "You’re a Lord who survived facing a god like us, yet you insist on living in such a... profoundly tiny shoe box... A single living area? No central atrium? How do you even circulate your spiritual pathways in such a cramped little cupboard?"
Silas nearly choked on his own saliva. He stared at her with his blue-and-gold eyes wide in offended disbelief.

’A shoe box?!’ he screamed internally. ’It has a half-acre walled courtyard in one of the most expensive residential districts in Valoria City! The place has empty rooms! Martha counted them! What part of this is cramped?!’
He opened his mouth to defend the integrity of his real estate, but Harper stepped smoothly up to his left side.
She adjusted her glasses which she had pulled out of somewhere with an elegant flick of her index finger, and her cool polished-glass voice rang out with as much defensiveness as she could muster.
"Pay no attention to her, Silas," she said softly, her violet eyes glinting with serene calm.
A desperate spark of hope kindled in Silas’s chest as he looked down at her.
’Yes! Thank you, Harper! Tell this spoiled council brat what normal housing looks like.’
Harper continued without skipping a beat.

"She has no concept of modest living. Though, to be fair to her criticism... my own estate is about thirty times the size of this plot... There are several pavilions, an artificial lake, and a lawn so large the groundskeepers use carts."
The spark of hope in Silas’s chest withered into ash as he turned his flat dead stare on the Head of House Whitmore.
Harper didn’t notice.
She turned toward him with a sweet smile and lightly brushed a speck of lint from the lapel of his violet pajamas.

"If you ever feel the walls closing in, Silas," she purred, "House Whitmore would be more than happy to extend an interest-free line of sovereign credit... Forty million credits? Fifty? You could purchase a sector and build a proper estate worthy of your station... You wouldn’t even have to worry about collateral, Your personal company would be collateral enough."

"Hah!" Seraphina scoffed loudly, throwing her head back with a sharp, derisive laugh. "Fifty million? How quaint! How painfully bourgeois! House Bloom could wire eighty million credits into his account before noon, and we wouldn’t even require a promissory note! If Silas wants an estate, he won’t be groveling for Whitmore scraps!"

"Scraps?" Harper’s voice dropped into a silky whisper with her glasses flashing. "At least House Whitmore manages its own liquidity, unlike certain council heiresses who run to their mothers whenever an investment account dips below eight figures."
"Why you...! You insolent little corporate leech!"
"Spoiled brat."
"Purple-haired vulture!"
Silas stood between them with his left eyelid spasming in a rhythmic, agonizing beat.
He pressed the palms of his hands to his temples and let out a long groan that vibrated down his collarbone.
Over by the hearth, Valerius had already kicked off his loafers and collapsed onto the broad leather sofa.
He stretched his long legs out, rested his arms along the back cushions, and let out a loud contented sigh as the leather molded to his back.
His golden eyes tracked the bickering women for a second before drifting to the matching violet silk.
"Hey, Silas," he called, pointing an idle thumb at the pajamas. "What’s with the matching set? You guys joining a private cultivation cult, or did you buy a two-for-one bundle at the night market?"
Harper’s chin snapped around, and her face brightened into an expression of proud triumph.

"It is not a cult, Valerius," she corrected smoothly, smoothing the soft silk over her hip with a graceful, deliberate stroke. "It is House of Valois silk with micro-temperature wards woven into the thread... I commissioned bespoke sets for the entire household. Midnight blue for Martha, lavender for Penelope, forest green for Lia, and this one for Silas and myself. It regulates spiritual fluctuations during REM cycles and prevents nocturnal meridian strain. Do you like the cut? The little golden stars were embroidered by hand in the southern workshops."
Valerius tilted his head and whistled softly with genuine appreciation.
"It actually looks pretty sharp and sleek lines too... The shoulders look comfortable as hell."
FREEZE!
A wave of volcanic heat washed over the sofa, and Valerius’s words trailed off.
Three feet away, Seraphina was glaring at him.
Her red eyes burned with an intensity that suggested she was calculating how many degrees of third-degree burns she could inflict on his torso before the city guard arrived.
Her jaw was set in rigid stone, and her hands were balled into tight fists at the ends of her oversized sleeves.
Valerius’s golden skin went pale.
’A-ah... I fucked up.’
He snapped his mouth shut, swallowed hard and stared straight ahead at the empty television screen, locking into the stiff motionless discipline of a soldier waiting for an artillery shell.
’Rule number one of surviving Seraphina Bloom,’ he reminded himself frantically. ’Never compliment the enemy’s wardrobe... Keep your mouth shut, Sterling...’
Silas took a deep breath and clapped his hands once to shatter the suffocating tension in the room.

"Look," he said, rubbing the back of his neck. "Martha already left to take the girls to the academy and handle some morning logistics. She only prepared enough breakfast for the household, and since the table’s cleared... I can head into the kitchen and whip up something quick. Eggs, toast, whatever we have in the pantry."
He turned toward the kitchen archway and behind him, two pairs of eyes locked onto each other.
BZZZZT!
An invisible bolt of competitive electricity flashed between Seraphina and Harper.

These were two nobles and now they had been presented with the most primitive way of resolving a territorial dispute... It was the best known one to civilization, providing morning sustenance to the male in question.
"I’ll do it!" Seraphina barked, stepping forward so fast her loafers squeaked against the wood.

"Out of the question," Harper countered instantly, cutting across her path with the grace of a dancing blade. "You are an uninvited guest who arrived at dawn without notice... I have been residing in this house since yesterday evening so domestic duties naturally fall to the established occupant."
"You don’t live here, you parasite!" Seraphina snarled, baring her teeth. "You slept on his couch!"
"I slept in his bed," Harper purred, with venomous calm. She really was like a snake.
Seraphina’s jaw dropped, and her hair sparked with tiny red embers of ambient fire-mana.
"Ladies," Silas interrupted, holding both hands up like a referee trying to separate two rabid mastiffs. "Do either of you even know how to cook?"

chapters.title: Chapter 659: How Are We Friends If I Don’t Have Your Number? [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The silence that fell over the parlor was instantaneous and heavy with wounded pride.
Harper stared at him.
Her violet eyes narrowed behind her spectacles, and her chin lifted in deep personal insult, as though he had just suggested she couldn’t multiply single-digit numbers.
Seraphina’s red eyes flared with equal indignation, and she planted her hands on her hips.

"I am the recognized heiress of House Bloom," she declared coldly. "I have memorized seventeenth-century alchemical compounding matrices and synthesized complex elemental reagents... A simple culinary process of combining proteins and heat is basic physics. It is child’s play! I’m insulted that you think otherwise."
"House Whitmore maintains the trade lines in organic agricultural commodities," Harper stated, with icy composure.
She not only handled the LAB now but was doing other things that truly made her a noble.
"To imply that I cannot prepare a morning spread is a severe misjudgment of my administrative capabilities."
Silas stared at the two of them for three long seconds.
He raised both hands and took two cautious steps backward toward the living room.
"Fine," he muttered. "Go. The pantry is through the archway... Cook whatever you want."
The two girls immediately turned their backs on him and marched shoulder-to-shoulder through the kitchen’s swinging door like two rival generals deploying to the front line.

"Wait!" Silas called after them, a cold spike of panic suddenly piercing his sleep-deprived brain. "Just, do not destroy the kitchen! If you burn the counter or crack the induction stove, I swear to the gods I am billing both your houses ten times the replacement cost!"
The swinging door paused.
Harper’s head poked out of the gap, and she looked at him over the rim of her glasses with a feline amused smirk.

"Ten times the cost, Silas?" she teased, in a voice sweet as honeyed poison. "A kitchen renovation is light work for my treasury... If things get out of hand, I’ll simply purchase the entire residential block, demolish it, and build you a three-story culinary wing of polished marble. Try to relax!"
Fwip!
She disappeared behind the door, leaving Silas standing in the hall with his fist raised and his whole body fighting the urge to throw a piece of furniture at the woodwork.
"Infuriating," he growled under his breath, turning around and trudging back toward the parlor. "Rich people are completely unhinged."

He collapsed into the empty armchair beside Valerius, leaned back until his head rested against the leather, and stared up at the ceiling molding while the faint sounds of clattering metal began to echo from the kitchen.
Now it was just the two of them.
The morning sun climbed higher and cast broad golden rectangles across the Persian rug.
The silence between the two young men was comfortable, born of having stood back-to-back beneath collapsing ice while horrors clawed at their shields.
Silas reached down, picked up a half-empty glass of cold water from the side table, and took a slow sip.
"So," he said, his voice returning to its normal, steady pitch. "How’s the family? How’s Lohan holding up? What about Mia too?"
Valerius let out a long groan and threw his head back against the cushions until his golden hair spilled over the top.

"Don’t get me started, man," he sighed, dragging both hands down his face. "My old man has been riding my ass non-stop since the Secret Realm collapsed... Every single morning it’s ledgers, contracts, quarterly yield projections... The man treats my existence like an underperforming branch office."
"Still pushing trade agreements?"

"Worse," Valerius muttered, rolling his neck until the joints popped. "You remember the Grand Assembly? Well you weren’t there but I was, The Sterling Conglomerate just closed the Tsardom of Borealis deal so now ten automated heavy-munitions foundries along the northern railway corridor, standardized artillery, mana-core casings, and void-iron penetrators, are all underwritten by us, with replenishment times cut by sixty percent... In exchange, we get an exclusive fifteen-year concession on the raw titanium and unrefined void-iron out of the newly stabilized northern trench sectors."
Silas raised an eyebrow. "How did the Tsar take it?"

"Volkov slammed his fist on the table and said yes before my father finished the sentence," Valerius said, with a grin he couldn’t quite suppress. "He’s sick to death of Columbian shells jamming in his cannon breeches because some pinstripe bureaucrat shaved an eighth of an inch off the brass to save a few credits... We walked out with the monopoly and a military alliance with Borealis in under five minutes and President Vanderbilt looked like he was going to burst a vein."
"I would have paid good money to see that."

"It was beautiful," Valerius sighed. "And now my father has the whole corporate structure on twenty-four-hour rotations to get the foundry sites and the transport convoys ready... I haven’t slept more than four hours a night all week and it isn’t just us but the whole Council sector is buzzing."
Silas raised an eyebrow. "House Bloom too?"

"Yeah," Valerius nodded, glancing toward the closed kitchen door. "Matriarch Bloom won the three coastal mining sectors in the southern gulf... Albion’s Prime Minister threw a huge scene, because those sectors sit right on his trade route, but she pointed out that his navy can’t keep sea-krakens and pirates off his own freighters, and Australis voted with her. Now she’s hammering out patrol terms with Albion, and Sera’s getting dragged into the negotiations next week to represent the younger lineage. Her mother’s grooming her for a council seat, so she’s been swamped with legal briefs and diplomatic protocol."
He let out a quiet chuckle and his golden eyes softened.

"It’s been completely hectic for both of us. But... well, after the desert, after everything that happened down in the dark, we both wanted to come see you. Make sure you were actually breathing and not buried under some mountain of paperwork or something, Oh and Mia’s doing alright... She wants us to meet up sometime and see Aeliana again."
Silas paused and looked at the blond giant beside him.
A quiet warmth settled into his chest.

In the cutthroat world of high-tier Awakened nobility, where every conversation was an exchange of leverage and every alliance had an expiration date, having people who simply showed up at your door because they wanted to verify you were alive was a rare precious commodity.
’Friends in the real world, huh? Feels nice.’
Valerius turned his head to look straight at him.
The easygoing smirk on the blond scion’s face faded, replaced by a sudden awkward hesitation.
"Hey, Silas," he said, his voice dropping into a lower, more serious tone. "We’re... friends, right?"
Silas blinked, caught off guard.
"Yeah?" He nodded with an easy shrug. "Of course we’re friends. We split that Guardian together in the Ititius Realm and you covered my back down in the dark. That makes you solid in my book."
Valerius’s eyes widened, and then his expression shifted into one of aggrieved dramatic betrayal.

"Then why the hell don’t we have each other’s personal comm codes?!" he bellowed, leaning forward and throwing his hands into the air. "We fought through an ancient god’s tomb together! We survived a tectonic collapse and I had to track your damn residential address through my father’s corporate surveillance registry just to find out where you sleep at night! Do you know how pathetic that feels?!"
Silas froze.
His eyes darted to the side, and a nervous sheepish laugh escaped his throat. "Ah... ha ha... right. That."
He reached into the pocket of his violet silk pajamas and pulled out his utilitarian smartphone.
"My bad," he admitted, tapping the screen to unlock the contacts menu. "I’m not exactly great with social stuff, Half the time I forget the device is even charged."
"Unbelievable," Valerius grumbled, pulling a sleek state-of-the-art golden communicator from his vest pocket.
The two devices clicked softly as their proximity sensors engaged, exchanging secure frequencies and personal comm numbers in a flash of pale blue light.
Valerius pocketed his communicator and leaned back into the cushions with a triumphant satisfied nod.
A mischievous boyish grin spread across his handsome face.
"Alright," he said. "Since we have a few minutes before the kitchen inevitably detonates into high-grade shrapnel... you play Lord of the Outer Rings?"
Silas looked up and raised an eyebrow. "The mobile territorial strategy game? The one with the micro-transactions and the base-building timers?"

"The very same," Valerius smirked, tapping his screen with rapid, practiced thumb strikes. "I’ve got a Tier 4 fortress in Sector Seven... My automated ballistas are tearing through the barbarian encampments. Let’s run a co-op siege while the ladies burn your cookware."
Silas looked at the kitchen door, listened to the sound of something heavy and metallic falling onto the linoleum, and shrugged.
"Why not?" he said, booting up the application on his phone. "Let’s see your setup."
Behind the closed swinging door of the kitchen, the atmosphere was thick enough to choke an ox.
Seraphina Bloom stood in front of the expansive marble kitchen island with her hands hanging awkwardly at her sides and her red eyes darting across the stainless steel countertop in mounting panic.
’What... what are all these things?!’
Before her sat an array of culinary implements that looked less like cooking tools and more like torture devices from an ancient dungeon.

There was a heavy cast-iron skillet with a ribbed bottom, a ceramic mandoline with a terrifyingly exposed razor blade, a double-balloon wire whisk, four wooden spoons of varying curvature, a digital food scale, and a stainless steel bowl filled with raw brown eggs.
In the Bloom estate, food simply appeared.

A bell would chime, three uniformed footmen would glide into the private dining pavilion bearing silver cloches, and a five-course spread of pan-seared sea bass, truffle-infused consommé, and glazed root vegetables would be set before her without a speck of grease touching her fingers.
...She had never touched raw poultry in her life, Sera didn’t even know where the shells of eggs went after they were cracked.
Seraphina shifted her weight and cast a cautious defensive glance toward the other side of the counter.
Harper Whitmore stood there, inspecting a clear glass bottle of cold-pressed olive oil.
The Head of House Whitmore appeared to be the picture of effortless competence.

Her long violet hair was tied back with a clean silver clip, her wire-rimmed spectacles sat perfectly on the bridge of her nose, and she held the oil bottle up to the light and tapped the glass with a slender fingernail, whistling a cheerful unhurried melody through her teeth as she arranged a loaf of sourdough, a block of yellow butter, and a carton of milk on the cutting board.

’Damn her,’ Seraphina thought, her teeth grinding in a quiet surge of bitter envy. ’Look at her... So calm... So domestic... She actually knows how to do this... She’s going to whip up a three-star gourmet spread, Silas is going to look at her like she’s a household goddess, and I’m going to be standing here holding an empty frying pan like a complete idiot.’
Her knuckles tightened around the edge of her oversized shirt then Harper’s cheerful whistling abruptly stopped.
She glanced toward the swinging door to verify that Silas and Valerius were out of line of sight, then slid a hand into the pocket of her violet silk pajamas.
With rapid movements she pulled out a sleek, purple-cased smartphone, unlocked the screen with her thumb, opened the global video streaming application LordTube, and clicked on the search bar.
Seraphina’s sharp red eyes narrowed.
She leaned forward by half an inch, tracking the movement of Harper’s thumbs against the glass keyboard.
Harper typed with blistering speed.
[How to make Omlet]
’Omlet?’ Seraphina thought, her brow furrowing. ’She misspelled omelet.’
On the screen, the search engine automatically corrected the query and pulled up hundreds of cooking tutorials.
Harper’s eyes scanned the thumbnails frantically with her cool polished composure cracking into tiny desperate fractures of panic.
She tapped a video titled... [Easy 3-Minute Fluffy Omelet for Beginners (No Skills Required!)]
The video loaded and Harper leaned her hip against the marble counter, turned the volume down to a barely audible whisper, and held the screen close to her spectacles.
A soft feminine voice emanated from the tiny speaker:
"Hello, everyone! Welcome back to Auntie Mae’s Home Kitchen! Today, we are going to make the simplest, most delicious classic rolled egg omelet that anyone can master in five minutes!"
Seraphina stood motionless on the other side of the island.
She looked at Harper’s rigid laser-focused posture as she looked at the tiny screen displaying a cheerful middle-aged woman holding a yellow plastic bowl.
The tension in her shoulders slowly drained away and a tiny breathless snort escaped her nose.
Harper froze.
Her head slowly rotated ninety degrees to the left, her violet eyes wide behind her glasses, and caught Seraphina’s gaze.
For three seconds, neither woman moved.
Harper was holding an instructional video for toddlers while Seraphina was holding an empty wire whisk like a club.
Both of them were completely out of their depth.
Seraphina walked slowly around the edge of the marble island, her footsteps quiet against the linoleum, and came to a halt beside Harper’s shoulder.
She looked down at the illuminated screen, where Auntie Mae was demonstrating how to crack an egg against a flat surface without getting shells in the bowl and Harper didn’t turn the phone off.
She simply tilted the display toward Seraphina so the crimson-haired heiress had a clear view of the instructions.
The two noble prodigies leaned against the counter side by side, their shoulders brushing in the quiet kitchen with their eyes glued to the three-minute beginner tutorial.
"Now, remember," Auntie Mae chimed through the speaker, "the secret is low heat, gentle stirring, and plenty of butter!"
Harper pushed her glasses up her nose with one finger.
Seraphina nodded slowly, her expression grave, as though she were memorizing the coordinates of an enemy fortress.
A silent unspoken truce descended over the marble island.
’Just this once,’ Harper thought, her jaw tightening with grim determination.
’Just this once,’ Seraphina agreed silently, her red eyes burning with fierce resolve.
’...We conquer the eggs.’

sentences.text: The silence that fell over the parlor was instantaneous and heavy with wounded pride.
Harper stared at him.
Her violet eyes narrowed behind her spectacles, and her chin lifted in deep personal insult, as though he had just suggested she couldn’t multiply single-digit numbers.
Seraphina’s red eyes flared with equal indignation, and she planted her hands on her hips.
"I am the recognized heiress of House Bloom," she declared coldly.
"I have memorized seventeenth-century alchemical compounding matrices and synthesized complex elemental reagents...
A simple culinary process of combining proteins and heat is basic physics.
It is child’s play!
I’m insulted that you think otherwise."
"House Whitmore maintains the trade lines in organic agricultural commodities," Harper stated, with icy composure.
She not only handled the LAB now but was doing other things that truly made her a noble.
"To imply that I cannot prepare a morning spread is a severe misjudgment of my administrative capabilities."
Silas stared at the two of them for three long seconds.
He raised both hands and took two cautious steps backward toward the living room.
"Fine," he muttered.
"Go.
The pantry is through the archway...
Cook whatever you want."
The two girls immediately turned their backs on him and marched shoulder-to-shoulder through the kitchen’s swinging door like two rival generals deploying to the front line.
"Wait!" Silas called after them, a cold spike of panic suddenly piercing his sleep-deprived brain.
"Just, do not destroy the kitchen!
If you burn the counter or crack the induction stove, I swear to the gods I am billing both your houses ten times the replacement cost!"
The swinging door paused.
Harper’s head poked out of the gap, and she looked at him over the rim of her glasses with a feline amused smirk.
"Ten times the cost, Silas?" she teased, in a voice sweet as honeyed poison.
"A kitchen renovation is light work for my treasury...
If things get out of hand, I’ll simply purchase the entire residential block, demolish it, and build you a three-story culinary wing of polished marble.
Try to relax!"
Fwip!
She disappeared behind the door, leaving Silas standing in the hall with his fist raised and his whole body fighting the urge to throw a piece of furniture at the woodwork.
"Infuriating," he growled under his breath, turning around and trudging back toward the parlor.
"Rich people are completely unhinged."

He collapsed into the empty armchair beside Valerius, leaned back until his head rested against the leather, and stared up at the ceiling molding while the faint sounds of clattering metal began to echo from the kitchen.
Now it was just the two of them.
The morning sun climbed higher and cast broad golden rectangles across the Persian rug.
The silence between the two young men was comfortable, born of having stood back-to-back beneath collapsing ice while horrors clawed at their shields.
Silas reached down, picked up a half-empty glass of cold water from the side table, and took a slow sip.
"So," he said, his voice returning to its normal, steady pitch.
"How’s the family?
How’s Lohan holding up?
What about Mia too?"
Valerius let out a long groan and threw his head back against the cushions until his golden hair spilled over the top.
"Don’t get me started, man," he sighed, dragging both hands down his face.
"My old man has been riding my ass non-stop since the Secret Realm collapsed...
Every single morning it’s ledgers, contracts, quarterly yield projections...
The man treats my existence like an underperforming branch office."
"Still pushing trade agreements?"
"Worse," Valerius muttered, rolling his neck until the joints popped.
"You remember the Grand Assembly?

Well you weren’t there but I was, The Sterling Conglomerate just closed the Tsardom of Borealis deal so now ten automated heavy-munitions foundries along the northern railway corridor, standardized artillery, mana-core casings, and void-iron penetrators, are all underwritten by us, with replenishment times cut by sixty percent...
In exchange, we get an exclusive fifteen-year concession on the raw titanium and unrefined void-iron out of the newly stabilized northern trench sectors."
Silas raised an eyebrow.
"How did the Tsar take it?"
"Volkov slammed his fist on the table and said yes before my father finished the sentence," Valerius said, with a grin he couldn’t quite suppress.
"He’s sick to death of Columbian shells jamming in his cannon breeches because some pinstripe bureaucrat shaved an eighth of an inch off the brass to save a few credits...
We walked out with the monopoly and a military alliance with Borealis in under five minutes and President Vanderbilt looked like he was going to burst a vein."
"I would have paid good money to see that."
"It was beautiful," Valerius sighed.
"And now my father has the whole corporate structure on twenty-four-hour rotations to get the foundry sites and the transport convoys ready...
I haven’t slept more than four hours a night all week and it isn’t just us but the whole Council sector is buzzing."
Silas raised an eyebrow.
"House Bloom too?"
"Yeah," Valerius nodded, glancing toward the closed kitchen door.
"Matriarch Bloom won the three coastal mining sectors in the southern gulf...

Albion’s Prime Minister threw a huge scene, because those sectors sit right on his trade route, but she pointed out that his navy can’t keep sea-krakens and pirates off his own freighters, and Australis voted with her.
Now she’s hammering out patrol terms with Albion, and Sera’s getting dragged into the negotiations next week to represent the younger lineage.
Her mother’s grooming her for a council seat, so she’s been swamped with legal briefs and diplomatic protocol."
He let out a quiet chuckle and his golden eyes softened.
"It’s been completely hectic for both of us.
But... well, after the desert, after everything that happened down in the dark, we both wanted to come see you.
Make sure you were actually breathing and not buried under some mountain of paperwork or something, Oh and Mia’s doing alright...
She wants us to meet up sometime and see Aeliana again."
Silas paused and looked at the blond giant beside him.
A quiet warmth settled into his chest.

In the cutthroat world of high-tier Awakened nobility, where every conversation was an exchange of leverage and every alliance had an expiration date, having people who simply showed up at your door because they wanted to verify you were alive was a rare precious commodity.
’Friends in the real world, huh?
Feels nice.’
Valerius turned his head to look straight at him.
The easygoing smirk on the blond scion’s face faded, replaced by a sudden awkward hesitation.
"Hey, Silas," he said, his voice dropping into a lower, more serious tone.
"We’re... friends, right?"
Silas blinked, caught off guard.
"Yeah?" He nodded with an easy shrug.
"Of course we’re friends.
We split that Guardian together in the Ititius Realm and you covered my back down in the dark.
That makes you solid in my book."
Valerius’s eyes widened, and then his expression shifted into one of aggrieved dramatic betrayal.
"Then why the hell don’t we have each other’s personal comm codes?!" he bellowed, leaning forward and throwing his hands into the air.
"We fought through an ancient god’s tomb together!
We survived a tectonic collapse and I had to track your damn residential address through my father’s corporate surveillance registry just to find out where you sleep at night!
Do you know how pathetic that feels?!"
Silas froze.
His eyes darted to the side, and a nervous sheepish laugh escaped his throat.
"Ah... ha ha... right.
That."
He reached into the pocket of his violet silk pajamas and pulled out his utilitarian smartphone.
"My bad," he admitted, tapping the screen to unlock the contacts menu.
"I’m not exactly great with social stuff, Half the time I forget the device is even charged."
"Unbelievable," Valerius grumbled, pulling a sleek state-of-the-art golden communicator from his vest pocket.
The two devices clicked softly as their proximity sensors engaged, exchanging secure frequencies and personal comm numbers in a flash of pale blue light.
Valerius pocketed his communicator and leaned back into the cushions with a triumphant satisfied nod.
A mischievous boyish grin spread across his handsome face.
"Alright," he said.
"Since we have a few minutes before the kitchen inevitably detonates into high-grade shrapnel... you play Lord of the Outer Rings?"
Silas looked up and raised an eyebrow.
"The mobile territorial strategy game?
The one with the micro-transactions and the base-building timers?"
"The very same," Valerius smirked, tapping his screen with rapid, practiced thumb strikes.
"I’ve got a Tier 4 fortress in Sector Seven...
My automated ballistas are tearing through the barbarian encampments.
Let’s run a co-op siege while the ladies burn your cookware."
Silas looked at the kitchen door, listened to the sound of something heavy and metallic falling onto the linoleum, and shrugged.
"Why not?" he said, booting up the application on his phone.
"Let’s see your setup."
