chapters.title: Chapter 660: Omelet [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: In theory, an omelet was one of the simplest culinary undertakings known to mortal civilization.
It required three ingredients... Eggs, butter, and heat.
A child in the lower districts could toss two cracked shells into an iron pan over dry wood and produce a serviceable fold of yellow curds before the kettle boiled.
"Haah..."

Both Harper and Seraphina had eaten hundreds of them, delicate pale golden crescents stuffed with smoked trout, shaved white truffles, or aged sharp cheddar, delivered on heated porcelain by soft-footed estate staff while the morning sun warmed the marble terraces of House Bloom and House Whitmore.
...Eating an omelet was an effortless delight.
Making one, as it turned out, was a world crisis.
For Seraphina Bloom, the kitchen of the Silverleaf residence was an alien dimension running on hostile physics.
She had never chopped a scallion and she had never operated a stove either.
In the high sanctuaries of the Bloom matriarchy, stepping into the scullery was something one did only if an assassin had poisoned the pantry or if one wished to inspect the cold-storage wards.
Her hands were made for balancing curved crimson daggers, weaving high-tier combustion spells, and signing multi-million-credit trade pacts with her signature.
Harper, at least, had familiarity.

During the darkest months of her childhood, when her father Collin was playing the doting patriarch while quietly orchestrating the slow poisoning of her core, she had sometimes sneaked down to the manor’s secondary scullery late at night to scramble an egg when the household staff had been dismissed.
But "scrambling an egg" in Harper’s dictionary meant poking a rubbery yellow puck with a fork until it stopped looking raw, dousing it in coarse salt, and choking it down while studying manuals.
She had never made a proper rolled omelet in her life.
...Yet here they were.
The phone rested against a glass jar of pickled peppercorns on the marble island, and Auntie Mae’s gentle motherly voice echoed through the quiet kitchen.

"Now, darlings, the secret to a fluffy, cloud-like texture is whisking with love! Add just a splash of whole milk, and when cutting your vegetables, remember... uniformity is key! A sharp knife does all the work for you!"
Harper pushed her wire-rimmed glasses up her nose, her violet eyes narrowing behind the lenses with analytical intensity.

"Uniformity," she whispered seriously, when she was very nervous... Harper had discovered that she had a knack for talking like a nerd. "She means a millimeter dimension... A deviation of more than zero-point-two millimeters in the diced shallots will result in uneven heat during the sauté."

"Obviously," Seraphina muttered, rolling the oversized sleeves of her white shirt past her elbows with grim determination. "Any novice knows variable surface area disrupts thermal transfer... Hand me the knife."
Fortunately for her, Harper didn’t judge.
Harper paused and cast a deeply skeptical sideways glance at the crimson-haired heiress.
"Do you even know which end to hold?"
"It has a blade and a handle, you condescending purple crow!" Seraphina snapped, snatching an eight-inch Damascus chef’s knife from the magnetic block on the wall.
She weighed it in her palm and the balance was completely wrong.
It lacked the rear-weighted pommel of her throwing daggers while the grip felt absurdly light.
"I shall handle the bell peppers and scallions," she declared haughtily, grabbing a glossy red pepper from the wire basket. "You prepare the poultry ova..."

"They are called eggs, Seraphina," Harper sighed, picking up a heavy ceramic mixing bowl and cracking her knuckles. "And try not to amputate your fingers, I have no desire to explain to Matriarch Etilga why her only daughter bled to death over a cutting board."
"Worry about your own limbs, Whitmore."
Seraphina slammed the red pepper onto the end-grain butcher block.
She raised the chef’s knife high above her shoulder with her red eyes locked on the vegetable with pure bloodlust.
SWISH-CHUNK!
The blade came down with enough force to cleave an armored goblin’s pauldron.
As for the vegetable... under the concussive pressure of a Purple Core who had completely forgotten how to hold back her strength, the vegetable detonated.
Watery red seeds and crushed pulp exploded across the counter and splattered the white tile backsplash.
Half the pepper ricocheted off the wall and landed in the sink with a wet thwack.
BANG!
The knife was buried three inches deep in the solid maple block, and the wood groaned in protest.
Seraphina froze.
Harper slowly turned her head as a single slimy red seed was stuck to the left lens of her glasses.
The only sound in the kitchen was Auntie Mae.
"—and remember to use a gentle rocking motion with your wrist—"
Harper reached up, pinched the seed off her spectacles, and flicked it onto the counter.
"Magnificent," she said, in a voice that could have dehydrated an ocean. "Truly exceptional technique... I believe the recipe called for diced peppers, not a spell bombardment."

"The cutting board had an uneven grain!" Seraphina hissed, her face burning crimson as she yanked at the handle, trying to wrench the steel out of the ruined wood. "The vegetable is obviously defective!"
"Of course it was," Harper muttered.
Refusing to be outdone by House Bloom’s catastrophic failure, the Head of House Whitmore turned to the carton of brown eggs.
She picked one up and cradled it in her slender pale fingers.
’Auntie Mae said tap firmly on a flat surface, then pry apart with the thumbs,’ she reviewed. ’It’s a bit simple.’
She brought the egg down on the marble counter.
Crack!
The shell gave with a crisp satisfying snap and Harper’s lips curved into a smug smirk as she held the egg over the bowl and pulled the halves apart.
Unfortunately, her idea of "minimum force" was still too much especially for a woman with over ten thousand mana points.
SQUELCH!
The egg was pulverized into a yellow-and-white slurry in her clenched fist.
Yolk squirted between her fingers, ran down her wrist, and soaked into the fine silk cuff of her violet pajama sleeve, while a dozen jagged brown shards rained into the bowl like gravel.
Harper’s smirk froze into a paralyzed grimace.
Across the island, Seraphina, who had finally wrenched the knife free of the butcher block with a loud creak, let out a sharp hysterical bark of laughter.
"Oh, brilliant!" she crowed, pointing the blade at Harper’s dripping hand. "Is that the legendary precision?! A calculation of eggshell extraction?! You look like you tried to strangle a canary!"

"I was testing the tensile strength of the shell!" Harper snarled, violet eyes flashing as static crackled along her pajama collar. "And at least my ingredient remained in the bowl, unlike your pepper, which is currently decorating the ceiling molding!"
"Shut up!"
"You shut up!"
Both girls glared at each other while breathing hard as their faces flushed with equal parts embarrassment and furious pride.
"Now, let’s get that skillet hot!" Auntie Mae chimed. "Add two tablespoons of butter and watch for that gentle sizzle!"
They looked down at the counter.
A cutting board covered in red mush, a bowl of pulverized yolk and jagged shell, a dripping silk sleeve and an oversized white shirt spattered with vegetable water.
Then they looked at the kitchen door.
On the other side, in the living room, Silas was chatting with Valerius, expecting two nobles to produce breakfast.
If they walked out with empty hands, or worse, if he walked in and found them standing in three hundred credits of ruined produce, they would never live it down.
Harper could never tease him about domestic hospitality again and Seraphina’s claim to be a worthy "prospective wife" would be laughed out of the hemisphere.
"Truce," Seraphina whispered with her voice sounding tight and trembling with desperate necessity.
"Agreed," Harper said through clenched teeth. "We do not speak of this."
"We’ll call it Operation Omelet," Seraphina said, she liked the name... after all, she had heard it in a movie.
"We are not naming it."
"It has a name now."
With unspoken coordination, they went to work.
Harper pulled a fine-mesh tea strainer out of a drawer and began sifting eggshell from the bowl with a silver spoon, like an archaeologist excavating fossils.
Seraphina abandoned the chef’s knife, drew her curved crimson throwing dagger from her belt and sliced the remaining scallions with the precision of an assassin carving an artery.
The green rings fell in perfect paper-thin sheets.
"Why does that look so terrifying?" Harper murmured.
"It’s an assassination technique... Not like you’d know."
"On a scallion, really? Isn’t that too much?"
Sera fell silent and grinned.
"...On a scallion that did not see me coming."
Next they got a fresh bowl and fresh eggs too.
’I’ll buy some more before I leave... so Martha won’t get suspicious.’
Harper took a breath and tapped a new one against the counter with the delicacy of a woman defusing a bomb and the shell split cleanly.
CRACK!
’Good...’
She opened it and it split into two halves as the yolk dropped into the bowl whole.
For three whole seconds she just stared at it.
"I did it..." she whispered.
"It’s an egg, you don’t need to look so happy."
"I’ve never cracked an egg before."
Sera wanted to insult her for it, but she too had never cracked an egg open before though she did know how to crack a skull.
"Auntie Mae says some people separate the yolks from the whites," Seraphina said, frowning at the screen. "Why would anyone separate them? They’re already together..."
"It’s for a different recipe."
"Then why is she telling us?"
"BECAUSE SHE IS TRYING TO RUIN US," Harper whispered fiercely.
Auntie Mae continued.
"—and don’t worry if you break the yolk! It happens to everyone!"
"Heh, we’re going to forget all about that..." Harper said as she looked down.
Her thumb had somehow found its way through the yolk and she put the egg down very slowly.
The video froze as a banner slid across the screen.
[This video is sponsored by Mothers’ Choice Cast Iron. Skip ad in 5...]
’Why isn’t this bitch using Lordtube Premium?!’
"Skip it," Seraphina said. "Skip! Skip!"
"I’m trying!"
"HOW DO YOU TURN THIS OFF?"
"It’s five seconds! You can’t turn off the five seconds!"
They stood motionless, staring at the screen, while a cheerful narrator described the many wonders of seasoned cast iron.
"...Mothers’ Choice," Seraphina muttered with dead eyes, she wanted to punch the phone. "Order yours today."
"Skip," Harper whispered, and at last the ad vanished.
"Whisk," Seraphina ordered, dumping the scallions into the bowl.
"I am whisking," Harper said with her arm moving in a mechanical blur as the balloon whisk whipped the eggs into a pale yellow vortex. "A splash of milk... Hand me the carton."
"Too much milk will cause the curds to separate during coagulation!"
"Auntie Mae said one tablespoon!"
"Auntie Mae is an unawakened human who cooks on regular stoves!"
"It is an induction stove, Seraphina," Harper said, lowering her voice in the tone of a woman explaining to a child why the sun does not go to sleep. "Do not touch the flame...? There is no flame..."
"I know what induction is!"
"Do you?"
Seraphina glared at the dial.
"...It’s like fire, but sneaky."
Harper rolled her eyes.
’Mind you, she’s a mage that uses fire... How bad does it have to be?’ Harper thought.
"Step away from the heat."
"I’m a Bloom! Heat is my domain!"
"Then stand there and judge the temperature with your hand, and do not touch the controls."
That, strangely enough, worked.
Seraphina held her palm an inch above the cold skillet and closed her eyes.
Her fire sense, honed since the age of six, hummed through her fingers as Harper turned the dial to the notch Auntie Mae called "medium-low."
...Nothing happened for a moment then the surface began to warm.
"Higher," Seraphina murmured.
Click!
"Not that high."
Click!
"...There."
She held out her hand like a conductor stopping an orchestra as Harper took her fingers off the dial.
"Next is the butter," Seraphina commanded. "We’re using half an ounce... Not a block, you savage..."
"I wasn’t going to use a block." Harper’s voice trailed off. "...Maybe I was."
"Bitch, you were looking at the block."
"I was admiring the block, you red haired bitch."
Harper cut a tidy knob of butter and slid it into the pan.
It melted at once, sighed into a pale golden pool, and began to foam softly at the edges, exactly like the video.
The two of them stared at the pan in reverent silence.

Harper wiped a smudge of soot from her cheek with the back of her violet silk sleeve and adjusted her glasses with unshakable dignity.

sentences.text: In theory, an omelet was one of the simplest culinary undertakings known to mortal civilization.
It required three ingredients...
Eggs, butter, and heat.
A child in the lower districts could toss two cracked shells into an iron pan over dry wood and produce a serviceable fold of yellow curds before the kettle boiled.
"Haah..."

Both Harper and Seraphina had eaten hundreds of them, delicate pale golden crescents stuffed with smoked trout, shaved white truffles, or aged sharp cheddar, delivered on heated porcelain by soft-footed estate staff while the morning sun warmed the marble terraces of House Bloom and House Whitmore.
...Eating an omelet was an effortless delight.
Making one, as it turned out, was a world crisis.
For Seraphina Bloom, the kitchen of the Silverleaf residence was an alien dimension running on hostile physics.
She had never chopped a scallion and she had never operated a stove either.
In the high sanctuaries of the Bloom matriarchy, stepping into the scullery was something one did only if an assassin had poisoned the pantry or if one wished to inspect the cold-storage wards.
Her hands were made for balancing curved crimson daggers, weaving high-tier combustion spells, and signing multi-million-credit trade pacts with her signature.
Harper, at least, had familiarity.

During the darkest months of her childhood, when her father Collin was playing the doting patriarch while quietly orchestrating the slow poisoning of her core, she had sometimes sneaked down to the manor’s secondary scullery late at night to scramble an egg when the household staff had been dismissed.
But "scrambling an egg" in Harper’s dictionary meant poking a rubbery yellow puck with a fork until it stopped looking raw, dousing it in coarse salt, and choking it down while studying manuals.
She had never made a proper rolled omelet in her life.
...Yet here they were.
The phone rested against a glass jar of pickled peppercorns on the marble island, and Auntie Mae’s gentle motherly voice echoed through the quiet kitchen.
"Now, darlings, the secret to a fluffy, cloud-like texture is whisking with love!
Add just a splash of whole milk, and when cutting your vegetables, remember... uniformity is key!
A sharp knife does all the work for you!"
Harper pushed her wire-rimmed glasses up her nose, her violet eyes narrowing behind the lenses with analytical intensity.
"Uniformity," she whispered seriously, when she was very nervous...
Harper had discovered that she had a knack for talking like a nerd.
"She means a millimeter dimension...
A deviation of more than zero-point-two millimeters in the diced shallots will result in uneven heat during the sauté."
"Obviously," Seraphina muttered, rolling the oversized sleeves of her white shirt past her elbows with grim determination.
"Any novice knows variable surface area disrupts thermal transfer...
Hand me the knife."
Fortunately for her, Harper didn’t judge.
Harper paused and cast a deeply skeptical sideways glance at the crimson-haired heiress.
"Do you even know which end to hold?"
"It has a blade and a handle, you condescending purple crow!" Seraphina snapped, snatching an eight-inch Damascus chef’s knife from the magnetic block on the wall.
She weighed it in her palm and the balance was completely wrong.
It lacked the rear-weighted pommel of her throwing daggers while the grip felt absurdly light.
"I shall handle the bell peppers and scallions," she declared haughtily, grabbing a glossy red pepper from the wire basket.
"You prepare the poultry ova..."
"They are called eggs, Seraphina," Harper sighed, picking up a heavy ceramic mixing bowl and cracking her knuckles.
"And try not to amputate your fingers, I have no desire to explain to Matriarch Etilga why her only daughter bled to death over a cutting board."
"Worry about your own limbs, Whitmore."
Seraphina slammed the red pepper onto the end-grain butcher block.
She raised the chef’s knife high above her shoulder with her red eyes locked on the vegetable with pure bloodlust.
SWISH-CHUNK!
The blade came down with enough force to cleave an armored goblin’s pauldron.
As for the vegetable... under the concussive pressure of a Purple Core who had completely forgotten how to hold back her strength, the vegetable detonated.
Watery red seeds and crushed pulp exploded across the counter and splattered the white tile backsplash.
Half the pepper ricocheted off the wall and landed in the sink with a wet thwack.
BANG!
The knife was buried three inches deep in the solid maple block, and the wood groaned in protest.
Seraphina froze.
Harper slowly turned her head as a single slimy red seed was stuck to the left lens of her glasses.
The only sound in the kitchen was Auntie Mae.
"—and remember to use a gentle rocking motion with your wrist—"
Harper reached up, pinched the seed off her spectacles, and flicked it onto the counter.
"Magnificent," she said, in a voice that could have dehydrated an ocean.
"Truly exceptional technique...
I believe the recipe called for diced peppers, not a spell bombardment."
"The cutting board had an uneven grain!" Seraphina hissed, her face burning crimson as she yanked at the handle, trying to wrench the steel out of the ruined wood.
"The vegetable is obviously defective!"
"Of course it was," Harper muttered.
Refusing to be outdone by House Bloom’s catastrophic failure, the Head of House Whitmore turned to the carton of brown eggs.
She picked one up and cradled it in her slender pale fingers.
’Auntie Mae said tap firmly on a flat surface, then pry apart with the thumbs,’ she reviewed. ’It’s a bit simple.’
She brought the egg down on the marble counter.
Crack!
The shell gave with a crisp satisfying snap and Harper’s lips curved into a smug smirk as she held the egg over the bowl and pulled the halves apart.
Unfortunately, her idea of "minimum force" was still too much especially for a woman with over ten thousand mana points.
SQUELCH!
The egg was pulverized into a yellow-and-white slurry in her clenched fist.
Yolk squirted between her fingers, ran down her wrist, and soaked into the fine silk cuff of her violet pajama sleeve, while a dozen jagged brown shards rained into the bowl like gravel.
Harper’s smirk froze into a paralyzed grimace.
Across the island, Seraphina, who had finally wrenched the knife free of the butcher block with a loud creak, let out a sharp hysterical bark of laughter.
"Oh, brilliant!" she crowed, pointing the blade at Harper’s dripping hand.
"Is that the legendary precision?!
A calculation of eggshell extraction?!
You look like you tried to strangle a canary!"
"I was testing the tensile strength of the shell!" Harper snarled, violet eyes flashing as static crackled along her pajama collar.
"And at least my ingredient remained in the bowl, unlike your pepper, which is currently decorating the ceiling molding!"
"Shut up!"
"You shut up!"
Both girls glared at each other while breathing hard as their faces flushed with equal parts embarrassment and furious pride.
"Now, let’s get that skillet hot!" Auntie Mae chimed.
"Add two tablespoons of butter and watch for that gentle sizzle!"
They looked down at the counter.
A cutting board covered in red mush, a bowl of pulverized yolk and jagged shell, a dripping silk sleeve and an oversized white shirt spattered with vegetable water.
Then they looked at the kitchen door.
On the other side, in the living room, Silas was chatting with Valerius, expecting two nobles to produce breakfast.
If they walked out with empty hands, or worse, if he walked in and found them standing in three hundred credits of ruined produce, they would never live it down.
Harper could never tease him about domestic hospitality again and Seraphina’s claim to be a worthy "prospective wife" would be laughed out of the hemisphere.
"Truce," Seraphina whispered with her voice sounding tight and trembling with desperate necessity.
"Agreed," Harper said through clenched teeth.
"We do not speak of this."
"We’ll call it Operation Omelet," Seraphina said, she liked the name... after all, she had heard it in a movie.
"We are not naming it."
"It has a name now."
With unspoken coordination, they went to work.
Harper pulled a fine-mesh tea strainer out of a drawer and began sifting eggshell from the bowl with a silver spoon, like an archaeologist excavating fossils.
Seraphina abandoned the chef’s knife, drew her curved crimson throwing dagger from her belt and sliced the remaining scallions with the precision of an assassin carving an artery.
The green rings fell in perfect paper-thin sheets.
"Why does that look so terrifying?" Harper murmured.
"It’s an assassination technique...
Not like you’d know."
"On a scallion, really?
Isn’t that too much?"
Sera fell silent and grinned.
"...On a scallion that did not see me coming."
Next they got a fresh bowl and fresh eggs too.
’I’ll buy some more before I leave... so Martha won’t get suspicious.’
Harper took a breath and tapped a new one against the counter with the delicacy of a woman defusing a bomb and the shell split cleanly.
CRACK!
’Good...’
She opened it and it split into two halves as the yolk dropped into the bowl whole.
For three whole seconds she just stared at it.
"I did it..." she whispered.
"It’s an egg, you don’t need to look so happy."
"I’ve never cracked an egg before."
Sera wanted to insult her for it, but she too had never cracked an egg open before though she did know how to crack a skull.
"Auntie Mae says some people separate the yolks from the whites," Seraphina said, frowning at the screen.
"Why would anyone separate them?
They’re already together..."
"It’s for a different recipe."
"Then why is she telling us?"
"BECAUSE SHE IS TRYING TO RUIN US," Harper whispered fiercely.
Auntie Mae continued.
"—and don’t worry if you break the yolk!
It happens to everyone!"
"Heh, we’re going to forget all about that..." Harper said as she looked down.
Her thumb had somehow found its way through the yolk and she put the egg down very slowly.
The video froze as a banner slid across the screen.
[This video is sponsored by Mothers’ Choice Cast Iron.
Skip ad in 5...]
’Why isn’t this bitch using Lordtube Premium?!’
"Skip it," Seraphina said.
"Skip!
Skip!"
"I’m trying!"
"HOW DO YOU TURN THIS OFF?"
"It’s five seconds!
You can’t turn off the five seconds!"
They stood motionless, staring at the screen, while a cheerful narrator described the many wonders of seasoned cast iron.
"...Mothers’ Choice," Seraphina muttered with dead eyes, she wanted to punch the phone.
"Order yours today."
"Skip," Harper whispered, and at last the ad vanished.
"Whisk," Seraphina ordered, dumping the scallions into the bowl.
"I am whisking," Harper said with her arm moving in a mechanical blur as the balloon whisk whipped the eggs into a pale yellow vortex.
"A splash of milk...
Hand me the carton."
"Too much milk will cause the curds to separate during coagulation!"
"Auntie Mae said one tablespoon!"
"Auntie Mae is an unawakened human who cooks on regular stoves!"
"It is an induction stove, Seraphina," Harper said, lowering her voice in the tone of a woman explaining to a child why the sun does not go to sleep.
"Do not touch the flame...?
There is no flame..."
"I know what induction is!"
"Do you?"
Seraphina glared at the dial.
"...It’s like fire, but sneaky."
Harper rolled her eyes.
’Mind you, she’s a mage that uses fire...
How bad does it have to be?’ Harper thought.
"Step away from the heat."
"I’m a Bloom!
Heat is my domain!"
"Then stand there and judge the temperature with your hand, and do not touch the controls."
That, strangely enough, worked.
Seraphina held her palm an inch above the cold skillet and closed her eyes.
Her fire sense, honed since the age of six, hummed through her fingers as Harper turned the dial to the notch Auntie Mae called "medium-low."
...Nothing happened for a moment then the surface began to warm.
"Higher," Seraphina murmured.
Click!
"Not that high."
Click!
"...There."
She held out her hand like a conductor stopping an orchestra as Harper took her fingers off the dial.
"Next is the butter," Seraphina commanded.
"We’re using half an ounce...
Not a block, you savage..."

chapters.title: Chapter 661: Sera’s Proposal [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: In the living room, the atmosphere was vastly more relaxed.
Silas sat sunk deep in the leather armchair with his bare feet propped on the cedar coffee table with his smartphone held between both hands.
Beside him, Valerius was leaning forward on the sofa with his golden hair catching the morning light and his thumbs tapping his sleek communicator speedily.
"VICTORY!" A deep booming orchestral fanfare blasted from Valerius’s speakers.
A gilded banner flashed across the screen.
[OPPOSING CITADEL CAPTURED! ALLIED FORCES ROUTED!]

"YES!" Valerius bellowed, throwing both arms into the air and laughing like a lunatic. "Down goes the Graves garrison! How’s that for strategy, Silas?! My floating Thunder Bastion tore your eastern ramparts into toothpicks, and Sir Gawain took your gate in four seconds flat...! Do you know how hard it is to summon a Knight of the Round Table?! It took me three weeks and a prayer!"
Silas stared at his own screen, where the words [DEFEAT: CITADEL RAZED] were pulsing in mocking crimson.
He slowly lowered the phone and turned a flat, deadpan glare on the blond scion.
"Valerius," he said, entirely without warmth. "You didn’t ’maneuver’ anything."
"I took the high ground!"

"You spent a hundred thousand Spirit Credits on the full thing," Silas said, tapping the battle log. "You bought three Tier 5 Divine Aegis shields, summoned a Round Table knight that isn’t even available on the standard servers yet, hovered a floating bastion over my palisade, and dropped an orbital mana-strike on my walls... You are a shameless pay-to-win dairy cow."
Silas used to play the game before he awakened so he wasn’t around recently, still he shouldn’t have lost so easily!
Valerius threw his head back and laughed, looking very unbothered.

"Hey, a win is a win!" he grinned, teeth flashing. "The game allowed the transaction, didn’t it? A true commander deploys every resource at his disposal! Capital is just another form of martial prowess, my friend!"
CREAK.
The kitchen’s swinging door opened and both men turned.
Marching out of the hallway like two decorated field marshals returning from a bloody campaign were Harper and Seraphina.

Harper carried a wide porcelain platter bearing two rolled omelets garnished with a fan of sliced sourdough, and Seraphina carried a ceramic pot of freshly brewed black tea and four small bowls of pickled radish.
Their appearances told a harrowing tale.
Harper’s violet pajama shirt was dusted with flour around the midsection with one cuff was soaked in egg white, and her hair clip hung slightly crooked.

Seraphina’s oversized white shirt had a prominent circular grease stain over her left ribs, a flake of black charcoal clung to her cheekbone, and her crimson hair looked like it had survived a minor hurricane.
Valerius blinked.
"Uh... did a grease fire break out in there?"
GLARE!
Seraphina’s red eyes snapped toward him and the temperature in the parlor dropped twenty degrees.
A wave of concentrated heat rolled off her, silently promising that if another syllable about her appearance left his lips, his next training spar would be conducted inside an active volcano.
Valerius’s survival instincts, honed by years of dealing with the Bloom heiress, fired with breathtaking speed.

"I mean—!" He snapped his face into a wide dazzling smile of shameless adulation. "What an incredible aesthetic! Look at that golden-brown coloration on the crust! That is the mark of pan-searing that only a World class chef would be able to produce! Only a prodigy could achieve such artisanal caramelization!"
’Isn’t the glaze a bit too much...?’
Seraphina sniffed, her chin lifting slightly as she set the tea tray down with a smug clack.
"Naturally... A refined palate recognizes true technique."
Harper set the platter between Silas and Valerius, sat on the sofa beside the blond scion, and folded her hands neatly in her lap.
"Eat," she said softly, though her violet eyes darted toward Silas’s face with quiet and barely concealed nervousness. "We prepared them to ensure your daily calories are maintained."
Silas looked down at the two omelets.
They were... lumpy.

One was slightly flatter than the other, as if it had been aggressively squashed by a blunt instrument, and the second had a distinct brown scorch mark along its spine that strongly resembled a tire tread.
He picked up a fork, sliced a generous portion off each, and lifted it to his mouth under the laser-focused unblinking scrutiny of the noblewomen that watched him.
He chewed.
The salt was uneven, one bite was completely bland, and the next had a saline punch that made his jaw tighten.
The texture was half velvety and there was an unmistakable undertone of burnt butter on the roof of his mouth.
’Truly they don’t know how to cook at all...’
He swallowed.
"Well?" Seraphina demanded, leaning over the back of the sofa with her face inches from his ear. "It’s exceptional, isn’t it? You’ve never tasted anything so complex."
Silas reached for his water glass and took a slow deliberate sip.
"I like it," he said honestly with a smirk. "It’s warm and it has protein."
Harper let out a quiet breath, and her shoulders visibly relaxed.

"However," Silas continued, pointing his fork at the scorch mark, "this side tastes like it was held over an exhaust pipe and this half has enough salt to cure a side of beef... For two geniuses who claim to understand thermodynamics and agriculture, you really have no idea how to make a basic three-minute omelet, do you?"
SMACK!
Seraphina’s palm came down hard on the back of his head.
"Ow!" Silas yelped, rubbing the spot with a scowl. "What was that for?!"

"Ungrateful brute!" she fumed, cheeks bright red as she stomped her loafer on the Persian rug. "We slaved over that scorching element for twenty minutes... We diced scallions to the millimeter! You should be writing us formal letters of appreciation, not offering unsolicited restaurant critiques!"
"I’m just saying, Martha doesn’t burn the butter," Silas muttered, taking another bite anyway.
Despite the flaws, it wasn’t terrible, and having two terrifyingly powerful women bicker over cooking for him had a strange absurd charm he couldn’t hate.
Valerius was already devouring his half with hollow-legged enthusiasm, nodding around a mouthful of egg and bread.
"Actually pretty damn good with the tea! Pass the pickled radish, Silas!"
The tension in the room dissolved into the soft sounds of breakfast.
Sun poured through the high windows, warming the leather and wood, and the easy banter of young people who had briefly escaped the weight of their bloodlines filled the hall.
Silas finished his portion, leaned back in the armchair with a contented sigh, and reached up to unbutton the top of his violet pajamas so his neck could breathe.
Chink!
A metallic chime sounded as a piece of jewelry slipped out from beneath the silk.
Resting against Silas’s collarbone was a heavy dark chain with a light-devouring void-chrysolite stone carved with microscopic runes, held by a silver clasp.
Seraphina paused.
She had been reaching for the teapot with her red eyes casually tracking Silas’s movements.
The instant the dark stone caught the morning light, her fingers froze around the porcelain handle.
Her pupils contracted to sharp pinpricks.
’Ah... I almost forgot.’
The flustered petulance vanished from her face as her spine snapped straight, and her jaw set into the rigid terrifying line of an interrogator.
She put the teapot down without a sound.
"Silas," she said.
Her voice was flat and quiet and carried a sudden, chilling drop in temperature that made Valerius freeze with his fork halfway to his mouth.
Silas looked up.
"Yeah?"
She stepped around the coffee table and stopped in front of his chair.
Sera reached down, took the collar of his pajama shirt between two fingers, and pulled it down.
"Turn it over," she said.
"Sera—"
"Turn it over."
He turned the clasp.
On the back of the silver, so small a person would need to know where to look, were four tiny lines, scratched crookedly with a dagger point.

"I bought this for you on the double date with Harper," Seraphina said, her red eyes burning with an intense unblinking fire as she locked onto his pupils. "I made you promise never to take it off but I carved those four lines while you were looking the other way, so that if you ever lost it, I would know it was yours."
CLATTER!
Valerius’s fork slipped from his fingers, bounced off the porcelain plate, and rattled onto the cedar table.

"I saw it again at the Succession Exhibition," she went on. "On the collarbone of that woman named Kara White... or Vespera, The Gold core and you stood there in that crowd, smiling, with my four little lines on your neck."
She straightened and crossed her arms over her butter-stained shirt.
"So I’ll ask you a question, Silas. When were you planning on telling us that you are Vespera?"
Valerius made a strangled noise.

"V-V-Vespera?!" His golden eyes bulged out of his head with his gaze darting between Seraphina and Silas as though one of them had just pulled the pin on an antimatter grenade. "The Lord of Blessed Land?! The single-armed Lord who swept the leaderboards and even the Tournament of succession?! Silas... is Vespera?!"
On the other side of the sofa, Harper didn’t drop her cutlery.
She sat perfectly still, hands in her lap with violet eyes widening slightly behind her glasses.
’She knew?’ Harper thought, a sharp spike of surprise tightening her chest. ’Since the Exhibition, huh? What exhibition?’
Harper had known Silas’s dual identity since the whole thing with Ititius, but she wasn’t being like this... Seraphina didn’t look at her however, her eyes stayed on Silas.

"You didn’t tell me," she said, more quietly. "I figured it out at the tournament I kept my mouth shut... I didn’t tell Valerius... I didn’t tell my mother... I waited... I thought, he’ll tell me when he trusts me enough..."
A muscle flickered in her jaw.
"You never did. I’m not angry about the secret, Silas. I understand secrets but you should have told me."
Silas didn’t panic.
He leaned his head back against the armchair and let out a long, heavy sigh through his nose.
’She’s sharp,’ he thought, fingers tapping his knee. ’Terrifyingly sharp.’
What had he expected? She was the heiress to a noble house.
She had spent her whole adolescence navigating Council politics, corporate espionage, and trade auctions where one overlooked detail could cost a dynasty millions.
’I really need to take the damn necklace off when I switch to the ring,’ he thought, with a dry grimace. ’What a rookie mistake.’
He ran down the mental roster.
Harper knew... Martha knew... Lia and the girls knew...
And now Seraphina Bloom and Valerius Sterling were in his living room, staring at his collarbone with the truth laid bare.
Silas took a slow breath, closed his eyes for two seconds, and opened them again, meeting Seraphina’s gaze.
’Whatever,’ he thought, with quiet resignation. ’It’s fine.’
Neither of them was an enemy.
They’d bled in the sand beside him... If his identity had to leak beyond Blessed Land, better that it rest with allies than with the hostile factions in the World Council.
"Alright," Silas said. "You caught me. I’m Vespera... Sorry for not telling you but I had my reasons."
Valerius let out a strangled, squeaking wheeze and slumped back onto the cushions like a deflated balloon.
"Holy shit man!"
So essentially Silas was cross-dressing as that hot woman...? So did that make him gay?
Harper pushed up her glasses with a proud smile touching her lips, and said nothing.
Seraphina stood in front of the chair as now that the secret was confirmed, the triumphant smirk faded.
The domestic absurdity of the burnt omelets, the grease stains on her shirt, the bickering, all of it seemed to evaporate from her frame.
Her red eyes ignited with a deep fire, and the temperature in the parlor surged as a dry crackling heat radiating off her skin as her Purple Core began to hum.
’I don’t want much...’
She leaned forward, rested one palm on the armrest, put her face inches from his as well.
"Good," she whispered, her eyes locked on his with fiery intensity. "I don’t give a damn about the politics, Silas... I don’t care about the Council, and I don’t care about the rankings..."
Her lips parted into a wild grin that sent a sharp chill down his spine.
"Right now... I want you to step out into the courtyard."
Her crimson dagger materialized in her palm with a metallic shing.
"And I want you to spar me at full power."

sentences.text: In the living room, the atmosphere was vastly more relaxed.
Silas sat sunk deep in the leather armchair with his bare feet propped on the cedar coffee table with his smartphone held between both hands.
Beside him, Valerius was leaning forward on the sofa with his golden hair catching the morning light and his thumbs tapping his sleek communicator speedily.
"VICTORY!" A deep booming orchestral fanfare blasted from Valerius’s speakers.
A gilded banner flashed across the screen.
[OPPOSING CITADEL CAPTURED!
ALLIED FORCES ROUTED!]
"YES!" Valerius bellowed, throwing both arms into the air and laughing like a lunatic.
"Down goes the Graves garrison!
How’s that for strategy, Silas?!
My floating Thunder Bastion tore your eastern ramparts into toothpicks, and Sir Gawain took your gate in four seconds flat...!
Do you know how hard it is to summon a Knight of the Round Table?!
It took me three weeks and a prayer!"
Silas stared at his own screen, where the words [DEFEAT: CITADEL RAZED] were pulsing in mocking crimson.
He slowly lowered the phone and turned a flat, deadpan glare on the blond scion.
"Valerius," he said, entirely without warmth.
"You didn’t ’maneuver’ anything."
"I took the high ground!"
"You spent a hundred thousand Spirit Credits on the full thing," Silas said, tapping the battle log.

"You bought three Tier 5 Divine Aegis shields, summoned a Round Table knight that isn’t even available on the standard servers yet, hovered a floating bastion over my palisade, and dropped an orbital mana-strike on my walls...
You are a shameless pay-to-win dairy cow."
Silas used to play the game before he awakened so he wasn’t around recently, still he shouldn’t have lost so easily!
Valerius threw his head back and laughed, looking very unbothered.
"Hey, a win is a win!" he grinned, teeth flashing.
"The game allowed the transaction, didn’t it?
A true commander deploys every resource at his disposal!
Capital is just another form of martial prowess, my friend!"
CREAK.
The kitchen’s swinging door opened and both men turned.
Marching out of the hallway like two decorated field marshals returning from a bloody campaign were Harper and Seraphina.

Harper carried a wide porcelain platter bearing two rolled omelets garnished with a fan of sliced sourdough, and Seraphina carried a ceramic pot of freshly brewed black tea and four small bowls of pickled radish.
Their appearances told a harrowing tale.
Harper’s violet pajama shirt was dusted with flour around the midsection with one cuff was soaked in egg white, and her hair clip hung slightly crooked.

Seraphina’s oversized white shirt had a prominent circular grease stain over her left ribs, a flake of black charcoal clung to her cheekbone, and her crimson hair looked like it had survived a minor hurricane.
Valerius blinked.
"Uh... did a grease fire break out in there?"
GLARE!
Seraphina’s red eyes snapped toward him and the temperature in the parlor dropped twenty degrees.
A wave of concentrated heat rolled off her, silently promising that if another syllable about her appearance left his lips, his next training spar would be conducted inside an active volcano.
Valerius’s survival instincts, honed by years of dealing with the Bloom heiress, fired with breathtaking speed.
"I mean—!" He snapped his face into a wide dazzling smile of shameless adulation.
"What an incredible aesthetic!
Look at that golden-brown coloration on the crust!
That is the mark of pan-searing that only a World class chef would be able to produce!
Only a prodigy could achieve such artisanal caramelization!"
’Isn’t the glaze a bit too much...?’
Seraphina sniffed, her chin lifting slightly as she set the tea tray down with a smug clack.
"Naturally...
A refined palate recognizes true technique."
Harper set the platter between Silas and Valerius, sat on the sofa beside the blond scion, and folded her hands neatly in her lap.
"Eat," she said softly, though her violet eyes darted toward Silas’s face with quiet and barely concealed nervousness.
"We prepared them to ensure your daily calories are maintained."
Silas looked down at the two omelets.
They were... lumpy.

One was slightly flatter than the other, as if it had been aggressively squashed by a blunt instrument, and the second had a distinct brown scorch mark along its spine that strongly resembled a tire tread.
He picked up a fork, sliced a generous portion off each, and lifted it to his mouth under the laser-focused unblinking scrutiny of the noblewomen that watched him.
He chewed.
The salt was uneven, one bite was completely bland, and the next had a saline punch that made his jaw tighten.
The texture was half velvety and there was an unmistakable undertone of burnt butter on the roof of his mouth.
’Truly they don’t know how to cook at all...’
He swallowed.
"Well?" Seraphina demanded, leaning over the back of the sofa with her face inches from his ear.
"It’s exceptional, isn’t it?
You’ve never tasted anything so complex."
Silas reached for his water glass and took a slow deliberate sip.
"I like it," he said honestly with a smirk.
"It’s warm and it has protein."
Harper let out a quiet breath, and her shoulders visibly relaxed.
"However," Silas continued, pointing his fork at the scorch mark, "this side tastes like it was held over an exhaust pipe and this half has enough salt to cure a side of beef...
For two geniuses who claim to understand thermodynamics and agriculture, you really have no idea how to make a basic three-minute omelet, do you?"
SMACK!
Seraphina’s palm came down hard on the back of his head.
"Ow!" Silas yelped, rubbing the spot with a scowl.
"What was that for?!"
"Ungrateful brute!" she fumed, cheeks bright red as she stomped her loafer on the Persian rug.
"We slaved over that scorching element for twenty minutes...
We diced scallions to the millimeter!
You should be writing us formal letters of appreciation, not offering unsolicited restaurant critiques!"
"I’m just saying, Martha doesn’t burn the butter," Silas muttered, taking another bite anyway.
Despite the flaws, it wasn’t terrible, and having two terrifyingly powerful women bicker over cooking for him had a strange absurd charm he couldn’t hate.
Valerius was already devouring his half with hollow-legged enthusiasm, nodding around a mouthful of egg and bread.
"Actually pretty damn good with the tea!
Pass the pickled radish, Silas!"
The tension in the room dissolved into the soft sounds of breakfast.
Sun poured through the high windows, warming the leather and wood, and the easy banter of young people who had briefly escaped the weight of their bloodlines filled the hall.
Silas finished his portion, leaned back in the armchair with a contented sigh, and reached up to unbutton the top of his violet pajamas so his neck could breathe.
Chink!
A metallic chime sounded as a piece of jewelry slipped out from beneath the silk.
Resting against Silas’s collarbone was a heavy dark chain with a light-devouring void-chrysolite stone carved with microscopic runes, held by a silver clasp.
Seraphina paused.
She had been reaching for the teapot with her red eyes casually tracking Silas’s movements.
The instant the dark stone caught the morning light, her fingers froze around the porcelain handle.
Her pupils contracted to sharp pinpricks.
I almost forgot.’
The flustered petulance vanished from her face as her spine snapped straight, and her jaw set into the rigid terrifying line of an interrogator.
She put the teapot down without a sound.
"Silas," she said.
Her voice was flat and quiet and carried a sudden, chilling drop in temperature that made Valerius freeze with his fork halfway to his mouth.
Silas looked up.
"Yeah?"
She stepped around the coffee table and stopped in front of his chair.
Sera reached down, took the collar of his pajama shirt between two fingers, and pulled it down.
"Turn it over," she said.
"Sera—"
"Turn it over."
He turned the clasp.
On the back of the silver, so small a person would need to know where to look, were four tiny lines, scratched crookedly with a dagger point.
"I bought this for you on the double date with Harper," Seraphina said, her red eyes burning with an intense unblinking fire as she locked onto his pupils.
"I made you promise never to take it off but I carved those four lines while you were looking the other way, so that if you ever lost it, I would know it was yours."
CLATTER!
Valerius’s fork slipped from his fingers, bounced off the porcelain plate, and rattled onto the cedar table.
"I saw it again at the Succession Exhibition," she went on.
"On the collarbone of that woman named Kara White... or Vespera, The Gold core and you stood there in that crowd, smiling, with my four little lines on your neck."
She straightened and crossed her arms over her butter-stained shirt.
"So I’ll ask you a question, Silas.
When were you planning on telling us that you are Vespera?"
Valerius made a strangled noise.
"V-V-Vespera?!" His golden eyes bulged out of his head with his gaze darting between Seraphina and Silas as though one of them had just pulled the pin on an antimatter grenade.
"The Lord of Blessed Land?!
The single-armed Lord who swept the leaderboards and even the Tournament of succession?!
Silas... is Vespera?!"
On the other side of the sofa, Harper didn’t drop her cutlery.
She sat perfectly still, hands in her lap with violet eyes widening slightly behind her glasses.
’She knew?’ Harper thought, a sharp spike of surprise tightening her chest. ’Since the Exhibition, huh?
What exhibition?’
Harper had known Silas’s dual identity since the whole thing with Ititius, but she wasn’t being like this...
Seraphina didn’t look at her however, her eyes stayed on Silas.
"You didn’t tell me," she said, more quietly.
"I figured it out at the tournament I kept my mouth shut...
I didn’t tell Valerius...
I didn’t tell my mother...
I waited...
I thought, he’ll tell me when he trusts me enough..."
A muscle flickered in her jaw.
"You never did.
I’m not angry about the secret, Silas.
I understand secrets but you should have told me."
Silas didn’t panic.
He leaned his head back against the armchair and let out a long, heavy sigh through his nose.
’She’s sharp,’ he thought, fingers tapping his knee. ’Terrifyingly sharp.’
What had he expected?
She was the heiress to a noble house.
She had spent her whole adolescence navigating Council politics, corporate espionage, and trade auctions where one overlooked detail could cost a dynasty millions.
’I really need to take the damn necklace off when I switch to the ring,’ he thought, with a dry grimace. ’What a rookie mistake.’
He ran down the mental roster.
Harper knew...
Martha knew...
Lia and the girls knew...
And now Seraphina Bloom and Valerius Sterling were in his living room, staring at his collarbone with the truth laid bare.
Silas took a slow breath, closed his eyes for two seconds, and opened them again, meeting Seraphina’s gaze.
’Whatever,’ he thought, with quiet resignation. ’It’s fine.’
Neither of them was an enemy.
They’d bled in the sand beside him...
If his identity had to leak beyond Blessed Land, better that it rest with allies than with the hostile factions in the World Council.
"Alright," Silas said.

Sorry for not telling you but I had my reasons."

I want you to step out into the courtyard."

chapters.title: Chapter 662: What A Scary Woman [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Silas blinked.

He lowered his ceramic teacup back onto its hand-carved cedar saucer with a slow deliberate clink, staring at the fiery-haired heiress standing in the middle of his living room rug as if she had just declared her intention to commit a war crime.
"A spar?" Silas echoed, his brow creasing into deep incredulous ridges. "Right now? In pajamas?"
"Yes, obviously!" Seraphina snapped.
She crossed her arms beneath her bust with aggressive authority.
The motion caused the hem of her oversized white button-down shirt to billow around her hips, and with that subtle shift in posture... a swell of heat surged outward.
The draft was so dry, so intensely concentrated, that the varnished edges of Silas’s low cedar coffee table gave a protesting crackle with the air warping around her slippers in a shimmering mirage.

"You are my prospective husband, Silas!" Seraphina continued, her voice rising in a sharp melodic tone that filled the vaulted ceiling of the parlor. "Do you honestly expect me to simply accept rumors, secondhand intelligence dossiers, and tournament gossip regarding your foundation? A Gold Core..."
Her red eyes flashed with a razor-thin glint of predatory hunger, tracking the rise and fall of his chest like a raptor measuring the wind before diving on prey.

"I want to feel the weight of it myself," she purred, her chin lifting with royal unshakeable confidence. "I want to see if that spine of yours can actually hold up that ridiculous reputation, or if you’re merely an inflated paper tiger that got lucky."
Of course she knew he was strong but would he be able to use that against her...? If he beat her up... It made her wet just thinking about it.
She stepped forward, closing the distance between them until the toes of her soft indoor slippers lightly nudged the toe of his.
She leaned down, bringing her face inches from his with her scent completely enveloping him.
"And if you manage to beat me," she whispered, her voice dropping into a teasing hush that made the tiny hairs along the nape of his neck prickle with electric static, "you get a reward."
Silas raised an eyebrow, his expression entirely deadpan. "What kind of reward?"

The confident predatory swagger instantly short-circuited as a violent shade of vermilion detonated across the high planes of Seraphina’s cheekbones, racing with terrifying speed straight to the tips of her ears and down the exposed pale expanse of her collarbones.
She jerked her chin away, snapping her spine straight with her teeth sinking hard into her lower lip until a bead of white-hot mana hissed against her skin.
Suddenly, she found the plaster crown moldings along the parlor ceiling endlessly fascinating.
"T-That is reserved for after the match!" She stammered.
Her fingers knotted into the cuffs of her oversized sleeves, tugging at the fabric. "Shut up and don’t ask stupid questions! Just get off the couch and fight me!"

"I’d rather not turn my front driveway into a smoking crater of vitrified asphalt," Silas muttered, leaning back against the leather cushions and glancing past her shoulder toward the front bay window.
On the other side of the low table, Harper sat with her ankles neatly crossed, in violet pajamas with little gold stars that matched his, cradling her teacup with a small content smile.
She had been in a good mood all morning as she pushed her wire-rimmed glasses up the bridge of her nose with one finger, humming softly into her tea.
Then she heard the word "fight" and the humming stopped.

"Excuse me?" Harper set her teacup down and pressed a hand to her chest like she’d been shot. "A spar? In pajamas? Sera, my Valkyrie is parked in that courtyard! It’s custom mythril, you barbarian! I know exactly what you’re planning... You want to throw your stupid fire around next to my car on purpose!"
She jabbed a finger at the heiress with her cheeks flushed and her eyes wide with wounded outrage.
"If you singe so much as one speck of clear coat, I will sue you! And your mother! And your entire stupid house!"
Seraphina’s lips peeled back into a wicked, feline grin.

"Oh? And what if I do, Whitmore?" Seraphina purred, her tone dripping with venomous amusement. "Are you going to draft an angry formal grievance with your little gold-plated lawyer quill? Or maybe file a three-part petition to the council? You talk like an accountant who got lost on a battlefield..."
Harper’s violet eyes narrowed into lethal dead slits.
A single microscopic grain of light-devouring black sand flickered into existence directly above her left knuckle.

It hung in the air, humming with an ominous vibration, and for a terrifying half-second, the morning light in the living room curved toward her fingers as though she were genuinely contemplating hurling a void straight through the center of Seraphina’s forehead.

"Enough," Silas groaned, pinching the bridge of his nose until his fingers went numb. "Both of you, sit down... There will be no fights in the courtyard. Harper’s interceptor and my car are parked out there, and the neighbors already give me enough looks... I’m not getting a complaint on top of it."

"Then we drive to an arena," Seraphina insisted, stamping her slipper against the parquet floor with a sharp concussive thwack that rattled the teacups. "Right now! We can take my convoy to the Bloom Clan’s secondary estate... Mother is currently in the city finalizing the diplomatic contracts with the Albion delegation—"
Beneath her scowl, however, her internal thoughts were settled.

’Yes... exactly that! We drive to the Bloom compound! I drag him into the central martial ring in front of Mother and the inner-circle elders! I’ll force him to limit himself to a single element so he doesn’t expose the Vespera persona to the public registry, and once he completely stonewalls my primary assault with that ridiculous Gold Core foundation, Mother won’t be able to say a single word against him... Those fossilized clan elders who keep whispering about arranged matches can swallow their own tongues! We’ll be engaged before autumn ends...’
Sera didn’t really care about much, she just wanted to show that he was good and get them engaged as soon as possible.
"Uh, hey. Before you two start drafting marriage annexes, measuring curtain fabrics, and booking courtrooms..."
Valerius’s deep cheerful voice cut smoothly through the brewing domestic squall.
The golden-haired scion leaned forward on the leather sofa, resting his forearms on his knees, reaching deep into the interior pocket of his charcoal vest.
With a dramatic flourish of his thick wrist, he produced a heavy, matte-black metallic cube roughly four inches across.
It was inlaid with intricate microscopic silver runes that bent the dust motes in the air around it into tiny swirling ellipses.
"What is that?" Silas asked, his blue eyes instantly locking onto the geometric rune patterns carved into the dark metal. "A cube that has space runes?"
"Better," Valerius grinned with his white teeth flashing as he tossed the heavy cube lightly from hand to hand.
The metal gave a dull thud against his palm.

"It’s a prototype isolation chamber... Sterling Technologies has been co-developing this with high-tier rune masters contracted directly from the Sovereign Realm, It essentially folds space into an artificial sub-pocket so basically, a self-contained mobile training arena that won’t leak a single drop of force, shockwaves or radiation into the real world."
Seraphina narrowed her eyes at it, her chin tilting up with pure disdain at her plan being foiled.
"It’s the size of a tea canister, Valerius. What are we supposed to do inside that? Spar with our pinky fingers?"
"Watch and learn, fiery," Valerius scoffed playfully.
He stood up, tapped a sequence of three silver nodes along the cube’s upper bevel, and underhanded it toward the center of the hardwood floor.
CLACK!
The moment the dark metal struck the floorboards, it didn’t bounce. It expanded.

The edges uncoupled with a series of heavy hydraulic hisses with the metal unfolding like an origami lotus forged from dark iron, rising, stretching, and warping the air until a freestanding eight-foot-tall obsidian archway stood solidly in the middle of Silas’s living room.
Within the frame of the arch, the air did not lead to the dining room as instead, it swirled with deep pale-gray mist.
Valerius stepped up, gesturing toward the gray mist like an enthusiastic shopkeeper presenting his finest wares.
"After you, contestants."
Silas raised an eyebrow, stepping through the archway first, with Harper and Seraphina following close behind.
The transition was seamless.
The moment they crossed the threshold, the ceiling of the Silverleaf residence vanished.
Silas looked up into an artificial vault stretching at least two hundred feet into the air, illuminated by glowing simulated starlight embedded in the high basalt dome.
Beneath their feet was a massive, reinforced combat platform paved with heavy mana-dampening granite slabs, easily the size of two full regulation football stadiums.
The colossal scale was completely invisible from the outside.
"Woah..." Harper murmured, pushing her glasses up as she scanned the perimeter runic baffles.
Her eyes were shining. "Wait... this is actually insane. You folded a whole stadium into a tea canister?! Valerius, how much do you want for it? I’m serious, name a price!"
Valerius laughed, rubbing the back of his golden neck.

"Not for sale yet, Harper! It’s still an unstable prototype... It took four high-rank mages six months just to stabilize the atmospheric pressure inside this one box so it won’t hit commercial production for at least five years."
He walked over toward the outer boundary line, leaning back against the raised observation railing, crossing his arms with an eager wolfish grin.

’Man...’ Valerius thought, his golden eyes sparkling with pure anticipation. ’Before I found out Silas was Vespera... I honestly thought he was just a solid prodigy around my level but seeing the shit he pulled in the tournament? Knowing he’s sitting on an actual Gold Core?’
He glanced between the two combatants taking their positions on the gray stone.

’Who do I even bet on?’ Valerius mused, a cold sweat breaking out on the back of his neck. ’Logically, Silas washes her... A Gold Core Lord is a walking natural disaster but if I say that out loud and Sera overhears me, she’ll turn my eyebrows into ash before the match even starts...’
Sixty paces away, Silas and Seraphina stood facing each other.
The air between them had already begun to thin with the temperature in the cube dropping into an eerie electric hush.
Seraphina reached behind her waist.
SHING!
With a clean, fluid flick of her wrists, the second of the curved daggers materialized in her grip.
The blades were forged from deep volcanic steel with their edges glowing with a dangerous orange shimmer that distorted the air around her fingers like a desert mirage.
She rolled her shoulders, shaking out the loose cuffs of her oversized white shirt, her red eyes locking onto Silas with ferocious focus.

"You better fight me with everything you have, Silas Graves," Seraphina warned, her voice dropping into a low breathless tone. "If you hold back because you think I’m fragile... if you treat me like a delicate little noble girl... I swear on my mother’s name, I will shatter every bone in your legs. You won’t walk for a month!"
Silas chuckled, reaching into his spatial storage.
Clink!
He didn’t draw the Dawn Blade.
It rested within his soul and drawing it in a domestic spar was equivalent to swinging a live artillery shell at someone’s forehead.
He wasn’t going to risk hurting Sera with it at all.
Instead, he withdrew a standard longsword forged from tempered mythril... It was a simple balanced weapon with a dark leather grip.
He rested the flat of the blade against his shoulder, looking at her with a lazy teasing smirk.
"Is that your idea of pillow talk, Sera? Threatening to cripple your future husband before the wedding?"
FWOOSH!
A sudden violent ring of bright red sparks ignited around Seraphina’s collarbones.
"SHUT UP!" she yelled, her face instantly turning the exact shade of a ripe strawberry as her embarrassment transformed instantly into explosive combustible fury. "DIE, YOU ARROGANT BASTARD!"
Across the ring, Silas’s posture relaxed, but his mind shifted into cold clarity.

’Well I should hold back a bit,’ Silas analyzed, feeling the thrum of his core circulating behind his ribs. ’If I start layering lightning, light, as well as all of the other spells I know, the spatial cube won’t hold the pressure.’
His blue eyes settled on the fiery girl across the stone.
’I’ll stick to water... Maybe a bit of wind for displacement. Let’s see how sharp House Bloom’s claws really are.’
Harper walked to the center line between them with her violet pajamas rustling in the rising heat.
She raised her right hand with her eyes flicking from one fighter to the other, and a little grin tugged at her mouth.

"Okay, rules!" Harper called, her voice bouncing off the basalt walls. "No hitting the head, no wrecking each other’s cores, and whoever gets knocked out of the ring or gives up loses... If either of you actually tries to kill the other, I’m stopping it. Got it?"
She glanced at Seraphina, then at Silas.
"And Sera, if you set the cube on fire, I’m telling Valerius you did it on purpose."
"HEY!" Valerius yelled from the railing.
She lowered her hand by half an inch.
"Three."
Seraphina lowered her center of gravity with the soles of her slippers grinding against the granite.
"Two."
Silas brought the sword forward, holding it in a low loose mid-guard as a crystalline sheen of azure water-mana began to coat the steel like a layer of clear oil.
"One."
Harper’s arm slashed down.
"Begin."
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The granite beneath Seraphina’s slippers vaporized into glowing molten slag as she became a crimson comet of compressed solar combustion.
In less than a few seconds, sixty paces of open air ceased to exist.

The atmospheric displacement of her forward acceleration produced a deafening crack that rattled the teeth in Valerius’s skull as the heat from her wake bent the light in the cavern into a swirling prism.
’FAST!’
Silas didn’t blink.
His pupils tracked the crimson streak with his body moving on instinct.
SHING! CLANG!
Seraphina’s right dagger struck his guard in a vicious upward diagonal slash aimed straight for his throat.
The collision of volcanic steel against tempered iron sounded like a church bell being struck by a sledgehammer.
Sparks erupted in a blinding, white-hot shower, but the moment her flame touched his blade, it hissed violently.
TSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSS!
The thin coating of water-mana along Silas’s steel flared into a dense curtain of pressurized steam.
The superheated steam acted as a buffer, stripping the three-thousand-degree solar flame of its concussive bite before it could melt the sword...
Seraphina didn’t even pause to register the defense.
’Yes!’ her mind screamed ecstasy with her teeth bared in a wild grin. ’He didn’t flinch!’
Usually when she attacked like this... her opponents would go down at once.
SWOOSH!
Her left arm whipped around in a reverse-grip horizontal cleave with the blade trailing a crescent arc of white-hot plasma.
’Flame Slash!’
Silas ducked.

The crescent of solar fire screamed a fraction of an inch above his messy dark bangs with the radiant heat singeing a few stray hairs, before the arc crashed into the distant basalt wall, cleaving a fifty-foot molten trench into the stone.
KRA-KOOOOM!
’Holy shit! That would’ve taken my head!’

She stepped forward, closing the distance between them until the toes of her soft indoor slippers lightly nudged the toe of his.
