"And if you manage to beat me," she whispered, her voice dropping into a teasing hush that made the tiny hairs along the nape of his neck prickle with electric static, "you get a reward."
Silas raised an eyebrow, his expression entirely deadpan.
"What kind of reward?"

The confident predatory swagger instantly short-circuited as a violent shade of vermilion detonated across the high planes of Seraphina’s cheekbones, racing with terrifying speed straight to the tips of her ears and down the exposed pale expanse of her collarbones.
She jerked her chin away, snapping her spine straight with her teeth sinking hard into her lower lip until a bead of white-hot mana hissed against her skin.
Suddenly, she found the plaster crown moldings along the parlor ceiling endlessly fascinating.
"T-That is reserved for after the match!" She stammered.
Her fingers knotted into the cuffs of her oversized sleeves, tugging at the fabric.
"Shut up and don’t ask stupid questions!
Just get off the couch and fight me!"

"I’d rather not turn my front driveway into a smoking crater of vitrified asphalt," Silas muttered, leaning back against the leather cushions and glancing past her shoulder toward the front bay window.
On the other side of the low table, Harper sat with her ankles neatly crossed, in violet pajamas with little gold stars that matched his, cradling her teacup with a small content smile.
She had been in a good mood all morning as she pushed her wire-rimmed glasses up the bridge of her nose with one finger, humming softly into her tea.
Then she heard the word "fight" and the humming stopped.
"Excuse me?" Harper set her teacup down and pressed a hand to her chest like she’d been shot.
"A spar?
In pajamas?
Sera, my Valkyrie is parked in that courtyard!
It’s custom mythril, you barbarian!
I know exactly what you’re planning...
You want to throw your stupid fire around next to my car on purpose!"
She jabbed a finger at the heiress with her cheeks flushed and her eyes wide with wounded outrage.
"If you singe so much as one speck of clear coat, I will sue you!
And your mother!
And your entire stupid house!"
Seraphina’s lips peeled back into a wicked, feline grin.
"Oh?
And what if I do, Whitmore?" Seraphina purred, her tone dripping with venomous amusement.
"Are you going to draft an angry formal grievance with your little gold-plated lawyer quill?
Or maybe file a three-part petition to the council?
You talk like an accountant who got lost on a battlefield..."
Harper’s violet eyes narrowed into lethal dead slits.
A single microscopic grain of light-devouring black sand flickered into existence directly above her left knuckle.

It hung in the air, humming with an ominous vibration, and for a terrifying half-second, the morning light in the living room curved toward her fingers as though she were genuinely contemplating hurling a void straight through the center of Seraphina’s forehead.
"Enough," Silas groaned, pinching the bridge of his nose until his fingers went numb.
"Both of you, sit down...
There will be no fights in the courtyard.
Harper’s interceptor and my car are parked out there, and the neighbors already give me enough looks...
I’m not getting a complaint on top of it."
"Then we drive to an arena," Seraphina insisted, stamping her slipper against the parquet floor with a sharp concussive thwack that rattled the teacups.
"Right now!
We can take my convoy to the Bloom Clan’s secondary estate...
Mother is currently in the city finalizing the diplomatic contracts with the Albion delegation—"
Beneath her scowl, however, her internal thoughts were settled.
’Yes... exactly that!
We drive to the Bloom compound!
I drag him into the central martial ring in front of Mother and the inner-circle elders!

I’ll force him to limit himself to a single element so he doesn’t expose the Vespera persona to the public registry, and once he completely stonewalls my primary assault with that ridiculous Gold Core foundation, Mother won’t be able to say a single word against him...
Those fossilized clan elders who keep whispering about arranged matches can swallow their own tongues!
We’ll be engaged before autumn ends...’
Sera didn’t really care about much, she just wanted to show that he was good and get them engaged as soon as possible.
"Uh, hey.
Before you two start drafting marriage annexes, measuring curtain fabrics, and booking courtrooms..."
Valerius’s deep cheerful voice cut smoothly through the brewing domestic squall.
The golden-haired scion leaned forward on the leather sofa, resting his forearms on his knees, reaching deep into the interior pocket of his charcoal vest.
With a dramatic flourish of his thick wrist, he produced a heavy, matte-black metallic cube roughly four inches across.
It was inlaid with intricate microscopic silver runes that bent the dust motes in the air around it into tiny swirling ellipses.
"What is that?" Silas asked, his blue eyes instantly locking onto the geometric rune patterns carved into the dark metal.
"A cube that has space runes?"
"Better," Valerius grinned with his white teeth flashing as he tossed the heavy cube lightly from hand to hand.
The metal gave a dull thud against his palm.
"It’s a prototype isolation chamber...

Sterling Technologies has been co-developing this with high-tier rune masters contracted directly from the Sovereign Realm, It essentially folds space into an artificial sub-pocket so basically, a self-contained mobile training arena that won’t leak a single drop of force, shockwaves or radiation into the real world."
Seraphina narrowed her eyes at it, her chin tilting up with pure disdain at her plan being foiled.
"It’s the size of a tea canister, Valerius.
What are we supposed to do inside that?
Spar with our pinky fingers?"
"Watch and learn, fiery," Valerius scoffed playfully.
He stood up, tapped a sequence of three silver nodes along the cube’s upper bevel, and underhanded it toward the center of the hardwood floor.
CLACK!
The moment the dark metal struck the floorboards, it didn’t bounce.
It expanded.

The edges uncoupled with a series of heavy hydraulic hisses with the metal unfolding like an origami lotus forged from dark iron, rising, stretching, and warping the air until a freestanding eight-foot-tall obsidian archway stood solidly in the middle of Silas’s living room.
Within the frame of the arch, the air did not lead to the dining room as instead, it swirled with deep pale-gray mist.
Valerius stepped up, gesturing toward the gray mist like an enthusiastic shopkeeper presenting his finest wares.
"After you, contestants."
Silas raised an eyebrow, stepping through the archway first, with Harper and Seraphina following close behind.
The transition was seamless.
The moment they crossed the threshold, the ceiling of the Silverleaf residence vanished.
Silas looked up into an artificial vault stretching at least two hundred feet into the air, illuminated by glowing simulated starlight embedded in the high basalt dome.
Beneath their feet was a massive, reinforced combat platform paved with heavy mana-dampening granite slabs, easily the size of two full regulation football stadiums.
The colossal scale was completely invisible from the outside.
"Woah..." Harper murmured, pushing her glasses up as she scanned the perimeter runic baffles.
Her eyes were shining.
"Wait... this is actually insane.
You folded a whole stadium into a tea canister?!
Valerius, how much do you want for it?
I’m serious, name a price!"
Valerius laughed, rubbing the back of his golden neck.
"Not for sale yet, Harper!
It’s still an unstable prototype...
It took four high-rank mages six months just to stabilize the atmospheric pressure inside this one box so it won’t hit commercial production for at least five years."
He walked over toward the outer boundary line, leaning back against the raised observation railing, crossing his arms with an eager wolfish grin.
’Man...’ Valerius thought, his golden eyes sparkling with pure anticipation. ’Before I found out Silas was Vespera...
I honestly thought he was just a solid prodigy around my level but seeing the shit he pulled in the tournament?
Knowing he’s sitting on an actual Gold Core?’
He glanced between the two combatants taking their positions on the gray stone.
’Who do I even bet on?’ Valerius mused, a cold sweat breaking out on the back of his neck. ’Logically, Silas washes her...
A Gold Core Lord is a walking natural disaster but if I say that out loud and Sera overhears me, she’ll turn my eyebrows into ash before the match even starts...’
Sixty paces away, Silas and Seraphina stood facing each other.
The air between them had already begun to thin with the temperature in the cube dropping into an eerie electric hush.
Seraphina reached behind her waist.
SHING!
With a clean, fluid flick of her wrists, the second of the curved daggers materialized in her grip.
The blades were forged from deep volcanic steel with their edges glowing with a dangerous orange shimmer that distorted the air around her fingers like a desert mirage.
She rolled her shoulders, shaking out the loose cuffs of her oversized white shirt, her red eyes locking onto Silas with ferocious focus.
"You better fight me with everything you have, Silas Graves," Seraphina warned, her voice dropping into a low breathless tone.
"If you hold back because you think I’m fragile... if you treat me like a delicate little noble girl...
I swear on my mother’s name, I will shatter every bone in your legs.
You won’t walk for a month!"
Silas chuckled, reaching into his spatial storage.
Clink!
He didn’t draw the Dawn Blade.
It rested within his soul and drawing it in a domestic spar was equivalent to swinging a live artillery shell at someone’s forehead.
He wasn’t going to risk hurting Sera with it at all.
Instead, he withdrew a standard longsword forged from tempered mythril...
It was a simple balanced weapon with a dark leather grip.
He rested the flat of the blade against his shoulder, looking at her with a lazy teasing smirk.
"Is that your idea of pillow talk, Sera?
Threatening to cripple your future husband before the wedding?"
FWOOSH!
A sudden violent ring of bright red sparks ignited around Seraphina’s collarbones.
"SHUT UP!" she yelled, her face instantly turning the exact shade of a ripe strawberry as her embarrassment transformed instantly into explosive combustible fury.
"DIE, YOU ARROGANT BASTARD!"
Across the ring, Silas’s posture relaxed, but his mind shifted into cold clarity.

’Well I should hold back a bit,’ Silas analyzed, feeling the thrum of his core circulating behind his ribs. ’If I start layering lightning, light, as well as all of the other spells I know, the spatial cube won’t hold the pressure.’
His blue eyes settled on the fiery girl across the stone.
’I’ll stick to water...
Maybe a bit of wind for displacement.
Let’s see how sharp House Bloom’s claws really are.’
Harper walked to the center line between them with her violet pajamas rustling in the rising heat.
She raised her right hand with her eyes flicking from one fighter to the other, and a little grin tugged at her mouth.
"Okay, rules!" Harper called, her voice bouncing off the basalt walls.
"No hitting the head, no wrecking each other’s cores, and whoever gets knocked out of the ring or gives up loses...
If either of you actually tries to kill the other, I’m stopping it.
Got it?"
She glanced at Seraphina, then at Silas.
"And Sera, if you set the cube on fire, I’m telling Valerius you did it on purpose."
"HEY!" Valerius yelled from the railing.
She lowered her hand by half an inch.
"Three."
Seraphina lowered her center of gravity with the soles of her slippers grinding against the granite.
"Two."
Silas brought the sword forward, holding it in a low loose mid-guard as a crystalline sheen of azure water-mana began to coat the steel like a layer of clear oil.
"One."
Harper’s arm slashed down.
"Begin."
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The granite beneath Seraphina’s slippers vaporized into glowing molten slag as she became a crimson comet of compressed solar combustion.
In less than a few seconds, sixty paces of open air ceased to exist.

The atmospheric displacement of her forward acceleration produced a deafening crack that rattled the teeth in Valerius’s skull as the heat from her wake bent the light in the cavern into a swirling prism.
’FAST!’
Silas didn’t blink.
His pupils tracked the crimson streak with his body moving on instinct.
SHING!
CLANG!
Seraphina’s right dagger struck his guard in a vicious upward diagonal slash aimed straight for his throat.
The collision of volcanic steel against tempered iron sounded like a church bell being struck by a sledgehammer.
Sparks erupted in a blinding, white-hot shower, but the moment her flame touched his blade, it hissed violently.
TSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSS!
The thin coating of water-mana along Silas’s steel flared into a dense curtain of pressurized steam.
The superheated steam acted as a buffer, stripping the three-thousand-degree solar flame of its concussive bite before it could melt the sword...
Seraphina didn’t even pause to register the defense.
’Yes!’ her mind screamed ecstasy with her teeth bared in a wild grin. ’He didn’t flinch!’
Usually when she attacked like this... her opponents would go down at once.
SWOOSH!
Her left arm whipped around in a reverse-grip horizontal cleave with the blade trailing a crescent arc of white-hot plasma.
’Flame Slash!’
Silas ducked.

The crescent of solar fire screamed a fraction of an inch above his messy dark bangs with the radiant heat singeing a few stray hairs, before the arc crashed into the distant basalt wall, cleaving a fifty-foot molten trench into the stone.
KRA-KOOOOM!
’Holy shit!
That would’ve taken my head!’

chapters.title: Chapter 663: Beat Me More! [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: From the crouch, Silas twisted his hips with his left palm snapping upward in a short brutal strike aimed at her floating ribs.
WHOOSH!
’Tidal Impact...’
A dense sphere of heavy water erupted from his palm and Seraphina’s combat instincts were terrifying.
’What a strong attack...’
She dropped her weight, throwing her entire body into a spinning, horizontal axis mid-air with her right foot snapping out like a whip.
CRASH!
Her heel, wreathed in roaring crimson fire, intercepted the water sphere mid-flight.
The collision between heavy hydro-mana and solar fire detonated into an apocalyptic cloud of scalding vapor that blanketed the central ring.
Within the blinding white fog, the tempo didn’t slow at all... It accelerated into unrestrained madness.
CLANG! CLANG! SHING! CLANG!
The sound of steel striking steel rang out in a continuous deafening staccato as twenty exchanges were in the span of two heartbeats.
’Ah... So hot...’
Seraphina was a tempest of flame.
She moved like a dancing demon, utilizing the unnatural leverage of her petite frame to weave around Silas’s longer reach.
A low sweep aimed at his ankles, a rising reverse-grip stab toward his armpit, a spinning backhand slash coated in searing plasma... She did it all.
WHOOSH!
Every strike was infused with the pride of House Bloom and every movement executed with the lethal elegance of a predator who was trying her best to hunt down her prey.
...And with every strike that Silas parried, her heart hammered harder, faster, drunk on an intoxicating rush of adrenaline.
It felt amazing.
’He’s matching me!’ Seraphina thought, her red eyes going wide and sparkling with breathless joy. ’He’s not even using his Gold Core suppression or overwhelming me with a higher mana pool!’
No...
’He’s reading my angles! He’s parrying with a third-rate iron sword! This is the man... this is the man who stands above the world huh?!’
SHING!
Her right dagger skated down the length of his blade, straight for his knuckles but Silas rolled his wrist and let it slide off the flat.
CLANG!
Her left dagger came up from underneath, Silas dropped the pommel and cracked it aside.
SKRRRRRK!
She hooked both daggers over his blade like a pair of scissors and pinned it against his hip.
’Got you!’ Seraphina thought, her grin splitting wider but Silas didn’t pull back.
He drove the pinned sword forward with his whole body, spun in a tight circle, and tore it free.
KRAAAAANG!
A fan of orange sparks lit the fog for half a second as Seraphina’s feet skidded back a full step.
’How’s he doing this...? Is it some secret technique...?’
Silas pulsed a thin ring of water mana eyes and blue lines should have bloomed across her body however they flickered and then they twisted into unstable wisps and snapped apart in her heat.
’Rip-Current Perception is a bust, huh?’
He wasn’t surprised by it, it was pretty bad against people who had a high body heat as he wondered how Morwenna got past this whole thing.
’Still, how hot is her body?’
Seraphina saw the half-second he spent thinking.
’Hesitation!’
She crossed both daggers and swung them out in an X!
SHHHHHK!
An X-shaped arc of white-hot fire ripped through the fog toward his chest, however a hard gust burst under his heels and shoved him sideways.
WHOOSH!
The X tore through the space where his ribs had been and carved two glowing scars across the stone.
’That was close...’
Still, was Sera trying to kill him? This was like the third flame attack that would have crippled or even killed him if he didn’t think fast.
"Don’t think I’m done with you!"
She stomped.
BWOOOOOM!

The floor under Silas erupted as a spiraling cage of crimson fire tore out of the bedrock and wrapped around him in huge interlocking petals, twisting upward and closing over his head like the bud of a monstrous flower.
’She already set it up...?’
Inside the bud, the heat pressed against his skin like a hand and his water coating sizzled off the steel, however he planted both feet and thrust his left palm at the petals.
’Hurricane Repulsion!’
BWAAAAAAAM!
A shockwave of compressed air punched outward in every direction as the petals ripped apart, flaring open like a flower hit by a bomb, and burning shreds rained across the platform.
Seraphina skidded back three paces with her cuffs snapping in the wind.
’One palm!’ she thought, her eyes shining. ’That bastard broke it with one palm!’
She didn’t give him a second to breathe as she lunged back in.
CLANG!
Silas deflected her left dagger outward with the flat of his blade with his footwork shifting into a tight circular pivot.
’Severing Horizon!’
He swung the training sword in a horizontal sweep and a thirty-foot crescent of heavy, pressurized water detached from the edge, screaming across the stone like a hydraulic guillotine.
Seraphina’s eyes ignited.
Instead of dodging, she crossed both daggers before her chest.
FWOOM!
Two spiraling, crimson fire serpents erupted from her forearms, coiling tightly around her daggers as she brought the cross-guard down squarely into the center of the heavy-water crescent.
KRA-BOOOOOOM!

The solar flame swallowed the water wave whole and the ungodly temperature boiled the entire thirty-foot construct into vapor in half a second with the concussive shockwave blasting the mist apart, leaving both of them standing in the clear scorched center of the arena.
"Ugh—!"
The recoil pushed Seraphina’s daggers wide and her guard was open for a fraction of a heartbeat but Silas didn’t use the sword.
’Using blades against this woman is like asking for an invite to be countered...’
With that thought, he released his grip on the leather hilt, letting the iron weapon drop toward the ground with his right hand shooting forward like an uncoiled iron spring.
GRASP!
His fingers locked around Seraphina’s right wrist, arresting her momentum but Sera didn’t panic.
’Is that so?’
With her left hand, she reversed her dagger, plunging it downward toward his forearm.
SHING!
Silas’s left hand snapped up with his palm catching the base of her thumb, violently twisting her wrist outward with a textbook joint-lock.
CLICK-CLATTER.
Both of her volcanic steel daggers slipped from her numb fingers, clattering uselessly against the stone!
"No weapons?" Seraphina snarled with her grin widening. "FINE BY ME!"
Did he think that without her weapons, it would be much easier to force her to submit...?
’That’s a foolish thought...’
Deprived of their blades, members of the Bloom clan could turn their bodies into engines of war!
Sera drove her left elbow straight toward Silas’s jaw with her forearm wrapped in a roaring mantle of solar flame.
FWOOSH!
Silas leaned his head back by two inches as the heat blistered the skin of his chin and countered with a lightning-fast palm strike to her sternum.
THUD!
Seraphina caught his wrist with both hands, using his forward momentum to kick off his chest, flipping over his head like an acrobat.
’I’ve been practicing since I was three... You won’t be able to beat me like that.’ Sera thought.
Before her feet even touched the granite behind him, she spun, throwing a vicious rising roundhouse kick aimed squarely at the side of his neck.
THWACK!
Silas brought his left forearm up, blocking the kick and the impact drove his slippers an inch into the shattered stone, but his frame didn’t yield an inch.
"...Amazing."
She didn’t stop.
WHAM!
Her left fist slammed into his ribs.
’Ow! Fuck!’ Silas thought with his breath hissing out through his teeth.
CRACK!
His right elbow smashed into her cheekbone and her head snapped sideways, and she spat a bead of fire onto the stone.
’You hit me in the face!’ Seraphina thought. ’But I want more! Beat me more!’
She grabbed his collar and headbutted him.
BAM!
Stars burst behind Silas’s eyes.
’Ahh! Is her head made of rock?!’
He dropped into a low sweep and his heel scythed under both her ankles.
WHOOSH!
She fell, planted both palms on the stone, and flipped herself upright on a burst of fire from her hands.
FWOOOSH!
Sera came back down with a blazing heel drop aimed at the crown of his head as he crossed his arms over his face.
BOOOM!
The granite rippled under his slippers and the heat licked through his sleeves.
’She’s a goddamn furnace...’
He twisted her ankle, spun, and flung her across the ring.
WHAM!
She hit the stone and sprang up laughing with fire trailing from both fists.
"AHAHAHAHA! AGAIN!" she screamed as she came at him in a flurry which Silas weaved.
WHOOSH! WHOOSH! WHOOSH!
’Is she perhaps... enjoying getting beat up?’ Silas thought with a chill going down his spine as Sera’s hand shot forward once more.
BANG!
The punch grazed his temple however Sera had already prepared for that as she slid under his guard and drove a rising knee at his gut.
THUD!
Silas folded around it, caught her ankle, and heaved her over his shoulder.
WHAM!
Her spine slammed flush against the reinforced floor.
The granite beneath her shattered instantly blooming outward into a spiderwebbed crater of jagged gray stone but she didn’t even grunt.
’I really want more!’

Before her momentum settled, her right palm snapped down and slapped the fractured stone as a concussive detonation of raw flame erupted directly beneath her hand with the kickback violently launching her back up into the air and snapping her right back onto her feet.
FWOOSH!
"Is that all you’ve got, Graves?!"
"Don’t push it!"
She spat a mouthful of smoke and wiped her split lip with her thumb.
’Damn him,’ she thought. ’He’s actually good at this...’
Without pausing, Silas stepped inside her guard with his right shoulder slamming hard into her chest in a devastating close-quarters shoulder check.
BOOM!
The breath exploded from Seraphina’s lungs as she stumbled backward three paces.

Silas didn’t give her room to breathe as he closed the distance with a low sliding step with his left hand swatting aside her blazing left hook and his right arm cocking back like a heavy industrial piston.
’I fell for the trap!’ She thought as Silas’s eyes glinted, Sera tried to defend herself but it was... too late.
Silas stepped into the punch, driving his right fist squarely into the center of her solar plexus.
BAAAAAAAAAANG!
The strike landed with the dull sickening thud of an iron wrecking ball hitting reinforced concrete and a violent concussive ring echoed off the walls.
All the air, all the pride, and all the breath inside Seraphina Bloom was instantly, violently expelled from her mouth in a gasping choke.
"Gah!"
Her eyes bulged with the color completely draining from her face as her knees buckled under the shockwave rippling through her abdominal wall.
WHOOSH!
She was sent flying backward as her body began to fold forward around his fist with gravity claiming her frame.

Silas immediately pulled his punch back with his left hand rising as he prepared to deliver a gentle concussive chop to the side of her neck to end the match cleanly and catch her before she hit the stone.
’I can finish this easily,’ Silas thought while moving forward.
He was half an inch away.
Then...
The world stopped.
The word rang inside Seraphina’s skull with her vision going white at the edges as her legs were not answering her at all.
’Not like this... Not in front of him... Not in front of Harper.’
’I’m a Bloom. I’ve been burning since I was a child and I am not losing to a single punch...’
Her fingers curled against the stone... she refused to go out like this, she hadn’t made him push that far yet.
"BURN."
She opened the floodgates of her Primordial Fire Spirit.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A cataclysmic detonation of pure white heat erupted directly from the center of Seraphina’s chest and Silas’s blue eyes widened.
’SHIT!’
The concussive force of the thermal release slammed into Silas like an oncoming locomotive, blowing him backward through the air.
WHOOOSH!
He twisted mid-flight, digging his slippers into the granite and carving two long smoking trenches thirty yards across the arena before coming to a halt.
’This got a bit more troublesome...’
The entire cube turned into a blinding shadowless sea of white.
In the center of the ring, the girl with the messy crimson hair and the oversized white shirt was gone.
Hovering four inches above the molten, bubbling granite was a being of pure destruction.

Seraphina’s hair was no longer crimson... It had transformed into a flowing, magnificent cascade of brilliant luminous silver-white fire, billowing around her shoulders like molten starlight and her red eyes had vanished, replaced by two glowing orbs of pure white-hot plasma.
Across the pale skin of her neck, her forearms, and her cheeks were burning runes ignited with pulsing brilliance.
The Floodgates were wide open and the ten-times multiplier of the Primordial Fire Spirit began to alter the fundamental laws of combustion within the chamber.
CRACKLE-FWOOSH!
A towering swirling cyclone of three-thousand-degree solar flame erupted outward in a three-hundred-and-sixty-degree wave as the air itself began to burn.

The nitrogen and oxygen molecules within the artificial vault sheared apart into glowing plasma with the heat radiating with such terrifying intensity that the massive basalt walls of the dimensional cube began to glow dull red.
Her white eyes found Silas and she vanished.
BOOM!
Silver-white fire punched through the spot where Silas had been standing.
’Left!’
He was already moving with his forearm snapped up, wrapped in a skin of heavy water as he caught her fist.
CRAAAAAASH!
The impact drove him ten feet backward across the glass-slick floor and steam screamed off his arm.
"Is that all?" Seraphina asked.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
She released three punches in a single breath.
He swayed under the first, rolled his shoulder through the second, and took the third on his crossed wrists though it shook every bone in his arms.
Water flashed to steam on his skin with every hit.
TSSSSSSSSSS!
’Okay... Okay! That’s enough!’
Fifty yards away at the observation railing, Valerius screamed:
"MY HAIR! SHIT, MY HAIR IS ON FIRE!"
A stray lick of the superheated air had drifted over the barrier, instantly igniting the tips of Valerius’s golden bangs into tiny yellow embers.
The blond noble was frantically slapping the top of his head with both hands with panic written across his face as he looked at the glowing runic seams of the ceiling.

"SERA, STOP!" Valerius bellowed, his voice cracking with genuine terror. "COMPRESS IT! COMPRESS THE DAMN MANA! THE RUNES CAN’T HOLD THIS OUTPUT! YOU’RE GOING TO BLOW UP THE PROTOTYPE AND VAPORIZE SILAS’S PLACE!"
Above the sea of white fire, the entity tilted its head.
The silver-white flames dancing along her eyelashes flickered slightly as Valerius’s panicked screams pierced the roar of the inferno.
Slowly... Seraphina drew a breath.
She didn’t dispel the transformation though, instead, with terrifying willpower, she clamped down on the Primordial Spirit’s wild raging torrent.
’I need to calm myself down...’
VUUUUUUUUUUUM!
The colossal three-hundred-foot storm of white fire was forcefully sucked backward, collapsing inward toward her core like water draining into a whirlpool.
Within three seconds, the raging sea of flame had condensed into a tight razor-thin aura of blinding silver-white light hugging the contours of her body.
The air around her bent into a violent shimmering heat mirage as she hovered in the air with her glowing white eyes staring across the molten glass-slick floor straight at Silas Graves.
’So cute...’
Silas stood with his arms slightly raised and crystalline mist of water-mana swirling around his forearms while his blue eyes locked onto her with a bit of worry in them.
’Stop looking at me like that...’
For a long heavy heartbeat, the shattered cavern was dead silent, save for the crackling of cooling stone then, Seraphina’s chin tilted slightly.
The silver-white flames of her hair brushed against her bare throat as her lips parted.
She leaned forward, her plasma-white eyes locking squarely onto his pupils.
"...how many children do you think we should have?"

She did it all.
WHOOSH!
Every strike was infused with the pride of House Bloom and every movement executed with the lethal elegance of a predator who was trying her best to hunt down her prey.
...And with every strike that Silas parried, her heart hammered harder, faster, drunk on an intoxicating rush of adrenaline.
It felt amazing.
’He’s matching me!’ Seraphina thought, her red eyes going wide and sparkling with breathless joy. ’He’s not even using his Gold Core suppression or overwhelming me with a higher mana pool!’
No...
’He’s reading my angles!
He’s parrying with a third-rate iron sword!
This is the man... this is the man who stands above the world huh?!’
SHING!
Her right dagger skated down the length of his blade, straight for his knuckles but Silas rolled his wrist and let it slide off the flat.
CLANG!
Her left dagger came up from underneath, Silas dropped the pommel and cracked it aside.
SKRRRRRK!
She hooked both daggers over his blade like a pair of scissors and pinned it against his hip.
’Got you!’ Seraphina thought, her grin splitting wider but Silas didn’t pull back.
He drove the pinned sword forward with his whole body, spun in a tight circle, and tore it free.
KRAAAAANG!
A fan of orange sparks lit the fog for half a second as Seraphina’s feet skidded back a full step.
’How’s he doing this...?
Is it some secret technique...?’
Silas pulsed a thin ring of water mana eyes and blue lines should have bloomed across her body however they flickered and then they twisted into unstable wisps and snapped apart in her heat.
’Rip-Current Perception is a bust, huh?’
He wasn’t surprised by it, it was pretty bad against people who had a high body heat as he wondered how Morwenna got past this whole thing.
’Still, how hot is her body?’
Seraphina saw the half-second he spent thinking.
’Hesitation!’
She crossed both daggers and swung them out in an X!
SHHHHHK!
An X-shaped arc of white-hot fire ripped through the fog toward his chest, however a hard gust burst under his heels and shoved him sideways.
WHOOSH!
The X tore through the space where his ribs had been and carved two glowing scars across the stone.
’That was close...’
Still, was Sera trying to kill him?
This was like the third flame attack that would have crippled or even killed him if he didn’t think fast.
"Don’t think I’m done with you!"
She stomped.
BWOOOOOM!

The floor under Silas erupted as a spiraling cage of crimson fire tore out of the bedrock and wrapped around him in huge interlocking petals, twisting upward and closing over his head like the bud of a monstrous flower.
’She already set it up...?’
Inside the bud, the heat pressed against his skin like a hand and his water coating sizzled off the steel, however he planted both feet and thrust his left palm at the petals.
’Hurricane Repulsion!’
BWAAAAAAAM!
A shockwave of compressed air punched outward in every direction as the petals ripped apart, flaring open like a flower hit by a bomb, and burning shreds rained across the platform.
Seraphina skidded back three paces with her cuffs snapping in the wind.
’One palm!’ she thought, her eyes shining. ’That bastard broke it with one palm!’
She didn’t give him a second to breathe as she lunged back in.
CLANG!
Silas deflected her left dagger outward with the flat of his blade with his footwork shifting into a tight circular pivot.
’Severing Horizon!’
He swung the training sword in a horizontal sweep and a thirty-foot crescent of heavy, pressurized water detached from the edge, screaming across the stone like a hydraulic guillotine.
Seraphina’s eyes ignited.
Instead of dodging, she crossed both daggers before her chest.
FWOOM!
Two spiraling, crimson fire serpents erupted from her forearms, coiling tightly around her daggers as she brought the cross-guard down squarely into the center of the heavy-water crescent.
KRA-BOOOOOOM!

The solar flame swallowed the water wave whole and the ungodly temperature boiled the entire thirty-foot construct into vapor in half a second with the concussive shockwave blasting the mist apart, leaving both of them standing in the clear scorched center of the arena.
"Ugh—!"
The recoil pushed Seraphina’s daggers wide and her guard was open for a fraction of a heartbeat but Silas didn’t use the sword.
’Using blades against this woman is like asking for an invite to be countered...’
With that thought, he released his grip on the leather hilt, letting the iron weapon drop toward the ground with his right hand shooting forward like an uncoiled iron spring.
GRASP!
His fingers locked around Seraphina’s right wrist, arresting her momentum but Sera didn’t panic.
’Is that so?’
With her left hand, she reversed her dagger, plunging it downward toward his forearm.
SHING!
Silas’s left hand snapped up with his palm catching the base of her thumb, violently twisting her wrist outward with a textbook joint-lock.
CLICK-CLATTER.
Both of her volcanic steel daggers slipped from her numb fingers, clattering uselessly against the stone!
"No weapons?" Seraphina snarled with her grin widening.
"FINE BY ME!"
Did he think that without her weapons, it would be much easier to force her to submit...?
’That’s a foolish thought...’
Deprived of their blades, members of the Bloom clan could turn their bodies into engines of war!
Sera drove her left elbow straight toward Silas’s jaw with her forearm wrapped in a roaring mantle of solar flame.
FWOOSH!
Silas leaned his head back by two inches as the heat blistered the skin of his chin and countered with a lightning-fast palm strike to her sternum.
THUD!
Seraphina caught his wrist with both hands, using his forward momentum to kick off his chest, flipping over his head like an acrobat.
’I’ve been practicing since I was three...
You won’t be able to beat me like that.’ Sera thought.
Before her feet even touched the granite behind him, she spun, throwing a vicious rising roundhouse kick aimed squarely at the side of his neck.
THWACK!
Silas brought his left forearm up, blocking the kick and the impact drove his slippers an inch into the shattered stone, but his frame didn’t yield an inch.
"...Amazing."
She didn’t stop.
WHAM!
Her left fist slammed into his ribs.
’Ow!
Fuck!’ Silas thought with his breath hissing out through his teeth.
CRACK!
His right elbow smashed into her cheekbone and her head snapped sideways, and she spat a bead of fire onto the stone.
’You hit me in the face!’ Seraphina thought. ’But I want more!
Beat me more!’
She grabbed his collar and headbutted him.
BAM!
Stars burst behind Silas’s eyes.
’Ahh!
Is her head made of rock?!’
He dropped into a low sweep and his heel scythed under both her ankles.
WHOOSH!
She fell, planted both palms on the stone, and flipped herself upright on a burst of fire from her hands.
FWOOOSH!
Sera came back down with a blazing heel drop aimed at the crown of his head as he crossed his arms over his face.
BOOOM!
The granite rippled under his slippers and the heat licked through his sleeves.
’She’s a goddamn furnace...’
He twisted her ankle, spun, and flung her across the ring.
WHAM!
She hit the stone and sprang up laughing with fire trailing from both fists.
"AHAHAHAHA!
AGAIN!" she screamed as she came at him in a flurry which Silas weaved.
WHOOSH!
WHOOSH!
WHOOSH!
’Is she perhaps... enjoying getting beat up?’ Silas thought with a chill going down his spine as Sera’s hand shot forward once more.
BANG!
The punch grazed his temple however Sera had already prepared for that as she slid under his guard and drove a rising knee at his gut.
THUD!
Silas folded around it, caught her ankle, and heaved her over his shoulder.
WHAM!
Her spine slammed flush against the reinforced floor.
The granite beneath her shattered instantly blooming outward into a spiderwebbed crater of jagged gray stone but she didn’t even grunt.
’I really want more!’

Before her momentum settled, her right palm snapped down and slapped the fractured stone as a concussive detonation of raw flame erupted directly beneath her hand with the kickback violently launching her back up into the air and snapping her right back onto her feet.
FWOOSH!
"Is that all you’ve got, Graves?!"
"Don’t push it!"
She spat a mouthful of smoke and wiped her split lip with her thumb.
’Damn him,’ she thought. ’He’s actually good at this...’
Without pausing, Silas stepped inside her guard with his right shoulder slamming hard into her chest in a devastating close-quarters shoulder check.
BOOM!
The breath exploded from Seraphina’s lungs as she stumbled backward three paces.

Silas didn’t give her room to breathe as he closed the distance with a low sliding step with his left hand swatting aside her blazing left hook and his right arm cocking back like a heavy industrial piston.
’I fell for the trap!’ She thought as Silas’s eyes glinted, Sera tried to defend herself but it was... too late.
Silas stepped into the punch, driving his right fist squarely into the center of her solar plexus.
BAAAAAAAAAANG!
The strike landed with the dull sickening thud of an iron wrecking ball hitting reinforced concrete and a violent concussive ring echoed off the walls.
All the air, all the pride, and all the breath inside Seraphina Bloom was instantly, violently expelled from her mouth in a gasping choke.
"Gah!"
Her eyes bulged with the color completely draining from her face as her knees buckled under the shockwave rippling through her abdominal wall.
WHOOSH!
She was sent flying backward as her body began to fold forward around his fist with gravity claiming her frame.

Silas immediately pulled his punch back with his left hand rising as he prepared to deliver a gentle concussive chop to the side of her neck to end the match cleanly and catch her before she hit the stone.
’I can finish this easily,’ Silas thought while moving forward.
He was half an inch away.
Then...
The world stopped.
The word rang inside Seraphina’s skull with her vision going white at the edges as her legs were not answering her at all.
’Not like this...
Not in front of him...
Not in front of Harper.’
’I’m a Bloom.
I’ve been burning since I was a child and I am not losing to a single punch...’
Her fingers curled against the stone... she refused to go out like this, she hadn’t made him push that far yet.
"BURN."
She opened the floodgates of her Primordial Fire Spirit.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A cataclysmic detonation of pure white heat erupted directly from the center of Seraphina’s chest and Silas’s blue eyes widened.
’SHIT!’
The concussive force of the thermal release slammed into Silas like an oncoming locomotive, blowing him backward through the air.
WHOOOSH!
He twisted mid-flight, digging his slippers into the granite and carving two long smoking trenches thirty yards across the arena before coming to a halt.
’This got a bit more troublesome...’
The entire cube turned into a blinding shadowless sea of white.
In the center of the ring, the girl with the messy crimson hair and the oversized white shirt was gone.
Hovering four inches above the molten, bubbling granite was a being of pure destruction.
Seraphina’s hair was no longer crimson...

It had transformed into a flowing, magnificent cascade of brilliant luminous silver-white fire, billowing around her shoulders like molten starlight and her red eyes had vanished, replaced by two glowing orbs of pure white-hot plasma.
Across the pale skin of her neck, her forearms, and her cheeks were burning runes ignited with pulsing brilliance.
The Floodgates were wide open and the ten-times multiplier of the Primordial Fire Spirit began to alter the fundamental laws of combustion within the chamber.
CRACKLE-FWOOSH!
A towering swirling cyclone of three-thousand-degree solar flame erupted outward in a three-hundred-and-sixty-degree wave as the air itself began to burn.

The nitrogen and oxygen molecules within the artificial vault sheared apart into glowing plasma with the heat radiating with such terrifying intensity that the massive basalt walls of the dimensional cube began to glow dull red.
Her white eyes found Silas and she vanished.
BOOM!
Silver-white fire punched through the spot where Silas had been standing.
’Left!’
He was already moving with his forearm snapped up, wrapped in a skin of heavy water as he caught her fist.
CRAAAAAASH!
The impact drove him ten feet backward across the glass-slick floor and steam screamed off his arm.
"Is that all?" Seraphina asked.
BOOM!
BOOM!
BOOM!
She released three punches in a single breath.
He swayed under the first, rolled his shoulder through the second, and took the third on his crossed wrists though it shook every bone in his arms.
Water flashed to steam on his skin with every hit.
TSSSSSSSSSS!
’Okay...
Okay!
That’s enough!’
Fifty yards away at the observation railing, Valerius screamed:
"MY HAIR!
SHIT, MY HAIR IS ON FIRE!"
A stray lick of the superheated air had drifted over the barrier, instantly igniting the tips of Valerius’s golden bangs into tiny yellow embers.
The blond noble was frantically slapping the top of his head with both hands with panic written across his face as he looked at the glowing runic seams of the ceiling.
"SERA, STOP!" Valerius bellowed, his voice cracking with genuine terror.
"COMPRESS IT!
COMPRESS THE DAMN MANA!
THE RUNES CAN’T HOLD THIS OUTPUT!
YOU’RE GOING TO BLOW UP THE PROTOTYPE AND VAPORIZE SILAS’S PLACE!"
Above the sea of white fire, the entity tilted its head.
The silver-white flames dancing along her eyelashes flickered slightly as Valerius’s panicked screams pierced the roar of the inferno.
Slowly...
Seraphina drew a breath.
She didn’t dispel the transformation though, instead, with terrifying willpower, she clamped down on the Primordial Spirit’s wild raging torrent.
’I need to calm myself down...’
VUUUUUUUUUUUM!
The colossal three-hundred-foot storm of white fire was forcefully sucked backward, collapsing inward toward her core like water draining into a whirlpool.
Within three seconds, the raging sea of flame had condensed into a tight razor-thin aura of blinding silver-white light hugging the contours of her body.
The air around her bent into a violent shimmering heat mirage as she hovered in the air with her glowing white eyes staring across the molten glass-slick floor straight at Silas Graves.
’So cute...’
Silas stood with his arms slightly raised and crystalline mist of water-mana swirling around his forearms while his blue eyes locked onto her with a bit of worry in them.
’Stop looking at me like that...’
For a long heavy heartbeat, the shattered cavern was dead silent, save for the crackling of cooling stone then, Seraphina’s chin tilted slightly.
The silver-white flames of her hair brushed against her bare throat as her lips parted.
She leaned forward, her plasma-white eyes locking squarely onto his pupils.
"...how many children do you think we should have?"

chapters.title: Chapter 664: The Bloom Family Doctrine [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: "What...?"
The single syllable fell from Silas’s mouth like a dry pebble dropping into an abyss.
His hands remained half-raised with the water-mana still swirling across his knuckles, but his posture had completely unraveled from battle-ready vigilance into bewilderment.
Behind the observation railing, the silence was deafening.
Harper stood frozen, her index finger poised mid-air where she had been pushing up her glasses.
The lenses caught the blinding silver glare of Seraphina’s spirit form, masking her eyes, but her jaw had gone slack enough that her mouth formed a perfect silent ’O’.
Beside her, Valerius was still patting at the scorched ends of his golden bangs, but his hand froze midway against his skull.
The blond scion blinked once and twice as he looked at Seraphina, then looked at Silas, his brain visibly stalling out like an engine starved of fuel.
"Children...?" Valerius croaked, his voice cracking violently in the hollow cavern. "Did the atmospheric pressure drop break my ears, or did she just--"
"Quiet, Valerius!" Seraphina snapped, though the terrifying dual-toned resonance of the Primordial Spirit couldn’t entirely mask the sudden desperate tremor in her voice.
She drifted down until the soles of her slippers touched the vitrified glass of the floor.
The tight compressed sheath of silver-white fire hugging her skin flickered with the runic marks glowing like molten tin along her collarbones.
She crossed her arms tightly over her chest, trying desperately to summon the haughty authority of a Bloom heir, but the furious crimson rushing beneath her glowing cheeks betrayed her.

"It is standard clan doctrine!" she declared, her plasma-white eyes darting nervously toward the basalt floor before snapping back to Silas. "In House Bloom... if an heir secures a prospective fiancé of verified caliber, the clan directives explicitly instruct us to consolidate the bloodline and produce heirs as soon as possible! It prevents succession disputes!"
She puffed her cheeks out with her silver bangs falling across her face.

"I am satisfied that your foundation is genuine!" she mumbled, her voice shrinking into a soft mortified squeak that sounded absurd coming from a being clad in cosmic fire. "So... how many do you want? Personally... I think... four would be adequate..."
A deep collective wheeze escaped Valerius’s lungs as Silas stood in the center of the ring, staring at her.
’Four...?’ Silas thought, his mind racing through the absurdity of the conversation happening inside an active smoking dimensional containment cube. ’She’s haggling over a kindergarten classroom?’
He sighed, lowering his arms completely.
"Haah..."
The water-mana dissipated into harmless mist around his wrists.
Silas reached up with his right hand, scratching the messy hair at the back of his neck with a slow resigned grimace.
He knew Seraphina.
Trying to argue logic with her when her pride and her fire were both dialed to maximum was like trying to put out an oil fire with paper towels.
...There was no escaping this. If he tried to deflect, she’d probably summon a volcanic lance just to interrogate his commitment.
He was just going to have to chest the entire thing and roll with the hit.
"Honestly?" Silas said as he looked straight into those glowing silver eyes. "As many as you want."
Seraphina froze.

The silver-white plasma in her eyes flared violently as a shade of red so intense it rivaled an active volcano rushed up her neck, across her cheeks, and straight to the tips of her ears, completely overpowering the divine radiance of the Primordial Spirit.
Her jaw dropped with her chest hitching as her breath hitched in her throat.
For three agonizing seconds, she stood paralyzed by his answer, completely short-circuited by how easily he had given in.
Then... her face went terrifyingly flat as the mortified bashfulness vanished and her features settled into an icy stone-cold mask of scrutiny.
’Did I do something...?’
SNAP!
Seraphina snapped her fingers.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
Without a single microsecond of warning, the entire pocket of oxygen within a five-foot sphere surrounding Silas spontaneously combusted into a concussive shockwave.

The detonation sounded like an artillery shell firing point-blank inside a sealed vault as a blinding flash of yellow-white flame ripped across the platform, the concussive pressure slamming violently into the basalt dome, rattling the runic seams of the isolation cube so hard that dust rained down from the ceiling baffles.
Silas emerged from the smoke with his slippers sliding backward three inches and a thin hastily deployed film of high-pressure water sizzling around his shoulders as he coughed against the acrid air.
"What was that for?!" Silas yelled through the haze.
Seraphina lowered her smoking hand with her glowing white eyes narrowing into two razor-thin slits of judgment as she stared through the vapor at him.
"I see..." Seraphina said, her dual-toned voice dripping with dangerous accusation that made the hair on Silas’s arms stand up.
"...So you want to knock me up four different times?"
’Why are you mad at me for going along with the flow...?’
Silas now stood three paces back from his original mark, rubbing the soot off his forearms where the water film had hissed into white steam.
Across the glass-slick platform, Seraphina’s hand dropped slowly to her hip with her smoking fingers curling into loose fists.
The silver-white fire clinging to her frame rippled like watered silk and threw long sharp shadows across the cracked slabs.
’...I don’t really mind,’ she thought, as the realization bloomed behind her breastbone in a dizzying rush of heat that had nothing to do with her core.
Honestly, she wouldn’t have cared if he’d said ten.
Her chest felt absurdly full of a warm fluttery lightness that made her want to kick the nearest boulder into dust just to burn off the extra energy.
He hadn’t balked and he hadn’t laughed it off as a joke either.
He had stood there in his violet pajamas and agreed to it with that irritating, unflinching calm of his, like anchoring his bloodline to hers weighed no more than ordering tea.
But she was young and she had no idea what to do with the warmth pooling behind her ribs other than set something on fire...

"Merging with the Primordial Fire Spirit grants my combustion a flat tenfold amplification," Seraphina said, her dual-toned voice slicing through the haze with a clear bell-like ring. "Every drop of mana I circulate right now carries ten times the output, ten times the density, and ten times the acceleration."
She rolled her shoulders and tilted her head from side to side until her neck gave a crisp crack.
The silver-white aura around her arms tightened until it clung to her skin like a second layer of molten scales.
Her red eyes had dissolved into solid plasma, and the runes across her cheekbones throbbed with luminous beats.

"So take this seriously, Graves," she warned, pointing a glowing finger at his chest. "If you try to hold back on me now, you won’t walk out of this cube on your own two feet... Draw your sword... Circulate your core and show me what a Gold Core looks like when it actually stops holding its breath. I know you’re capable of much more..."
She waited with her breath hitching slightly.

In her mind she could already see it... the foundation of a Gold Core Lord, the golden pressure tearing through the artificial ceiling and the crushing weight of a man who had killed so many monsters in the Khemet incident.
’I want the same feeling he gave off when he was with the World council...’
Sera wanted to see him unmasked, she wanted to feel the ceiling of the man she had claimed and across the ring, Silas let out a short quiet breath through his nose.
"Alright," he said simply. "I’ll take it seriously."
He nodded and rolled his right shoulder once then... nothing happened.
No golden aura tore through the floor and no world-ending pressure crashed down on the dome like Sera expected.
The full weight of a Gold Core stayed sealed beneath his flesh as if it didn’t exist at all.

The only thing that changed was his posture as his center of gravity settled by a fraction of an inch, his shoulders leveled, and the lazy teasing smirk vanished from his face, replaced by a cold flat stillness that made the air between them feel brittle.
Seraphina’s teeth clicked together.
’That’s it?!’
A furious indignant flame surged from her stomach into her throat as her knuckles went white as the fire coiled tighter around her forearms, hissing like agitated vipers.
"You arrogant—!"
Before the word cleared her lips, Silas vanished.
He didn’t dash at all... It was almost like he stopped existing...
One instant he was forty paces away, standing loose on the scorched stone and the next the air in front of her face folded inward with a crack that rattled the dome.
’—FAST!’
Her battle senses, sharpened by the spirit’s cosmic awareness, screamed down her spine.
Her silver-white pupils snapped left just in time to catch the blur of a violet pajama sleeve, dotted with little gold stars, cutting through the heat haze.
SWISH!
Silas arrived without a sound with his body pivoting on a needle-thin axis.
His left palm was already open with his fingers curved like talons, slicing through the barrier around her torso with effortless movements.
’Abyssal Sever!’

It wasn’t a sword strike but the thin crescent of hydro-mana coating his palm was compressed to a microscopic edge and as a result, it produced a blade of heavy water so dense it sheared the air into a high-pitched metallic shriek.
As expected, Seraphina didn’t retreat.
Backing down wasn’t in her blood, instead she snapped her right arm up and drove her elbow forward in a short vicious intercept wreathed in a three-thousand-degree solar mantle.
KRA-SHING!
It sounded like a diamond chisel striking a high-pressure boiler but his strike didn’t dissolve against her heat at all...
It bit into the solar mantle and sent the silver-white plasma scattering in ragged spitting chunks!
’His weight... it’s completely different from before!’ Seraphina realized, as the shockwave raced down her arm and rattled the bones of her shoulder.
He hadn’t raised his mana output but he had stopped pulling his weight.
And as a result... The raw power of a Lord who had tempered his flesh and marrow in battle was bearing down on her with the momentum of an iron press.
Before she could torque her hips to counter, Silas’s right hand whipped out from beneath his ribs.
’Hurricane Repulsion!’
He compressed the gale into a two-inch cylinder and pressed it flat against her solar plexus.
BANG!
The detonation punched through her balance as her feet left the stone and the violence hurled her backward like a ragdoll.
"Not yet!" she snarled mid-flight.
She twisted her spine with gymnastic ferocity and dug her heels into empty air.
Two jets of white-hot plasma exploded from the soles of her slippers and acted as retro-thrusters, murdering her backward momentum.
She planted herself sixty feet back with her slippers carving two glowing glass troughs into the platform and thrust both palms forward.
’That’s It... Flame-Slash!’
Sera was capable of producing several and so, she threw twelve.
Her arms became a blur of silver-white motion.
Crescent after crescent of compressed solar fire peeled off her fingertips and crisscrossed the cavern in an interlocking web of white-hot death that spanned the entire arena.
The radiant heat vitrified the broken stone under their path and turned the dust into drifting sparks of red glass.
One stray crescent sliced through the ceiling baffles and sent a rain of molten runes pouring down.
Valerius threw himself flat against the railing.
"THAT WAS A LOAD-BEARING RUNE! SHIT! THAT WAS A LOAD-BEARING RUNE!"
He had nabbed the prototype... how was he supposed to explain this to his father?!
’Cyclone Slipstream!’
A razor-thin current of wind wrapped around his ankles and calves like coiled springs, and his movement stopped being steps at all.
The air cracked every time he changed direction as where he’d stood a heartbeat earlier, a pale afterimage hung in the heat and tore apart.
Shift! Slide! Pivot! Whoosh!
He slipped through the gaps of her barrage with millimeter precision.
The first crescent screamed past his right shoulder and singed the hem of his violet collar.
The second shaved the air over his ducking head with the heat turning the moisture on his skin into vapor and a third cut through his afterimage a full half-second after he’d left it.
’S-so fast...!’ Harper gulped, she was aware that she was much stronger now but Silas could still beat her easily... Could Nitocris even beat him?
He rode the thermal updrafts her own spells created with his footwork flowing like water poured down an uneven slope, and closed the sixty-pace gap before she’d released the final crescent.
’He’s reading the trajectory before the mana even leaves my fingers!’ Seraphina thought with her battle high peaking into delirium. ’This is it! This is what I wanted!’
She didn’t wait for him to arrive, Sera slammed both palms into the glass and a wall of fire stood up between them like a curtain.
Silas went straight through it.
The Slipstream tore a hole in the flames, and his violet sleeve came out the other side smoking with one gold star scorched black and a fist already cocked at her face.
’Got you—’
’Not yet!’
She dropped under the punch, spun on her heel, and her flaming heel clipped his shoulder.
BAM!
He rolled with it, came up on one knee, and the glass behind him exploded outward in a ring of red shards.
’She’s good,’ Silas thought. ’She’s really good...’
"BURN TO ASH!" she roared, abandoning the weapons made of flame as she clapped her hands together.
BWOOOOOOM!

A colossal pillar of silver-white fire detonated from the bedrock directly under Silas’s feet and the column roared toward the basalt ceiling in a fifty feet wide geyser of primordial solar plasma meant to swallow him whole and atomize his water mantle down to hydrogen.
At the observation railing, Valerius ducked behind the barrier with his arm thrown over his face as the heat wave hammered his skin.
"SILAS!"
From the heart of the roaring white pillar, a deep hum rolled through the floor.
’Tidal Impact!’
The pillar didn’t hold him.
Two swirling spheres of black-blue heavy water, each the size of a siege carriage, tore outward from the center of the column like rotating mills.
The mass of the water was pressurized and freezing cold, and it crashed into the inward-curving walls of the solar pillar.
TSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSS!
A scream of boiling steam ripped through the cube and drowned out the baffles.
The shock between primordial heat and abyssal water shattered the bedrock for forty yards around them with the stone cracking into fine silt under the explosive expansion.
Through the blinding curtain of vapor, Seraphina saw the blue eyes and they...
...They looked cold and unimpressed
