She puffed her cheeks out with her silver bangs falling across her face.
"I am satisfied that your foundation is genuine!" she mumbled, her voice shrinking into a soft mortified squeak that sounded absurd coming from a being clad in cosmic fire.
"So... how many do you want?
Personally...
I think... four would be adequate..."
A deep collective wheeze escaped Valerius’s lungs as Silas stood in the center of the ring, staring at her.
’Four...?’ Silas thought, his mind racing through the absurdity of the conversation happening inside an active smoking dimensional containment cube. ’She’s haggling over a kindergarten classroom?’
He sighed, lowering his arms completely.
"Haah..."
The water-mana dissipated into harmless mist around his wrists.
Silas reached up with his right hand, scratching the messy hair at the back of his neck with a slow resigned grimace.
He knew Seraphina.
Trying to argue logic with her when her pride and her fire were both dialed to maximum was like trying to put out an oil fire with paper towels.
...There was no escaping this.
If he tried to deflect, she’d probably summon a volcanic lance just to interrogate his commitment.
He was just going to have to chest the entire thing and roll with the hit.
"Honestly?" Silas said as he looked straight into those glowing silver eyes.
"As many as you want."
Seraphina froze.

The silver-white plasma in her eyes flared violently as a shade of red so intense it rivaled an active volcano rushed up her neck, across her cheeks, and straight to the tips of her ears, completely overpowering the divine radiance of the Primordial Spirit.
Her jaw dropped with her chest hitching as her breath hitched in her throat.
For three agonizing seconds, she stood paralyzed by his answer, completely short-circuited by how easily he had given in.
Then... her face went terrifyingly flat as the mortified bashfulness vanished and her features settled into an icy stone-cold mask of scrutiny.
’Did I do something...?’
SNAP!
Seraphina snapped her fingers.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
Without a single microsecond of warning, the entire pocket of oxygen within a five-foot sphere surrounding Silas spontaneously combusted into a concussive shockwave.

The detonation sounded like an artillery shell firing point-blank inside a sealed vault as a blinding flash of yellow-white flame ripped across the platform, the concussive pressure slamming violently into the basalt dome, rattling the runic seams of the isolation cube so hard that dust rained down from the ceiling baffles.
Silas emerged from the smoke with his slippers sliding backward three inches and a thin hastily deployed film of high-pressure water sizzling around his shoulders as he coughed against the acrid air.
"What was that for?!" Silas yelled through the haze.
Seraphina lowered her smoking hand with her glowing white eyes narrowing into two razor-thin slits of judgment as she stared through the vapor at him.
"I see..." Seraphina said, her dual-toned voice dripping with dangerous accusation that made the hair on Silas’s arms stand up.
"...So you want to knock me up four different times?"
’Why are you mad at me for going along with the flow...?’
Silas now stood three paces back from his original mark, rubbing the soot off his forearms where the water film had hissed into white steam.
Across the glass-slick platform, Seraphina’s hand dropped slowly to her hip with her smoking fingers curling into loose fists.
The silver-white fire clinging to her frame rippled like watered silk and threw long sharp shadows across the cracked slabs.
’...I don’t really mind,’ she thought, as the realization bloomed behind her breastbone in a dizzying rush of heat that had nothing to do with her core.
Honestly, she wouldn’t have cared if he’d said ten.
Her chest felt absurdly full of a warm fluttery lightness that made her want to kick the nearest boulder into dust just to burn off the extra energy.
He hadn’t balked and he hadn’t laughed it off as a joke either.
He had stood there in his violet pajamas and agreed to it with that irritating, unflinching calm of his, like anchoring his bloodline to hers weighed no more than ordering tea.
But she was young and she had no idea what to do with the warmth pooling behind her ribs other than set something on fire...
"Merging with the Primordial Fire Spirit grants my combustion a flat tenfold amplification," Seraphina said, her dual-toned voice slicing through the haze with a clear bell-like ring.
"Every drop of mana I circulate right now carries ten times the output, ten times the density, and ten times the acceleration."
She rolled her shoulders and tilted her head from side to side until her neck gave a crisp crack.
The silver-white aura around her arms tightened until it clung to her skin like a second layer of molten scales.
Her red eyes had dissolved into solid plasma, and the runes across her cheekbones throbbed with luminous beats.
"So take this seriously, Graves," she warned, pointing a glowing finger at his chest.
"If you try to hold back on me now, you won’t walk out of this cube on your own two feet...
Draw your sword...
Circulate your core and show me what a Gold Core looks like when it actually stops holding its breath.
I know you’re capable of much more..."
She waited with her breath hitching slightly.

In her mind she could already see it... the foundation of a Gold Core Lord, the golden pressure tearing through the artificial ceiling and the crushing weight of a man who had killed so many monsters in the Khemet incident.
’I want the same feeling he gave off when he was with the World council...’
Sera wanted to see him unmasked, she wanted to feel the ceiling of the man she had claimed and across the ring, Silas let out a short quiet breath through his nose.
"Alright," he said simply.
"I’ll take it seriously."
He nodded and rolled his right shoulder once then... nothing happened.
No golden aura tore through the floor and no world-ending pressure crashed down on the dome like Sera expected.
The full weight of a Gold Core stayed sealed beneath his flesh as if it didn’t exist at all.

The only thing that changed was his posture as his center of gravity settled by a fraction of an inch, his shoulders leveled, and the lazy teasing smirk vanished from his face, replaced by a cold flat stillness that made the air between them feel brittle.
Seraphina’s teeth clicked together.
’That’s it?!’
A furious indignant flame surged from her stomach into her throat as her knuckles went white as the fire coiled tighter around her forearms, hissing like agitated vipers.
"You arrogant—!"
Before the word cleared her lips, Silas vanished.
He didn’t dash at all...
It was almost like he stopped existing...
One instant he was forty paces away, standing loose on the scorched stone and the next the air in front of her face folded inward with a crack that rattled the dome.
’—FAST!’
Her battle senses, sharpened by the spirit’s cosmic awareness, screamed down her spine.
Her silver-white pupils snapped left just in time to catch the blur of a violet pajama sleeve, dotted with little gold stars, cutting through the heat haze.
SWISH!
Silas arrived without a sound with his body pivoting on a needle-thin axis.
His left palm was already open with his fingers curved like talons, slicing through the barrier around her torso with effortless movements.
’Abyssal Sever!’

It wasn’t a sword strike but the thin crescent of hydro-mana coating his palm was compressed to a microscopic edge and as a result, it produced a blade of heavy water so dense it sheared the air into a high-pitched metallic shriek.
As expected, Seraphina didn’t retreat.
Backing down wasn’t in her blood, instead she snapped her right arm up and drove her elbow forward in a short vicious intercept wreathed in a three-thousand-degree solar mantle.
KRA-SHING!
It sounded like a diamond chisel striking a high-pressure boiler but his strike didn’t dissolve against her heat at all...
It bit into the solar mantle and sent the silver-white plasma scattering in ragged spitting chunks!
’His weight... it’s completely different from before!’ Seraphina realized, as the shockwave raced down her arm and rattled the bones of her shoulder.
He hadn’t raised his mana output but he had stopped pulling his weight.
And as a result...
The raw power of a Lord who had tempered his flesh and marrow in battle was bearing down on her with the momentum of an iron press.
Before she could torque her hips to counter, Silas’s right hand whipped out from beneath his ribs.
’Hurricane Repulsion!’
He compressed the gale into a two-inch cylinder and pressed it flat against her solar plexus.
BANG!
The detonation punched through her balance as her feet left the stone and the violence hurled her backward like a ragdoll.
"Not yet!" she snarled mid-flight.
She twisted her spine with gymnastic ferocity and dug her heels into empty air.
Two jets of white-hot plasma exploded from the soles of her slippers and acted as retro-thrusters, murdering her backward momentum.
She planted herself sixty feet back with her slippers carving two glowing glass troughs into the platform and thrust both palms forward.
’That’s It...
Flame-Slash!’
Sera was capable of producing several and so, she threw twelve.
Her arms became a blur of silver-white motion.
Crescent after crescent of compressed solar fire peeled off her fingertips and crisscrossed the cavern in an interlocking web of white-hot death that spanned the entire arena.
The radiant heat vitrified the broken stone under their path and turned the dust into drifting sparks of red glass.
One stray crescent sliced through the ceiling baffles and sent a rain of molten runes pouring down.
Valerius threw himself flat against the railing.
"THAT WAS A LOAD-BEARING RUNE!
SHIT!
THAT WAS A LOAD-BEARING RUNE!"
He had nabbed the prototype... how was he supposed to explain this to his father?!
’Cyclone Slipstream!’
A razor-thin current of wind wrapped around his ankles and calves like coiled springs, and his movement stopped being steps at all.
The air cracked every time he changed direction as where he’d stood a heartbeat earlier, a pale afterimage hung in the heat and tore apart.
Shift!
Slide!
Pivot!
Whoosh!
He slipped through the gaps of her barrage with millimeter precision.
The first crescent screamed past his right shoulder and singed the hem of his violet collar.
The second shaved the air over his ducking head with the heat turning the moisture on his skin into vapor and a third cut through his afterimage a full half-second after he’d left it.
’S-so fast...!’ Harper gulped, she was aware that she was much stronger now but Silas could still beat her easily...
Could Nitocris even beat him?
He rode the thermal updrafts her own spells created with his footwork flowing like water poured down an uneven slope, and closed the sixty-pace gap before she’d released the final crescent.
’He’s reading the trajectory before the mana even leaves my fingers!’ Seraphina thought with her battle high peaking into delirium. ’This is it!
This is what I wanted!’
She didn’t wait for him to arrive, Sera slammed both palms into the glass and a wall of fire stood up between them like a curtain.
Silas went straight through it.
The Slipstream tore a hole in the flames, and his violet sleeve came out the other side smoking with one gold star scorched black and a fist already cocked at her face.
’Got you—’
’Not yet!’
She dropped under the punch, spun on her heel, and her flaming heel clipped his shoulder.
BAM!
He rolled with it, came up on one knee, and the glass behind him exploded outward in a ring of red shards.
’She’s good,’ Silas thought. ’She’s really good...’
"BURN TO ASH!" she roared, abandoning the weapons made of flame as she clapped her hands together.
BWOOOOOOM!

A colossal pillar of silver-white fire detonated from the bedrock directly under Silas’s feet and the column roared toward the basalt ceiling in a fifty feet wide geyser of primordial solar plasma meant to swallow him whole and atomize his water mantle down to hydrogen.
At the observation railing, Valerius ducked behind the barrier with his arm thrown over his face as the heat wave hammered his skin.
"SILAS!"
From the heart of the roaring white pillar, a deep hum rolled through the floor.
’Tidal Impact!’
The pillar didn’t hold him.
Two swirling spheres of black-blue heavy water, each the size of a siege carriage, tore outward from the center of the column like rotating mills.
The mass of the water was pressurized and freezing cold, and it crashed into the inward-curving walls of the solar pillar.
TSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSS!
A scream of boiling steam ripped through the cube and drowned out the baffles.
The shock between primordial heat and abyssal water shattered the bedrock for forty yards around them with the stone cracking into fine silt under the explosive expansion.
Through the blinding curtain of vapor, Seraphina saw the blue eyes and they...
...They looked cold and unimpressed

chapters.title: Chapter 665: Sign These Papers [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Silas broke through the steam like a phantom and Seraphina met him head-on.
They collided in the center of the crater, and the ground gave up.
WHAM!
Her fist met his palm and the shockwave blew the steam apart in a perfect ring.
CRACK!
His elbow met her forearm.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
Three more in a single blink as she hooked high and he slipped low.
’So fast and annoying... Let me win this already!’
She drove a knee at his ribs and he checked it with his shin.
"HUAAAA!"
She spat a lance of fire at his face as an explosion occured mid-air however Silas parted it with a sweep of wind with the flames splitting around his head and scorching the glass behind him black.
Every clash cracked the floor wider, and the cracks raced out to the walls and climbed them.
’More! More! MORE!’ Seraphina thought while laughing as her blood sang.
’She’s still speeding up...’ Silas thought, his jaw tightening. ’How is she still speeding up?!’
She caught his sleeve and yanked.

He went with it and hooked a leg around hers, and the two of them crashed to the floor and rolled with fire and water hissing between them, until he planted a foot in her stomach and kicked her off him like a stone from a catapult.
WHAM!
She hit the wall thirty yards out and the wall caved in around her shoulders.
"HAHAHAHA!" came a voice from the dust. "AGAIN!"
She came back at him with the rubble still falling off her.
She threw a vicious solar-infused uppercut meant to shear his jaw from his skull with her knuckles trailing a tail of silver lightning.
’...She’s like a masochist.’
Silas tilted his head back half an inch, felt the heat lick his eyelashes, and slipped his left forearm over her bicep.
Catch! Trap! Twist!
He deflected her arm upward, stepped deep into her stance with his right foot hooked behind her heel, and drove his right palm into her collarbone with a concussive burst of wind.
THUD!
The force rattled her teeth.
Her knees buckled, but the spirit state refused to let her fall as she turned the rebound into a spinning back-elbow with the flames along her arm flaring into a jagged blade of compressed plasma.
Silas dropped under the arc with his dark hair brushing her burning sleeve.
’I need to end this quickly...’
Sera was a good opponent but this heat was getting annoying and also, she was burning his pajamas and he liked them...

Silas brought his right fist up from his hip in a short devastating hook and caught her squarely in the side of the ribs which was the exact point where her spirit circulation looped through her core.
CRACK-BANG!
It sounded like a timber splintering under an axe.
"Guh—!"
The breath ripped out of her lungs as the silver-white runes along her ribs flickered like a dying lamp.
Her momentum stalled completely, and her vision narrowed to a pinprick of dark gray and Silas didn’t hesitate.
He finished the pivot with his left hand coming down like an iron guillotine toward the base of her neck.

In one last feral surge of pride, Seraphina gathered every remaining drop of the spirit’s unbound energy into her right palm and thrust it at his chest in a point-blank volcanic lance meant to trade blows at the cost of her own consciousness.
"DIE—!"
WHOOSH!
Before the lance could leave her hand, Silas was simply no longer there.
’Cyclone Slipstream!’
He moved faster than her perception could follow, creating an instant high-velocity displacement that left a swirling vacuum of cool air where his torso had been.
Her blast tore through empty space, soared into the basalt dome, and carved a smoking molten trench through the ceiling.
A fraction of a second later and a solid heavy palm pressed against the small of her back.
Tap!
It was a gentle pulse of soul magic, slipping between the seams of her active meridians and finding the place where her soul and the Primordial Spirit’s were fused together.
’Spirit Tap.’
SHATTER!
The silver-white flames covering her body snapped out like a blown candle.

Her starlit silver hair collapsed back into its natural unruly deep crimson and tumbled limp across her bare shoulders as the plasma in her eyes dissolved, leaving wide dazed red eyes that couldn’t find their focus.
The runes vanished from her skin, leaving only pale flushed porcelain covered in a light sheen of sweat.
Seraphina’s knees gave way.
She hit the shattered floor with a dull clumsy thud with her palms sliding against the cooling glass.
Her chest heaved in shallow gasps, and her fingers trembled as she tried to find purchase on the smooth stone.

The cavern fell into ringing silence as Silas stood two paces away with his hands resting easily at his sides with his violet pajama shirt stained with soot and steam, breathing slowly as if he had just finished an unhurried morning jog around the garden.
"He stopped it...?"
Seraphina stared down at her trembling hands.
The heat was gone... The tenfold multiplier was gone and her body felt heavier than lead as every muscle was aching with the dull hollow ache of spirit backlash.
She let out a long shuddering breath and let her head hang so her red hair hid her face.
"...I lost," she mumbled, the words tasting like copper and ash on her tongue. "Completely."
A loud piercing whistle shattered the quiet.
"YES! That’s what I’m talking about!" Harper cheered from the railing, leaning over the brass bar with a bright triumphant grin.

She pushed her glasses up with a sharp finger and tossed her long violet hair over her shoulder. "Did you see that footwork?! Silas, you dismantled her like a cheap grandfather clock! Absolutely immaculate!"
Beside her, Valerius let out a breath he felt like he’d been holding for ten minutes with his shoulders dropping in relief.
He leaned against the railing, staring down at the ruined glass-slick crater with wide reverent golden eyes.

’Holy hell...’ Valerius thought, his hands still trembling slightly from the mana pressure that had leaked past the dampers. ’He didn’t even use the Gold Core’s true reserve... He took her down with basic water arts and wind against a tenfold spirit multiplier... I really need to learn that technique if I ever want to keep up with these monsters, even Harper has gotten noticeably sharper since the Secret Realm expedition... if I keep slacking off on father’s business, I’m going to be left so far behind I won’t even see their dust.’
He glanced at Harper, who was still grinning down at the pit, then shook his head with an appreciative chuckle.
"Remind me never to get on Silas’s bad side. He’d kill me..."
Down on the platform, Seraphina hadn’t moved.
She stayed on her hands and knees with her face burning hotter than her flames ever could.
Under the thin fabric of her clothes, a different and mortifying sensation was registering through her dazed nerves.
’I’m... I’m completely soaked,’ she realized, her jaw clenching as a hot shameful shiver ran up her spine.
It wasn’t just the residual steam from Silas’s water arts clinging to her skin.
Her core felt molten, and her thighs trembled with a heavy ache that made her cheeks burn like live coals.
’Perhaps... this is the difference between Mother and me,’ the thought wandered through her scattered mind which was already half-delirious from exhaustion.
According to everything Etilga had drilled into her during the clan’s private matriarchal lectures, a true daughter of House Bloom was meant to dominate.
Her mother reveled in looking down on men, breaking their pride across negotiation tables, and keeping consorts on short leash-length lines of deference.
Etilga commanded the room, commanded the clan, and commanded the bed too.
Seraphina, on the other hand...
She liked this.
She liked the overwhelming certainty of a man who could look at her apex flames, casually step inside her reach, and fold her pride over his knee without raising his voice.
Having him stand over her looking victorious and unmovable... it made her feel deliciously... shamefully weak.
’It makes me completely degenerate,’ she thought, burying her burning face in her hands with her shoulders shaking slightly. ’I’m a total pervert... but gods, it feels good.’
Before she could finish wallowing in her own scandalous thoughts, a shadow fell over her.
Silas walked up, paused, and bent at the waist.

Without a word of warning or a single request for permission, he slid his right arm beneath her knees and his left arm behind her back and scooped her off the shattered granite in a smooth effortless princess carry.
"W-What—?!" Seraphina gasped, her arms flying up to knot around his neck.

"You’re done for the morning," Silas said, turning toward the perimeter exit with an easy, unbothered stride. "The spirit backlash is going to lock your meridians in five minutes so I’m taking you outside before you pass out on the rubble."
Seraphina’s mouth opened and closed like a stranded carp.
Her face was pressed against the curve of his collarbone with the scent of rainwater filling her nose.

She squeezed her eyes shut and tried to sink into the fabric of his shirt to hide how red she was, then Silas’s left hand shifted with his fingers adjusting their grip beneath her lower back and thighs.
His brow furrowed.
He paused mid-step and looked down at her with a remarkably puzzled expression.
"Hey, Sera," Silas asked curiously. "Did you... pee yourself or something? Your shorts are completely soaked."
The artificial cavern seemed to freeze solid.
Seraphina’s eyes snapped open. Her pupils shook with an mix of mortification and violent panic.
"I DID NOT PEE MYSELF, YOU OBTUSE, INSENSITIVE BRUTE!" she shrieked at the top of her lungs.
Her fists flew out, raining furious smacks against his chest, his shoulder and the side of his face.
Smack! Thwack! Pat!
There was zero mana behind them.
Silas burst out laughing and leaned his head back to dodge the wild fists as he kept walking.
They didn’t hurt in the slightest... After the iron-splitting solar hooks she’d been throwing two minutes ago, this felt like being pelted with wet cotton balls.
"Alright, alright! Calm down!" Silas chuckled, shaking his head. "I was just asking! You don’t have to break my jaw over it!"
"DIE! DROWN IN A DITCH AND DIE!" she wailed, burying her face into his pajama collar again, though her arms refused to loosen their iron grip around his neck.
They reached the perimeter platform where Harper and Valerius were waiting by the archway.
Harper leaned against the railing with her arms crossed, looking down at Seraphina with a smug satisfied smirk that radiated petty triumph.

"Well, well," Harper purred, her violet eyes gleaming with mocking delight. "Look who got her teeth handed to her before breakfast was even digested... Congratulations, Silas. It’s always a public service when someone reminds the Bloom clan that shouting loudly doesn’t substitute for actual skill, Weak!"
Seraphina’s head whipped around with her red hair flying wild.
Even carried like a sack of flour, her pride flared like an open gas line.
"Who are you calling weak, you oversized corporate vulture?!" Seraphina snarled.
Without warning, she snapped her right foot out in a vicious spiteful kick aimed squarely at Harper’s smug face but Harper didn’t even flinch.
With the effortless grace of someone who had seen the childish retaliation coming five seconds in advance, she simply tilted her upper body three inches to the left.
The kick whistled through empty air and stirred a lock of Harper’s violet hair.
Harper’s smirk only widened.
"Missed... How typical."

"Agh! Let me down! Silas, put me down right now so I can strangle her!" Seraphina complained, squirming in his arms like a petulant toddler and kicking her legs at the air. "She’s insufferable! She’s a menace to society!"
"Stop moving before I drop you on your head," Silas grunted, tightening his grip around her waist as he stepped past Harper toward the shimmering gray mist of the archway.
Valerius followed close behind, laughing under his breath.
As they crossed the threshold back into the warmth of Silas’s living room, he reached out and tapped the silver runes along the arch’s frame.
With a series of sharp pressurized hisses, the obsidian archway folded inward, collapsing like an origami box until the matte-black cube clicked shut on the hardwood.
Valerius scooped it up with one hand, tossed it lightly in the air, and slid it back into the interior pocket of his charcoal vest.
"Man," Valerius sighed, running a hand through his slightly charred golden hair. "Remind me to charge my old man double for the stress-testing data... That was wild."
Silas walked over to the leather sectional, turned around, and deposited Seraphina onto the cushions.
"Oof," she grunted as she sank into the deep leather, pulling her knees up to her chest and wrapping her oversized white sleeves around her shins.
She looked thoroughly rumpled with her red hair a tangled mess, but the arrogant satisfied curve of her lips was slowly returning now that she was off the cold stone.
Silas collapsed into the armchair across from her and let his head fall back against the headrest.
He took a long deep breath through his nose and let his shoulders drop completely.
"Alright," he said, opening one eye and looking straight at her with a slow teasing smirk. "I won... Decisively, if I recall... Where’s my reward?"
Seraphina’s posture went rigid.
The pale length of her throat flushed bright pink again. She tugged the oversized cuffs of her shirt down over her knuckles and avoided his eyes as she shifted against the cushions.

"I... I haven’t finalized the exact details yet," she stammered with her voice dropping to a quietembarrassed mumble. "A reward of that caliber requires proper aristocratic preparation... You can’t just demand it on the spot like a street urchin."
"Right," Silas chuckled, rolling his eyes. "Classic stall tactic."
"I am not stalling!" Seraphina fired back, her chin snapping up.
She reached into her spatial inventory.
Fwip!

With a crisp flick of her wrist, she pulled out a thick sheaf of parchment bound with a dark crimson silk ribbon and sealed with the wax crest of House Bloom, a blooming lotus entwined with twin curved daggers.
She leaned across the low table and thrust the parchment into his chest.
"Sign it," she commanded, trying desperately to sound authoritative.
Silas took the heavy papers and glanced at the ornate calligraphy stamped across the cover.
His eyebrows climbed toward his hairline.

"These are..." Silas slowly turned the first page, his blue eyes scanning the dense legal clauses, the mutual property annexes, and the ancestral seal at the bottom. "...the formal engagement registries for House Bloom? The papers that officially make me your betrothed consort?"

She hit the shattered floor with a dull clumsy thud with her palms sliding against the cooling glass.
Her chest heaved in shallow gasps, and her fingers trembled as she tried to find purchase on the smooth stone.

The cavern fell into ringing silence as Silas stood two paces away with his hands resting easily at his sides with his violet pajama shirt stained with soot and steam, breathing slowly as if he had just finished an unhurried morning jog around the garden.
"He stopped it...?"
Seraphina stared down at her trembling hands.
The heat was gone...
The tenfold multiplier was gone and her body felt heavier than lead as every muscle was aching with the dull hollow ache of spirit backlash.
She let out a long shuddering breath and let her head hang so her red hair hid her face.
"...I lost," she mumbled, the words tasting like copper and ash on her tongue.
"Completely."
A loud piercing whistle shattered the quiet.
"YES!
That’s what I’m talking about!" Harper cheered from the railing, leaning over the brass bar with a bright triumphant grin.
She pushed her glasses up with a sharp finger and tossed her long violet hair over her shoulder.
"Did you see that footwork?!
Silas, you dismantled her like a cheap grandfather clock!
Absolutely immaculate!"
Beside her, Valerius let out a breath he felt like he’d been holding for ten minutes with his shoulders dropping in relief.
He leaned against the railing, staring down at the ruined glass-slick crater with wide reverent golden eyes.
’Holy hell...’ Valerius thought, his hands still trembling slightly from the mana pressure that had leaked past the dampers. ’He didn’t even use the Gold Core’s true reserve...
He took her down with basic water arts and wind against a tenfold spirit multiplier...

I really need to learn that technique if I ever want to keep up with these monsters, even Harper has gotten noticeably sharper since the Secret Realm expedition... if I keep slacking off on father’s business, I’m going to be left so far behind I won’t even see their dust.’
He glanced at Harper, who was still grinning down at the pit, then shook his head with an appreciative chuckle.
"Remind me never to get on Silas’s bad side.
He’d kill me..."
Down on the platform, Seraphina hadn’t moved.
She stayed on her hands and knees with her face burning hotter than her flames ever could.
Under the thin fabric of her clothes, a different and mortifying sensation was registering through her dazed nerves.
I’m completely soaked,’ she realized, her jaw clenching as a hot shameful shiver ran up her spine.
It wasn’t just the residual steam from Silas’s water arts clinging to her skin.
Her core felt molten, and her thighs trembled with a heavy ache that made her cheeks burn like live coals.
’Perhaps... this is the difference between Mother and me,’ the thought wandered through her scattered mind which was already half-delirious from exhaustion.
According to everything Etilga had drilled into her during the clan’s private matriarchal lectures, a true daughter of House Bloom was meant to dominate.
Her mother reveled in looking down on men, breaking their pride across negotiation tables, and keeping consorts on short leash-length lines of deference.
Etilga commanded the room, commanded the clan, and commanded the bed too.
Seraphina, on the other hand...
She liked this.
She liked the overwhelming certainty of a man who could look at her apex flames, casually step inside her reach, and fold her pride over his knee without raising his voice.
Having him stand over her looking victorious and unmovable... it made her feel deliciously... shamefully weak.
’It makes me completely degenerate,’ she thought, burying her burning face in her hands with her shoulders shaking slightly. ’I’m a total pervert... but gods, it feels good.’
Before she could finish wallowing in her own scandalous thoughts, a shadow fell over her.
Silas walked up, paused, and bent at the waist.

Without a word of warning or a single request for permission, he slid his right arm beneath her knees and his left arm behind her back and scooped her off the shattered granite in a smooth effortless princess carry.
"W-What—?!" Seraphina gasped, her arms flying up to knot around his neck.
"You’re done for the morning," Silas said, turning toward the perimeter exit with an easy, unbothered stride.
"The spirit backlash is going to lock your meridians in five minutes so I’m taking you outside before you pass out on the rubble."
Seraphina’s mouth opened and closed like a stranded carp.
Her face was pressed against the curve of his collarbone with the scent of rainwater filling her nose.

She squeezed her eyes shut and tried to sink into the fabric of his shirt to hide how red she was, then Silas’s left hand shifted with his fingers adjusting their grip beneath her lower back and thighs.
His brow furrowed.
He paused mid-step and looked down at her with a remarkably puzzled expression.
"Hey, Sera," Silas asked curiously.
"Did you... pee yourself or something?
Your shorts are completely soaked."
The artificial cavern seemed to freeze solid.
Seraphina’s eyes snapped open.
Her pupils shook with an mix of mortification and violent panic.
"I DID NOT PEE MYSELF, YOU OBTUSE, INSENSITIVE BRUTE!" she shrieked at the top of her lungs.
Her fists flew out, raining furious smacks against his chest, his shoulder and the side of his face.
Smack!
Thwack!
Pat!
There was zero mana behind them.
Silas burst out laughing and leaned his head back to dodge the wild fists as he kept walking.
They didn’t hurt in the slightest...
After the iron-splitting solar hooks she’d been throwing two minutes ago, this felt like being pelted with wet cotton balls.
"Alright, alright!
Calm down!" Silas chuckled, shaking his head.
"I was just asking!
You don’t have to break my jaw over it!"
"DIE!
DROWN IN A DITCH AND DIE!" she wailed, burying her face into his pajama collar again, though her arms refused to loosen their iron grip around his neck.
They reached the perimeter platform where Harper and Valerius were waiting by the archway.
Harper leaned against the railing with her arms crossed, looking down at Seraphina with a smug satisfied smirk that radiated petty triumph.
"Well, well," Harper purred, her violet eyes gleaming with mocking delight.
"Look who got her teeth handed to her before breakfast was even digested...
Congratulations, Silas.
It’s always a public service when someone reminds the Bloom clan that shouting loudly doesn’t substitute for actual skill, Weak!"
Seraphina’s head whipped around with her red hair flying wild.
Even carried like a sack of flour, her pride flared like an open gas line.
"Who are you calling weak, you oversized corporate vulture?!" Seraphina snarled.
Without warning, she snapped her right foot out in a vicious spiteful kick aimed squarely at Harper’s smug face but Harper didn’t even flinch.
With the effortless grace of someone who had seen the childish retaliation coming five seconds in advance, she simply tilted her upper body three inches to the left.
The kick whistled through empty air and stirred a lock of Harper’s violet hair.
Harper’s smirk only widened.
"Missed...
How typical."
"Agh!
Let me down!
Silas, put me down right now so I can strangle her!" Seraphina complained, squirming in his arms like a petulant toddler and kicking her legs at the air.
"She’s insufferable!
She’s a menace to society!"
"Stop moving before I drop you on your head," Silas grunted, tightening his grip around her waist as he stepped past Harper toward the shimmering gray mist of the archway.
Valerius followed close behind, laughing under his breath.
As they crossed the threshold back into the warmth of Silas’s living room, he reached out and tapped the silver runes along the arch’s frame.
With a series of sharp pressurized hisses, the obsidian archway folded inward, collapsing like an origami box until the matte-black cube clicked shut on the hardwood.
Valerius scooped it up with one hand, tossed it lightly in the air, and slid it back into the interior pocket of his charcoal vest.
"Man," Valerius sighed, running a hand through his slightly charred golden hair.
"Remind me to charge my old man double for the stress-testing data...
That was wild."
Silas walked over to the leather sectional, turned around, and deposited Seraphina onto the cushions.
"Oof," she grunted as she sank into the deep leather, pulling her knees up to her chest and wrapping her oversized white sleeves around her shins.
She looked thoroughly rumpled with her red hair a tangled mess, but the arrogant satisfied curve of her lips was slowly returning now that she was off the cold stone.
Silas collapsed into the armchair across from her and let his head fall back against the headrest.
He took a long deep breath through his nose and let his shoulders drop completely.
"Alright," he said, opening one eye and looking straight at her with a slow teasing smirk.
"I won...
Decisively, if I recall...
Where’s my reward?"
Seraphina’s posture went rigid.
The pale length of her throat flushed bright pink again.
She tugged the oversized cuffs of her shirt down over her knuckles and avoided his eyes as she shifted against the cushions.
I haven’t finalized the exact details yet," she stammered with her voice dropping to a quietembarrassed mumble.
"A reward of that caliber requires proper aristocratic preparation...
You can’t just demand it on the spot like a street urchin."
"Right," Silas chuckled, rolling his eyes.
"Classic stall tactic."
"I am not stalling!" Seraphina fired back, her chin snapping up.
She reached into her spatial inventory.
Fwip!

With a crisp flick of her wrist, she pulled out a thick sheaf of parchment bound with a dark crimson silk ribbon and sealed with the wax crest of House Bloom, a blooming lotus entwined with twin curved daggers.
She leaned across the low table and thrust the parchment into his chest.
"Sign it," she commanded, trying desperately to sound authoritative.
Silas took the heavy papers and glanced at the ornate calligraphy stamped across the cover.
His eyebrows climbed toward his hairline.
"These are..." Silas slowly turned the first page, his blue eyes scanning the dense legal clauses, the mutual property annexes, and the ancestral seal at the bottom.
"...the formal engagement registries for House Bloom?
The papers that officially make me your betrothed consort?"

chapters.title: Chapter 666: Alleyway Trouble [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Seraphina nodded with her expression suddenly remarkably sweet as her red eyes went wide and bright with a mix of desperate hope and stubborn pride.

"Yes," she said softly, leaning forward on her elbows. "Those are the papers. You beat me at full power... You proved your foundation is solid enough to stand beside me, so naturally I want you to sign them right now so we can submit them to the archives before the council convenes."
Silas stared down at the crisp paper in his hands and a cold tingle ran across the back of his neck.
’I really don’t want to sign this right now,’ Silas thought, as a quiet drop of cold sweat rolled down his temple.
It wasn’t that he disliked her.

Despite her temper, her ridiculous pride and her borderline crazy combat habits, Seraphina was fiercely loyal, genuine to a fault, and absurdly endearing when she wasn’t trying to incinerate his eyebrows.
But an official legally binding betrothal to the heiress of House Bloom?
That meant dragging the whole bureaucratic monster of the World Council into his private life.
It meant clan elders, political audits, and endless formal inquiries that would inevitably draw unwanted attention toward him and his family too.
’It’s a massive mountain of added stress,’ he mused, tapping his thumb against the wax seal. ’Though... having House Bloom’s backing in the high courts wouldn’t be the worst thing in the world—’
CRACKLE-SNAP!
A blinding violet bolt of lightning struck the low table.
Silas flinched and pulled his hands back as the electric discharge scorched the cedar.

The heavy paper in his grip was instantly caught in a miniature vortex of black sand and purple voltage with the high-tier paper disintegrating into a shower of harmless gray ash that drifted down onto the Persian rug.
Silas blinked at his empty hands and Seraphina’s jaw dropped.
Standing right beside the couch, Harper slowly lowered her right hand, her violet eyes burning with furious indignation from behind her glasses.
"What?!" Harper snapped, her voice ringing out in sharp, incredulous outrage. "You shameless little bitch! Why are you trying to jump the line?!"
Seraphina shot up from the couch like a launched missile, her hands clenched into trembling fists.
"YOU, YOU RUINED THE SEALS!"

"Of course I ruined them!" Harper yelled back, pointing an accusing finger at Seraphina’s nose. "We went on one double date, the shopping, the dinner, that stupid auction, not even a month ago! He hasn’t even visited your family’s main estate, and you’re already ambushing him in his own living room with binding marriage contracts?! What kind of desperate garbage is this?!"

"It is strategic consolidation!" Seraphina shrieked, stamping her foot. "He beat me! The terms were set! You’re just jealous because House Whitmore doesn’t have an approved consort draft ready to deploy!"
"Jealous of what?! An unhinged firebug who pees herself during a friendly spar?!"
"I DID NOT PEE MYSELF, YOU PURPLE-HAIRED PARASITE!"

The two women were practically nose to nose with sparks of crimson fire and crackles of violet static dancing between their glares and their voices bouncing off the walls in a chaotic escalating war of words that showed no sign of slowing down.
"You couldn’t even wait for him to finish his tea, you impatient little furnace!" Harper snapped. "He hasn’t even had breakfast!"
"At least I’m brave enough to put it on paper, you coward! You’ve been hiding behind your glasses and your stupid lightning for weeks, waiting for him to notice you!"
"I’m not hiding!"
"You’re being a coward!"
"You peed yourself!"
"I DID NOT PEE MYSELF!" Seraphina screamed, and a ring of sparks flew off her shoulders and set the corner of a sofa cushion smoking.
"The cushion, Sera!" Harper shrieked. "That’s a good cushion!"
"Then put it out, you purple-haired witch!"
"With what?! I don’t have water powers!"
Both of them froze and looked at Silas.
Silas, who had already lifted his teacup to cover his face, took a calm sip.
"Don’t look at me," he said. "Also I’m charging you too from the couch."
Silas lowered the teacup an inch with a huge bead of sweat rolling down the side of his neck, and looked over at Valerius.
The blond noble was sitting at the opposite end of the sectional, staring at Silas with an expression of soul-deep disgust.

’Lucky, miserable bastard,’ Valerius thought bitterly, slumping against the armrest. ’Two heiresses tearing the room apart over who gets to marry him first, and he’s sitting there drinking cold tea like it’s a Tuesday morning... I hate him... I genuinely hate his entire existence...’
Valerius cleared his throat loudly, deliberately tuning out the screaming match two feet to his left.
He leaned forward with his elbows on his knees and looked straight at Silas.
"Hey, Silas," Valerius called out, raising his voice to cut through the bickering. "Do you want to meet up in the Sovereign Realm later this week?"
Silas blinked and set his cup down. "The Sovereign Realm?"

"Yeah," Valerius nodded, his golden eyes brightening with real interest. "The Umbral Basin where Blessed Land sits is classified as an Unknown Zone, right? It’s completely cut off from the standard trade routes... After the whole mess with the Council, did you ever manage to get yourself some kind of access to Central City?"
Silas paused as his memory clicked into place.
"Oh," he said, rubbing the back of his neck. "Yeah, I got something."

He remembered the dense black basalt tile Musvi had handed him across the bone counter of the archive, the silver and violet mandala etched across its face with the hawk and compass stamped on the back.
It was sitting in his inventory, completely unused.

’It only works once I embed it into the Keep’s bedrock,’ Silas thought. ’I haven’t done that yet. Once I do, I’ll be able to walk straight to Central City whenever I want... but until then, I’ll just follow Evelyn there. She’s leaving anyway.’
Valerius slapped his knee with a wide infectious grin.

"Perfect! Then let’s meet in Central City! Sterling Enterprises has a permanent commercial lodge in the Third Ring. I’ll give you a proper tour of the whole metropolis, the sovereign exchanges, the black market pavilions, the high-tier alchemy guilds, all of it... I’ll bring Mia along, too. She’s been wanting to stretch her legs outside the territory and you should bring Aeliana! It’ll be a solid group."
Silas let out a quiet, appreciative chuckle and ran a hand through his dark hair.
"Man, I’d love to," he said honestly, with an apologetic grimace. "Sounds like a great time. But... I’m actually already heading to Central City with someone else later today."
The living room went dead silent as the screaming match between Harper and Seraphina cut off so fast it was as if someone had severed the audio feed.
Both girls slowly turned their heads toward the armchair.
Harper’s violet eyes narrowed behind her glasses, and her arms dropped to her sides with sudden chilling poise.
Seraphina’s red eyes widened, and a low dangerous heat began radiating from her collarbones again.
Valerius raised an eyebrow and leaned in with open curiosity. "With someone else? Who?"
Silas looked between the three of them, completely unbothered by the sudden spike in atmospheric pressure.
"Evelyn," Silas answered simply.
Seraphina’s mouth opened and closed.
The heat creeping off her collarbones dropped a few degrees, replaced by the sulky deflated look of someone who had been ready for a much better fight.
"Evelyn," Harper repeated slowly, pushing her glasses up her nose. "The one in the hoodie that saved us last time right?"
"She’s heading to Central City today anyway, and I haven’t set up my own way there yet," Silas said, scratching his cheek. "So I’m just going to follow her... It’s the easiest option."
"That’s it?" Seraphina demanded. "That’s the whole reason?"
"What else would it be?"
The two of them stared at him the way people stare at a very handsome rock, and Valerius dropped his face into his palm and groaned into it.
"I’ll come later today then."
"Mm," Harper said, and took the teacup out of Silas’s hand and sipped from it herself with enormous dignity, as if to prove she was perfectly calm.
"That’s my tea."
"...It’s cold anyway, bitch."
Seraphina tried to launch off the couch to protest, got about halfway up, and her legs promptly folded like wet paper.
She flopped back onto the cushions with a thump and a long wounded wheeze, and Harper’s smirk came back so fast it was almost rude.
"Just sit for five minutes..."
"I will remember this," Seraphina muttered into a cushion. "All of it. Every second."
"I’ll send you the lodge address, Silas," Valerius said, already standing and brushing soot off his vest. "Whenever you’re through the gate, just find me."
"Thanks, Val. I can call you that right?"
In the other district of Valoria City’s southern edge, the afternoon sun rarely touched the ground.

Steam drifted from an iron exhaust pipe overhead and wrapped around the fire escapes that clung to the brickwork like skeletons as a small woman walked down the center of the passage with her boots stepping over the cracked cobblestones without a sound.
She was swallowed by an oversized dark-gray hoodie with the hem hanging down over her cargo pants and her hood pulled low over a messy bun of black hair.
"Mmm... I’ll soon be going back to the Sovereign Realm."
A slim cigarette hung from her lips, lit with a snap of mana and a thin ribbon of blue-gray smoke trailing over her shoulder.
Her face looked permanently exhausted, but beneath the hood, her sharp dark eyes scanned the masonry.
’So... I’m meeting Silas later today, and he’s following me to Central City,’ Evelyn thought, pulling the cigarette from her lips with two fingers and blowing a cloud of smoke at the damp brickwork.
She watched it curl and fade against the cold iron of an overhead fire escape.
Lord Sky had been quiet for weeks.
The comment sections were probably a warzone by now, hundreds of millions of followers screaming into the void, wondering whether the undefeated Lord had finally fallen off the face of the earth.
A masked voice-modulated persona didn’t just keep itself running so she had a stream to restart.
She tugged the hood down a little further and glanced at the sleeve of her hoodie.
’He asked me once if I only wear hoodies,’ she thought. ’Idiot... I own other clothes...’
She considered that then she shoved her hands into the front pocket and kept walking.
From the fragmented reports filtering through the underworld networks, the negotiations with the World Council had ended with almost miraculous success.
Blessed Land’s boundaries were recognized and it only got better for Silas from here, he also got a shit ton of money.
’Which begs the question,’ she mused, tapping ash from the glowing tip. ’Do we really have any business left with each other?’
Were they even friends?
Evelyn let out a dry self-deprecating snort.
In her line of work, "friendship" was an expensive luxury that usually ended with a poisoned dagger in your kidneys or a shallow grave under an unmarked stone.
People like her had contracts, temporary alliances of mutual survival, and debts paid in blood or coin.
Yet... she had spent a while walking the quiet paths of Blessed Land.
She had watched him tend to his people, watched the way Eluned looked at him, and shared food.
She took another slow pull with the bitter smoke burning her throat in a way that grounded her scattered thoughts.
She had already given the order that morning.
Her soldiers were to round up the stragglers, break camp, and head back to the territory to prepare it for the day the rest of them left Blessed Land.
They had grumbled, but they had gone so the housing block stood quiet now, and the western ridge was empty.
’Well then,’ Evelyn thought, flicking ash into a puddle of murky water by her boots. ’I’ll get him a proper parting gift. Something useful...’
She had enjoyed her time in Blessed Land.
It was peaceful, perhaps the only truly peaceful place she had set foot in since her core awakened.
And now that the dust had settled and the treaties were signed, there was nothing left to hold her there.
She had a fortress to run, an audience to feed, and it was time for Lord Sky to stream again.
Still... leaving didn’t mean disappearing.
Silas lived in the Human world too, in the same city she did so she could still see him there.
That thought sat a little more comfortably than she wanted it to.
’Don’t tell me I fell for the bastard or something?’
Regardless, somebody was following her and they weren’t really that much of a pro at it...
’Since when did I have stalkers?’ she thought, drawing on the cigarette. ’It’s obviously not a pro, a pro would have dropped back by now but this one just keeps coming.’
She was almost tempted to let it go on a little longer, if only to see where it ended.
But she had a boy to meet, a stream to restart, and a very bad habit of finishing things quickly so her footsteps slowed.
She stopped in the center of the damp cobblestones, right beneath a rusted drainpipe that dripped murky water onto a pile of broken glass.
Drip! Drip! Drip!
Why was she in this place...? Well it was near somewhere she wanted to forget.
Evelyn didn’t turn around.
She simply lifted her head slightly with her gaze locking onto a shattered second-story window framed by rotting pine shutters, twenty feet behind her right shoulder.
She took the cigarette from her lips, flicked an ember into the wet shadows, and her voice cut through the alley with cold certainty.
"I know you’ve been following me for four blocks," Evelyn said calmly into the dark. "Come on out."

The two of them stared at him the way people stare at a very handsome rock, and Valerius dropped his face into his palm and groaned into it.
"I’ll come later today then."
"Mm," Harper said, and took the teacup out of Silas’s hand and sipped from it herself with enormous dignity, as if to prove she was perfectly calm.
"That’s my tea."
"...It’s cold anyway, bitch."
Seraphina tried to launch off the couch to protest, got about halfway up, and her legs promptly folded like wet paper.
She flopped back onto the cushions with a thump and a long wounded wheeze, and Harper’s smirk came back so fast it was almost rude.
"Just sit for five minutes..."
"I will remember this," Seraphina muttered into a cushion.
"All of it.
Every second."
"I’ll send you the lodge address, Silas," Valerius said, already standing and brushing soot off his vest.
"Whenever you’re through the gate, just find me."
"Thanks, Val.
I can call you that right?"
In the other district of Valoria City’s southern edge, the afternoon sun rarely touched the ground.

Steam drifted from an iron exhaust pipe overhead and wrapped around the fire escapes that clung to the brickwork like skeletons as a small woman walked down the center of the passage with her boots stepping over the cracked cobblestones without a sound.
She was swallowed by an oversized dark-gray hoodie with the hem hanging down over her cargo pants and her hood pulled low over a messy bun of black hair.
"Mmm...
I’ll soon be going back to the Sovereign Realm."
A slim cigarette hung from her lips, lit with a snap of mana and a thin ribbon of blue-gray smoke trailing over her shoulder.
Her face looked permanently exhausted, but beneath the hood, her sharp dark eyes scanned the masonry.
I’m meeting Silas later today, and he’s following me to Central City,’ Evelyn thought, pulling the cigarette from her lips with two fingers and blowing a cloud of smoke at the damp brickwork.
She watched it curl and fade against the cold iron of an overhead fire escape.
Lord Sky had been quiet for weeks.
The comment sections were probably a warzone by now, hundreds of millions of followers screaming into the void, wondering whether the undefeated Lord had finally fallen off the face of the earth.
A masked voice-modulated persona didn’t just keep itself running so she had a stream to restart.
She tugged the hood down a little further and glanced at the sleeve of her hoodie.
’He asked me once if I only wear hoodies,’ she thought. ’Idiot...
I own other clothes...’
She considered that then she shoved her hands into the front pocket and kept walking.
From the fragmented reports filtering through the underworld networks, the negotiations with the World Council had ended with almost miraculous success.
Blessed Land’s boundaries were recognized and it only got better for Silas from here, he also got a shit ton of money.
’Which begs the question,’ she mused, tapping ash from the glowing tip. ’Do we really have any business left with each other?’
Were they even friends?
Evelyn let out a dry self-deprecating snort.
In her line of work, "friendship" was an expensive luxury that usually ended with a poisoned dagger in your kidneys or a shallow grave under an unmarked stone.
People like her had contracts, temporary alliances of mutual survival, and debts paid in blood or coin.
Yet... she had spent a while walking the quiet paths of Blessed Land.
She had watched him tend to his people, watched the way Eluned looked at him, and shared food.
She took another slow pull with the bitter smoke burning her throat in a way that grounded her scattered thoughts.
She had already given the order that morning.
Her soldiers were to round up the stragglers, break camp, and head back to the territory to prepare it for the day the rest of them left Blessed Land.
They had grumbled, but they had gone so the housing block stood quiet now, and the western ridge was empty.
’Well then,’ Evelyn thought, flicking ash into a puddle of murky water by her boots. ’I’ll get him a proper parting gift.
Something useful...’
She had enjoyed her time in Blessed Land.
It was peaceful, perhaps the only truly peaceful place she had set foot in since her core awakened.
And now that the dust had settled and the treaties were signed, there was nothing left to hold her there.
She had a fortress to run, an audience to feed, and it was time for Lord Sky to stream again.
Still... leaving didn’t mean disappearing.
Silas lived in the Human world too, in the same city she did so she could still see him there.
That thought sat a little more comfortably than she wanted it to.
’Don’t tell me I fell for the bastard or something?’
Regardless, somebody was following her and they weren’t really that much of a pro at it...
’Since when did I have stalkers?’ she thought, drawing on the cigarette. ’It’s obviously not a pro, a pro would have dropped back by now but this one just keeps coming.’
She was almost tempted to let it go on a little longer, if only to see where it ended.
But she had a boy to meet, a stream to restart, and a very bad habit of finishing things quickly so her footsteps slowed.
She stopped in the center of the damp cobblestones, right beneath a rusted drainpipe that dripped murky water onto a pile of broken glass.
Drip!
Drip!
Drip!
Why was she in this place...?
Well it was near somewhere she wanted to forget.
Evelyn didn’t turn around.
She simply lifted her head slightly with her gaze locking onto a shattered second-story window framed by rotting pine shutters, twenty feet behind her right shoulder.
She took the cigarette from her lips, flicked an ember into the wet shadows, and her voice cut through the alley with cold certainty.
"I know you’ve been following me for four blocks," Evelyn said calmly into the dark.
"Come on out."

chapters.title: Chapter 667: Kidnapping...?
paragraphs: The silence in the alley hung heavy in the air and Evelyn didn’t move.
"Haah..."
Her worn combat boots stayed planted on the cracked cobblestones with her hands buried deep in the front pouch of her oversized dark-gray hoodie.

A thin plume of blue-gray smoke drifted lazily from the slim cigarette clamped between her teeth and the moisture dripping from the rotting pine fire escape overhead fell in slow deliberate intervals, measuring out the stillness until the tension became almost suffocating.
"I can sense you, you know," she said, her voice dripping with a bit of exhaustion.
The alley didn’t answer, but the air stiffened.
The nearly imperceptible shift in mana pressure made the damp brickwork feel colder like a wire drawn too taut across a bare knuckle.
Evelyn cleared her dry throat, tilting her chin up just enough for her messy black bun to brush against the inside of her cotton hood.
"People, rather. Plural... You’re not exactly subtle with that suppression field, It leaks like a cracked pipe."
From the shadows behind a cluster of dented waste bins forty paces back, boots scraped against wet gravel.
A figure stepped out into the dull, filtered light of the alleyway.
He was broad-shouldered, tall, and moving with the practiced movements of a trained soldier.
Across his torso was a fitted tactical breastplate laced with intricate cerulean runic veins that hummed with a suppressed high-frequency drone.
It was a sleek vacuum-sealed kit... the kind of gear that cost an obscene mountain of Spirit Credits to license outside the World Council’s core districts.
Evelyn slowly turned her head over her shoulder with her sharp dark eyes hooded beneath the cotton rim.

’Third-generation mana-weave alloy,’ she cataloged instantly, her instincts processing the plating before her cigarette ash could drop. ’Adaptive kinetic baffles, inertia dampening... These are high-tier private security or an elite strike team, not your standard back-alley scavengers.’

"Stand down, Miss Evelyn," the lead man said. "We have no intention of harming you... Step away from the main thoroughfare and come with us quietly, It will save everyone involved an unnecessary amount of grief."
Evelyn pulled the cigarette from her lips with two calloused fingers, exhaling a dense aromatic stream of white smoke into the cold air.
She laughed.
It was a short dry chuckle that carried zero warmth.

"Come with you?" she asked, her voice scraping like sandpaper. "What, are we doing an impromptu kidnapping in broad daylight now?... I thought the local precinct at least pretended to have bylaws around here."
The man’s expression didn’t waver.
His jaw remained set and his eyes fixed firmly on her slender frame, completely unbothered by her mockery.
"We don’t need bylaws for this," he replied steadily. "Comply, and this remains a civil escort... Refuse, and we will take you by force... The outcome does not change."
Beneath the visor of his tactical helmet, his mind was cold and single-minded.

’I’m only doing this for Lady Elora,’ he reminded himself with his breathing disciplined and his mana pathways quietly pre-loading the arrays in his gauntlets. ’For some reason, the City Lord’s daughter, Miss Elora Verinda, specifically requested that this woman be brought in untouched... I have my orders so I simply have to deliver.’
He raised his right hand with two fingers snapping outward.
"Down... Secure her limbs..."
CREAK!

Two figures dropped from the rusted fire escapes above with their boots striking the cobblestones on either side of her, and two more slipped from the narrow recess of an adjoining service corridor, cutting off her route back to the main street.
Four operatives and a squad leader, all clad in matched composite armor with their hands already drawing shock-batons and suppression cuffs laced with nullification runes.
’Five of them,’ Evelyn counted, almost bored. ’Six if the guy hiding behind the bins counts but he doesn’t.’
In the second between the squad leader’s fingers snapping and his hand returning to his side, Evelyn moved.
She kept her hands in her pouch and she kept the cigarette in her mouth.
The only thing she did was shift her weight onto the ball of her right foot, and a concussive pop of compressed water-mana detonated beneath the heel of her boot.
BANG!
It launched her forward like a released catapult string, and the forty paces between them vanished in an eye-blink.
’Too fast—!’ the squad leader had time to think.
Before his adaptive armor could flare its kinetic baffles, Evelyn’s left hip torqued and her torso twisted horizontally mid-air.
Her combat boot whipped out in a vicious rising kick with the steel-capped toe driving up beneath his chin and straight through the exposed seam of his gorget.
CRACK!

His head snapped back with a wet thud and the shock rattled down his cervical spine, lifting his two-hundred-pound armored frame clear off the cobblestones and hurling him backward into a pile of rotting wooden crates.
The alley erupted.
"Engage! Suppress her!"
The two operatives from the fire escapes closed in from her flanks.

The one on the left lunged with an electrified baton with the tip crackling with jagged arcs of blue lightning aimed straight for her kidneys, while the one on the right dropped low and swept a heavy titanium-reinforced leg meant to shatter her knee.
Evelyn landed between them with the cigarette still burning with a perfect inch of ash hanging from its tip, and her sharp eyes flicked sideways.
’Again... who’s trying to kidnap me?’
She sank her center of gravity and let the low sweep shave harmlessly beneath her thighs, hopping over the follow-up with a lazy little skip like a kid jumping a rope.
As the lightning baton screamed down toward her collarbone she raised her left forearm, and a dense shimmering glaze of solid light-mana hardened over her skin like a translucent diamond gauntlet.
CLANG-ZZZZT!
The high-voltage baton hit her light-reinforced arm with the ringing shriek of steel on an anvil.
...The blue lightning crawled across the radiant barrier, found nothing to bite, and grounded itself harmlessly into the damp air.
"What the—" the operative started behind his visor.
"My turn," Evelyn muttered through her teeth.
Her right fist shot forward, wrapped in a pressurized vortex of swirling water-mana that condensed into an iron-hard hydraulic fist.
THUD!
It landed dead center on his chest plate and the hydraulic shockwave went straight through the exterior plating and into his thoracic cavity.
BOOM!
The air exploded out of his lungs in a strangled wheeze as he folded over her knuckles and he was unconscious before his knees hit the wet stone.
The sweeper was already back on his feet with a combat knife clearing its sheath, and Evelyn didn’t give him the half-second he needed.
She pivoted on the ball of her left boot without resetting her feet and whipped her right elbow around in a backward reverse-strike.
CRACK!
’I’m a bit good at hand to hand...’
The reinforced elbow caught the side of his tactical helmet, shearing the visor’s mounting brackets and shattering the tempered glass.
The man spun twice from the torque, bounced off the brick wall, and slid down into the muck completely limp.
Two down in less than three seconds, and the ash on her cigarette still hadn’t fallen.
The remaining two operatives from the service corridor hesitated with their boots freezing in the puddles.
One of them slapped a disc the size of a coaster against the cobbles, and a translucent dome of nullification light began to climb up from it like a rising tide.
"Back up! Back up, deploy the containment field—"
"Too loud," Evelyn breathed.
FLASH!
She vanished in a blinding flicker of light and the dome closed over an empty patch of cobblestones with a soft useless hum.
The warp displaced the air with a hollow pop as a second later she materialized between the two men, hovering inches above the ground, and her hands shot outward with the palms open.
Two miniature rings of blinding light-mana detonated point-blank in their faces.
FLASH-BANG!
The pure luminosity seared straight through their visors, overloading their eyes and cooking their equilibrium.

They were still clutching their eyes and screaming when Evelyn dropped, swept both of their lead legs with a low scything kick, and hammered their temples with two short, mana-hardened palm strikes as they fell.
THWACK! THWACK!
Both men went ragdoll with their heads bouncing off the cobblestones before settling into stillness.
Evelyn stood up straight, rolling her shoulders with a soft aching grimace.
She plucked the slim cigarette from her mouth and tapped a neat cylinder of gray ash into a puddle.
"Garbage," she muttered. "Corporate lackeys who think shiny armor makes up for garbage reaction times."
From across the alley, amidst the splintered wreckage of the wooden crates, a deep hum began to rise.
VUUUUUUUUUM!
The shattered wood was forcefully repelled outward by a dense, expanding geometric field of dark-amber mana as the squad leader rose to his feet.
His tactical gorget was dented, a thin line of dark blood trickled from the corner of his split lip, and his stance was rock-solid.
The shock that should have paralyzed a normal combatant had been absorbed by something far denser than armor.
His entire core was circulating, not with basic elemental fire or wind, but with structured mana.
’What a weird signature... Is he one of them?’ Evelyn thought, she was a bit sure of it... He was a constructor-type Adventurer.

After losing their territories, most cores underwent a mutation... An Adventurer would never be as strong as a Lord of the same rank however some cores went through transformations and lost their elements.
"I see," the leader spat, wiping the blood from his chin with the back of his armored glove. "The intelligence report didn’t mention light displacement... You’re not just some back-alley Lord."
Evelyn narrowed her eyes slightly with her casual posture settling into a sharper one.
’An architect, huh?’ she noted, her tactical mind categorizing the mana signature. ’That’s probably why my kick didn’t snap his neck... He pre-cast an internal spell over his vertebrae.’
The man slammed his palms together.
CLACK!
"Bound!" he roared.
CRACKLE-CRUNCH!

The cobblestones beneath Evelyn’s boots surged upward as four slabs of dense, mana-reinforced stone ripped free of the ground and folded inward like the jaws of an iron bear trap, ready to crush her legs.
She couldn’t jump, and she knew it as the light above her was already fluctuating... the man actively anchoring it down to stop a second warp.
’Smart bastard,’ she thought.
Instead of retreating, she thrust both palms downward.
A dense sheet of pressurized water erupted from her sleeves and flooded the narrow gaps between the rising slabs.
"Flash-Freeze!"

The water turned to ice in seconds as jagged crystalline wedges expanded through every seam and locked the slabs mid-clasp with a groan of straining stone, and the raw hydraulic force of the freezing cracked their structural integrity down the middle.
The leader didn’t pause.
He charged, his boots leaving glowing amber runes on the cobblestones with every step, and in his right hand the mana condensed into a massive hexagonal hammer forged from solid crystallized mana.
’It’s pretty useless... well unless for certain situations.’
He swung it in a horizontal cleave with the roar of a falling boulder.
Evelyn leaned her torso back with the flat of the hammer missing the tip of her nose by two inches as the displacement tore her hood off and sent her messy black hair whipping around her face.
SWOOSH!
The hammer slammed into the brick wall behind her and turned three feet of solid masonry into a shower of red dust and flying shards!
Before he could pull it back, Evelyn stepped into his guard.
Her light-gauntleted left arm came up and caught the haft, pinning the hammer against the wall, and her right hand shot out like a viper with the palm open, aimed at his exposed throat.
CLANG!
A geometric amber shield snapped into existence between her palm and his neck, and the impact sent a jolt of kinetic feedback up her forearm.
The man smirked behind his bloodied lips.
"You rely too much on speed. My constructs are—"
"Loud," Evelyn interrupted coldly.
She kept her palm pressed flat against his shield and didn’t pull back an inch.
Deep within her core, the light and water currents surged together and spiraled into a hyper-compressed volatile needle at her fingertips.

She fed it into the barrier, not as a blow but as a pressure that kept building with the light finding every hairline seam of the construct while the water behind it pushed in like a flood against a dam wall.
The shield began to hum then it began to crack.
"Wait, what are you—" the leader started as his smirk was gone.
SHATTER!
The hexagonal barrier burst, and the concussive backfire shattered the gauntlet on his right arm and stripped his armor down to the bare arming coat.
The man staggered back with his balance broken as the backlash sent a wave of internal bleeding through his chest.
Evelyn followed through instantly.
She skipped the spell and stepped forward, anchored her left heel, and whipped her right boot up in a clean ruthless high kick that took him flush on the side of the temple.
WHAM!
His eyes rolled back into his skull as his two-hundred-pound frame left the ground and crashed onto the fractured cobblestones, skidding three feet through the damp gravel before it finally stopped.
The alley fell silent once more, with nothing left but the steady dripping of the rusted drainage pipe.
Drip! Drip! Drip!
Evelyn stood over him with her chest rising and falling in shallow breaths.
Her oversized gray hoodie was dusted with brick powder, and a single lock of black hair hung across her forehead.
She flicked the remaining ash from the cigarette and took a slow deep drag with the glowing cherry lighting the sharp tired angles of her face.
She stepped on the man’s broken wrist with just enough grinding pressure to force consciousness back into his battered skull.
"Aaargh!" The leader gasped and his eyes fluttered open with blood leaking from his nose and mouth as he stared up at the dark silhouette looming over him.
"You’re going to talk," Evelyn said, her voice dropping into a quiet monotone. "I don’t have the patience for posturing, and my cigarette is almost down to the filter... Who gave the order?"
The man gritted his teeth, his bruised face twisting with pain and stubborn pride. "I told you... standard client privilege... you can’t just—"
Evelyn’s heel pressed down harder with the sound of shifting carpal bones echoed sharply off the alley walls.
"Wrong answer," she said softly.
A needle of pure light mana ignited at the tip of her forefinger and hovered half an inch above his right eye, the heat singeing his eyelashes. "Try again."
The man’s resolve shattered under the cold unblinking certainty in her dark eyes.
He had faced hardened mercenaries before, but there was something unnatural in her presence, perhaps a microscopic bleed of true Lord aura that pressed against his soul like an iron tombstone.
"L-Lady Elora!" he choked out, his voice cracking in terror. "Elora Verinda! Miss Elora ordered it! Directly!"
Evelyn froze as the needle of light hovered motionless above his pupil.
