Her light-gauntleted left arm came up and caught the haft, pinning the hammer against the wall, and her right hand shot out like a viper with the palm open, aimed at his exposed throat.
CLANG!
A geometric amber shield snapped into existence between her palm and his neck, and the impact sent a jolt of kinetic feedback up her forearm.
The man smirked behind his bloodied lips.
"You rely too much on speed.
My constructs are—"
"Loud," Evelyn interrupted coldly.
She kept her palm pressed flat against his shield and didn’t pull back an inch.
Deep within her core, the light and water currents surged together and spiraled into a hyper-compressed volatile needle at her fingertips.

She fed it into the barrier, not as a blow but as a pressure that kept building with the light finding every hairline seam of the construct while the water behind it pushed in like a flood against a dam wall.
The shield began to hum then it began to crack.
"Wait, what are you—" the leader started as his smirk was gone.
SHATTER!
The hexagonal barrier burst, and the concussive backfire shattered the gauntlet on his right arm and stripped his armor down to the bare arming coat.
The man staggered back with his balance broken as the backlash sent a wave of internal bleeding through his chest.
Evelyn followed through instantly.
She skipped the spell and stepped forward, anchored her left heel, and whipped her right boot up in a clean ruthless high kick that took him flush on the side of the temple.
WHAM!
His eyes rolled back into his skull as his two-hundred-pound frame left the ground and crashed onto the fractured cobblestones, skidding three feet through the damp gravel before it finally stopped.
The alley fell silent once more, with nothing left but the steady dripping of the rusted drainage pipe.
Drip!
Drip!
Drip!
Evelyn stood over him with her chest rising and falling in shallow breaths.
Her oversized gray hoodie was dusted with brick powder, and a single lock of black hair hung across her forehead.
She flicked the remaining ash from the cigarette and took a slow deep drag with the glowing cherry lighting the sharp tired angles of her face.
She stepped on the man’s broken wrist with just enough grinding pressure to force consciousness back into his battered skull.
"Aaargh!" The leader gasped and his eyes fluttered open with blood leaking from his nose and mouth as he stared up at the dark silhouette looming over him.
"You’re going to talk," Evelyn said, her voice dropping into a quiet monotone.
"I don’t have the patience for posturing, and my cigarette is almost down to the filter...
Who gave the order?"
The man gritted his teeth, his bruised face twisting with pain and stubborn pride.
"I told you... standard client privilege... you can’t just—"
Evelyn’s heel pressed down harder with the sound of shifting carpal bones echoed sharply off the alley walls.
"Wrong answer," she said softly.
A needle of pure light mana ignited at the tip of her forefinger and hovered half an inch above his right eye, the heat singeing his eyelashes.
"Try again."
The man’s resolve shattered under the cold unblinking certainty in her dark eyes.
He had faced hardened mercenaries before, but there was something unnatural in her presence, perhaps a microscopic bleed of true Lord aura that pressed against his soul like an iron tombstone.
"L-Lady Elora!" he choked out, his voice cracking in terror.
"Elora Verinda!
Miss Elora ordered it!
Directly!"
Evelyn froze as the needle of light hovered motionless above his pupil.

chapters.title: Chapter 668: Returning To The Sovereign Realm [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: ’Elora...’ Evelyn thought, the name echoing through her mind with a sour weight.
...Elora Verinda.
The pampered sharp-tongued daughter of the City Lord, the golden scion of the central administration, who moved through high-society galas draped in silks and surrounded by retainers.
Why would someone of that tier be sending extraction teams into the southern periphery for an unregistered contractor like her?
Her thoughts flicked backward, tracing the events of the past few weeks.

’The hotel,’ she realized, a cold knot settling into the pit of her stomach. ’The Skybli... When I walked into that luxury suite with Kara... with Silas, when we were coordinating the back-channel logistics for Blessed Land.’
Was that why she was being targeted? Had the City Lord’s security apparatus flagged her presence entering a high-profile suite alongside the anomalous scion?
Evelyn had never exactly been a stranger to cameras, but nobody had ever followed her out of a lobby before.
Her eyes narrowed into sharp calculating slits.

’No... wait,’ she reasoned, her mind cutting through the first wave of paranoia. ’It’s not that serious... If Elora Verinda genuinely wanted me gone, if the City Lord’s office were running a black-bag purge, she wouldn’t use middle-tier private contractors who know her name. A real extraction unit would be faceless, scrubbed from the registry, and wiped of every identifying tie.’
She looked down at the bleeding man beneath her boot.
’He knew her face and he knew her name too...’
Which meant the operation was never an assassination... It wasn’t even a real capture...
Was it a message?
Elora Verinda wanted Evelyn to know she was being watched.
A reminder that in this city the walls had ears, the shadows had eyes, and the daughter of the high seat could reach into any alley she pleased.
’What sort of ridiculous high-society trouble have I gotten myself dragged into...’ Evelyn sighed internally, rubbing the bridge of her nose with her free hand.
Dealing with monsters and Lords was clean but dealing with the petty passive-aggressive territorialism of bored noble heiresses was a headache.
She lowered her foot and let the needle of light wink out, then drove the heel of her boot into the leader’s jaw in a short concussive kick.
THWACK!
His head snapped sideways as his eyes rolled back, and he slumped into unconsciousness silently.
Evelyn stood in the quiet alley, surrounded by five unconscious armored operatives, and took a slow drag from what was left of her cigarette.
The logical course of action was simple.
Any experienced person in the outer rim knew the rule... Leave no loose ends.
If she put a beam of light through each of their skulls right now, there would be no witnesses, no immediate tracking signatures, and no one to confirm the failure to Elora Verinda for several hours.
It was safe.
She slowly raised her right hand.

A sphere of incandescent light mana gathered in the center of her palm, glowing with enough concentrated heat to vaporize flesh and bone down to ash in a fraction of a second as she aimed it at the chest of the squad leader lying at her feet.
One pulse... That was all it would take.
Her fingers tightened then... her hand twitched.
A violent tremor shot up her wrist and seized the muscles in her forearm like an icy cramp.
Her breath hitched in her throat and turned into a ragged terrified gasp that rattled through her teeth.
The sphere of light flickered wildly, its stable form breaking apart into jagged uneven sparks.
Her vision swam for a terrifying second.
The cobblestones seemed to tilt, and the scent of the alley was replaced by the phantom smell of old stagnant blood and shattered glass.
A face flashed in her mind looking wrinkled and terrified while looking up at her with eyes that didn’t understand why the light was burning him.
’Stop it,’ she told herself, her teeth grinding so hard her jaw ached. ’Just close your hand and fire.’
She couldn’t.
Her fingers refused to obey, her chest heaved, and a cold sickening sweat broke out across the back of her neck beneath her oversized hoodie.
The mana in her palm dissolved and collapsed back into her pathways in a ragged disordered rush that left her knuckles numb.
Evelyn lowered her trembling hand and shoved it deep into the pouch of her hoodie, her head hanging low.
"Pathetic," she whispered into the empty alley, the self-loathing in her voice so thick it tasted like bile. "What kind of Lord can’t even kill with her own hands...?"

She had commanded fortresses and she had directed sieges from behind heavy mythril plating, barking orders that turned entire fields of beasts into red mist but here, up close, looking at a helpless, unconscious man lying in the dirt?
She was useless... A coward who froze at the finish line...

’I’m going to pay for this one of these days,’ she thought bitterly, turning her back on the fallen squad and walking toward the mouth of the alley. ’All this hesitation... all this soft-hearted rot... One day someone I spare is going to put a knife through Elm’s throat, or Hiro’s, or mine and it’ll be my own blood paying the bill.’
She just didn’t know when the debt would come due.
Ten minutes later, Evelyn arrived at the secluded overgrown corner of the southern quarter.
It was an abandoned plot of ground, tucked between two crumbling brick storehouses that had burned down decades ago.
Tall pale weeds pushed through the cracked pavement, swaying gently in the damp autumn breeze.

In the center of the clearing stood a handful of simple weather-worn headstones looking unmarked and unkempt like a forgotten graveyard for those who died without families or guild registries to claim their remains.
Evelyn walked down the narrow dirt path, her boots silent against the grass.
She stopped before a modest uneven stone slab half-swallowed by creeping ivy.
There was no name carved into the granite... only a pair of deep horizontal grooves worn smooth by years of rain.
Slowly, Evelyn sank to her knees.
The damp earth soaked through the knees of her cargo pants and the cold seeped into her skin, but she didn’t care.
She reached into the interior pocket of her dark hoodie and pulled out a single fresh white blossom which was a wild mountain chicory she had bought from a street vendor near the gate.
She gently set the flower down at the base of the stone.
’It’s my fault,’ she thought, her dark eyes staring at the weathered gray rock.
The guilt was a heavy stone that had sat in her chest for years, never getting lighter, never eroding.

’I was the one who killed him with my own hands,’ the memory played behind her eyelids with agonizing clarity. ’He was an old man who had gotten too curious, a civilian who asked the wrong questions in the wrong district, looking into things that weren’t meant for regular ears.’
And she, in her panic, in her desperate need to protect the fortress and the false name of Lord Sky, had unleashed her mana.
She had fired and by the time the smoke cleared, there was barely anything left to apologize to.
Evelyn’s hand clenched tight against her knee with her knuckles turning bone-white.
’I don’t know if you’ll ever be able to forgive me, old man,’ she whispered internally with her throat tight and dry. ’I don’t think you should but I still remember.’
It was very pathetic of her... Just the simple act of killing this man had brought her here.
She stayed there for a long time with the cold wind rustling the weeds around her and the single white flower resting quietly against the damp granite.
"I’m sorry," she whispered aloud.
With that quiet confession, Evelyn pushed herself to her feet.
She dusted the dirt from her knees, pulled her cotton hood back over her messy black bun, and stepped away from the grave.
She pulled a fresh slim cigarette from the pack in her pocket, clamped it between her lips, and snapped her fingers.
A tiny controlled spark of light-mana ignited at her thumb and lit the tip with a soft glow.
Fwump!
She took a long deep drag, letting the bitter tobacco fill her lungs and ground her scattered thoughts back in the present.

’Well then...’ Evelyn exhaled a thick cloud of smoke toward the overcast sky. ’I’m meeting Silas later today... I’m leaving Blessed Land for now, but I’ll come back later, obviously. Still, what kind of parting gift do you even get for a man who sits on a Gold Core and owns a territory like that...?’
She puffed her cheeks out and blew a smoke ring through the weeds as she walked back toward the city gates with her hand already reaching into her pocket for her phone.
If she was going to be followed the whole way to Central City, she might as well make sure the one person she was actually walking with knew where to find her.
For Silas on the other hand, the world dissolved into pure darkness.
There was no sound as his Gold Core circulated smoothly, stabilizing his physical shell against the dimensional drag as the transition took hold.
HUUUUUUUUM!
A soft golden chime echoed in the back of his consciousness, and the darkness peeled away like a parting curtain.
Silas opened his eyes to find himself standing in the center of his personal quarters on the top floor of the Keep in Blessed Land.
The deep mahogany floors were polished to a mirror shine, and the arched windows let in the warm golden light of the late afternoon.
Through the glass, the canopy of the trees stretched across the horizon with their leaves rustling in a gentle breeze that carried the scent of blooming life and rich earth as well as fruits.
Silas lifted both arms over his head, interlocking his fingers and arching his spine until three distinct satisfying cracks echoed through his vertebrae.
"Man..." he groaned, shaking out his shoulders. "What a day it has been."

He had barely finished breakfast at home, and between Seraphina trying to turn his living room into a nursery, Harper disintegrating betrothal contracts with high-voltage lightning, and Valerius having a full-scale panic attack over his singed bangs, his head felt like it had been run through a mythril threshing mill.

The three of them had finally left for the day, still arguing in the driveway, and Silas had stood in his own doorway listening to the voices fade down the lane with the strange feeling of having survived a minor war.
He had no idea what kind of chaotic passive-aggressive alliance Seraphina and Harper were plotting wherever they had stormed off to, and quite frankly, he had zero intention of finding out.

’I’ll be heading to Central City today anyway,’ Silas thought, unbuttoning his soot-stained pajama shirt and tossing it toward the laundry basket. ’Better to let the dust settle before I walk back into that particular battlefield... Evelyn said later today so that gives me a few hours.’
He pulled a fresh tailored tunic of dark charcoal linen from his wardrobe, fastened the leather vambraces around his forearms, and walked out of the bedroom.
His boots made a quiet thud on the polished cedar staircase as he descended into the lower levels of the Keep.
The halls were unusually quiet.
At this hour Eluned would normally be pacing the corridors or Morwenna would too but today the main hall was completely deserted.
Silas pushed open the heavy oak doors leading into the Keep’s expansive kitchen.
Sitting alone at the massive cedar dining table was Aeliana.
The tall blond-haired Elf sat with impeccable poise with a delicate porcelain cup of herbal spirit-tea resting between her long slender fingers.
"Mhm~"
The afternoon sunlight filtered through the ivy-draped kitchen windows and caught the pale contours of her face and the luminous tips of her pointed ears.
As Silas stepped over the threshold, Aeliana lifted her head.
A serene and remarkably gentle smile touched her lips with her silver-green eyes softening as she set her teacup down on its saucer.
"Welcome back, Lord Sy," she greeted him, her voice smooth and melodic, like running water over river stones. "You look as though you have been wrestling mountain drakes..."
Silas snorted, walking over to the counter and pouring himself a tall glass of cold spring water.
"Close enough. A certain fire heiress decided she wanted to stress-test my ribs."
He downed the glass in three massive gulps, wiped his mouth with the back of his wrist, and pulled out a chair across from her.
"Where is everyone?" he asked, glancing around the quiet kitchen. "The Keep feels completely empty... I didn’t see Eluned anywhere, and Morwenna’s usually grumbling about training by now."
Aeliana chuckled softly and took a delicate sip of her tea.
"Lady Eluned and Morwenna are currently away. Thor went along with them as well. They have crossed over into the new Vassal Territory to inspect the initial boundary settlements..."
Silas paused, his memory clicking into place. "Aki’s territory?"

"Indeed," Aeliana nodded, her silver-green eyes bright with fond amusement. "Lady Aki officially completed her core awakening. Her foundation stabilized remarkably fast, and the territory bonded without the slightest rejection... The land has begun to terraform."
Silas smiled with a genuine warmth blooming in his chest.
"That’s great to hear. She’s been stressing about awakening for years. How has she been holding up? How’s the territory looking?"
Aeliana tapped her chin thoughtfully, a playful glint dancing in her gaze.
"It is... unique, Lord Sy. It would be far better for you to see it with your own eyes than for me to describe it. Words do not quite do justice to Lady Aki’s architectural vision."
Silas chuckled, rising from his chair. "Alright, you’ve got me curious... Lead the way."
Aeliana stood with effortless grace, smoothed the folds of her pale green robe, and led him out through the Keep’s rear courtyard.
Just beyond the manicured herb gardens, upon a raised dais of polished white marble, sat a massive circular array of spatial runes.
The glyphs were carved deep into the stone and pulsed with a golden luminescence.
"These are the runes linked directly to her territory," Aeliana explained, stepping up onto the edge of the dais. "It has been like that since she awakened."
Silas stepped up beside her, admiring the clean precise line-work of the runes, truly the System was the best.
"Has she given the territory an official designation yet? The Sovereign Realm requires a name on the territory... She can’t just file it as ’Blessed Land’s Vassal.’ after all."
Aeliana tapped her lower lip with a slender finger with a suppressed smirk twitching at the corners of her mouth.
"If I recall the declaration Lady Aki made to everyone this morning..." she murmured, "...she officially registered it as Aki’s Wonderland."

chapters.title: Chapter 669: A Usurper [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Silas froze mid-stride and he slowly turned his head to look at the Elf.
Aeliana looked back at him with her expression completely serene and her eyes were serious.
For five full seconds neither of them said a word. The only sound in the courtyard was the rustling of the spirit herbs in the gentle wind.
"Aki’s Wonderland," Silas repeated flatly. "Are you serious?"
Aeliana nodded once, maintaining absolute aristocratic composure.
"I’m very serious, Lord Sy... She wrote it in colored inks and stamped it with three separate flower crests. Eluned liked it and well Morwenna said it was childish so they bullied her."
Silas pinched the bridge of his nose and let out a deep defeated groan that came straight from his soul.

’Aki’s Wonderland...’ he thought, staring up at the canopy of the World Tree. ’I mean... it’s not that it’s inherently bad. It’s Aki. She’s whimsical and she’s colorful too but does she really expect the other lords to take her seriously if a Lord war ensues?!’
He could already picture someone hearing the name Aki’s Wonderland.
It sounded like a children’s amusement park, not an armed vassal dominion capable of fielding high-tier awakened warriors.

’What happened to proper imposing territory names?’ Silas mused with an exasperated sigh. ’Names like the Obsidian Spire! Or the Reach! Even The Iron Citadel or Verdant Bastion would have sounded respectable! Hell, even Valerius had the sense to call his territory the Sterling Aegis... I’m just joking.’
He dropped his hand and looked down at the glowing runes beneath his boots, and a quiet helpless laugh broke through his chest.
"Well," Silas chuckled, shaking his head with fond resignation. "Honestly... I think it fits her perfectly. Though they bullied Morwenna?"
"She will be very pleased to hear you approve," Aeliana smiled, stepping into the center of the dais beside him. "Yes, she’s been very bullied since morning and has been awaiting for your arrival..."
Silas channeled a tiny thread of his Gold Core mana into the activation rune.
VUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!

The runes flared with blinding brilliance and wrapped around them in a twisting pillar of spatial light that folded the distance between Blessed Land and its new vassal territory into a single heartbeat.
FLASH!
The spatial displacement cleared instantly, and the fresh crisp scent of wild mountain pine and blooming starlight-lilies flooded his senses.

The grass under his boots was impossibly soft, the sky overhead a deeper blue than any he had seen in the Sovereign Realm, and somewhere in the distance a wind chime made of what sounded like glass bells was playing a cheerful slightly out-of-tune melody.
’Okay,’ Silas thought, taking it all in. ’I can see where the name came from...’
SHREEEEEEEEEK!
Before his boots could even fully settle, a high-pitched whistling tore through the air directly in front of his face!
Silas didn’t think.
His body moved before his mind had finished registering the sound, and his right hand snapped up and closed around the incoming shaft three inches from his nose.
CLANG-KRAAAASH!

It wasn’t an iron arrow or a thrown dagger, the weapon itself was a six-foot spear forged from solid crystallized starlight... it was a blinding, iridescent shaft of pure starlight mana humming with enough piercing force to punch a hole through a person.

The throw sent a concussive shockwave rippling outward and flattened the grass for ten yards around the transit pad, and Silas stood in the middle of it with his boots exactly where they had been, holding the spear in one bare hand like a man who had been handed a walking stick.
"Eh?"
Silas fingers tightened until the humming strangled itself into a dull whine.
"What’s this?"
He flicked his wrist and drove the starlight shaft deep into the earth beside his boot, where it shivered like a plucked harp string and then dissolved into glittering dust.
Silas slowly lifted his head with his blue eyes narrowing through the settling spatial dust and a thin ring of gold flashing around each pupil.
Standing twenty paces away at the top of a blooming grassy knoll was an elf.
She was nearly as tall as Silas himself, with a lean athletic frame draped in form-fitting silver plate that gleamed under the soft sky of the territory.

Her long silver hair whipped around her shoulders in the wind, and across both of her cheekbones glittered a scatter of tiny silver marks, a constellation of stars that pulsed with a faint lilac light.
Her angular striking face was pulled into an ugly venomous sneer, and her cold blue eyes were fixed on him with pure hatred.
In her left hand, a second spear of crackling starlight was already condensing out of the air.
She pointed the glowing weapon directly at his throat.
"Usurper," Ther’Abella spat.
’I’m a Usurper...?’ Silas thought.
Ther’Abella’s blue eyes narrowed into slits of unfiltered venom as she dragged her gaze up Silas’s frame.
’This is the man bearing Lady Eluned’s surname...’
The bitter vile realization burned in the back of her throat like acid...
She had pictured a bloated wretched parasite, perhaps a fat decrepit old lord who had somehow bound the pristine peerless high lady to his service through manipulation.
But the reality standing twenty paces away was quite different... He was young, tall and lean, with the effortless poise of a man in his prime and a sharp undeniably handsome jawline.
And he had caught her Starlight Spear with a bare hand, without drawing a weapon and without taking a single backward step.

’It doesn’t matter,’ she raged internally. ’It changes nothing! A pretty face and stolen parlor tricks! Nobody in the mortal realm or the heavens above deserves to breathe the same air as Lady Eluned, least of all a filthy arrogant usurper like him!’
Before she threw it, her gaze flicked left on instinct and locked onto Aeliana standing by the edge of the transit dais.
A spike of raw humiliating outrage lanced through her heart.
’Why is she looking at me like that...?’
Aeliana wasn’t raising a hand.
She wasn’t preparing a barrier or reaching for a bow, instead she was watching with a soft mournful sigh as her silver-green eyes were full of open pity.
’Pity?! For me?!’
"Die!" Ther’Abella screamed, her pride fracturing into blind violence.
SHREEEEEEEEK!
She poured every ounce of her starlight foundation into the second spear.

The grass beneath her boots turned to white ash as the constellations on her cheeks flared and her blue eyes ignited into a blazing lilac, and she hurled it with enough velocity to break through the air.
’I’ll kill him...’
She didn’t wait to see where it landed either.

Two daggers of condensed radiance snapped into being in her fists, and she blurred across the meadow in a serpentine sprint with her blade points trailing ribbons of silver plasma, meant to open his throat the instant he tried to parry the missile.
Silas didn’t parry.
’What—’
He didn’t even lift an arm.
WHOOSH!

The spear shrieked through the place where his head had been and pulverized the hillock behind him into a fountain of dirt and flowers as Silas was already gone with only a pale afterimage hanging in the grass where he had stood and tearing apart in the wind.
’Behind me?! No, above—where is he?!’
Her instincts screamed, but her eyes couldn’t track him.
The air directly before her face folded inward with a concussive crack and Silas now stood inside her guard.
’IMPOSSIBLE!’
In pure panic, Ther’Abella crossed her radiant daggers into a desperate X-guard and flashed a luminous star-shield over her chest to buy distance but Silas didn’t bother stepping back.
He lifted one open hand and slapped it flat against the shield.
SHATTER!
The starlight construct burst into drifting dust, and the shockwave kicked her daggers wide and left her standing with her arms spread like a scarecrow.
’He broke it with his palm,’ Ther’Abella thought, staring at the falling motes. ’That shield has stopped a wyrm and he hit it like he was closing a door...?’
She refused to believe it.
She whipped her right dagger across in a vicious backhand slash aimed at his throat, and Silas leaned his head back an inch as the blade went through the space his neck had been.
’Again!’
She poured everything into a flurry, left and right, high and low with each strike faster than the last.
WHOOSH! WHOOSH!

Silas moved his head, his shoulders and his waist with small and lazy adjustments that left her blades slicing through empty space by a hair, and almost politely, he tapped the flat of her wrist with two fingers and sent a dagger spinning off into the clover.
’He’s playing with me,’ she realized, and the thought left a cold nauseating hollow in her chest. ’He’s not even trying to hit me.’
"Is that all?!" she snarled, her eyes blazing. "Fight me, usurper! Fight me like a man who deserves her!"

She whipped her left wrist in a tight circle and a chain of woven starlight lashed out from her bracer, wrapping three times around his forearm, and she planted her heels and hauled with a roar that cracked the ground at her feet.
’Now! If I can pull him off his stance—!’
The chain went taut and Silas didn’t move an inch.
’What—?!’
She heaved again with her whole body with the muscles in her back screaming and the constellations on her cheeks blazing white but it was like trying to drag a mountain across a field by a thread.
He looked down at the chain wrapped around his sleeve, then at her, and raised his arm.
She came off her feet.
’HE LIFTED ME—’
She flew toward him on her own chain, and he closed his fist around the glowing links and pulled.
CRACK!
The chain snapped apart in a shower of silver sparks, and the recoil sent her tumbling backward across the meadow in a long skidding roll that carved a trench through the clover.
She came up on one knee, already forming a starlight glaive in both hands with its curved blade as long as her arm.
"Not enough!" she screamed, and swung.
A crescent of lilac light peeled off the glaive and tore across the meadow, cutting the grass in a perfectly straight line aimed squarely at his waist.
Silas lifted his hand and slapped the crescent aside like a fly, and it exploded against the hillside in a glittering fan that drifted down through the air like confetti.
Ther’Abella stared at it.
’That was my strongest cut,’ she thought numbly. ’That cut once split a siege tower in half... He swatted it... With a hand?’
’No. No! I am not afraid of him! I am of the Viridian Guard! I swore my life to Lady Eluned!’
She flung both arms wide.
Behind her, a dozen spears of starlight bloomed in the air like the spokes of a wheel with each one humming at a different pitch until the whole meadow rang like a struck chime.
"FALL!"
SHREEEEEEEEEEEEEEK!
The volley came down in a spreading fan, and the ground erupted wherever a spear touched it, geysers of dirt and burning white light climbing into the sky in a ragged line toward him.
He simply walked with one unhurried step after another, and the spears punched craters on his left and right and the shockwaves did nothing but flutter the hem of his tunic.
At the edge of the dais, Aeliana lifted her teacup to keep the dust out of it.
’Not one,’ Ther’Abella thought, watching the dust settle with her mouth hanging open. ’Not one of twelve... He didn’t even look at them...’
He was ten paces away now then five.
"Don’t look at me like that!" she shrieked, though his face was calm and almost bored. "Don’t you dare look at me like that, you leech!"
She came again behind the last of her own volley, the daggers snapping back into her fists, and fought him at close range with everything she had.

’Why can’t I touch him?!’ she raged, throwing her whole body into a savage swing. ’Four hundred years! I survived four hundred years of butchers and warlords and beasts, and he’s not even breathing hard!’
Her right dagger arced out in a long desperate swing that carried her whole shoulder with it, and for half a heartbeat her ribs were wide open.
Silas stepped into the pocket.

He planted his back heel, torquing his hips with the unadorned physical power of a Gold Core, and his right fist drove forward like an industrial ram, plunging beneath her sternum and burying itself in her solar plexus.
BAAAAAAAAAANG!
’GUH—!’
Every lungful of air in her body was blasted out through her teeth as her vision strobed white.
She started to fold over his arm, and her mind even half-conscious, was already reaching for a spell.
’I can still—!’
Silas pulled his fist back and drove it in again, a hair to the left of the first but in exactly the same place.
BAAAAAAAAAANG!
’Ah—’
The second shockwave rattled her organs and sent black nausea crashing over her brain.
Her legs dissolved beneath her as the daggers slipped from her numb fingers with the starlight fading before the hilts struck the dirt and the lilac fire in her eyes went out like a snuffed candle.
She was already falling, but Silas didn’t let her hit the ground cleanly.

His foot hooked behind her ankle and swept her legs out from under her, his hand clamped onto the nape of her silver cuirass and turned her limp frame in mid-air as he laid her face-first in the damp turf.
THUD!
Before she could draw a single ragged gasp, a heavy boot settled onto the center of her spine and pinned her flat against the earth.
’I can’t... I can’t move...’

Ther’Abella choked on dirt as Silas took both of her wrists in one big hand and drew them back and up toward her shoulder blades in a joint-lock that sat right on the edge of tearing the bone from the socket.

’Four hundred years,’ she thought, and her eyes burned with something that wasn’t only pain. ’Four hundred years of surviving and the end is a stranger’s boot in a field of flowers... Lady Eluned, I’m sorry... I failed you again...’
A shadow fell over the back of her head.
At the edge of the runes, Aeliana lifted her teacup to her lips with a long sigh. She expected it and she was happy that this woman had been disciplined...
"Lord Sy," she called mildly, "do try to leave her enough ribs to answer questions."
"I’m working on it," Silas said without looking up.
He leaned down slightly, his voice dropping into a low chill with the weight of his boot pressing down just enough to make her vertebrae creak.
"Start talking," Silas said. "Who are you, and why are you throwing spears at me in my own territory?"

chapters.title: Chapter 670: Luggage Elf [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The damp earth smelled of crushed wild clover and ozone, but beneath Ther’Abella’s cheek, it tasted like bitter humiliating ash.
She tried to twist her hips.

She tried to channel even a thread of her starlight foundation down into her thighs to lever herself upward, but the heavy boot planted between her shoulder blades didn’t give so much as a millimeter.
It felt less like a man standing over her and more like the root of an ancient mountain had been ripped from the earth and dropped squarely onto her spine.
"Nngh...!"
A strained muffled hiss slipped past her grit teeth as dirt gritted against her lips.
Every time she tried to expand her ribs to draw a breath, the pressure increased by an exact agonizing fraction of a pound.

Behind her back, both of her wrists were gathered into a single calloused hand, twisted backward and pulled up toward her nape in a vise-like grip that had her shoulder ligaments singing in sharp hot agony.

"I wouldn’t squirm if I were you," Silas’s voice drifted down from above, he didn’t even sound strained from suppressing her. "Your joint capsules are about two degrees of twisting away from popping like dry twigs... Answer the question, or you’re going to lose the use of both arms before noon."
A cold prickly jolt of genuine fear struck the base of Ther’Abella’s skull.
She had stood guard beneath the World Tree for three centuries and she had spent four hundred years afterward alone on the outer rim, killing things that wanted her dead.
Ther-Abella knew the difference between a blusterer making idle threats and a person who treated violence like an accountant balancing a ledger.
The man pinning her into the dirt wasn’t angry... That was the terrifying part.

There was no bloodlust radiating from him, it was just a flat certainty that if she didn’t provide a satisfactory answer, he would snap her limbs, toss her aside, and go about his afternoon without losing a single second of sleep.
’Curse him...’ she thought, her teeth aching from how hard she clamped down. ’Curse this usurping brute...’
Before she could force out a defiant retort through the dirt, a soft, amused voice chimed from the edge of the transit dais.
"Lord Sy," Aeliana spoke, her tone as light and refreshing as a spring breeze passing through willow branches. "You may release her... That is Ther’Abella, She is Lady Aki’s First Hero."
Silas paused as the suffocating grip on her wrists loosened instantly.
"Oh," Silas said, blinking down at the silver hair splayed across the turf. "Aki’s hero?"
He let go of her hands completely, though the boot remained firmly stationed on her back, keeping her pinned to the ground like a pinned beetle.
"Then why the hell did she just try to put an orbital starlight lance through my nose?" Silas asked, genuinely baffled.

He glanced over his shoulder toward Aeliana, who was standing with her hands tucked demurely into the wide sleeves of her pale green robes. "If Aki finds out her primary summon spent her first afternoon picking fights with the me, she’s going to have a breakdown or something... I’d rather avoid that headache."
"I am not merely a summon!" Ther’Abella snapped, finding her voice the second the pressure on her throat eased.

She turned her head sideways, spitting a mouthful of loam and crushed grass onto the sod, her blue eyes burning with righteous fury. "I am of the Viridian Guard! I stood among Lady Eluned’s sworn protectors for three centuries! I held the north gate of the sanctum when—"
Creak!
Silas casually leaned an extra twenty pounds of weight into his heel.
"Oof—!"
The breath was shoved straight out of her lungs in a sharp wheeze, cutting her grand pedigree off mid-sentence.
"I didn’t ask for your resume," Silas said flatly, looking past her toward the High Elf princess. "Aeli, translate... Why is she trying to take my head off?"
Aeliana couldn’t hold it in anymore.
A bright musical laugh bubbled past her lips with her pointed ears twitching with unmasked amusement as she stepped down from the marble dais.

"She served in Lady Eluned’s Viridian Guard," Aeliana explained, her silver-green eyes dancing with mischief. "And to put it plainly, Lord Sy... she is simply consumed with bitter jealousy over the fact that you managed to marry Lady Eluned."
Silas stared down at the back of Ther’Abella’s head.
"Oh," Silas said, his lips twitching into an amused smirk. "She’s jealous."

"I am not—!" Ther’Abella snarled, her face flushing a furious, incandescent crimson that burned hotter than her starlight mana. "I am defending the honor of the High Seat! Lady Eluned is a paragon of celestial grace! A sovereign jewel of the ancient lineages! And she is bound to a—a—"
"A guy who just folded you in half with two punches?" Silas offered helpfully.
He shifted his weight and smoothly lifted his boot off her spine, stepping back to give her room.
The crushing pressure vanished.
Ther’Abella dragged in a deep burning lungful of mountain air with her chest heaving as she pushed herself up onto her hands and knees.
Every muscle along her ribs throbbed with a deep hollow ache where his bare knuckles had driven into her solar plexus, but her pride refused to let her stay down.

"I was off-balance!" she hissed, whirling around on her knees to glare up at him, her silver bangs sticking to her sweaty forehead. "You caught me mid-stride! If we engaged at true range beneath the open heavens, I would have—"
Pat! Pat!
Ther’Abella froze.
Her jaw clicked shut an her blue eyes went wide as saucers.

Silas had leaned down, his face split into a warm disarming smile and casually patted the top of her head twice, exactly the way one might comfort an overzealous guard dog that had barked at the mailman.

"Hey, it’s alright," Silas said, his voice dropping into a tone of gentle earnest approval. "It’s good that you’re looking out for Eluned. Honestly... As her former guard, it’s your job to be suspicious. A lady such as herself shouldn’t marry just anyone, and checking out the guy to see if he’s actually got the spine to protect her is exactly what a loyal soldier is supposed to do... I respect it..."
Ther’Abella sat completely paralyzed on the grass.
Her brain simply refused to process what she was hearing.
’Wh-what?’
She had expected him to sneer... She had expected him to draw a blade, demand an oath of submission, or brand her with a punishment spell or something.

Instead, his calloused hand was resting gently against the crown of her skull with his palm radiating a faint soothing warmth that somehow made the lingering starlight static in her meridians settle into quiet submission.

’What... what is wrong with this man?!’ her thoughts screamed, her cheeks burning so hot she felt dizzy. ’He’s patronizing me! He has to be! No sovereign treats an assassin like a petulant niece! Why isn’t he angry?!’
Before she could slap his hand away, Silas’s posture shifted.
He stepped inside her space, bent at the knees, hooked his thick right arm under her waist, and hoisted her straight off the ground.
"Whoa—hey!"
Ther’Abella let out an un-warrior-like squeak as the world flipped upside down.
In the span of a single heartbeat, the proud silver-armored veteran of the Viridian Guard found herself slung over Silas Graves’s right shoulder like a fifty-pound sack of winter potatoes.
Her legs dangled down his chest, her breastplate clanked against his back, and her face hung suspended behind his hip, staring directly at the damp heels of his boots.
"Put me down!" she shrieked, her hands frantically pushing against the small of his back. "Unclasp me this instant, you uncivilized brute! I am an elite officer! I have a name! I have rank!"
"Yeah, yeah, you’re an elite potato," Silas said cheerfully, adjusting his grip so she wouldn’t slip.
He turned toward Aeliana, gesturing with his free hand toward the winding stone path that cut through the rolling green hills. "Aeli, lead the way. Let’s go see what Aki’s been cooking up."
Aeliana stood a few paces back with her arms crossed beneath her bust.
Her silver-green eyes lingered on the way Silas’s hand was casually bracing Ther’Abella’s armored thigh, and for a fraction of a second, her lips pursed into a tiny unmistakable pout.
’Lucky bitch...’
A subtle sharp flicker of territorial jealousy rippled across her ethereal features before she quickly smoothed it over with a practiced angelic smile.

"Yes, Lord Sy," Aeliana purred, her voice dripping with melodic pointed sweetness as she stepped into stride beside him. "Let us go~. It would not do to keep Lady Aki waiting while you collect stray guards."
’Let me down! Let me down, curse your entire bloodline!’
Ther’Abella was throwing her entire weight from side to side, her armored boots kicking uselessly at the empty air.
She tried to drive her elbow into his ribs but Silas’s arm remained clamped around her middle like a band of forged dwarven steel.
His stride didn’t stutter and his breathing didn’t hitch either.
’Damn you!’

He walked with the effortless rolling gait of a man carrying a light satchel through an orchard, completely ignoring the fact that a high-tier Viridian warrior was throwing a full-blown tantrum against his spine.

’He is a monster,’ she realized in mortified despair with her fingers clawing helplessly at the thick linen of his tunic. ’He isn’t even circulating mana to hold me! This is pure unrefined physical power! How does a mortal man possess bones this heavy?!’
"Man," Silas murmured, tilting his head back to take in the sprawling vista ahead. "What a nice place."
The territory didn’t look anything like the rugged grandeur of Blessed Land.
Where his own domain was defined by what made it special, this new land felt vibrant and impossibly bright.
The sky above was a soft, twilight lavender, dotted with gentle pulsing constellations that cast a pearlescent sheen across the rolling hills.
The grass was a deep, vivid emerald, swaying in rhythm with a warm floral-scented breeze that carried none of the bitter chill of the Umbral Basin.

As they crested the first low ridge, Silas’s eyes caught a massive circular platform carved from pure crystalline quartz, ringed by spiraling silver pillars that looked like frozen water fountains and roses too.
"Is that her summoning altar?" Silas asked, his eyebrows lifting in genuine appreciation.

"It is," Aeliana confirmed, gliding gracefully over the cobblestone path. "Lady Aki’s one is a bit different from ours... She said that standard gray stone was ’aesthetically offensive’ to potential heroes."

"She’s not wrong," Silas chuckled, shaking his head. "Look at that... It looks way more luxurious than mine. Mine looks like an ancient sacrificial slab where you butcher goats while hers looks like a royal garden pavilion."
Well what mattered at the end of the day was what you pulled.
The perimeter of the quartz altar was blanketed in cascading beds of flowers.
Giant velvety roses in shades of deep violet and pastel peach spilled over the silver balustrades, their petals dusting the flagstones with glowing spirit pollen.
Beside them grew clusters of delicate bell-shaped blossoms that hummed with a soft chiming melody whenever the breeze caught them.

"The floral arrangement was Eluned’s gift," Aeliana noted, a fond smile gracing her lips as she lightly brushed the petal of a passing rose. "Aki begged her for half a day, and you know how weak Eluned is when it comes to that girl but I must admit, it gives the territory a remarkably serene atmosphere... Perhaps we should consider planting decorative flora around our own altar in Blessed Land, it would soften the imposing architecture."
"Not a bad idea," Silas agreed. "Remind me to talk to Eluned when we get back... A few flowerbeds might keep the place from looking like a military fortress all the time."
Over his shoulder, Ther’Abella let out an exasperated, muffled groan.
"Are you two genuinely critiquing landscape design while you treat me like luggage?!"
Silas casually tapped the flat of his hand against her armored thigh.
"Hush now, potato. The adults are talking."
"I am seven hundred years older than you!" she shrieked into his back.
Silas merely laughed, his gaze already shifting toward the horizon and there, nestled in the center of the valley beneath the shadow of a crystalline cliffside, stood the Keep.
Silas’s mouth slowly curled upward, his lips twitching as he struggled and failed to maintain a straight face.
"Well," Silas remarked, his shoulders shaking with silent laughter. "That’s... certainly a statement."
The structure was undeniably impressive.
Like his own Keep, it stood five full stories tall, constructed from heavy seamless stone blocks that spoke of defensive stability.

It was broad at the base, tapering into elegant sweeping towers with high arched balconies, graceful spires, and an abundance of wide diamond-paned bay windows that caught the starlight like polished gems.
One of the other differences was the color... The entire building was painted a soft pastel baby pink.

The window frames were trimmed in gleaming white marble, the high conical roofs of the corner spires were tiled in shimmering rose-gold slate, and fluttering from the highest parapet was a massive, silk banner bearing an embroidered crest... a smiling white bunny wearing a golden crown, surrounded by a ring of sparkling stars.
"It’s pink," Silas stated.

"It is," Aeliana replied, her composure breaking as a quiet snicker escaped her. "Lady Aki informed Eluned that if her Keep looked like a brooding dungeon, she would refuse to sleep in it... She personally mixed the mineral dyes for the outer masonry."

"Honestly?" Silas smiled, shaking his head with genuine affection. "It looks great. It’s totally her... A lot better than some grim, soot-stained fortress where you expect gargoyles to start weeping blood."

chapters.title: Chapter 671: Aki’s Wonderland
paragraphs: Just beyond the pastel Keep, situated along a lower terrace of the hill, lay the military district.
Unlike the playful aesthetic of the main residence, the barracks were built with serious craftsmanship.
Long sturdy longhouses constructed from dark pine and reinforced with iron braces formed an orderly quadrangle around a wide dirt training yard, and the yard was nearly empty.
The rest of the vanguard was out hunting as only two women sat on the perimeter bench by the weapon racks in the afternoon sun, one waxing a recurve bow and the other oiling a spearhead.
They were tall, athletic, and possessed the sharp disciplined posture of seasoned soldiers, but what caught Silas’s eye immediately was their gear.
Both of them wore a new uniform of dark steel plate and forest-green cloaks, cut in the style of Blessed Land’s own vanguard and stitched along the hem with fresh gold thread.
’Hm... a new uniform?’
Silas walked down the sloping path toward the yard, shifting Ther’Abella slightly on his shoulder.
"How many did she pull on her initial summoning batch?"
From over his shoulder, Ther’Abella grumbled, having finally given up on squirming to conserve her breath.

"Lady Aki has summoned thirty auxiliaries, and myself," she muttered reluctantly. "Twenty on the first day and ten more this morning... She told us she would construct additional residential quarters as the territory stabilized, but for now, we share the primary longhouse."
"Thirty-one," Silas mused, nodding in approval. "Solid starting pool... That’s enough to establish perimeter watches and run perimeter sweeps without burning everyone out."
The crunch of Silas’s boots on the gravel of the training yard drew immediate attention.
One of the warrior women, a tall broad-shouldered archer with a scar across her jaw, looked up from her bow.
Her eyes widened as she caught sight of Aeliana, and then drifted toward the dark-haired young man walking beside her, carrying their First Hero upside down like a sack of grain.
"Stand to!" the archer barked, rising instantly.
Beside her, the younger spearwoman dropped her spearhead into the dirt and scrambled upright, snapping into the same crisp posture half a second later.
Aeliana stepped forward, raising her chin with regal grace.
"At ease, soldiers of the vanguard... Presenting Lord Silas Graves, Sovereign of Blessed Land and Lord of this domain’s High Seat."
The reaction was instantaneous.
The two women dropped smoothly onto one knee with their armored plates clanking in unison against the packed dirt of the yard and their heads bowed in reverent respect.
"We greet the Sovereign!" they chorused, two voices ringing out with crisp discipline.
Silas chuckled warmly, waving his free hand to signal them up.
"At ease, both of you. Please, stand up. You don’t need to kneel in the dirt every time I walk by."
The two women rose, their posture relaxing slightly, but their eyes remained fixed on him.
Curious, vibrant gazes swept over his frame, taking in the casual, unbothered way he stood, the easy confidence in his posture, and the undeniably handsome sharp features of his face.
A startled breath escaped the younger one.
’He’s... he’s the High Lord?’ the young spearwoman thought, a sudden bright flush creeping up her neck. ’He looks so young! And he’s... remarkably cute...’
’He took down Ther’Abella without even drawing a blade?’ the archer thought, her eyes wide with admiration. ’Look at him! He’s carrying her like she weighs nothing at all!’

"I’m glad to have all of you as part of Blessed Land’s extended family," Silas said, offering them a bright genuine smile that made the younger spearwoman blush furiously. "I hope Aki’s treating you well? She can be a bit of a whirlwind when she gets excited, but her heart’s always in the right place..."

"Lady Aki is wonderful, my Lord!" the scarred archer replied eagerly, stepping forward with a broad grin. "She provided us with fresh rations within an hour of our arrival, and she’s already promised us custom armaments once the forge is made! She is an exceptional Lady!"
"Glad to hear it," Silas smiled. "Where is she right now? I came over to see how she was settling in."
The archer gestured toward the southern boundary of the valley.

"Lady Aki and the rest of the unit are currently outside the perimeter wall, my Lord! They’re running a suppression sweep through the outer groves, clearing wild beasts to stock up our cold storage with fresh meat... Would you like us to escort you to the front line?"
Silas nodded. "Lead the way."
The two women fell in on either side of them, their faces beaming with pride at the assignment, and began guiding them along the main flagstone avenue that cut through the center of the settlement.
As they walked, the two escort guards eagerly pointed out the layout of the burgeoning territory.

"Lady Aki designed the residential sectors to circle the Keep in rings," the lead guard explained, her hand sweeping toward the wide open plazas currently marked with white chalk lines and foundation pegs. "The barracks sit here on the inner flank, while the workshop pavilions and alchemy shop will be positioned near the eastern riverbed to utilize the water currents."
Soon, the open fields gave way to the outer perimeter, and Silas found himself looking up at a massive imposing barrier.
’I’m jealous...’
Silas couldn’t do this with the Umbral Basin if he tried, why couldn’t he get a better zone, huh?
The wall was at least forty feet high, forged from solid interlocking slabs of dark, matte-black steel that drank in the starlight.
It was thick, imposing, and lined with sharp runic bevels that hummed with heavy dampening fields.

Despite its density, the design was remarkably clever with narrow, reinforced slit-windows and elevated parapets allowing a panoramic view of the wild untamed forests that stretched beyond the settlement’s borders.
Nestled along the inner base of the black steel wall were several sprawling, lush gardens.

"Lady Eluned grew these yesterday," the second escort said proudly, pointing toward the rows of vibrant, shimmering flora. "She spent three hours channeling her wood mana into the soil before she went outside to watch Lady Aki."
Among the neatly tilled rows of spirit herbs stood a grove of low, elegant trees with twisting silver bark and broad, emerald leaves.
Hanging from the branches were clusters of large, perfectly spherical fruits that glowed with a soft radiant golden light.
Without waiting for permission, one of the escort guards nimbly leaped into the branches, plucked two of the glowing fruits, and dropped back down to the path with a bright grin.

"Here, my Lord!" she said, offering one to Silas and one to Aeliana. "Lady Eluned said these are Golden Star Apples! She told us they nourish both the physical marrow and the soul pathways, helping newly awakened warriors stabilize their core channels after prolonged combat."
Silas took the fruit.
The skin was cool and smooth, glowing faintly against his palm like a polished topaz as he brought it to his mouth and took a crisp hearty bite.
Crunch!
A burst of intensely sweet nectar flooded his mouth, tasting of wild honey, crisp mountain pear, and fresh spring water.
The moment the juice slid down his throat with a gentle soothing warmth bloomed behind his breastbone, radiating outward through his meridians like a wave of pure liquid vitality.
It swept away the microscopic fatigue from his earlier clash with Seraphina, leaving his senses sharp and refreshed.
"Damn," Silas breathed, his eyes lighting up. "That is incredible. Eluned really outdid herself with these... Remind me to steal a dozen saplings for the main garden back home."
Aeliana took a delicate bite of her own fruit with a serene smile gracing her lips.
"I am certain she has already prepared a nursery bed specifically for your Keep, Lord Sy. She knows how fond Morwenna is of fresh orchard produce."
They reached the massive southern gatehouse.
Instead of heavy iron winches, chains, or cumbersome manual wheels, the gate was sealed by a single monolithic slab of black steel inscribed with a massive array of interlocking runes.
The lead guard stepped up to a raised pedestal beside the archway.
She placed her bare palm against the central crystal node, channeling a thin measured thread of her mana into the stone.
HUUUUUUUUM.
The runes flared with brilliant cerulean light.

With a deep hiss that sounded like a hydraulic vault unsealing, the colossal steel slab split down the center, sliding smoothly into hidden recesses within the flanking towers without making a single screech of metal.
Silas watched the mechanism with keen interest.

’Now that is slick,’ Silas thought, admiring the clean engineering. ’A simple mana-keyed bypass. I really need to implement this on the the side gates we plan to build back at Blessed Land... This is many times more efficient than opening a new one.’
He looked up at the empty parapets flanking the high gatehouse.

’And turrets,’ he reminded himself, his mind already drifting toward his upcoming trip to Central City. ’I need to browse the high-tier defensive artificer stalls... If I can purchase automated mana-pulse ballistas or autonomous crystal turrets, the guards won’t have to mount twenty-four-hour watches on the walls in freezing rain as the arrays can handle standard perimeter deterrence on their own.’
He reached into his mental ledger, reviewing his assets.

’I still have those Troop Summoning tickets sitting in my reserve storage... I should crack a few open later If I can pull more craft-oriented dwarves to join the dozen we already have, we can finally build our own heavy munitions forges and if the tickets don’t drop what I need... Central City has mercenary exchanges and specialized artisan markets. I can get skilled dwarves directly from guilds or other places, There’s a lot of business to settle out there.’
The heavy gates completed their cycle, revealing the untamed wilderness beyond.
The moment they stepped through the threshold, the warm tranquil atmosphere of the valley vanished, replaced by the wild chill of the outer territory.
The canopy overhead grew dense and tangled, the trees towering nearly eighty feet into the lavender sky with their gnarled roots twisting across the damp forest floor like dormant serpents.
The lead escort guard immediately raised her hand, her posture stiffening into active combat vigilance.

"Keep your senses sharp, my Lord," she warned softly, her hand resting on the hilt of her broadsword. "The wild zones in this territory harbor two distinct varieties of threats. There are the standard roving predators... dire wolves, horned drakes, and underground burrowers but the more dangerous ones are the flora... Plant-type ambush monsters that mimic vegetation. They have no beating hearts, so reading their presence through aura detection is nearly impossible until they strike."
"Understood," Silas said, though he didn’t tense up in the slightest.
With his Gold Core foundation, the mana fluctuations of the entire forest were already mapped out in his mind like ink drawn across white paper.
As they walked down a mossy deer trail, the escort guards keeping their eyes glued to the thickets, a massive ancient-looking willow tree with thick weeping vines suddenly trembled.
CREEEEEAK!
The bark along the trunk split open with a sickening wet tearing sound.

Two hollow glowing yellow eyes flared to life within the timber, and four colossal branch-like arms tipped with razor-sharp wooden barbs lashed outward, shrieking through the air directly toward the two escort guards!
Behind it the roots tore free of the forest floor in a spray of black soil, a tangle of limbs as thick as siege columns thrashing across the trail to cut off any retreat.
"Ambush—!" the archer began, reaching for her quiver.
SNAP!
Aeliana didn’t break stride as she lifted her left hand and flicked her wrist toward the charging horror as casually as shaking water off her fingers.
FROOOOOST!
A blinding crystalline wave of absolute zero ice-mana erupted from her fingertips...
The air temperature plummeted instantly with frost crystallizing across the grass in a sixty-foot cone, and the vines whipping through the air stiffened, whitened, and snapped off like glass rods.
The wave raced up the nearest barbed arm faster than the eye could follow, and the moisture within its cellular fibers froze solid.
The azure frost crawled up the trunk, along every branch, down into the thrashing roots, and into the glowing core in less than a microsecond.
The monster’s yellow eyes went wide as it tried to roar, and the sound came out as a thin brittle crack as the ice reached its throat.
Aeliana closed her fist.
SHATTER!

The massive eight-ton arboreal terror exploded into a million glittering harmless fragments of blue ice, raining down onto the forest floor like a winter hailstorm and chiming against the stones of the trail.
A single frost-white splinter drifted lazily past the archer’s nose and settled on her sleeve.
Upside down over Silas’s shoulder, Ther’Abella had stopped squirming.
’One flick,’ she thought, staring at the glittering ice. ’Everyone in this territory is a monster.’
The two escort guards stared at the shower of ice crystals with their weapons half-drawn and their breath catching in their throats.
They turned to look at the serene High Elf princess with a collective shiver running down their spines.
"T-This place is truly bizarre and dangerous..." the archer stammered, swallowing hard as she sheepishly sheathed her sword. "Thank you, Miss Aeliana."
"Pay it no mind," Aeliana smiled gently, brushing a stray snowflake from her sleeve. "A weed is simply a flower in the wrong place and that one was remarkably poorly placed."

They continued down the winding trail for another five minutes until the dense forest opened up into a massive sunlit clearing bordered by a rushing mountain stream and the scene that greeted them was... chaos.

Silas couldn’t do this with the Umbral Basin if he tried, why couldn’t he get a better zone, huh?
