chapters.title: Chapter 672: Enhanced Destruction
paragraphs: In the center of the meadow, the remaining twenty-eight summoned warrior women were locked in combat with a massive pack of shadow-tusk boars and stone-carapace badgers.
’Nice...’
They were executing textbook military coordination.

A boar the size of a wagon thundered into the shield line and the front rank braced as one with their boots sliding through the dirt and earth-mana flaring up through their greaves to lock their stances.

As the beast bounced off the wall of steel with a boom that shook leaves from the trees... Two spears punched through the gaps on either side of the shields, one into the eye and one up under the jaw, and the boar dropped.
A stone-carapace badger burrowed beneath the line and erupted behind the archers, and the nearest two women dropped their bows, drew short blades, and carved it open before the dust settled.

"Switch!" a sergeant barked, and the shield-bearers cycled out in rotation without a single gap while fresh arrows whistled overhead in tight mana-infused volleys that shattered skulls from fifty paces away.
Silas watched the display, nodding in quiet appreciation.
’That’s good,’ Silas thought. ’They aren’t just strong individuals... their teamwork is exceptional as well, Aki won’t have to micromanage every border skirmish with troops this well-drilled.’
His gaze drifted past the main skirmish toward a colossal weeping willow situated on a raised knoll by the riverbank.
Sitting casually against the thick trunk was Thor.

The hulking golden-haired warrior was completely ignoring the battle, an enormous wooden flagon of ale clutched in one massive hand while her other held a half-eaten roasted wild boar leg that was the size of a man’s torso.
She tore off a massive hunk of meat with her teeth, chewing contentedly before letting out a boisterous thunderous burp that made the leaves above her rustle.
Sitting right beside her on a flat boulder was Morwenna.

The dark-haired Captain had Tidebringer propped against her knee, calmly slicing thin elegant strips of roasted meat with a small utility knife and popping them into her mouth with stoic indifference.
’I miss Silas...’ Morwenna thought.
And standing just a few paces away at the edge of the knoll was Eluned.

The pristine former Goddess of the World Tree was waving a small silk handkerchief, bouncing lightly on her heels, and shouting encouragement at the top of her lungs with the doting enthusiasm of a mother at a children’s sports festival.
"That’s it, my darling! Step inside its guard! Watch the club! Beautiful footwork, sweet girl! Show that overgrown brute what a true lady can do!"
Silas followed Eluned’s frantic waving, his eyes landing on the far side of the clearing.
...There, standing in the middle of a flattened crater of crushed dirt, was Aki and facing her was a nine-foot-tall mountain troll.
The beast was a nightmare of muscle and stone, its mottled gray hide encrusted with jagged granite plates and a massive iron-banded tree trunk clutched in its fist like a club.
"RAAAHHHHH!" It roared with a deafening bellow that sent spit and foul breath spraying across the grass, and swung the club down in a devastating vertical slam that could have flattened a war wagon.
Silas’s instincts flared.
His foot shifted forward, his hand reflexively rising to unleash a gale-force wind blast to swat the beast aside then, he stopped.
’Wait...’ Silas narrowed his eyes, his foot settling back into the grass. ’She feels... confident.’
Aki did not run, scream, or cower behind a barrier.

Her movement was fluid and frighteningly precise... As the massive wooden club came crashing down, she took a single diagonal step forward, slipping inside the weapon’s lethal arc by less than an inch.
BOOOOOM!
The club pulverized the earth where her heels had just been, sending a shower of dirt and shattered rock into the air.
Aki was already moving through the debris with her hair streaming behind her.
She had no weapon, all she had there were her small delicate hands but as she closed the distance her posture dropped into a low coiled martial stance.
WHOOSH!
She stepped into the pocket with her bare palm driving upward like a piston into the soft joint beneath the troll’s armored kneecap.
CRACK!

A concussive shockwave of internal mana detonated through the joint and the nine-foot behemoth let out a startled howl as its right leg buckled and its massive frame crashed onto one knee, shaking the clearing.
Aki pivoted instantly.
She used the bent knee as a step and ran up the troll’s thigh in two light bounds with her left elbow whipping around to drive into the monster’s exposed solar plexus.
BANG!
"GAH!"
She landed on its forearm, spun, and brought a rising palm strike up under its stone-plated chin that snapped its head back with an audible crunch.
Thump, thump, thump!
Aki took a deep breath and her heartbeat counted in her ears.
’Good... Good... Keep moving!’

The beast swatted at her with a backhand that would have flattened a house however Aki dropped flat beneath it, felt the wind of its passing rip the ribbon from her hair, and rolled away across the dirt.
She came up in a crouch with her chest heaving slightly and a wide fierce grin on her face.
"Alright!"
The troll stumbled upright, shaking its massive head as its tiny red eyes burned with rage.
’I’ve raged it enough... It’s time to finish it.’
Aki leaped back, landing lightly on the balls of her feet.
Her bright cheerful blue eyes suddenly darkened with the vibrant azure swirling and bleeding into a deep ominous royal purple.
’Destruction...’ she thought, her focus narrowing down to a single razor-sharp point.
Deep within her soul, she reached for that foreign terrifying authority... the royal-purple primordial flame she had inherited through her lineage and she found it.
FWOOSH!
A jet of pure royal-purple fire erupted from her extended palm and struck the troll squarely in the center of its chest.
"SKREEEEEEEEEEEEEEE!"
The beast let out an ear-piercing unnatural shriek that sounded like grinding metal and tried patting it out, however the purple fire did not burn like normal flame... It consumed.

The jagged granite plates on its chest began to dissolve into drifting violet ash with the flesh beneath melting away as the conceptual law of Destruction tore through the monster’s physical structure on a cellular level.
Yet, beneath her bangs, Aki’s brow furrowed in frustration.
’I’ve wondered again and again... how does Father wield this power so effortlessly?’
Her internal thoughts raced as she watched the purple fire spread. Her natural affinity for Destruction was still painfully low compared to him.
To her father, the flame was an extension of his breath, a casual flick of the wrist that erased entire mountains from reality without a second thought but to her...?
To her, it felt like trying to channel molten lead through glass pipes.
Despite the fire eating away at its chest, the troll’s monstrous vitality and regenerative core refused to yield.
The flesh around the wound blackened and crumbled, but the beast roared through the agony, raised its massive fists, and charged straight at her with suicidal fury with each stride shaking the earth.
’It’s not enough,’ Aki realized, watching the nine-foot shadow loom over her. ’At this rate, it will reach me before the flame finishes consuming its heart.’
She planted her boots, locking her knees as she closed her eyes.
’I finally have it...’ she thought with a fierce defiant light igniting in her gaze. ’I know the frequency now. It’s going to hurt like hell... but I just have to force the output!’
She clamped down on her core with ruthless willpower.
THUMP!
Her soul throbbed violently with an agonizing white-hot spasm tearing through her internal pathways through her core.
Drip!
A thin line of crimson blood leaked from the corner of her right eye, trailing down her pale cheek like a bloody tear as the optic nerves screamed under the mana pressure.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The purple flames of Destruction violently flared outward, tripling in size, transforming from a thin jet into a roaring ravenous vortex of annihilation.
A shockwave of violet light rolled across the clearing and flattened the grass in a ring, whipped every cloak, and made the water of the mountain stream jump out of its bed.
Across the meadow, Thor stopped with the boar leg halfway to her mouth.
"Oho~" She muttered with her eyebrows climbing.
Morwenna’s knife paused mid-slice while Eluned’s handkerchief froze in the air as she pressed her other hand over her heart.
The charging troll never got the chance to swing.
The moment the expanded purple vortex touched its hide, the monster simply ceased to exist.
Its armored shoulders, its roaring head, its massive limbs, and its colossal stone club dissolved into fine glittering dust, scattering into the wind as if it had never existed in this realm at all.
WHOOSH.
The purple fire snapped out, leaving behind a clean, empty crater in the grass.
Aki staggered backward three steps with her small boots dragging through the dirt as her chest rising and falling in ragged breathless gasps.
’I’m good...’ she told herself, pressing a trembling hand against her ribs. ’I’m still on my feet.’

Her right eye was pitch black and her vision on that side completely blinded by the blown capillaries and ruptured mana channels but before the panic could set in, a soft emerald-green rune carved along her collarbone flared with warm soothing light.
Tingle!
The high-tier regeneration rune went to work instantly, knitting the delicate ocular vessels, clearing the pooled blood, and restoring her vision to crystal clarity within three heartbeats.
Aki reached up with the back of her sleeve, scrubbing the drying blood from her cheek with her heart still hammering against her ribs.

’So that’s what it really is...’ she thought, staring at the empty crater where the troll had been. ’Destruction doesn’t burn things, and it doesn’t break them either... It tells them they aren’t allowed to exist anymore, and they listen in a way. No wonder the regeneration couldn’t keep up... You can’t heal something that isn’t there.’
It was dumb but she always thought that Destruction just destroyed things on a molecular level, Aki flexed her tingling fingers.

’And at my level, it only just works... Once I push past the threshold, nothing survives it, not even a troll that regrows its own flesh but the price is awful. I just used one blast and my eye bled, if I do two in a row and I’m blind on this side for good... Father makes it look like breathing, and I’m over here pushing a boulder uphill with my face.’
She let out a long breath, shaking out her tingling hands then, she turned around and froze.
Standing at the edge of the clearing, watching her with a warm proud smile, was Silas.
Aki’s eyes went wide.
The grim expression of a warrior vanished in a fraction of a millisecond, replaced instantly by pure joy.
"SILAS!" she screamed at the top of her lungs.
She didn’t care about her sore muscles and she didn’t care about the twenty-eight warrior women watching her from the clearing, nor did she care that she was currently covered in dirt and soot.
She threw her arms out and sprinted across the meadow at full speed with her boots barely touching the grass as she charged straight toward him like an overly affectionate puppy.
"Silas! You came! You actually—"
She skidded to an abrupt halt five feet away, her arms dropping to her sides, her head tilting with comical confusion.
Her bright blue eyes slowly drifted from Silas’s face... downward... to the armored figure still slung unceremoniously over his right shoulder like a prize-winning salmon.
Aki blinked once then twice.
"Uhm..." Aki pointed a small, hesitant finger at the upside-down warrior. "Silas? Why do you have my First Hero on your shoulder? Is she... broken?"
From his shoulder, Ther’Abella let out a muffled dying whimper of irreparable shame.
She didn’t want Lady Aki to see her like this!
Silas chuckled.
He reached around, grabbed Ther’Abella by the collar of her silver cuirass, and casually set her down onto her feet on the grass beside him.

The proud Viridian officer immediately staggered, clutching her sore ribs with her face still burning a brilliant furious red as she glared daggers at the turf, completely unable to meet her Lady’s eyes.
Silas stepped forward, closing the distance between himself and Aki.
He reached out with both hands, gently ruffling the messy bangs on top of her head with an affectionate grin.
"We were just playing," Silas said, his voice warm, gentle, and utterly sincere. "Officially, though... congratulations on becoming a Lord, Aki. You did great."
Aki’s cheeks flushed a bright radiant pink at his words, her blue eyes shimmering with open affection.
"It’s only because of you, Silas," she murmured shyly, ducking her head slightly while shifting her weight from foot to foot.

She began hopping in place, tiny springy bounces with both heels leaving the grass at once and her bangs bouncing with every landing, looking so much like an excited bunny that Silas half expected a cottontail tail to start wagging behind her.
"If you hadn’t helped me with the core foundation... I would never have stabilized the territory."
She stopped hopping with her hands nervously fidgeting with the hem of her soot-stained tunic as she looked up through her lashes.
"Can I... hug you?" she asked in a small, hopeful voice.
Silas chuckled warmly, opening his arms wide in an easy invitation.
Aki didn’t hesitate for a single second.
She threw herself forward, wrapping her arms around his torso and burying her face into his chest, squeezing him with enough raw awakened enthusiasm that his ribs gave a small protesting creak.
Silas smiled, resting one hand against the back of her head, completely accustomed to her bursts of affection now.
Standing three paces away, clutching her still-tender ribs, Ther’Abella’s jaw dropped in horror.
’What in the celestial heavens am I looking at...?’ the First Hero thought, her blue eyes burning with outrage as she stared at the scene.

’He is embracing another woman! Right out in the open! Without a shred of shame or modesty!’ Her gaze darted frantically over toward Princess Aeliana, and then further toward the weeping willow where Lady Eluned had been watching. ’When his lawful wife is standing right there?! He is two-timi—’
Before the thought could even finish forming in her scandalized mind, the heavy crunch of gravel announced a new arrival.
Morwenna stepped into the clearing.
The tall dark-haired pirate carried her halberd loosely over one shoulder, still chewing on a strip of smoked meat.
Without waiting for Aki to fully disengage, Morwenna casually leaned in, caught Silas by the scruff of his collar, and planted a firm resounding kiss directly onto his cheek.
Smack!

"Welcome back, Silas," Morwenna said with chuckle, patting his back twice with a hand that lingered a half-second longer than it needed to with a small flush creeping along her cheekbones that she hid behind a bite of smoked meat. "You took your sweet time..."
Silas grinned, rubbing his cheek. "Good to see you too, Morwenna."
Ther’Abella’s knees nearly buckled.
Her eyes bulged so wide they threatened to roll right out of their sockets with her mouth working silently like a beached fish.
’No...’ she screamed internally, her hands flying up to grip her silver hair in panic. ’He isn’t two-timing! He’s three-timing! Three of them! In broad daylight! In front of the entire regiment!’
The depravity of it made her blood run cold.
What kind of degenerate unprincipled scoundrel had infiltrated Lady Eluned’s life?! He was a walking moral catastr—
"Darling~!"

sentences.text: In the center of the meadow, the remaining twenty-eight summoned warrior women were locked in combat with a massive pack of shadow-tusk boars and stone-carapace badgers.
’Nice...’
They were executing textbook military coordination.

A boar the size of a wagon thundered into the shield line and the front rank braced as one with their boots sliding through the dirt and earth-mana flaring up through their greaves to lock their stances.
As the beast bounced off the wall of steel with a boom that shook leaves from the trees...
Two spears punched through the gaps on either side of the shields, one into the eye and one up under the jaw, and the boar dropped.
A stone-carapace badger burrowed beneath the line and erupted behind the archers, and the nearest two women dropped their bows, drew short blades, and carved it open before the dust settled.

"Switch!" a sergeant barked, and the shield-bearers cycled out in rotation without a single gap while fresh arrows whistled overhead in tight mana-infused volleys that shattered skulls from fifty paces away.
Silas watched the display, nodding in quiet appreciation.
’That’s good,’ Silas thought. ’They aren’t just strong individuals... their teamwork is exceptional as well, Aki won’t have to micromanage every border skirmish with troops this well-drilled.’
His gaze drifted past the main skirmish toward a colossal weeping willow situated on a raised knoll by the riverbank.
Sitting casually against the thick trunk was Thor.

The hulking golden-haired warrior was completely ignoring the battle, an enormous wooden flagon of ale clutched in one massive hand while her other held a half-eaten roasted wild boar leg that was the size of a man’s torso.
She tore off a massive hunk of meat with her teeth, chewing contentedly before letting out a boisterous thunderous burp that made the leaves above her rustle.
Sitting right beside her on a flat boulder was Morwenna.

The dark-haired Captain had Tidebringer propped against her knee, calmly slicing thin elegant strips of roasted meat with a small utility knife and popping them into her mouth with stoic indifference.
’I miss Silas...’ Morwenna thought.
And standing just a few paces away at the edge of the knoll was Eluned.

The pristine former Goddess of the World Tree was waving a small silk handkerchief, bouncing lightly on her heels, and shouting encouragement at the top of her lungs with the doting enthusiasm of a mother at a children’s sports festival.
"That’s it, my darling!
Step inside its guard!
Watch the club!
Beautiful footwork, sweet girl!
Show that overgrown brute what a true lady can do!"
Silas followed Eluned’s frantic waving, his eyes landing on the far side of the clearing.
...There, standing in the middle of a flattened crater of crushed dirt, was Aki and facing her was a nine-foot-tall mountain troll.
The beast was a nightmare of muscle and stone, its mottled gray hide encrusted with jagged granite plates and a massive iron-banded tree trunk clutched in its fist like a club.
"RAAAHHHHH!" It roared with a deafening bellow that sent spit and foul breath spraying across the grass, and swung the club down in a devastating vertical slam that could have flattened a war wagon.
Silas’s instincts flared.
His foot shifted forward, his hand reflexively rising to unleash a gale-force wind blast to swat the beast aside then, he stopped.
’Wait...’ Silas narrowed his eyes, his foot settling back into the grass. ’She feels... confident.’
Aki did not run, scream, or cower behind a barrier.
Her movement was fluid and frighteningly precise...
As the massive wooden club came crashing down, she took a single diagonal step forward, slipping inside the weapon’s lethal arc by less than an inch.
BOOOOOM!
The club pulverized the earth where her heels had just been, sending a shower of dirt and shattered rock into the air.
Aki was already moving through the debris with her hair streaming behind her.
She had no weapon, all she had there were her small delicate hands but as she closed the distance her posture dropped into a low coiled martial stance.
WHOOSH!
She stepped into the pocket with her bare palm driving upward like a piston into the soft joint beneath the troll’s armored kneecap.
CRACK!

A concussive shockwave of internal mana detonated through the joint and the nine-foot behemoth let out a startled howl as its right leg buckled and its massive frame crashed onto one knee, shaking the clearing.
Aki pivoted instantly.
She used the bent knee as a step and ran up the troll’s thigh in two light bounds with her left elbow whipping around to drive into the monster’s exposed solar plexus.
BANG!
"GAH!"
She landed on its forearm, spun, and brought a rising palm strike up under its stone-plated chin that snapped its head back with an audible crunch.
Thump, thump, thump!
Aki took a deep breath and her heartbeat counted in her ears.
’Good...
Good...
Keep moving!’

The beast swatted at her with a backhand that would have flattened a house however Aki dropped flat beneath it, felt the wind of its passing rip the ribbon from her hair, and rolled away across the dirt.
She came up in a crouch with her chest heaving slightly and a wide fierce grin on her face.
"Alright!"
The troll stumbled upright, shaking its massive head as its tiny red eyes burned with rage.
’I’ve raged it enough...
It’s time to finish it.’
Aki leaped back, landing lightly on the balls of her feet.
Her bright cheerful blue eyes suddenly darkened with the vibrant azure swirling and bleeding into a deep ominous royal purple.
’Destruction...’ she thought, her focus narrowing down to a single razor-sharp point.
Deep within her soul, she reached for that foreign terrifying authority... the royal-purple primordial flame she had inherited through her lineage and she found it.
FWOOSH!
A jet of pure royal-purple fire erupted from her extended palm and struck the troll squarely in the center of its chest.
"SKREEEEEEEEEEEEEEE!"
The beast let out an ear-piercing unnatural shriek that sounded like grinding metal and tried patting it out, however the purple fire did not burn like normal flame...
It consumed.

The jagged granite plates on its chest began to dissolve into drifting violet ash with the flesh beneath melting away as the conceptual law of Destruction tore through the monster’s physical structure on a cellular level.
Yet, beneath her bangs, Aki’s brow furrowed in frustration.
’I’ve wondered again and again... how does Father wield this power so effortlessly?’
Her internal thoughts raced as she watched the purple fire spread.
Her natural affinity for Destruction was still painfully low compared to him.
To her father, the flame was an extension of his breath, a casual flick of the wrist that erased entire mountains from reality without a second thought but to her...?
To her, it felt like trying to channel molten lead through glass pipes.
Despite the fire eating away at its chest, the troll’s monstrous vitality and regenerative core refused to yield.
The flesh around the wound blackened and crumbled, but the beast roared through the agony, raised its massive fists, and charged straight at her with suicidal fury with each stride shaking the earth.
’It’s not enough,’ Aki realized, watching the nine-foot shadow loom over her. ’At this rate, it will reach me before the flame finishes consuming its heart.’
She planted her boots, locking her knees as she closed her eyes.
’I finally have it...’ she thought with a fierce defiant light igniting in her gaze. ’I know the frequency now.
It’s going to hurt like hell... but I just have to force the output!’
She clamped down on her core with ruthless willpower.
THUMP!
Her soul throbbed violently with an agonizing white-hot spasm tearing through her internal pathways through her core.
Drip!
A thin line of crimson blood leaked from the corner of her right eye, trailing down her pale cheek like a bloody tear as the optic nerves screamed under the mana pressure.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The purple flames of Destruction violently flared outward, tripling in size, transforming from a thin jet into a roaring ravenous vortex of annihilation.
A shockwave of violet light rolled across the clearing and flattened the grass in a ring, whipped every cloak, and made the water of the mountain stream jump out of its bed.
Across the meadow, Thor stopped with the boar leg halfway to her mouth.
"Oho~" She muttered with her eyebrows climbing.
Morwenna’s knife paused mid-slice while Eluned’s handkerchief froze in the air as she pressed her other hand over her heart.
The charging troll never got the chance to swing.
The moment the expanded purple vortex touched its hide, the monster simply ceased to exist.
Its armored shoulders, its roaring head, its massive limbs, and its colossal stone club dissolved into fine glittering dust, scattering into the wind as if it had never existed in this realm at all.
WHOOSH.
The purple fire snapped out, leaving behind a clean, empty crater in the grass.
Aki staggered backward three steps with her small boots dragging through the dirt as her chest rising and falling in ragged breathless gasps.
’I’m good...’ she told herself, pressing a trembling hand against her ribs. ’I’m still on my feet.’

Her right eye was pitch black and her vision on that side completely blinded by the blown capillaries and ruptured mana channels but before the panic could set in, a soft emerald-green rune carved along her collarbone flared with warm soothing light.
Tingle!
The high-tier regeneration rune went to work instantly, knitting the delicate ocular vessels, clearing the pooled blood, and restoring her vision to crystal clarity within three heartbeats.
Aki reached up with the back of her sleeve, scrubbing the drying blood from her cheek with her heart still hammering against her ribs.
’So that’s what it really is...’ she thought, staring at the empty crater where the troll had been. ’Destruction doesn’t burn things, and it doesn’t break them either...
It tells them they aren’t allowed to exist anymore, and they listen in a way.
No wonder the regeneration couldn’t keep up...
You can’t heal something that isn’t there.’
It was dumb but she always thought that Destruction just destroyed things on a molecular level, Aki flexed her tingling fingers.
’And at my level, it only just works...
Once I push past the threshold, nothing survives it, not even a troll that regrows its own flesh but the price is awful.
I just used one blast and my eye bled, if I do two in a row and I’m blind on this side for good...
Father makes it look like breathing, and I’m over here pushing a boulder uphill with my face.’
She let out a long breath, shaking out her tingling hands then, she turned around and froze.
Standing at the edge of the clearing, watching her with a warm proud smile, was Silas.
Aki’s eyes went wide.
The grim expression of a warrior vanished in a fraction of a millisecond, replaced instantly by pure joy.
"SILAS!" she screamed at the top of her lungs.
She didn’t care about her sore muscles and she didn’t care about the twenty-eight warrior women watching her from the clearing, nor did she care that she was currently covered in dirt and soot.
She threw her arms out and sprinted across the meadow at full speed with her boots barely touching the grass as she charged straight toward him like an overly affectionate puppy.
"Silas!
You came!
You actually—"
She skidded to an abrupt halt five feet away, her arms dropping to her sides, her head tilting with comical confusion.
Her bright blue eyes slowly drifted from Silas’s face... downward... to the armored figure still slung unceremoniously over his right shoulder like a prize-winning salmon.
Aki blinked once then twice.
"Uhm..." Aki pointed a small, hesitant finger at the upside-down warrior.
"Silas?
Why do you have my First Hero on your shoulder?
Is she... broken?"
From his shoulder, Ther’Abella let out a muffled dying whimper of irreparable shame.
She didn’t want Lady Aki to see her like this!
Silas chuckled.
He reached around, grabbed Ther’Abella by the collar of her silver cuirass, and casually set her down onto her feet on the grass beside him.

The proud Viridian officer immediately staggered, clutching her sore ribs with her face still burning a brilliant furious red as she glared daggers at the turf, completely unable to meet her Lady’s eyes.
Silas stepped forward, closing the distance between himself and Aki.
He reached out with both hands, gently ruffling the messy bangs on top of her head with an affectionate grin.
"We were just playing," Silas said, his voice warm, gentle, and utterly sincere.
"Officially, though... congratulations on becoming a Lord, Aki.
You did great."
Aki’s cheeks flushed a bright radiant pink at his words, her blue eyes shimmering with open affection.
"It’s only because of you, Silas," she murmured shyly, ducking her head slightly while shifting her weight from foot to foot.

She began hopping in place, tiny springy bounces with both heels leaving the grass at once and her bangs bouncing with every landing, looking so much like an excited bunny that Silas half expected a cottontail tail to start wagging behind her.
"If you hadn’t helped me with the core foundation...
I would never have stabilized the territory."
She stopped hopping with her hands nervously fidgeting with the hem of her soot-stained tunic as she looked up through her lashes.
"Can I... hug you?" she asked in a small, hopeful voice.
Silas chuckled warmly, opening his arms wide in an easy invitation.

chapters.title: Chapter 673: Bastard Man
paragraphs: A melodious ringing voice cut through the air like silver bells.
Aki reluctantly pulled back from Silas’s chest, taking a half-step aside just in time, because Eluned was already closing the distance at a dead sprint.
The pristine former Goddess of the World Tree didn’t bother slowing down as she reached him.
She leaped straight off the turf with an airy graceful bound, throwing her arms around Silas’s neck.
"Got you."
Silas caught her smoothly with his arm sliding beneath her thighs to form a secure seat as she wrapped her legs around his waist.
"Mwah!"
Eluned planted a soft lingering kiss squarely onto the center of his forehead, her emerald eyes glowing with radiant adoring warmth.
"Welcome home, my heart. We missed you dreadfully."
She turned her chin slightly over Silas’s shoulder, catching Morwenna’s amused gaze, and playfully stuck the tip of her tongue out at the pirate queen with childish triumph.
Morwenna merely rolled her eyes with a dry snort, completely unbothered by the petty display.
Ther’Abella looked as though she were about to faint into the grass.
Silas let out a long heavy sigh, resting his forehead against Eluned’s shoulder for a brief second to center himself before looking around at the gathered group.
Eluned tilted her head until her lips brushed the edge of his ear.
"Your wife kept the bed warm throughout, my heart," she breathed, low enough that only he could hear. "I would like to be thanked for it tonight... Thoroughly..."
Silas’s ear went red from the tip down to the collar.
He cleared his throat twice and decided not to look at Morwenna, whose stormy gray eyes had narrowed at the whispering.

"I managed to settle everything back on Earth for now," Silas said, shifting Eluned comfortably in his grip. "I’ll be in the Sovereign Realm until Aki’s Novice trial concludes... Central City is out here too, so I’ll take care of my business there in the meantime then me and her have some things to handle."
Aki blinked, tilting her head with a puzzled frown. "What...?"
Then, her eyes widened as the memory snapped into focus. "Oh!"

"Yeah," Silas nodded with a wry smile. "We won the Tournament of Succession, which means that the entire northern sector is officially ours for the taking and with the truce we signed with Amazonia, we have to sit down with them and sort out the demarcation before someone gets trigger-happy..."
Aki raised both hands, vigorously rubbing her temples as the sheer weight of logistics crashed down over her combat high.
’What a stressful day...’ she thought with a groaning sigh, looking between Silas, the Keep, and the endless horizon of her new realm.
The open clearing on the other hand fell into a breathless lull that was broken only by the crackle of distant grass embers and the gentle rush of the mountain stream over polished stones.
Across the flattened loam, the twenty-eight warrior women of the newly raised vanguard paused mid-action.
One of them, still holding a heavy spear through the brisket of a twitching stone-carapace badger, blinked through sweat-matted bangs.
Another, an archer with half a dozen fletchings notched in her quiver, lowered her composite bow by an inch with her jaw parting in unmasked astonishment.
From their position near the tree line, they had watched the entire impossible sequence unfold.

Their Lord, the petite devastating girl who had just erased a nine-foot mountain troll from conceptual existence with royal-purple flames of pure annihilation, had dropped all pretenses of authority the second she saw the dark-haired young man.
She had sprinted across the meadow like a child running to her favorite elder sibling, hopping on her toes like an over-excited hare, and practically threw herself into his chest.

...And then, as if that weren’t enough of an overload to the senses, the fearsome pirate queen who had split drakes during their crossing casually sauntered up and planted a kiss squarely on his cheek, followed immediately by Lady Eluned, the radiant peerless former Goddess of the World Tree, literally leaping into his arms, wrapping her slender thighs around his waist, and showering his forehead with kisses while sticking her tongue out in petty triumph.
The two escort guards who had accompanied Silas from the main gate quickly caught up to the perimeter line with their cheeks flushed with pride, eagerly whispering to their sisters-in-arms.

"That’s him," the lead archer murmured in an urgent hushed hiss that spread like wildfire through the ranks. "That is Lord Silas Graves... The Sovereign of Blessed Land and Master of the entire parent dominion!"
The ripple effect was instantaneous.
Clank! Clink-clank!
The sound of dark steel plates striking damp earth echoed across the meadow in crisp sequence.
Without a second’s hesitation, every single one of the warrior women dropped smoothly onto one knee.
They bowed their heads with their right fists pressed firmly against their breastplates right over the twin-leaf insignia of Blessed Land, paying homage to the sovereign of their lineage.
Silas, still holding Eluned comfortably against his hip while she rested her chin on his shoulder, blinked at the sudden sea of kneeling warriors.
An embarrassed smile tugged at the corner of his lips as he raised his free hand, waving it in an easy dismissive gesture.

"Hey, please, don’t do that," Silas said, his voice carrying easily across the meadow with that natural authority of a Lord. "Stand up, all of you. You’ve been working hard all morning, and you don’t need to scrape your knees in the dirt every time I walk by..."
The women rose to their feet as one with their armor rattling, but their eyes remained locked on him with undisguised adoration.

"I was watching the way you handled that flank," Silas added, nodding toward the fallen boar pack and the disciplined defensive circle they had maintained. "Your spacing was clean, the shield wall didn’t buckle once, and your spear thrusts were timed perfectly with the archers’ volleys... That kind of unit cohesion takes weeks to build, and you did it on your first few days, it’s exceptional work... I really like your coordination."
A collective high-pitched gasp rippled through the front rank.
"The Sovereign praises our coordination!" the scarred vanguard leader gasped, her eyes practically sparkling with light.

She snapped her hand to her brow in a rigid trembling salute. "We thank the Great Sovereign for thanking our coordination! We shall hone our coordination until it pierces the heavens themselves for the glory of Blessed Land!"
’What’s with this Sovereign Talk? Not that I mind... still...’
"Thank you, Lord Silas!" the rest chorused with synchronized enthusiasm, their faces practically glowing with pride.
Silas’s left eyebrow twitched as a massive invisible bead of sweat slid down the back of his neck.

’Why are they all so ridiculously eager...?’ Silas thought, his mouth curving into a strained helpless grin. ’They’re looking at me like I just handed them knighthoods but it was just a standard defensive sweep...’
He cleared his throat, shifting Eluned slightly as he looked over at Morwenna.
The dark-haired pirate queen was still standing beside him, leaning casually against her sword while chewing on her smoked boar meat with lazy half-lidded indifference.

"Anyway," Silas continued, gesturing toward the gathered auxiliaries, "since they’re fresh summons and their foundations are still adapting to the territory, I was thinking maybe Morwenna could indulge in a bit of sparring drill with them... Set up a basic combat regimen, teach them some practical footwork, maybe run them through some defensive drills to tighten up their—"
"No way in hell!" Morwenna whined instantly, cutting him off with a loud groan.
She stomped the heavy tip of Tidebringer into the sod with a dull thud, crossing her free arm over her generous leather-clad bust.
Her stormy gray eyes flashed with mutinous defiance with her plush lips pouting in a way that looked remarkably dangerous on a woman who could bisect a sea serpent with a flick of her wrist.

’At this rate...’ Morwenna thought, a violent frustrated heat blooming deep behind her breastbone as she stared at the young man standing mere inches away, ’how the hell am I ever going to lose my virginity?!’
The thought practically set her teeth on edge.
It wasn’t that she minded training fresh recruits.
She had commanded crews across the tempestuous northern seas for years, and breaking in new blood was second nature to her but gods above, that wasn’t why she had crossed over to this territory!
’I want to teach HIM more Tide-Blade Arts!’ her mind screamed in pure longing.
It had been far too long since the two of them had actually locked blades in the private training room back in the Keep.

For heaven’s sake, had he even fully mastered the Second Style yet? Didn’t he want to learn the Third Style?! The intricate water-slicked footwork, the close-quarters body checks, the heavy panting breaths exchanged in the heat of a duel...

’Plus...’ Morwenna’s breath hitched, her cheeks heating up beneath her sun-kissed skin as her memories drifted back to their last private session, ’if I push him just a little bit harder this time... if I corner him like last time and actually insist on it... maybe he’ll finally stop holding back and just take me! I could lose this cursed virginity once and for all! I’d finally be one step closer to carrying his children!’
Her fingers twitched, instinctively reaching out.
Her calloused hand caught Silas’s free fingers, intertwining them with hers but the moment his skin touched hers, her courage short-circuited.
She jerked her chin away, averting her gaze entirely, staring down at the clover by her boots with a furiously burning face.
’I’m—I’m so sick and tired of being cuck... cuck-something...’
She racked her brain, trying to recall the exact term that mischievous Elf had dropped during their late-night drinks by her desk in the Library.
’Cucked!’ the word snapped into focus with furious clarity. ’I’m tired of being cucked by everyone else in this damn Keep! It’s my time to shine too!’
Her gaze flicked sideways, glaring daggers at Eluned, who was still clinging happily to Silas’s waist like a pampered cat.
Eluned was actively trying for children every single night, whispering sweet blessings into his ear while pulling him beneath the sheets.

And Aeliana... That perverted blond elf had literally cornered Morwenna two days ago in the library, whispering detailed, shameless architectural plans about setting up "the perfect situation" with aphrodisiac incense and enchanted hot springs so Silas would have no choice but to ravish them both.

’That perverted elf is already scheming in the shadows!’ Morwenna growled internally, squeezing Silas’s hand with enough grip strength to crack granite. ’If I don’t put my foot down right now and claim my turn, I’m going to be left choking in their dust forever while they all get pregnant before me!’

"I’m not playing nursemaid to thirty recruits!" Morwenna declared out loud, her voice sounding stubborn and defiant as she refused to look him in the eye. "My blades are for high-seas slaughter and sparring, not daycare!"
Across the clearing, the warrior women collectively let out a quiet trembling sigh of pure relief.
Several of them subtly wiped cold sweat from their foreheads.
They had seen Morwenna in action a bit and the woman was a blood-soaked demon with a sword, laughing like a maniac while severing limbs and cleaving monsters in two.
The aura of terrifying cruelty radiating from her was enough to give a hardened veteran nightmares... None of them wanted to be handed over to that lunatic for "basic drills."
Silas blinked at Morwenna’s sudden vehement refusal, though he noticed the bright red flush creeping over the tips of her ears.
He chuckled softly, giving her hand an affectionate squeeze before letting go.
"Alright, alright, fair enough," Silas conceded with an easy smile. "If you’re not up for it, I’ll just have Brida come over from the main territory to take charge of their combat training..."
The effect on the recruits was electric.
"Brida...?" one of the spearwomen gasped, her eyes lighting up.

"Oh! That sounds wonderful!" an archer whispered eagerly, her shoulders relaxing entirely. "Brida... that sounds like the name of a very calm and gentle woman... A wise elder sister who dislikes violence and teaches with patience and grace!"
"Yes! A serene instructor!" several others murmured, nodding with bright optimistic smiles, practically buzzing with relief.
Silas looked at their shining, hopeful faces, his mouth twitching as an amused chuckle rumbled in his chest.

’Are they seriously this excited for Brida...?’ Silas mused, biting the inside of his cheek to keep from laughing out loud. ’Do they honestly think a woman named Brida is going to be gentle? That woman probably eats raw iron for breakfast and makes recruits run mountain sprints with boulders strapped to their spines... They have no idea what kind of meat grinder they just volunteered for.’
Standing a few paces away, Aki slowly shook her head, casting a look of pitying sorrow toward her innocent newly summoned troops.
’Poor girls...’ Aki thought, wincing internally. ’They really have no idea what they’re walking into. Eluned’s training makes you cry, but Brida’s training makes you pray for death...’
She decided it was best not to shatter their fragile dreams just yet.
Clearing her throat with dignity, Aki stepped forward, clapping her small hands together.

"Alright, everyone!" Aki ordered, her voice ringing out crisp and clear over the meadow. "We’ve secured the sector for now! Begin collecting the carcasses of the high-tier beasts and loading them onto the transport sleds... We need the cold storage filled before nightfall!"
"Understood, Lady Aki!" the women answered in unison, quickly scattering to begin butchering and hauling the massive boars and badgers with practiced efficiency.
Aeliana drifted up beside Silas while the vanguard scattered, her pale green sleeves swishing against his arm.
"Lord Sy, you have a leaf in your hair."
"Do I?" Silas bent his head to look.
"Stay still." She rose onto the toes of her slippers and combed her fingers slowly through his hair, taking far longer than any single leaf required.
When she finally pulled it free, she held it up between two fingers and studied it as though it were a rare gem.
"There... You collect things so easily, Lord Sy... Leaves... Troops... Ladies..."
"The leaf was an accident though."
"And the ladies?" Her silver-green eyes glittered. "I rather think they were deliberate."
She did not drop the leaf.
She tucked it into her sleeve with a small private smile, and Morwenna noticed every second of it.
Three paces off, with the dirt of her humiliation still smeared down her cuirass, Ther’Abella watched the leaf disappear.
’Her too?!’ the First Hero screamed internally. ’The elf, too?! The counselor of his own house?! This is not a keep, it is a den!’

sentences.text: A melodious ringing voice cut through the air like silver bells.
Aki reluctantly pulled back from Silas’s chest, taking a half-step aside just in time, because Eluned was already closing the distance at a dead sprint.
The pristine former Goddess of the World Tree didn’t bother slowing down as she reached him.
She leaped straight off the turf with an airy graceful bound, throwing her arms around Silas’s neck.
"Got you."
Silas caught her smoothly with his arm sliding beneath her thighs to form a secure seat as she wrapped her legs around his waist.
"Mwah!"
Eluned planted a soft lingering kiss squarely onto the center of his forehead, her emerald eyes glowing with radiant adoring warmth.
"Welcome home, my heart.
We missed you dreadfully."
She turned her chin slightly over Silas’s shoulder, catching Morwenna’s amused gaze, and playfully stuck the tip of her tongue out at the pirate queen with childish triumph.
Morwenna merely rolled her eyes with a dry snort, completely unbothered by the petty display.
Ther’Abella looked as though she were about to faint into the grass.
Silas let out a long heavy sigh, resting his forehead against Eluned’s shoulder for a brief second to center himself before looking around at the gathered group.
Eluned tilted her head until her lips brushed the edge of his ear.
"Your wife kept the bed warm throughout, my heart," she breathed, low enough that only he could hear.
"I would like to be thanked for it tonight...
Thoroughly..."
Silas’s ear went red from the tip down to the collar.
He cleared his throat twice and decided not to look at Morwenna, whose stormy gray eyes had narrowed at the whispering.
"I managed to settle everything back on Earth for now," Silas said, shifting Eluned comfortably in his grip.
"I’ll be in the Sovereign Realm until Aki’s Novice trial concludes...
Central City is out here too, so I’ll take care of my business there in the meantime then me and her have some things to handle."
Aki blinked, tilting her head with a puzzled frown.
"What...?"
Then, her eyes widened as the memory snapped into focus.
"Oh!"
"Yeah," Silas nodded with a wry smile.

"We won the Tournament of Succession, which means that the entire northern sector is officially ours for the taking and with the truce we signed with Amazonia, we have to sit down with them and sort out the demarcation before someone gets trigger-happy..."
Aki raised both hands, vigorously rubbing her temples as the sheer weight of logistics crashed down over her combat high.
’What a stressful day...’ she thought with a groaning sigh, looking between Silas, the Keep, and the endless horizon of her new realm.
The open clearing on the other hand fell into a breathless lull that was broken only by the crackle of distant grass embers and the gentle rush of the mountain stream over polished stones.
Across the flattened loam, the twenty-eight warrior women of the newly raised vanguard paused mid-action.
One of them, still holding a heavy spear through the brisket of a twitching stone-carapace badger, blinked through sweat-matted bangs.
Another, an archer with half a dozen fletchings notched in her quiver, lowered her composite bow by an inch with her jaw parting in unmasked astonishment.
From their position near the tree line, they had watched the entire impossible sequence unfold.

Their Lord, the petite devastating girl who had just erased a nine-foot mountain troll from conceptual existence with royal-purple flames of pure annihilation, had dropped all pretenses of authority the second she saw the dark-haired young man.
She had sprinted across the meadow like a child running to her favorite elder sibling, hopping on her toes like an over-excited hare, and practically threw herself into his chest.

...And then, as if that weren’t enough of an overload to the senses, the fearsome pirate queen who had split drakes during their crossing casually sauntered up and planted a kiss squarely on his cheek, followed immediately by Lady Eluned, the radiant peerless former Goddess of the World Tree, literally leaping into his arms, wrapping her slender thighs around his waist, and showering his forehead with kisses while sticking her tongue out in petty triumph.
The two escort guards who had accompanied Silas from the main gate quickly caught up to the perimeter line with their cheeks flushed with pride, eagerly whispering to their sisters-in-arms.
"That’s him," the lead archer murmured in an urgent hushed hiss that spread like wildfire through the ranks.
"That is Lord Silas Graves...
The Sovereign of Blessed Land and Master of the entire parent dominion!"
The ripple effect was instantaneous.
Clank!
Clink-clank!
The sound of dark steel plates striking damp earth echoed across the meadow in crisp sequence.
Without a second’s hesitation, every single one of the warrior women dropped smoothly onto one knee.
They bowed their heads with their right fists pressed firmly against their breastplates right over the twin-leaf insignia of Blessed Land, paying homage to the sovereign of their lineage.
Silas, still holding Eluned comfortably against his hip while she rested her chin on his shoulder, blinked at the sudden sea of kneeling warriors.
An embarrassed smile tugged at the corner of his lips as he raised his free hand, waving it in an easy dismissive gesture.
"Hey, please, don’t do that," Silas said, his voice carrying easily across the meadow with that natural authority of a Lord.
"Stand up, all of you.
You’ve been working hard all morning, and you don’t need to scrape your knees in the dirt every time I walk by..."
The women rose to their feet as one with their armor rattling, but their eyes remained locked on him with undisguised adoration.
"I was watching the way you handled that flank," Silas added, nodding toward the fallen boar pack and the disciplined defensive circle they had maintained.
"Your spacing was clean, the shield wall didn’t buckle once, and your spear thrusts were timed perfectly with the archers’ volleys...
That kind of unit cohesion takes weeks to build, and you did it on your first few days, it’s exceptional work...
I really like your coordination."
A collective high-pitched gasp rippled through the front rank.
"The Sovereign praises our coordination!" the scarred vanguard leader gasped, her eyes practically sparkling with light.
She snapped her hand to her brow in a rigid trembling salute.
"We thank the Great Sovereign for thanking our coordination!
We shall hone our coordination until it pierces the heavens themselves for the glory of Blessed Land!"
’What’s with this Sovereign Talk?
Not that I mind... still...’
"Thank you, Lord Silas!" the rest chorused with synchronized enthusiasm, their faces practically glowing with pride.
Silas’s left eyebrow twitched as a massive invisible bead of sweat slid down the back of his neck.

’Why are they all so ridiculously eager...?’ Silas thought, his mouth curving into a strained helpless grin. ’They’re looking at me like I just handed them knighthoods but it was just a standard defensive sweep...’
He cleared his throat, shifting Eluned slightly as he looked over at Morwenna.
The dark-haired pirate queen was still standing beside him, leaning casually against her sword while chewing on her smoked boar meat with lazy half-lidded indifference.

"Anyway," Silas continued, gesturing toward the gathered auxiliaries, "since they’re fresh summons and their foundations are still adapting to the territory, I was thinking maybe Morwenna could indulge in a bit of sparring drill with them...
Set up a basic combat regimen, teach them some practical footwork, maybe run them through some defensive drills to tighten up their—"
"No way in hell!" Morwenna whined instantly, cutting him off with a loud groan.
She stomped the heavy tip of Tidebringer into the sod with a dull thud, crossing her free arm over her generous leather-clad bust.
Her stormy gray eyes flashed with mutinous defiance with her plush lips pouting in a way that looked remarkably dangerous on a woman who could bisect a sea serpent with a flick of her wrist.

’At this rate...’ Morwenna thought, a violent frustrated heat blooming deep behind her breastbone as she stared at the young man standing mere inches away, ’how the hell am I ever going to lose my virginity?!’
The thought practically set her teeth on edge.
It wasn’t that she minded training fresh recruits.
She had commanded crews across the tempestuous northern seas for years, and breaking in new blood was second nature to her but gods above, that wasn’t why she had crossed over to this territory!
’I want to teach HIM more Tide-Blade Arts!’ her mind screamed in pure longing.
It had been far too long since the two of them had actually locked blades in the private training room back in the Keep.
For heaven’s sake, had he even fully mastered the Second Style yet?
Didn’t he want to learn the Third Style?!
The intricate water-slicked footwork, the close-quarters body checks, the heavy panting breaths exchanged in the heat of a duel...

’Plus...’ Morwenna’s breath hitched, her cheeks heating up beneath her sun-kissed skin as her memories drifted back to their last private session, ’if I push him just a little bit harder this time... if I corner him like last time and actually insist on it... maybe he’ll finally stop holding back and just take me!
I could lose this cursed virginity once and for all!
I’d finally be one step closer to carrying his children!’
Her fingers twitched, instinctively reaching out.
Her calloused hand caught Silas’s free fingers, intertwining them with hers but the moment his skin touched hers, her courage short-circuited.
She jerked her chin away, averting her gaze entirely, staring down at the clover by her boots with a furiously burning face.
’I’m—I’m so sick and tired of being cuck... cuck-something...’
She racked her brain, trying to recall the exact term that mischievous Elf had dropped during their late-night drinks by her desk in the Library.
’Cucked!’ the word snapped into focus with furious clarity. ’I’m tired of being cucked by everyone else in this damn Keep!
It’s my time to shine too!’
Her gaze flicked sideways, glaring daggers at Eluned, who was still clinging happily to Silas’s waist like a pampered cat.
Eluned was actively trying for children every single night, whispering sweet blessings into his ear while pulling him beneath the sheets.
And Aeliana...

That perverted blond elf had literally cornered Morwenna two days ago in the library, whispering detailed, shameless architectural plans about setting up "the perfect situation" with aphrodisiac incense and enchanted hot springs so Silas would have no choice but to ravish them both.

’That perverted elf is already scheming in the shadows!’ Morwenna growled internally, squeezing Silas’s hand with enough grip strength to crack granite. ’If I don’t put my foot down right now and claim my turn, I’m going to be left choking in their dust forever while they all get pregnant before me!’
"I’m not playing nursemaid to thirty recruits!" Morwenna declared out loud, her voice sounding stubborn and defiant as she refused to look him in the eye.
"My blades are for high-seas slaughter and sparring, not daycare!"
Across the clearing, the warrior women collectively let out a quiet trembling sigh of pure relief.
Several of them subtly wiped cold sweat from their foreheads.
They had seen Morwenna in action a bit and the woman was a blood-soaked demon with a sword, laughing like a maniac while severing limbs and cleaving monsters in two.
The aura of terrifying cruelty radiating from her was enough to give a hardened veteran nightmares...
None of them wanted to be handed over to that lunatic for "basic drills."
Silas blinked at Morwenna’s sudden vehement refusal, though he noticed the bright red flush creeping over the tips of her ears.
He chuckled softly, giving her hand an affectionate squeeze before letting go.
"Alright, alright, fair enough," Silas conceded with an easy smile.
"If you’re not up for it, I’ll just have Brida come over from the main territory to take charge of their combat training..."
The effect on the recruits was electric.
"Brida...?" one of the spearwomen gasped, her eyes lighting up.
"Oh!
That sounds wonderful!" an archer whispered eagerly, her shoulders relaxing entirely.
"Brida... that sounds like the name of a very calm and gentle woman...
A wise elder sister who dislikes violence and teaches with patience and grace!"
"Yes!
A serene instructor!" several others murmured, nodding with bright optimistic smiles, practically buzzing with relief.
Silas looked at their shining, hopeful faces, his mouth twitching as an amused chuckle rumbled in his chest.
’Are they seriously this excited for Brida...?’ Silas mused, biting the inside of his cheek to keep from laughing out loud. ’Do they honestly think a woman named Brida is going to be gentle?
That woman probably eats raw iron for breakfast and makes recruits run mountain sprints with boulders strapped to their spines...
They have no idea what kind of meat grinder they just volunteered for.’
Standing a few paces away, Aki slowly shook her head, casting a look of pitying sorrow toward her innocent newly summoned troops.
’Poor girls...’ Aki thought, wincing internally. ’They really have no idea what they’re walking into.
Eluned’s training makes you cry, but Brida’s training makes you pray for death...’
She decided it was best not to shatter their fragile dreams just yet.
Clearing her throat with dignity, Aki stepped forward, clapping her small hands together.
"Alright, everyone!" Aki ordered, her voice ringing out crisp and clear over the meadow.
"We’ve secured the sector for now!
Begin collecting the carcasses of the high-tier beasts and loading them onto the transport sleds...
We need the cold storage filled before nightfall!"
"Understood, Lady Aki!" the women answered in unison, quickly scattering to begin butchering and hauling the massive boars and badgers with practiced efficiency.
Aeliana drifted up beside Silas while the vanguard scattered, her pale green sleeves swishing against his arm.
"Lord Sy, you have a leaf in your hair."
"Do I?" Silas bent his head to look.
"Stay still." She rose onto the toes of her slippers and combed her fingers slowly through his hair, taking far longer than any single leaf required.
When she finally pulled it free, she held it up between two fingers and studied it as though it were a rare gem.
"There...
You collect things so easily, Lord Sy...
Leaves...
Troops...
Ladies..."
"The leaf was an accident though."
"And the ladies?" Her silver-green eyes glittered.
"I rather think they were deliberate."
She did not drop the leaf.
She tucked it into her sleeve with a small private smile, and Morwenna noticed every second of it.
Three paces off, with the dirt of her humiliation still smeared down her cuirass, Ther’Abella watched the leaf disappear.
’Her too?!’ the First Hero screamed internally. ’The elf, too?!
The counselor of his own house?!
This is not a keep, it is a den!’

chapters.title: Chapter 674: Are Dwarves An Endangered Species Perhaps?
paragraphs: WHIRRRR!
A hum of raw mana buzzed overhead, accompanied by the crackle of tiny golden static sparks as a shadow fell over Silas as Thor descended from the sky.
The golden-haired demigoddess floated down with effortless buoyant grace, landing on the turf with a soft thud that barely disturbed the grass.
She still held her massive wooden flagon in one hand, while the enormous half-gnawed roast boar leg was tucked casually under her arm.
A broad sunny grin spread across her rugged beautiful face as she looked down at Silas with her thunderous presence washing over him like a warm summer storm.

"Welcome back, Silas," Thor boomed, her voice rich with warmth as she reached out with a heavy armored gauntlet and ruffled his dark hair with enough force to sway his whole upper body. "Good to see you’re still in one piece after dealing with those weaklings..."
"Good to see you too, Thor," Silas laughed, ducking out from under her massive hand. "Thanks for looking after Aki while I was away."
"Bah, the girl can handle herself! You saw her turn that troll into cinders," Thor dismissed with a hearty grin.
She suddenly leaned in close, her bright blue eyes gleaming with mischievous curiosity. "Hey... Open your mouth."
Silas paused, his eyes narrowing slightly in suspicion. "What? Why? What are you going to do?"
"Just open it, you cowardly whelp! I’m not going to poison you!"
Silas sighed, rolling his eyes, but complied, tilting his head back and parting his lips.
Before he could even ask another question, Thor tipped the rim of her flagon directly over his face.
GLUG-GLUG-GLUG!
A thick viscous stream of deep amber liquid poured straight down his throat.
It smelled like fermented volcanic honey and ozone so dense it made the air around his nose crackle with miniature spark arcs.

Silas swallowed reflexively and the liquid hit his stomach with the concussive force of an exploding artillery shell... it was an ungodly torrent of alcohol so potent that a single drop would have liquefied the liver of a normal mortal man and put a high-tier awakened warrior into a three-day coma.
Silas blinked.
He swallowed the last drop, smacked his lips thoughtfully, and exhaled a warm puff of vapor that smelled faintly of cinnamon and roasted grain.
His Gold Core circulated smoothly with the golden foundation effortlessly breaking down the divine toxins and transmuting the liquid into pure harmless vitality within a fraction of a second.
"Not bad," Silas remarked casually, wiping a drop from his lower lip with the back of his thumb. "A bit spicy on the finish, but the flavor is great... What is that, spiced mead?"
Thor stared at his face.

She leaned down until her nose was two inches from his with her eyes turning wide as she scanned his pupils, his skin tone, and his breathing for the slightest hint of a drunken stagger, a flushed cheek, or a glazed expression.
...Nothing.
There was not even a single trace of intoxication, he was as sober as a stone pillar.
’Even with that...?!’ Thor screamed internally, her jaw practically unhinging in disbelief.

’I mixed that batch myself!’ she thought with a cold sweat breaking out under her leather tunic. ’That wasn’t standard mortal brew! I slipped in three measures of the thousand-year reserve from the high vaults of Asgard... the stuff I drink after slaying cosmic void-serpents! A single flagon of that could bring a storm giant to its knees, and this guy drinks it like tap water?!’
She pulled back, scratching her messy golden hair with a deep frustrated scowl.

’Dammit all...’ Thor grumbled to herself, looking at the empty flagon. ’A Gold Core foundation really is an impenetrable fortress against poisons and spirits... If I actually want to see him properly sloshed and loose-tongued, I might have to swallow my pride and send a prayer to Father... He has a Gold Core too, so the old man has to have some ancient divine vintage tucked away in his private cellar that can actually bypass that metabolism!’
Perhaps she could invite him over to Asgard or something...? Thor didn’t mind either way though she would need to choose a day when Loki was not around.
"Alright, pack it up, people!" Silas called out, breaking her train of thought as he turned back toward the path. "Let’s head back to the settlement."
With the women hauling the heavily laden supply sleds behind them, the group began the leisurely trek back toward the southern gate.
Aki walked closely by Silas’s side with her small hands clasped behind her back as her bright blue eyes swept over the landscape with proud affection.

"This land is called Vineworld," Aki explained, her melodic voice chiming over the rustle of the trees. "When I got here, the system classified it as an vegetative Unknown Zone... Geographically, it sits on a place very similar to the Umbral Basin where your main territory is located, Blessed Land sits inside the Basin, and my Wonderland sits inside Vineworld!"
Silas raised an eyebrow. "Similar how?"

"The ecological hierarchy," Aki replied, gesturing toward the wild groves in the distance. "Just like the Basin, the outer perimeter here is almost exclusively populated by Tier 2 beasts... The mana density is stable, the place is rich in natural wood and earth elements though there aren’t any sudden unpredictable dimensional tears dropping different kinds of weathers on our doorstep. Honestly... I would go as far as to call it the flowery colorful version of your Umbral Basin!"
Silas chuckled warmly, reaching down to playfully flick a stray leaf from her bangs.

"Well, that’s a massive relief. The Umbral Basin was a grim foggy place when we first got there and still is. Having a flowery version is a huge upgrade... except, of course, for the trees that try to eat your face off."
Aki giggled, a bright, cheerful sound that echoed through the woods.

"Oh, the carnivorous willows? They’re just territorial! Once the boundary towers finish synchronizing with the Keep’s core, their hostile aggression will be suppressed automatically... Don’t worry about me, Silas. I promise you, I’ll be more than alright here."
"I know you will," Silas smiled, looking at her with genuine pride. "You’ve done an incredible job, Aki."
Aki hopped twice on her toes with a pair of small springy hops that made her bangs bounce, and then her hand found his and slid inside it as though it had always belonged there.
Silas closed his fingers around hers without thinking about it.
"Mmm~"
Aki hummed under her breath and studied a nearby root with great concentration, pretending very hard not to be smiling.
They reached the massive black steel wall, passing through the gatehouse without incident.
Inside the perimeter, some of her people immediately rushed toward the supply depot, retrieving heavy wooden freight wagons to assist with unloading the slaughtered beasts.
Aki sighed contentedly, looking up at the sprawling layout of the burgeoning settlement.

"I have to say, the administrative interface for territory management is remarkably convenient... As long as we clear the timber and lay the foundation, the system allows Lords to erect residential quarters, storage vaults, and workshops almost instantaneously through the core console. It’s like playing in an architectural sandbox!"
As they walked past the orchard Eluned had grown along the inner wall, Morwenna casually broke away from the group.
She reached up with her arms, deftly plucking three large, perfectly radiant Golden Star Apples from the low branches.
She wiped one against her leather trousers and took a massive juicy bite with the sweet nectar dripping down her chin as she let out a satisfied hum.
’I hate Eluned but I guess it’s okay because of her apples...’
Eluned, who had finally detached herself from Silas’s side, trotted over with an expectant delicate palm extended outward.
"A fruit for me, please, Morwenna," Eluned said with a serene sweet smile. "I did spend three hours cultivating the soil, after all."
Morwenna immediately pulled the remaining two apples against her chest, turning her back with a sharp petty scoff. "Get your own, leaf-brain... My hands did the picking, so these are my plunder."
Eluned didn’t yell.
Instead, she simply lowered her extended hand, letting her head tilt downward with her large emerald eyes welling with an impossibly deep heartbreaking sorrow.
Her lower lip gave a pitiful quiver, looking for all the world like a forsaken goddess who had just been cruelly denied her only source of joy in the mortal realm.
Morwenna’s jaw clenched.
She stared at that pathetic guilt-inducing face for three agonizing seconds with her eye twitching violently.
"Gah! Fine! Take it!" Morwenna snapped with an exasperated Mmph, aggressively shoving one of the golden apples into Eluned’s waiting palms.
Eluned’s tearful sorrow vanished in a microsecond as she took the apple, cradled it against her cheek, and offered Morwenna a sugary venomous smile.
"Thank you, dear," Eluned purred softly, her voice dripping with mockery. "I expected as much from an uncultured virgin."
Morwenna froze.
Her vision turned red with her knuckles turned white around the remaining apple and her teeth grinding together so hard they sounded like millstones.
She looked genuinely on the verge of ripping out handfuls of her own dark hair in pure rage.

’Don’t fall for the bait,’ Morwenna chanted violently in her head, closing her eyes and taking three deep furious breaths through her nose. ’Don’t strangle the Goddess... She’s doing it on purpose... She’s trying to throw you off your game so Silas thinks you’re a savage... Stay calm and be graceful.’
Forcing her features into a stiff aggressive smile, Morwenna marched around Eluned and planted herself firmly at Silas’s other side.
She held the last golden apple out toward Aki first.
"Here... You worked hard on that troll. Eat up."
"Thank you, Morwenna!" Aki beamed, taking the fruit with both hands and immediately taking a happy, enthusiastic bite.
Then, Morwenna turned to Silas.
She didn’t hand the apple to him.
Instead, her stormy gray eyes softened with a sudden delicious flutter of nervousness seizing her chest as she held the freshly bitten half of her own fruit directly toward his lips.
"Here," she muttered, her raspy voice dropping into a quiet breathless hush. "Take a bite."
Silas blinked, but didn’t hesitate.
He leaned down with his lips brushing lightly against her calloused fingers as his teeth sank into the crisp sweet flesh of the golden apple.
The brief warm contact of his mouth against her skin sent a violent electric jolt shooting straight from Morwenna’s fingertips down into her stomach.
A furious radiant shade of crimson detonated across her sun-kissed cheeks, racing all the way to the tips of her ears.
"They taste good..."

She pulled her hand back as if she had touched an open flame, hastily biting into the other side of the apple to hide her flustered expression with her heart hammering against her ribs like a war drum.
’He... he ate it right out of my hand...’ she squealed silently, her toes curling inside her leather boots. ’And his lips touched my fingers! Gods above, he’s so damn smooth without even trying!’
Behind them, Aeliana had been watching the apple go by with the patient interest of a cat watching a bird.
She stepped up beside Silas the instant Morwenna pulled her hand away and laid a fingertip against the corner of his mouth.
"You missed a drop, Lord Sy," she said sweetly.
She drew the fingertip slowly along his lower lip, touched it to the tip of her own tongue, and never once looked away from his eyes. "Mm. Eluned does grow a fine orchard."
Silas forgot how to blink while Morwenna choked on her apple and two paces away, Eluned’s smile froze as well.
’The elf, AGAIN?!’ Ther’Abella shrieked silently, her fingers strangling the strap of her cuirass. ’Is there anyone in this keep he hasn’t—!’
As they approached the pastel pink Keep, Aki wiped a drop of apple juice from the corner of her mouth with her expression shifting from relaxed enjoyment to business-like contemplation.

"Silas," Aki began, glancing around the half-finished courtyards, "I’m running a bit low on raw construction materials. The territory is stable, but my personal inventory reserves are almost completely dry... I need heavy stone, mythril rebar, and refined lumber for the residential blocks... and most importantly, I need high-tier supplies for a central forge so do you think you can borrow me some building materials?"
She let out a small frustrated sigh, kicking a tiny pebble with the toe of her boot.
"I haven’t even pulled a single dwarf from the summoning pool yet! All of my summons were warriors and scouts... Not a single craftsman or blacksmith in the entire batch!"
Silas couldn’t help but chuckle, nodding in deep shared misery.

"Tell me about it," Silas sighed, running a hand through his dark hair. "I’ve been dealing with the exact same issue back in Blessed Land... I only ever pulled one dwarf out of my own tickets, Thora, and every other smith I have came out of the Lord War with Evelyn. Are dwarves some kind of critically endangered species in the sovereign realm? You can pull fifty spearwomen before you see a single dwarf with a hammer... It’s ridiculous."
He patted her shoulder reassuringly.

"Don’t stress about it too much. That’s actually one of the main reasons I came over to check on you right now... I’m heading to Central City in the Sovereign Realm after this, so I won’t be able to stay long today, I’m leaving momentarily."
The atmosphere in the group dropped like an anchor.

"What?!" Eluned gasped, her hands instantly flying to her chest, her emerald eyes wide with immediate devastation. "You’re leaving already?! But you only just arrived, my heart! You haven’t even rested your head in our garden!"

"Are you serious, Captain?!" Morwenna snapped, her brows furrowing into an angry disappointed scowl. "You just got back from the mortal world, and now you’re running off to some pompous metropolis?! We haven’t even had a single round of sparring!"
Beside them, Thor took another massive swig of her flagon, wiping her mouth with the back of her forearm as she watched the two women spiral into despair.

’Why the hell are they whining so much?’ Thor thought, rolling her eyes in mild amusement. ’The boy’s a Lord... He has lands to manage, markets to plunder, and treaties to forge, Sitting around an orchard smelling flowers all day isn’t how you build an empire so let him go buy his damn steel.’
Silas held his hands up in a placating gesture, chuckling dryly at the barrage of complaints.

"Relax, both of you. It’s not a permanent deployment," Silas explained. "I’m going to Central City to secure the construction materials, look into defense turrets for our walls, and browse the artisan markets and... after I finish the primary business, I’m planning to hang out for a bit with one of my friends from the human world. Aeliana is coming along with me as well."
The complaints cut off instantly.
A heavy suffocating silence descended over the courtyard.

Morwenna’s stormy gray eyes narrowed into lethal slits while Eluned’s serene expression froze completely with her lips curving into a tight eerily still smile that made the grass beneath her slippers faintly frost over.
Even Aki paused, her head tilting with sharp unblinking focus.
"A friend...?" Morwenna growled, her voice dropping into a low dangerous tone. "What friend?"
"And what..." Eluned whispered with terrifying sweetness, "...might be the gender of this ’friend’ from the human world, my darling?"
