His Gold Core circulated smoothly with the golden foundation effortlessly breaking down the divine toxins and transmuting the liquid into pure harmless vitality within a fraction of a second.
"Not bad," Silas remarked casually, wiping a drop from his lower lip with the back of his thumb.
"A bit spicy on the finish, but the flavor is great...
What is that, spiced mead?"
Thor stared at his face.

She leaned down until her nose was two inches from his with her eyes turning wide as she scanned his pupils, his skin tone, and his breathing for the slightest hint of a drunken stagger, a flushed cheek, or a glazed expression.
...Nothing.
There was not even a single trace of intoxication, he was as sober as a stone pillar.
’Even with that...?!’ Thor screamed internally, her jaw practically unhinging in disbelief.
’I mixed that batch myself!’ she thought with a cold sweat breaking out under her leather tunic. ’That wasn’t standard mortal brew!
I slipped in three measures of the thousand-year reserve from the high vaults of Asgard... the stuff I drink after slaying cosmic void-serpents!
A single flagon of that could bring a storm giant to its knees, and this guy drinks it like tap water?!’
She pulled back, scratching her messy golden hair with a deep frustrated scowl.
’Dammit all...’ Thor grumbled to herself, looking at the empty flagon. ’A Gold Core foundation really is an impenetrable fortress against poisons and spirits...
If I actually want to see him properly sloshed and loose-tongued, I might have to swallow my pride and send a prayer to Father...
He has a Gold Core too, so the old man has to have some ancient divine vintage tucked away in his private cellar that can actually bypass that metabolism!’
Perhaps she could invite him over to Asgard or something...?
Thor didn’t mind either way though she would need to choose a day when Loki was not around.
"Alright, pack it up, people!" Silas called out, breaking her train of thought as he turned back toward the path.
"Let’s head back to the settlement."
With the women hauling the heavily laden supply sleds behind them, the group began the leisurely trek back toward the southern gate.
Aki walked closely by Silas’s side with her small hands clasped behind her back as her bright blue eyes swept over the landscape with proud affection.
"This land is called Vineworld," Aki explained, her melodic voice chiming over the rustle of the trees.
"When I got here, the system classified it as an vegetative Unknown Zone...
Geographically, it sits on a place very similar to the Umbral Basin where your main territory is located, Blessed Land sits inside the Basin, and my Wonderland sits inside Vineworld!"
Silas raised an eyebrow.
"Similar how?"
"The ecological hierarchy," Aki replied, gesturing toward the wild groves in the distance.
"Just like the Basin, the outer perimeter here is almost exclusively populated by Tier 2 beasts...
The mana density is stable, the place is rich in natural wood and earth elements though there aren’t any sudden unpredictable dimensional tears dropping different kinds of weathers on our doorstep.
Honestly...
I would go as far as to call it the flowery colorful version of your Umbral Basin!"
Silas chuckled warmly, reaching down to playfully flick a stray leaf from her bangs.
"Well, that’s a massive relief.
The Umbral Basin was a grim foggy place when we first got there and still is.
Having a flowery version is a huge upgrade... except, of course, for the trees that try to eat your face off."
Aki giggled, a bright, cheerful sound that echoed through the woods.
"Oh, the carnivorous willows?
They’re just territorial!
Once the boundary towers finish synchronizing with the Keep’s core, their hostile aggression will be suppressed automatically...
Don’t worry about me, Silas.
I promise you, I’ll be more than alright here."
"I know you will," Silas smiled, looking at her with genuine pride.
"You’ve done an incredible job, Aki."
Aki hopped twice on her toes with a pair of small springy hops that made her bangs bounce, and then her hand found his and slid inside it as though it had always belonged there.
Silas closed his fingers around hers without thinking about it.
"Mmm~"
Aki hummed under her breath and studied a nearby root with great concentration, pretending very hard not to be smiling.
They reached the massive black steel wall, passing through the gatehouse without incident.
Inside the perimeter, some of her people immediately rushed toward the supply depot, retrieving heavy wooden freight wagons to assist with unloading the slaughtered beasts.
Aki sighed contentedly, looking up at the sprawling layout of the burgeoning settlement.
"I have to say, the administrative interface for territory management is remarkably convenient...
As long as we clear the timber and lay the foundation, the system allows Lords to erect residential quarters, storage vaults, and workshops almost instantaneously through the core console.
It’s like playing in an architectural sandbox!"
As they walked past the orchard Eluned had grown along the inner wall, Morwenna casually broke away from the group.
She reached up with her arms, deftly plucking three large, perfectly radiant Golden Star Apples from the low branches.
She wiped one against her leather trousers and took a massive juicy bite with the sweet nectar dripping down her chin as she let out a satisfied hum.
’I hate Eluned but I guess it’s okay because of her apples...’
Eluned, who had finally detached herself from Silas’s side, trotted over with an expectant delicate palm extended outward.
"A fruit for me, please, Morwenna," Eluned said with a serene sweet smile.
"I did spend three hours cultivating the soil, after all."
Morwenna immediately pulled the remaining two apples against her chest, turning her back with a sharp petty scoff.
"Get your own, leaf-brain...
My hands did the picking, so these are my plunder."
Eluned didn’t yell.
Instead, she simply lowered her extended hand, letting her head tilt downward with her large emerald eyes welling with an impossibly deep heartbreaking sorrow.
Her lower lip gave a pitiful quiver, looking for all the world like a forsaken goddess who had just been cruelly denied her only source of joy in the mortal realm.
Morwenna’s jaw clenched.
She stared at that pathetic guilt-inducing face for three agonizing seconds with her eye twitching violently.
"Gah!
Fine!
Take it!" Morwenna snapped with an exasperated Mmph, aggressively shoving one of the golden apples into Eluned’s waiting palms.
Eluned’s tearful sorrow vanished in a microsecond as she took the apple, cradled it against her cheek, and offered Morwenna a sugary venomous smile.
"Thank you, dear," Eluned purred softly, her voice dripping with mockery.
"I expected as much from an uncultured virgin."
Morwenna froze.
Her vision turned red with her knuckles turned white around the remaining apple and her teeth grinding together so hard they sounded like millstones.
She looked genuinely on the verge of ripping out handfuls of her own dark hair in pure rage.
’Don’t fall for the bait,’ Morwenna chanted violently in her head, closing her eyes and taking three deep furious breaths through her nose. ’Don’t strangle the Goddess...
She’s doing it on purpose...
She’s trying to throw you off your game so Silas thinks you’re a savage...
Stay calm and be graceful.’
Forcing her features into a stiff aggressive smile, Morwenna marched around Eluned and planted herself firmly at Silas’s other side.
She held the last golden apple out toward Aki first.
"Here...
You worked hard on that troll.
Eat up."
"Thank you, Morwenna!" Aki beamed, taking the fruit with both hands and immediately taking a happy, enthusiastic bite.
Then, Morwenna turned to Silas.
She didn’t hand the apple to him.
Instead, her stormy gray eyes softened with a sudden delicious flutter of nervousness seizing her chest as she held the freshly bitten half of her own fruit directly toward his lips.
"Here," she muttered, her raspy voice dropping into a quiet breathless hush.
"Take a bite."
Silas blinked, but didn’t hesitate.
He leaned down with his lips brushing lightly against her calloused fingers as his teeth sank into the crisp sweet flesh of the golden apple.
The brief warm contact of his mouth against her skin sent a violent electric jolt shooting straight from Morwenna’s fingertips down into her stomach.
A furious radiant shade of crimson detonated across her sun-kissed cheeks, racing all the way to the tips of her ears.
"They taste good..."

She pulled her hand back as if she had touched an open flame, hastily biting into the other side of the apple to hide her flustered expression with her heart hammering against her ribs like a war drum.
’He... he ate it right out of my hand...’ she squealed silently, her toes curling inside her leather boots. ’And his lips touched my fingers!
Gods above, he’s so damn smooth without even trying!’
Behind them, Aeliana had been watching the apple go by with the patient interest of a cat watching a bird.
She stepped up beside Silas the instant Morwenna pulled her hand away and laid a fingertip against the corner of his mouth.
"You missed a drop, Lord Sy," she said sweetly.
She drew the fingertip slowly along his lower lip, touched it to the tip of her own tongue, and never once looked away from his eyes.
"Mm.
Eluned does grow a fine orchard."
Silas forgot how to blink while Morwenna choked on her apple and two paces away, Eluned’s smile froze as well.
’The elf, AGAIN?!’ Ther’Abella shrieked silently, her fingers strangling the strap of her cuirass. ’Is there anyone in this keep he hasn’t—!’
As they approached the pastel pink Keep, Aki wiped a drop of apple juice from the corner of her mouth with her expression shifting from relaxed enjoyment to business-like contemplation.
"Silas," Aki began, glancing around the half-finished courtyards, "I’m running a bit low on raw construction materials.
The territory is stable, but my personal inventory reserves are almost completely dry...

I need heavy stone, mythril rebar, and refined lumber for the residential blocks... and most importantly, I need high-tier supplies for a central forge so do you think you can borrow me some building materials?"
She let out a small frustrated sigh, kicking a tiny pebble with the toe of her boot.
"I haven’t even pulled a single dwarf from the summoning pool yet!
All of my summons were warriors and scouts...
Not a single craftsman or blacksmith in the entire batch!"
Silas couldn’t help but chuckle, nodding in deep shared misery.
"Tell me about it," Silas sighed, running a hand through his dark hair.
"I’ve been dealing with the exact same issue back in Blessed Land...
I only ever pulled one dwarf out of my own tickets, Thora, and every other smith I have came out of the Lord War with Evelyn.
Are dwarves some kind of critically endangered species in the sovereign realm?
You can pull fifty spearwomen before you see a single dwarf with a hammer...
It’s ridiculous."
He patted her shoulder reassuringly.
"Don’t stress about it too much.
That’s actually one of the main reasons I came over to check on you right now...
I’m heading to Central City in the Sovereign Realm after this, so I won’t be able to stay long today, I’m leaving momentarily."
The atmosphere in the group dropped like an anchor.
"What?!" Eluned gasped, her hands instantly flying to her chest, her emerald eyes wide with immediate devastation.
"You’re leaving already?!
But you only just arrived, my heart!
You haven’t even rested your head in our garden!"
"Are you serious, Captain?!" Morwenna snapped, her brows furrowing into an angry disappointed scowl.
"You just got back from the mortal world, and now you’re running off to some pompous metropolis?!
We haven’t even had a single round of sparring!"
Beside them, Thor took another massive swig of her flagon, wiping her mouth with the back of her forearm as she watched the two women spiral into despair.
’Why the hell are they whining so much?’ Thor thought, rolling her eyes in mild amusement. ’The boy’s a Lord...
He has lands to manage, markets to plunder, and treaties to forge, Sitting around an orchard smelling flowers all day isn’t how you build an empire so let him go buy his damn steel.’
Silas held his hands up in a placating gesture, chuckling dryly at the barrage of complaints.
"Relax, both of you.
It’s not a permanent deployment," Silas explained.

"I’m going to Central City to secure the construction materials, look into defense turrets for our walls, and browse the artisan markets and... after I finish the primary business, I’m planning to hang out for a bit with one of my friends from the human world.
Aeliana is coming along with me as well."
The complaints cut off instantly.
A heavy suffocating silence descended over the courtyard.

Morwenna’s stormy gray eyes narrowed into lethal slits while Eluned’s serene expression froze completely with her lips curving into a tight eerily still smile that made the grass beneath her slippers faintly frost over.
Even Aki paused, her head tilting with sharp unblinking focus.
"A friend...?" Morwenna growled, her voice dropping into a low dangerous tone.
"What friend?"
"And what..." Eluned whispered with terrifying sweetness, "...might be the gender of this ’friend’ from the human world, my darling?"

chapters.title: Chapter 675: Second Hero Summoning
paragraphs: Silas stared at the two of them with a bead of cold sweat forming on his brow.

’Seriously...?’ Silas thought, his deadpan expression barely holding together under the twin beams of murderous jealousy boring into his skull. ’Are these death glares really necessary right now? I haven’t even said anything yet!’

"It’s a guy," Silas said quickly, pointing a thumb over his shoulder toward Aeliana. "His name is Valerius... He’s the golden-haired scion of Sterling Enterprises. You can ask Aeliana, she knows him, We’re meeting up in the city so he can show us the trade districts."
Aeliana stepped forward, smoothing the folds of her pale green robes with a calm, reassuring nod.
"It is the truth... Valerius is the male heir of House Sterling. He is my Lord’s best friend and a man too."
Morwenna’s shoulders lowered by half an inch, though her scowl remained firmly in place.
Eluned let out a soft relieved breath with the frost retreating from the grass.
Standing a few paces back, however, Ther’Abella crossed her arms, her blue eyes burning with fierce skepticism.

’Valerius...?’ the First Hero thought, sneering internally. ’A convenient male name fabricated on the spot! I don’t believe this ’Valerius’ exists for a single second! He’s undoubtedly using this fictitious merchant as cover to rendezvous with yet another illicit concubine in the realm! First Lady Eluned, then the pirate, then our sweet Lady Aki... the man is an insatiable multi-timing degenerate! I must tag along! I must bear witness to his depravity and expose his infidelity before Lady Eluned’s heart is shattered entirely!’
Before Ther’Abella could step forward to demand an escort role, Eluned and Morwenna spoke simultaneously.
"I am coming with you!" Eluned declared, stepping forward.
"The hell you are, I’m going with him!" Morwenna barked, stepping into her path.
Aki stood between them, her gaze drifting toward the Keep’s pink parapets as her heart began to ache with longing.
’I want to go too...’ Aki thought, her fingers knotting into the hem of her tunic. ’I really, really want to go to Central City with Silas...’
She bit her lower lip, shaking her head firmly to banish the temptation.

’No,’ she scolded herself sternly. ’I can’t... I just awakened my territory. The monsters are still prowling the borders, and the vanguard needs their Lord present to establish the boundary towers. Leaving right now, during my early settlement phase, would be an awful example for the troops. I have to stay and fulfill my duty as a Lord... even if it hurts.’
"There is no way we are both squeezing through with him!" Morwenna argued, glaring at Eluned. "I don’t want to be caught dead with you! One of us stays, one of us goes!"

"And naturally, that one should be his wife!" Eluned fired back, her chin lifting with divine arrogance. "A man requires an elegant consort of high birth to represent his house in foreign courts, not an unwashed pirate who smells like salt-pork..."
’Is it just me or does she start talking like a noble when Morwenna is involved...?’
"Who are you calling an unwashed pirate, you overgrown houseplant?!"

"Enough!" Silas groaned, rubbing his temples in exasperation. "I’m not listening to you two bicker for forty minutes... Settle it with rock-paper-scissors, best two out of three and the winner comes along, the loser stays behind and helps Aki with the boundary towers. Clear?"
Aeliana raised a single finger.
"For the record, Lord Sy, I am coming along regardless so the winner merely decides who travels with the two of us."
"Nobody asked the elf," Morwenna said.
"I believe the elf is the only one here who has actually met Valerius," Aeliana replied pleasantly.
Morwenna opened her mouth, found nothing to say to that, and closed it again then both women snapped their heads toward him as their eyes narrowed with deadly focus.
"Fine," Morwenna hissed, cracking her knuckles.
"Acceptable," Eluned smiled coldly, raising her delicate right hand.
They stepped onto the flagstones by the summoning altar, facing each other like gladiators entering an arena.
"Rock, paper, scissors... SHOOT!"
Eluned threw scissors and Morwenna threw rock.
"HAH!" Morwenna roared, thrusting her fist into the air with triumphant fury. "Point one to the high seas, you leafy tyrant!"
Eluned’s eyes narrowed into slits of concentration.
"...A fluke."
"Round two!" Silas called out, leaning against the altar’s balustrade. "Shoot!"
Morwenna threw paper and Eluned threw scissors.
"Aha~!" Eluned cheered, clapping her hands together with angelic delight. "Tied! The heavens favor balance, pirate!"
Morwenna’s jaw set into iron.
Her breath came in short focused huffs with her stormy gray eyes tracking every micro-twitch in Eluned’s slender fingers.
"Last round... Don’t blink, flower."
"Round three," Silas announced, watching the tension mount. "Shoot!"
Eluned threw rock and Morwenna threw... she threw... paper.
Silence descended upon the altar as Morwenna’s flat palm hovered in the air, spread wide over Eluned’s clenched fist.
"YESSSSSSSSSSSSS!"
Morwenna erupted into a wild cheer, pumping both fists into the sky with her laughter echoing across the entire valley.
"VICTORY! TAKE THAT, YOU SPOILED GODDESS! PACK YOUR BAGS, CAPTAIN, THE PIRATE QUEEN IS HITTING THE CITY!"
She grabbed Silas’s arm, practically vibrating with excitement as her earlier frustration was completely washed away by the thrill of victory.
’His arm is right here,’ she thought, and discovered that she had hooked it against her chest without noticing.
The warmth of it went straight through her leather vest. ’Don’t look down and say something normal.’
"So... Captain," she said, trying for casual and missing by a mile. "Central City... You and me..."
"You, me, and Aeliana," Silas said.
"Of course." Morwenna muttered.
Silas chuckled warmly, shaking his head.
"Alright, alright. You won fair and square so you can come along."
Eluned stood frozen by the balustrade.
Her lower lip trembled, her emerald eyes welling with deep jealousy as she watched Morwenna cling to his arm but she crossed her arms, looking away with a dramatic aggrieved huff.
"Hmph... very well," Eluned murmured, her voice dripping with sorrowful pride. "I suppose it is acceptable. A generous wife must occasionally allow the lesser retainers a moment of indulgence..."
Suddenly, before Silas could even register the movement, Eluned stepped forward, grabbed both sides of his face with her delicate hands, and pulled him downward!
SMUSH!
Silas’s entire face was completely buried directly into the soft overwhelming expanse of Eluned’s generous silk-clad cleavage!
"Mmph—?!" Silas choked, his muffled voice swallowed by the sea of warmth and sweet floral perfume.
Eluned wrapped her slender arms around the back of his head, squeezing him tightly against her bust, rubbing her chest against his cheeks and nose with deliberate shameless enthusiasm.
’Soft,’ Silas thought dazedly. ’Warm... She smells like rain in a flower field— Oxygen, I need oxygen.’
His hands fluttered uselessly in the air for a moment, unsure where it was safe to put them.
"Breathe through your nose, my heart," Eluned murmured sweetly over the top of his head. "I am told there is plenty of room."
’This... this shameless bitch.’
Morwenna just needed ten percent of her shamelessness, if she had ten percent, she would have been knocked up by now.

"There~!" Eluned declared proudly, looking straight over his dark hair at Morwenna with a triumphant wicked smirk. "I am rubbing my divine scent all over his face! Every single pore of his skin is now marked with the essence of his lawful wife! If you do anything with his face in Central City, Morwenna... that means you are kissing me! Which means you are gay!"
PFFFFFT!
Morwenna violently choked on her own spit, coughing so hard she had to bend over and slap her knee.
"WHAT THE HELL ARE YOU TALKING ABOUT, YOU CRAZY WOMAN?!"
Standing near the perimeter, Ther’Abella and the vanguard escort guards stared at the display with wide perverted fascination.
Several of the younger guards covered their mouths, giggling behind their gauntlets with their cheeks flushed a deep scandalized red.
Ther’Abella, on the other hand, looked like her entire worldview had shattered into a million irreparable shards.

’When...’ the First Hero thought, her jaw hanging slack as she watched the pristine holy former Goddess of the World Tree aggressively smother her husband’s face in her cleavage without a single shred of shame, ’when did our innocent pristine goddess who didn’t even understand mortal emotions become this shamelessly horny?!’
Eluned finally released Silas with a satisfied hum, stepping back and smoothing her robes as if she hadn’t just committed a public act of domestic warfare.
Silas stumbled backward half a step, gasping for fresh air with his dark hair becoming a tangled mess and his cheeks burning a bright mortified pink as he wiped his face with his sleeve.
He gave Eluned an exasperated helpless look, but she merely offered him a radiant innocent smile.
Aki had gone very quiet beside the altar as she looked at Eluned, looked down at herself, and let out one very small sigh.
Aki stepped up to the edge of the quartz altar with her small hands holding a thin glowing scroll.

"Since you’re heading out to the market now, Silas," Aki said, offering him the scroll with an earnest tone. "I wrote down the exact specifications of the building supplies and forge materials I need. Keep track of the ledger, and once my territory is ready, I’ll pay you back everything!"
Silas took the scroll, slipping it into his coat pocket without even glancing at the numbers.
He looked down at her with a soft affectionate smile, reaching out to gently tap the tip of her small nose.
"You don’t need to refund me anything, Aki," Silas said, his voice dropping into a gentle sincere murmur. "The fact that you’re happy and building something you love is more than enough for me."
Aki froze as his words hung in the quiet air.
Flutter!

A sudden gentle mountain breeze swept across the quartz altar. It stirred the hem of her tunic, lifting the long, dark locks of her hair and sending Silas’s messy dark bangs dancing across his forehead.
The soft lavender twilight of the realm filtered down through the silver pillars, illuminating the warm steady tenderness in his blue eyes ringed with gold.
His thumb was still resting against the tip of her nose and she could smell the apple on his breath as well his own scent while her pulse was loud enough to hear in her own ears.
Her fingers went completely slack.
Slip!

The golden-embossed Hero Summoning Ticket she had been holding unconsciously in her left hand slipped from her numb fingers, tumbling through the air and landing with a soft chime against the white quartz flagstones.
Aki didn’t look down at the ticket.

She stared straight into his face, the handsome calm features that Eluned had just released, framed by the gentle wind and the starlight as a feeling so intensely sweet and overwhelming bloomed behind her ribs that it stole every drop of air from her lungs.
Her heart hammered against her chest like a trapped bird.
The thought echoed in the silent sacred expanse of her soul, sounding so loud and clear it frightened her.
’I want to marry you...’
For three long suspended heartbeats, the entire universe seemed to shrink down to just the two of them standing beneath the starlit sky then, Silas blinked, glancing down at the polished stone.
"Hm?" Silas asked, tilting his head with a curious smile. "What did you drop?"
The spell shattered instantly.
Aki’s eyes bulged in pure panicked realization as a violent shade of crimson exploded across her cheeks, rushing straight to the tips of her ears and down her neck!
"A-Ah!" she squeaked, hastily bending over at the waist to scramble for the golden ticket, nearly tripping over her own boots in her desperate haste to hide her face from him.

She snatched the gleaming parchment from the stone, clutching it tightly against her chest like a shield with her breath coming in short flustered gasps as she kept her gaze glued firmly to his belt buckle.

"I-I wanted to summon my second Hero!" Aki stammered, her voice a bit higher than usual with a mortified adorable blush painting every inch of her skin. "A-And... I wanted you to be here when I did it..."
Silas looked down at her flushed trembling frame with a fond helpless chuckle rumbling in his chest.
’Cute,’ Silas thought, his smile softening as he stepped forward to wait for the summon.
Aki scrambled up from the quartz flagstones, clutching the golden-embossed parchment tightly against her ribs like a lifesaver.
"O-ok... I’ll do so now."
Her ears were still burning a furious shade of crimson, but she forced her feet forward, practically speed-walking across the terrace to put distance between herself and Silas’s teasing smile.
She reached the center of the quartz summoning altar, taking a long shuddering breath of mountain air to still her racing pulse.
With trembling fingers, she set the ticket flat against the central crystalline node.
Ding!
A translucent system prompt materialized directly before her eyes in a soft chime of light.
[Would you like to use (1) Hero Summoning Ticket to summon a Hero?]
[Y / N]
Aki didn’t hesitate as she lifted her hand and firmly tapped [Y].
VUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!
The silver pillars flanking the circle thrummed like massive tuning forks with their mana vibrating straight through the marrow of everyone standing in the courtyard.
Then...
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!

A pillar of pure golden radiance tore straight out of the array as the beam shot upward into the lavender twilight of Vineworld, piercing the high cloud cover easily... It was an exact mirror-image of the pillar that had heralded Ther’Abella’s arrival only days before.
Aki’s bright blue eyes widened as the radiant wind whipped her dark bangs wild.
’Another strong one...?!’ Aki thought, her breath catching in her throat as the raw mana pressure washed over her skin.
The glare of the pillar swept across the courtyard, and Eluned, who had been standing perfectly steady a heartbeat ago, swayed into Silas’s side with a soft gasp.
"Oh, my heart, how frightening," she said, in a voice that could not have been more composed. "Hold me."
"You’re not scared of a light," Silas said.
"Terribly scared," Eluned said, and wound both arms around his.
On his other side, Aeliana drifted close and slid her hand into the crook of his elbow without a word.
"I am steadying you, Lord Sy," she murmured. "The ground is uneven."
The ground was a flat slab of white quartz and Silas looked down at it, then at the two women hanging off his arms, deciding not to ask.
Beside Silas, Morwenna’s casual slouch straightened by a fraction of an inch.

The pirate queen squinted through the blinding gold glare with her stormy gray eyes flickering cyan and sharpening with an instinctive focus as a strange eerily familiar ripple in the current brushed against her senses.
"Huh..." Morwenna grunted, a puzzled frown tugging at her scarred brow. "...what the hell is that?"
Far across the Sovereign Realm, the sky was pitch black.
The sea beneath it was darker still like an endless expanse of ink-colored brine rolling in slow heavy swells that rose and fell like the breathing of a dormant leviathan.
There was no moon and no stars either, it was only the hollow groan of ancient timber cutting through the cold mist as a lone ship drifted across the quiet waves.
"Achoo!"

"I’m not listening to you two bicker for forty minutes...
Settle it with rock-paper-scissors, best two out of three and the winner comes along, the loser stays behind and helps Aki with the boundary towers.
Clear?"
Aeliana raised a single finger.
"For the record, Lord Sy, I am coming along regardless so the winner merely decides who travels with the two of us."
"Nobody asked the elf," Morwenna said.
"I believe the elf is the only one here who has actually met Valerius," Aeliana replied pleasantly.
Morwenna opened her mouth, found nothing to say to that, and closed it again then both women snapped their heads toward him as their eyes narrowed with deadly focus.
"Fine," Morwenna hissed, cracking her knuckles.
"Acceptable," Eluned smiled coldly, raising her delicate right hand.
They stepped onto the flagstones by the summoning altar, facing each other like gladiators entering an arena.
"Rock, paper, scissors...
SHOOT!"
Eluned threw scissors and Morwenna threw rock.
"HAH!" Morwenna roared, thrusting her fist into the air with triumphant fury.
"Point one to the high seas, you leafy tyrant!"
Eluned’s eyes narrowed into slits of concentration.
"...A fluke."
"Round two!" Silas called out, leaning against the altar’s balustrade.
"Shoot!"
Morwenna threw paper and Eluned threw scissors.
"Aha~!" Eluned cheered, clapping her hands together with angelic delight.
"Tied!
The heavens favor balance, pirate!"
Morwenna’s jaw set into iron.
Her breath came in short focused huffs with her stormy gray eyes tracking every micro-twitch in Eluned’s slender fingers.
"Last round...
Don’t blink, flower."
"Round three," Silas announced, watching the tension mount.
"Shoot!"
Eluned threw rock and Morwenna threw... she threw... paper.
Silence descended upon the altar as Morwenna’s flat palm hovered in the air, spread wide over Eluned’s clenched fist.
"YESSSSSSSSSSSSS!"
Morwenna erupted into a wild cheer, pumping both fists into the sky with her laughter echoing across the entire valley.
"VICTORY!
TAKE THAT, YOU SPOILED GODDESS!
PACK YOUR BAGS, CAPTAIN, THE PIRATE QUEEN IS HITTING THE CITY!"
She grabbed Silas’s arm, practically vibrating with excitement as her earlier frustration was completely washed away by the thrill of victory.
’His arm is right here,’ she thought, and discovered that she had hooked it against her chest without noticing.
The warmth of it went straight through her leather vest. ’Don’t look down and say something normal.’
Captain," she said, trying for casual and missing by a mile.
"Central City...
You and me..."
"You, me, and Aeliana," Silas said.
"Of course." Morwenna muttered.
Silas chuckled warmly, shaking his head.
"Alright, alright.
You won fair and square so you can come along."
Eluned stood frozen by the balustrade.
Her lower lip trembled, her emerald eyes welling with deep jealousy as she watched Morwenna cling to his arm but she crossed her arms, looking away with a dramatic aggrieved huff.
"Hmph... very well," Eluned murmured, her voice dripping with sorrowful pride.
"I suppose it is acceptable.
A generous wife must occasionally allow the lesser retainers a moment of indulgence..."
Suddenly, before Silas could even register the movement, Eluned stepped forward, grabbed both sides of his face with her delicate hands, and pulled him downward!
SMUSH!
Silas’s entire face was completely buried directly into the soft overwhelming expanse of Eluned’s generous silk-clad cleavage!
"Mmph—?!" Silas choked, his muffled voice swallowed by the sea of warmth and sweet floral perfume.
Eluned wrapped her slender arms around the back of his head, squeezing him tightly against her bust, rubbing her chest against his cheeks and nose with deliberate shameless enthusiasm.
’Soft,’ Silas thought dazedly. ’Warm...
She smells like rain in a flower field— Oxygen, I need oxygen.’
His hands fluttered uselessly in the air for a moment, unsure where it was safe to put them.
"Breathe through your nose, my heart," Eluned murmured sweetly over the top of his head.
"I am told there is plenty of room."
’This... this shameless bitch.’
Morwenna just needed ten percent of her shamelessness, if she had ten percent, she would have been knocked up by now.
"There~!" Eluned declared proudly, looking straight over his dark hair at Morwenna with a triumphant wicked smirk.
"I am rubbing my divine scent all over his face!
Every single pore of his skin is now marked with the essence of his lawful wife!
If you do anything with his face in Central City, Morwenna... that means you are kissing me!
Which means you are gay!"
PFFFFFT!
Morwenna violently choked on her own spit, coughing so hard she had to bend over and slap her knee.
"WHAT THE HELL ARE YOU TALKING ABOUT, YOU CRAZY WOMAN?!"
Standing near the perimeter, Ther’Abella and the vanguard escort guards stared at the display with wide perverted fascination.
Several of the younger guards covered their mouths, giggling behind their gauntlets with their cheeks flushed a deep scandalized red.
Ther’Abella, on the other hand, looked like her entire worldview had shattered into a million irreparable shards.

’When...’ the First Hero thought, her jaw hanging slack as she watched the pristine holy former Goddess of the World Tree aggressively smother her husband’s face in her cleavage without a single shred of shame, ’when did our innocent pristine goddess who didn’t even understand mortal emotions become this shamelessly horny?!’
Eluned finally released Silas with a satisfied hum, stepping back and smoothing her robes as if she hadn’t just committed a public act of domestic warfare.
Silas stumbled backward half a step, gasping for fresh air with his dark hair becoming a tangled mess and his cheeks burning a bright mortified pink as he wiped his face with his sleeve.
He gave Eluned an exasperated helpless look, but she merely offered him a radiant innocent smile.
Aki had gone very quiet beside the altar as she looked at Eluned, looked down at herself, and let out one very small sigh.
Aki stepped up to the edge of the quartz altar with her small hands holding a thin glowing scroll.
"Since you’re heading out to the market now, Silas," Aki said, offering him the scroll with an earnest tone.
"I wrote down the exact specifications of the building supplies and forge materials I need.
Keep track of the ledger, and once my territory is ready, I’ll pay you back everything!"
Silas took the scroll, slipping it into his coat pocket without even glancing at the numbers.
He looked down at her with a soft affectionate smile, reaching out to gently tap the tip of her small nose.
"You don’t need to refund me anything, Aki," Silas said, his voice dropping into a gentle sincere murmur.
"The fact that you’re happy and building something you love is more than enough for me."
Aki froze as his words hung in the quiet air.
Flutter!
A sudden gentle mountain breeze swept across the quartz altar.
It stirred the hem of her tunic, lifting the long, dark locks of her hair and sending Silas’s messy dark bangs dancing across his forehead.
The soft lavender twilight of the realm filtered down through the silver pillars, illuminating the warm steady tenderness in his blue eyes ringed with gold.
His thumb was still resting against the tip of her nose and she could smell the apple on his breath as well his own scent while her pulse was loud enough to hear in her own ears.
Her fingers went completely slack.
Slip!

The golden-embossed Hero Summoning Ticket she had been holding unconsciously in her left hand slipped from her numb fingers, tumbling through the air and landing with a soft chime against the white quartz flagstones.
Aki didn’t look down at the ticket.

She stared straight into his face, the handsome calm features that Eluned had just released, framed by the gentle wind and the starlight as a feeling so intensely sweet and overwhelming bloomed behind her ribs that it stole every drop of air from her lungs.
Her heart hammered against her chest like a trapped bird.
The thought echoed in the silent sacred expanse of her soul, sounding so loud and clear it frightened her.
’I want to marry you...’
For three long suspended heartbeats, the entire universe seemed to shrink down to just the two of them standing beneath the starlit sky then, Silas blinked, glancing down at the polished stone.
"Hm?" Silas asked, tilting his head with a curious smile.
"What did you drop?"
The spell shattered instantly.
Aki’s eyes bulged in pure panicked realization as a violent shade of crimson exploded across her cheeks, rushing straight to the tips of her ears and down her neck!
"A-Ah!" she squeaked, hastily bending over at the waist to scramble for the golden ticket, nearly tripping over her own boots in her desperate haste to hide her face from him.

She snatched the gleaming parchment from the stone, clutching it tightly against her chest like a shield with her breath coming in short flustered gasps as she kept her gaze glued firmly to his belt buckle.
"I-I wanted to summon my second Hero!" Aki stammered, her voice a bit higher than usual with a mortified adorable blush painting every inch of her skin.
"A-And...
I wanted you to be here when I did it..."
Silas looked down at her flushed trembling frame with a fond helpless chuckle rumbling in his chest.
’Cute,’ Silas thought, his smile softening as he stepped forward to wait for the summon.
Aki scrambled up from the quartz flagstones, clutching the golden-embossed parchment tightly against her ribs like a lifesaver.
I’ll do so now."
Her ears were still burning a furious shade of crimson, but she forced her feet forward, practically speed-walking across the terrace to put distance between herself and Silas’s teasing smile.
She reached the center of the quartz summoning altar, taking a long shuddering breath of mountain air to still her racing pulse.
With trembling fingers, she set the ticket flat against the central crystalline node.
Ding!
A translucent system prompt materialized directly before her eyes in a soft chime of light.
[Would you like to use (1) Hero Summoning Ticket to summon a Hero?]
[Y / N]
Aki didn’t hesitate as she lifted her hand and firmly tapped [Y].
VUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!
The silver pillars flanking the circle thrummed like massive tuning forks with their mana vibrating straight through the marrow of everyone standing in the courtyard.
Then...
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A pillar of pure golden radiance tore straight out of the array as the beam shot upward into the lavender twilight of Vineworld, piercing the high cloud cover easily...
It was an exact mirror-image of the pillar that had heralded Ther’Abella’s arrival only days before.
Aki’s bright blue eyes widened as the radiant wind whipped her dark bangs wild.
’Another strong one...?!’ Aki thought, her breath catching in her throat as the raw mana pressure washed over her skin.
The glare of the pillar swept across the courtyard, and Eluned, who had been standing perfectly steady a heartbeat ago, swayed into Silas’s side with a soft gasp.
"Oh, my heart, how frightening," she said, in a voice that could not have been more composed.
"Hold me."
"You’re not scared of a light," Silas said.
"Terribly scared," Eluned said, and wound both arms around his.
On his other side, Aeliana drifted close and slid her hand into the crook of his elbow without a word.
"I am steadying you, Lord Sy," she murmured.
"The ground is uneven."
The ground was a flat slab of white quartz and Silas looked down at it, then at the two women hanging off his arms, deciding not to ask.
Beside Silas, Morwenna’s casual slouch straightened by a fraction of an inch.

The pirate queen squinted through the blinding gold glare with her stormy gray eyes flickering cyan and sharpening with an instinctive focus as a strange eerily familiar ripple in the current brushed against her senses.
"Huh..." Morwenna grunted, a puzzled frown tugging at her scarred brow.
"...what the hell is that?"
Far across the Sovereign Realm, the sky was pitch black.
The sea beneath it was darker still like an endless expanse of ink-colored brine rolling in slow heavy swells that rose and fell like the breathing of a dormant leviathan.
There was no moon and no stars either, it was only the hollow groan of ancient timber cutting through the cold mist as a lone ship drifted across the quiet waves.
"Achoo!"

chapters.title: Chapter 676: Elowynn Embershade [I / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: It was a small vessel, a single-masted sloop with dark weathered oak planking and salt-stained sails that looked as though they had weathered a hundred tempests.
It lacked the grand imposing bulk of an imperial war galleon, but for her, it was more than enough.
It was fast, it was silent, and it carried everything she needed to outrun the ghosts of a broken sea.
Standing at the port railing, leaning heavily against the damp wood, was a woman.

She possessed a striking and dangerously seductive frame looking tall, full-hipped, and gifted with a remarkably heavy, generous bust that strained against the unbuttoned collar of her salt-crusted leather corset.
A wild untamed cascade of deep crimson hair spilled over her bare shoulders, glowing like smoldering embers in the darkness.
She stared down into the churning black foam below.
A sick miserable retch caught in her throat.
She gripped the railing with one calloused hand, squeezing her eyes shut as the motion of the waves threatened to turn her stomach inside out.
"Fuck..."
Cursing under her breath, she reached to her hip, unhooked an iron flask, and took a long burning swig of cheap fiery rum.
The alcohol scorched her throat, forcing the bile back down, but it did nothing to soothe the cold ache behind her ribs.
She rested her forehead against the damp wood of the rail, her eyelids drifting closed as the rhythmic sloshing of the sea began to blur.
’I miss the past...’ she thought with the memory washing over her like a warm tide.
The smell of black powder, burning canvas, and boiling brine filled the air.
Cannon fire roared across the churning reef as two pirate vessels ground their hulls together in a screeching spray of splinters.
"Morwenna!"
The crimson-haired woman had roared the name at the top of her lungs, leaping from the rigging with twin curved cutlasses blazing with violent volcanic fire.
Mid-air, a dark-haired woman met her blow for blow.
KRA-SHING!
Their blades collided with the concussive shriek of tearing iron with the shockwave peeling the foam off the waves for fifty paces in every direction.
Through the blinding spray of water and sparks, both women bared their teeth, grinning at each other like two feral sea wolves reunited on the blood-soaked deck.
The recoil threw them apart for half a heartbeat.

The crimson-haired woman landed on the pitching deck in a skid of smoking boot-soles, and before the planks stopped shaking she had already spun with both cutlasses whipping around in a pair of crossing arcs that left curtains of flame hanging in the air.
Morwenna did not back away however.
"This is good..."
She drew Tidebringer in a flash of blue, let the tide-water coiled in the runes along its fuller surge up the blade in a hissing sheet and swept it through both fire arcs at once.
PSSSSSHHH!
The flames died in a blast of white steam that swallowed half the deck, and out of the steam came her boot, aimed squarely at Morwenna’s jaw.
Morwenna ducked it by a hair and drove Tidebringer up under both blades, and the weapons locked again in a shower of sparks.
"Still swinging wild, Big Breasts?!" Morwenna had laughed through the spray, Tidebringer locking against the glowing cutlasses with raw insolent joy.
"Still swinging like a washerwoman, Morwenna?" the crimson-haired woman shot back, and leaned in.
The cutlasses flared white-hot as the steel of Tidebringer began to steam where it touched them and the wrap of the hilt smoked under Morwenna’s grip.
’Hotter than last time,’ Morwenna thought, grinning through her teeth. ’Good.’
Around them, both crews had stopped to watch.
A cannon went unfired and somebody dropped a rope.
"Washerwoman? Nice going, Big Breasts."

Morwenna let Tidebringer slide down the glowing blades, set her shoulder, and shoved with everything she had as the water in the blade roared up in a spiral and slammed into the fire, and the whole deck vanished in white steam.
BOOM!

The crimson-haired warrior vaulted backward off the flat of the saber, doing a graceful arrogant flip mid-air before landing boots-first on the narrow wooden tip of the main flagpole with her cloak billowing in the gale.
She drove her blazing cutlass into the wood, her eyes flashing with wicked defiant pride as she sneered down at the black-haired captain.
"It’s Embershade, you fool... Elowynn Embershade!"
"Didn’t hear you, Big Breasts!"
Morwenna’s laughter boomed across the churning black swells of the Abyssal Reach, cutting through the screech of tearing rigging and the concussive boom of broadside batteries.
Standing balanced upon the shuddering spar of the main mast, Elowynn Embershade gritted her teeth so hard she felt the enamel creak.
Yet, even as her jaw locked, the wicked feline tilt of her lips never wavered.

"Once again, My name," Elowynn purred, her voice dripping like poison honey over the roar of the gale, "is Elowynn but I suppose asking a sea-dog with salt-water for brains to remember three syllables is an exercise in futility, isn’t it, Dread Queen?"
Beneath her boots, the deck of the Cinder Maiden groaned under the rhythmic violent surge of mana.
Across the narrow gulf of foam, where the two sloops ground their ironwood bulwarks together in a storm of orange sparks, Morwenna stood tall.

Her long ink-black hair whipped wild against her broad shoulders with her leather arming coat open to the spray, and Tidebringer was already spinning in her grip in a lazy terrifying arc while the serpent-jawed guard flashed blue-green in the storm light.
To the rest of the fractured seas, Morwenna was similar to an extinction-level event, the nightmare that prowled the deep trade lanes, sinking galleons and leaving only floating charcoal in her wake.
To Elowynn, she was... well, what were they?
’Friends?’ Elowynn mused, her amethyst-purple eyes narrowing behind the stray strands of her glowing ember-red fringe. ’Can people in this trade even use that word?’
When your life is measured in the powder burn of an over-primed cannon and the fickle grace of an unmapped reef, tomorrow was never promised.

In a profession where your own quartermaster might slit your throat for a chest of unrefined mana-gold, having someone who locked eyes with you on the open water without instantly calling for your head was a miracle.
To Elowynn, they were friends.
...The closest thing to a sister she had ever known across three centuries of drifting.
The only problem was the woman’s intolerable habit of never, ever using her actual name.

"Quit preening on the timber like a gilded parrot, Embershade!" Morwenna barked, her scarred face splitting into a ferocious grin. "Let’s see if that third-rate crew of yours learned how to steer since the storm at Kraken’s Maw!"
"They steer well enough to board your carcass!" Elowynn hissed.
FWOOSH!
The twin curved cutlasses sheathed at her hips cleared their scabbards with a high-pitched metallic shriek.
The moment her palms locked around the ray-skin grips, her class identity roared to life.
[Class: Ember Corsair]
Deep within her pathways, her mana didn’t circulate like basic elemental flame.
"Haah!"
It surged and boiled releasing a torrent of pure liquid solar fire that rolled along the fullers of her blades like molten lava.
’I can produce much hotter flames than before...’
The rain touching her steel detonated into violent clouds of scalding white steam as Elowynn kicked off the spar.
The wood beneath her boots shattered into splinters under the sudden kinetic discharge.
She dropped like a falling meteor with her twin cutlasses tracing two blinding arcs of liquid crimson across the dark sky.
KRA-SHING!
Morwenna met her mid-fall, Tidebringer rising in an unyielding diagonal guard with the sea-serpent crossguard snarling over her knuckles.
The collision of oceanic alloy and molten liquid fire tore the air open.
BANGGGGGGGGGGGGG!!
A concussive shockwave ripped across the decks, peeling the canvas from the stays and sending a sheet of atomized brine fifty yards into the black water.
Across the gap, the ten girls on the Cinder Maiden’s deck stopped hauling lines to watch, and a few of them started trading coins.

"Ha! Weak!" Morwenna roared, her forearm muscles knotting under the strain as she pushed upward, using her raw physical leverage to throw Elowynn off her balance. "You’re still leading with your right shoulder, girl! How many times do I have to kick you in the ribs before you fix that pivot?!"
Elowynn flipped through the air with her boots grazing the rail, and hit the wet planks of Morwenna’s deck in a low feline slide.
"I don’t need to fix it when I’m aiming for your neck!" Elowynn countered, spinning on her heel.
’Liquid Lash!’
Her right blade whipped outward with a lash of molten crimson fire peeling off the tip.
WHOOSH!
The fire flowed like molten tar, bubbling through the salt-crust and snapping straight toward Morwenna’s knees but Morwenna didn’t even drop her guard.
She stamped one boot down on the planks.
THUD!
A pressurized wave of heavy ocean water surged from the seams of the ship, crashing into the molten fire with an ear-splitting hiss.
TSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSS!
Steam boiled up in a white wall, and inside it Elowynn heard what she could not see... the thin hiss of a curved blade parting the air a heartbeat before it arrived.
She threw herself sideways.
SHING!
Tidebringer’s edge sliced a lock of ember-red hair off her fringe, and the severed strand flared once like a tiny star and fell as ash.
White vapor blinded the space between them, but Morwenna moved through the fog like a shark in dark water.
Tidebringer’s curved edge hooked through the mist with a blue-green gleam aimed squarely at Elowynn’s hip.
CLANG! CLANG! SHING!
In the span of three heartbeats, they traded twenty blows as cutlass meeting saber...
Elowynn danced with grace, using her lithe curvaceous frame and natural feline agility to twist through Morwenna’s overwhelming reach.

Her hair, flickering like live coals in the dark, trailed arcs of heat through the mist while Morwenna stood like an immovable iron buoy with her heavy footwork anchoring her to the rolling deck as she parried every strike with minimal efficiency.
’What a monster...’
It didn’t matter what Elowyn did...
WHOOSH! SLASH! SLASH!
Tidebringer batted all of her attacks aside with the flat of the blade as shoulder check that rattled Elowynn’s teeth.
BANG!
"Ugh—!"
She tried to counter by whipping her blade forward however a boot heel stamped on her instep that made her hiss.
BANG!
"Stop moving bitc—"
BOOM!
She was hit in the stomach by a strong kick, knocking most of the saliva out of her mouth.

"I took down four Corporate galleons off the coast of the Iron Spire last season!" Morwenna laughed through her teeth, driving the pommel of her weapon toward Elowynn’s sternum. "Stripped their holds bare! Sixty barrels of refined mana-rum and a vault full of rune plating! What have you taken, Embershade? A rowboat of salt-fish?!"

"I raided the Governor’s personal supply transport at the Twin Atolls, you overgrown ape!" Elowynn spat, rolling under the strike with her boots sliding along the wet wood. "Took thirty crates of celestial silk and forty gold chests!"
"That was once!" Morwenna bellowed, pivoting with a devastating roundhouse sweep that forced Elowynn into a desperate high jump.
"One lucky haul six decades ago! Since then, all your girls do is run from the privateer cutters!"
’Damn her...’ Elowynn’s chest heaved with her corseted ribs burning as she landed on the gunwale.
It was true. She hated it, but it was true.
In all their years of crossing paths, in every skirmish, every boarding action, every drunken spar, Elowynn had never won against Morwenna.
...Not once.

Her crew of ten seasoned girls on the Cinder Maiden worked like an oiled machine, but whenever they tangled with Morwenna’s monsters, they were outmaneuvered, out-muscled, and run down at every single turn.
Elowynn was convinced the pirate queen deliberately dragged out their fights just to show off, just to flaunt that raw insurmountable gap in their combat foundation right in her face.
’You always look down on me,’ Elowynn thought with a spark of pure petty spite igniting behind her amethyst eyes.
She wasn’t going to win with pure martial power as she knew her physical stats couldn’t overpower Morwenna’s monstrous vitality but there were other ways to draw blood.
Elowynn’s eyes flashed.
’Ember Domain... Converging Flares!’
Eight distinct globes of liquid fire separated from her blades, floating in the humid air like burning lanterns.
With a flick of her wrists, the spheres converged on Morwenna from all directions, high, low, flank, and rear, trapping her in a cage of molten light.
The air screamed as sparks rained across the planks and every sailor on both ships dived behind a barrel.
"Ohoh, new trick?!"
Morwenna grunted, spinning Tidebringer into a high-speed wheel of water-mana to deflect the barrage.
CLANG-BOOM! CLANG-BOOM!
The liquid fire splattered against the rotating water barrier, throwing blinding light across the deck.
’Now,’ Elowynn thought, and her pulse thundered in her ears. ’Right now!’

’Friends?’ Elowynn mused, her amethyst-purple eyes narrowing behind the stray strands of her glowing ember-red fringe. ’Can people in this trade even use that word?’
When your life is measured in the powder burn of an over-primed cannon and the fickle grace of an unmapped reef, tomorrow was never promised.

In a profession where your own quartermaster might slit your throat for a chest of unrefined mana-gold, having someone who locked eyes with you on the open water without instantly calling for your head was a miracle.
To Elowynn, they were friends.
...The closest thing to a sister she had ever known across three centuries of drifting.
The only problem was the woman’s intolerable habit of never, ever using her actual name.
"Quit preening on the timber like a gilded parrot, Embershade!" Morwenna barked, her scarred face splitting into a ferocious grin.
"Let’s see if that third-rate crew of yours learned how to steer since the storm at Kraken’s Maw!"
"They steer well enough to board your carcass!" Elowynn hissed.
FWOOSH!
The twin curved cutlasses sheathed at her hips cleared their scabbards with a high-pitched metallic shriek.
The moment her palms locked around the ray-skin grips, her class identity roared to life.
[Class: Ember Corsair]
Deep within her pathways, her mana didn’t circulate like basic elemental flame.
"Haah!"
It surged and boiled releasing a torrent of pure liquid solar fire that rolled along the fullers of her blades like molten lava.
’I can produce much hotter flames than before...’
The rain touching her steel detonated into violent clouds of scalding white steam as Elowynn kicked off the spar.
The wood beneath her boots shattered into splinters under the sudden kinetic discharge.
She dropped like a falling meteor with her twin cutlasses tracing two blinding arcs of liquid crimson across the dark sky.
KRA-SHING!
Morwenna met her mid-fall, Tidebringer rising in an unyielding diagonal guard with the sea-serpent crossguard snarling over her knuckles.
The collision of oceanic alloy and molten liquid fire tore the air open.
BANGGGGGGGGGGGGG!!
A concussive shockwave ripped across the decks, peeling the canvas from the stays and sending a sheet of atomized brine fifty yards into the black water.
Across the gap, the ten girls on the Cinder Maiden’s deck stopped hauling lines to watch, and a few of them started trading coins.
"Ha!
Weak!" Morwenna roared, her forearm muscles knotting under the strain as she pushed upward, using her raw physical leverage to throw Elowynn off her balance.
"You’re still leading with your right shoulder, girl!
How many times do I have to kick you in the ribs before you fix that pivot?!"
Elowynn flipped through the air with her boots grazing the rail, and hit the wet planks of Morwenna’s deck in a low feline slide.
"I don’t need to fix it when I’m aiming for your neck!" Elowynn countered, spinning on her heel.
’Liquid Lash!’
Her right blade whipped outward with a lash of molten crimson fire peeling off the tip.
WHOOSH!
The fire flowed like molten tar, bubbling through the salt-crust and snapping straight toward Morwenna’s knees but Morwenna didn’t even drop her guard.
She stamped one boot down on the planks.
THUD!
A pressurized wave of heavy ocean water surged from the seams of the ship, crashing into the molten fire with an ear-splitting hiss.
TSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSS!
Steam boiled up in a white wall, and inside it Elowynn heard what she could not see... the thin hiss of a curved blade parting the air a heartbeat before it arrived.
She threw herself sideways.
SHING!
Tidebringer’s edge sliced a lock of ember-red hair off her fringe, and the severed strand flared once like a tiny star and fell as ash.
White vapor blinded the space between them, but Morwenna moved through the fog like a shark in dark water.
Tidebringer’s curved edge hooked through the mist with a blue-green gleam aimed squarely at Elowynn’s hip.
CLANG!
CLANG!
SHING!
In the span of three heartbeats, they traded twenty blows as cutlass meeting saber...
Elowynn danced with grace, using her lithe curvaceous frame and natural feline agility to twist through Morwenna’s overwhelming reach.

Her hair, flickering like live coals in the dark, trailed arcs of heat through the mist while Morwenna stood like an immovable iron buoy with her heavy footwork anchoring her to the rolling deck as she parried every strike with minimal efficiency.
’What a monster...’
It didn’t matter what Elowyn did...
WHOOSH!
SLASH!
SLASH!
Tidebringer batted all of her attacks aside with the flat of the blade as shoulder check that rattled Elowynn’s teeth.
BANG!
"Ugh—!"
She tried to counter by whipping her blade forward however a boot heel stamped on her instep that made her hiss.
BANG!
"Stop moving bitc—"
BOOM!
She was hit in the stomach by a strong kick, knocking most of the saliva out of her mouth.
"I took down four Corporate galleons off the coast of the Iron Spire last season!" Morwenna laughed through her teeth, driving the pommel of her weapon toward Elowynn’s sternum.
"Stripped their holds bare!
Sixty barrels of refined mana-rum and a vault full of rune plating!
What have you taken, Embershade?
A rowboat of salt-fish?!"
"I raided the Governor’s personal supply transport at the Twin Atolls, you overgrown ape!" Elowynn spat, rolling under the strike with her boots sliding along the wet wood.
"Took thirty crates of celestial silk and forty gold chests!"
"That was once!" Morwenna bellowed, pivoting with a devastating roundhouse sweep that forced Elowynn into a desperate high jump.
"One lucky haul six decades ago!
Since then, all your girls do is run from the privateer cutters!"
’Damn her...’ Elowynn’s chest heaved with her corseted ribs burning as she landed on the gunwale.
It was true.
She hated it, but it was true.
In all their years of crossing paths, in every skirmish, every boarding action, every drunken spar, Elowynn had never won against Morwenna.
...Not once.

Her crew of ten seasoned girls on the Cinder Maiden worked like an oiled machine, but whenever they tangled with Morwenna’s monsters, they were outmaneuvered, out-muscled, and run down at every single turn.
Elowynn was convinced the pirate queen deliberately dragged out their fights just to show off, just to flaunt that raw insurmountable gap in their combat foundation right in her face.
’You always look down on me,’ Elowynn thought with a spark of pure petty spite igniting behind her amethyst eyes.
She wasn’t going to win with pure martial power as she knew her physical stats couldn’t overpower Morwenna’s monstrous vitality but there were other ways to draw blood.
Elowynn’s eyes flashed.
’Ember Domain...
Converging Flares!’
Eight distinct globes of liquid fire separated from her blades, floating in the humid air like burning lanterns.
With a flick of her wrists, the spheres converged on Morwenna from all directions, high, low, flank, and rear, trapping her in a cage of molten light.
The air screamed as sparks rained across the planks and every sailor on both ships dived behind a barrel.
"Ohoh, new trick?!"
Morwenna grunted, spinning Tidebringer into a high-speed wheel of water-mana to deflect the barrage.
CLANG-BOOM!
CLANG-BOOM!
The liquid fire splattered against the rotating water barrier, throwing blinding light across the deck.
’Now,’ Elowynn thought, and her pulse thundered in her ears. ’Right now!’

chapters.title: Chapter 677: Elowynn Embershade [II / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: In that half-second of obscured vision, Elowynn didn’t attack from the front.
She used her lightweight momentum, slipping around the blind side of the saber’s rotation and stepping directly into Morwenna’s personal space.
Her face was inches from the other woman’s ear with her cheek practically brushing Morwenna’s dark hair but she didn’t swing her cutlasses.
Instead, a wicked triumphant smirk spread across Elowynn’s lips, and she whispered.
"At least I’ve slept with a man... You’re still a virg—"
BAM!
The universe seemed to caved in.

A massive calloused hand clamped onto the back of Elowynn’s neck with the speed and violence of an iron bear trap and before the word virgin could even finish vibrating between her teeth, Morwenna’s entire frame torqued.
CRRRRRRRR-RACK!
Morwenna slammed Elowynn’s face straight down into the reinforced ironwood deck.
The concussive impact shattered three planks, cratering the timber in a three-foot depression.
A cloud of oak splinters, pulverized salt, and steam exploded outward, accompanied by a literal column of white-hot vapor shooting violently out of Morwenna’s ears.
The pirate queen stood hunched over her with veins bulging along her neck as her scarred face contorted into an expression of such pure rage that the surrounding storm seemed to freeze in terror.

"Say that shit one more time," Morwenna snarled, her voice dropping into a guttural rumble that rattled the iron fixtures of the mast. "Say it. I dare you to let your lips form that word again, you little wretch..."
Beneath her hand, Elowynn lay in the splintered crater with her nose throbbing and her cheek pressed hard against the cold damp wood.
’Holy hell...’ Elowynn thought, her eyes spinning in dizzy circles as she stared at the cracked grain of the timber. ’She is... unbelievably sensitive about the virgin thing...’
Carefully, Elowynn tapped the flat of her palm twice against the wood, then rolled her hips and wiggled out of the depression, sliding five paces away across the deck like an eel.
She sat up, holding her bruised nose, waving both hands in exaggerated surrender.
"Yield! I yield, you maniac! Yield!"
Morwenna let out a long shuddering snort with the steam slowly clearing from her ears as she aggressively wiped her sleeve across her mouth.
She kicked the loose wood splinters away from her boots, grumbling a stream of filthy curses that could have stripped the paint off an imperial flagship.
Sitting on the damp deck while brushing wood dust from her voluminous cleavage, Elowynn let out a quiet sigh.
’I lost... again.’
To be completely honest... Elowynn had never slept with a man in her life.
She hadn’t even kissed one.
From the secluded island where she had awakened centuries ago, men had looked at her with one thing in their eyes... drooling lust.

With her bountiful curves, narrow waist, and the small mole beneath her left eye as well as her fox-like purple eyes, she had been a magnet for every swaggering lecherous pirate captain who thought a bag of stolen coin earned them the right to touch her.

She had gut-punched more men than she had killed beasts... It was the entire reason her crew on the Cinder Maiden was comprised exclusively of women, she couldn’t stand the way men postured, smelled, and looked at her like a prize to be hoarded.
In truth, she had never met a single soul who caught her interest.
’But...’ Elowynn smirked internally, rubbing her sore jaw, ’it pisses Morwenna off so wonderfully that I can never resist taking the shot.’
Besides, what did it even matter?
What was the practical difference between a virgin and a woman who had spent an hour with a man?
You had someone’s clumsy hands on you, so what? You got to taste those slimy things called dicks... So?
So what if she and Morwenna were both pushing past several centuries of life?

With the longevity granted by their high-tier classes, they had centuries more to burn. Sex wasn’t an operational necessity... it was an optional distraction for people who didn’t have ships to sail and hulls to patch.
The tension slowly drained from the air.
Across the water, the ten crew members of the Cinder Maiden waved enthusiastically across the gap, shouting greetings to Morwenna and calling for their captain.
Morwenna glanced down at Elowynn with her wild scowl softening into an exasperated familiar grimace.
"Fuck you."
Without a word, she reached down, caught Elowynn by the belt of her corset and hoisted her to her feet with one arm, setting her upright before nodding toward the aft cabin.
"Get in here before you catch a chill, Big Breasts," Morwenna grunted, turning her back and stomping toward the heavy oak door.
Elowynn rolled her eyes, smoothing her torn tunic, and followed her inside.
The captain’s quarters of Morwenna’s vessel were Spartan, smelling richly of pitch, cured leather, and high-grade spirits.
Weapons hung from iron pegs along the bulkheads, and half-rolled nautical charts were pinned to the cedar table with heavy boarding daggers.
Morwenna dropped into a wide battered leather chair, kicked her boots onto the table, and gestured vaguely toward the heavy iron cabinet bolted against the starboard wall.
"How do you feel?" Morwenna asked, rummaging through the drawer until she pulled out two dark glass bottles.
Elowynn leaned against the map table, crossing her long legs. "I feel fine... My nose is only slightly broken, thank you very much."
"Hah! Your fault for running your mouth with that oversized chest leading the way," Morwenna teased, uncorking one of the bottles with her teeth and spitting the wooden stopper across the room.
Elowynn sighed, staring down at her boots.
They only saw each other once every decade or so, meeting at unmapped coordinates in the outer reaches to trade intelligence and test their steel.
...And once again, she had performed miserably.
She had been forced to rely on a cheap childish distraction just to slip past Morwenna’s guard.

"I’m sorry," Elowynn murmured softly, the bravado slipping from her posture. "For wasting your time. I thought... I thought I had closed the gap this time but I’m still just as clumsy as I was a century ago."
Morwenna paused mid-swig.
She lowered the bottle, looking at Elowynn through the dim lantern light.
A genuinely warm smile touched her scarred lips as it was a look that lacked any sort of mockery or competition.
"You’re an idiot, Embershade," Morwenna said quietly.
She took a slow gulp of the dark liquor, wiping her mouth with the back of her wrist.

"You’re doing well... Better than well... Your mana control with that liquid flame is sharper than anyone I’ve crossed blades with in the last fifty years, You’re growing stronger every time we meet. It won’t be long before you can actually match me blow for blow."
Elowynn blinked with a faint surprised chuckle escaping her throat.
"You’re not just saying that to keep me from crying?"
"I don’t lie about steel," Morwenna snorted, taking another deep draught. "You fight smart... You read angles better than most admirals and you’ve got the instincts of a true corsair."
A quiet genuine warmth settled in Elowynn’s chest.
Hearing those words from Morwenna meant more than an entire mountain of stolen loot.
Morwenna finished half the bottle in three massive gulps, set it down with a heavy clatter, and stood up from the table.
She walked over to the cabin door, resting her hand on the iron latch, looking back over her shoulder.
"We’re friends, aren’t we?" Morwenna asked with her voice sounding very steady.
Elowynn nodded slowly. "We are."

"Good then don’t get yourself sunk by some two-bit privateer before our next meeting," Morwenna said, her lips curling into a soft fond grin. "See you in ten years, Elowynn... Pick up something new by then, will you?"
The heavy oak door swung shut behind her as Elowynn stood frozen in the center of the quiet cabin.
’Elowynn.’
The name echoed in her ears like a distant ringing bell.
She hadn’t imagined it. For the first time in three hundred years, the Dread Queen hadn’t called her a nickname... She had spoken her true name.
A radiant dizzying smile broke across Elowynn’s small face.
Her amethyst eyes sparkled, and she threw her arms up in a silent, ecstatic cheer, bouncing lightly on her heels like an excited girl.
’This calls for a celebration!’ she thought, practically floating out of the cabin and back across the gangplank to her own ship.
She stepped onto the quarterdeck of the Cinder Maiden, looking at her navigator with a wide bright grin.
"Captain’s orders!" Elowynn declared, her voice ringing with sheer joy. "Swerve us south! Set course for Kuvikui Island!"
She leaned against the helm, letting the wind whip through her glowing crimson hair as the sea sprayed over the bow.
’I’m going to drink to my heart’s content,’ she promised herself, her heart lighter than it had been in centuries. ’Ten years until the next spar... Tonight, I celebrate!’
A low miserable groan scraped past Elowynn’s dry parched throat.
The air was suffocating, thick with the stench of sour, stale ale, cheap tobacco, and the greasy film of cold tallow candles.
Her head felt as though an iron band had been forged around her temples and tightened with a heavy wrench.
Every pulse of her heartbeat sent a sickening thud through her optic nerves.
She peeled her face off the sticky beer-stained surface of a scarred pine table.
"Girls...?" she croaked, blinking against the dull murky light filtering through a grease-covered window. "Sabine? Vanya... where are you...?"
There was no answer.
It was only the rhythmic monotonous sound of a dry rag wiping down an oak counter twenty paces away.
"Excuse me, miss," a flat tired voice spoke from across the tavern.
An elderly tavern-master in a stained apron stopped his wiping, leaning heavily on the bar, looking at her with hollow unimpressed eyes.

"We’ve been closed since dawn," the man said. "The boys tried waking you three times. Doused your hands in cold well-water, shook your shoulders... nothing took. If you’re done sleeping off the barrel, I need you to settle your tab."
Elowynn rubbed her temples with trembling fingers, her thoughts dragging through a thick syrupy fog.
"My crew..." she mumbled, squinting through the gloom. "The women I came in with. Ten girls... they were armed, where did they go?"
The barkeep stared at her blankly.
"Your crew? Miss, they left hours ago... They walked out before midnight while you were still facedown in your cups."
Elowynn’s brow furrowed. "Left...?"
She pushed herself up from the bench, swaying slightly on her boots as she reached instinctively into the hidden pockets of her leather armor to fetch a purse of coins.
Her hands found nothing.
...Empty.
She checked the inner lining of her vest.
The small silk pouch of high-grade gems she always kept pinned against her ribs was gone.
Her wrist-cuffs, forged from silver-mana alloy, were missing.
Even the small spatial ring she wore on her right thumb, the one containing her emergency rations and sea-charts, had been cleanly stripped from her hand.
Her bare thumb looked strangely small without it.
’That’s... impossible,’ she thought, a cold prickling sensation washing over her skin, instantly cutting through the alcohol haze.
She hadn’t carried much physical cash into the tavern as she hated hauling heavy iron coin when traveling ashore, but her gear alone was worth a small fortune.
Desperate to leave, she unclasped the heavy masterwork brass gauntlet from her left forearm and slammed it onto the counter.
"This is forged from fourth-grade volcanic brass," she rasped, not waiting for his reply. "It covers the tab three times over... Keep the change."
She didn’t wait for his answer.
She burst through the swinging doors of the tavern, breaking into a dead sprint down the cobblestone incline leading to the docks of Kuvikui Island.
The morning air hit her face feeling cold and smelling of dead fish and low tide.
She vaulted over the wooden barricades, running straight onto the high stone pier, her sharp purple eyes scanning the forest of masts anchored in the harbor.
...The Cinder Maiden wasn’t there.
The slip was empty.
Only two frayed mooring ropes bobbed uselessly in the murky water, severed cleanly by a serrated knife.
She stood on the empty slip for a long moment, staring at the two frayed ends as though they might explain themselves.
"Looking for the crimson sloop, are you?"
Elowynn whirled around and standing near the harbormaster’s toll booth was a portly one-eyed dockmaster, chewing on a matchstick.
"Where is my ship?" she demanded, her voice shaking with a dangerous crackling heat.

"Cleared the breakwater four hours past midnight," the dockmaster replied casually, spitting into the harbor. "Your quartermaster signed the departure slip, she said the captain was resting below decks... paid the harbor tax in full and sailed east."
Elowynn’s breath hitched in her throat as her hands fell limp to her sides.
’They... left without me.’
The realization struck her with the sickening concussive weight of a falling spear.
