She pushed herself up from the bench, swaying slightly on her boots as she reached instinctively into the hidden pockets of her leather armor to fetch a purse of coins.
Her hands found nothing.
...Empty.
She checked the inner lining of her vest.
The small silk pouch of high-grade gems she always kept pinned against her ribs was gone.
Her wrist-cuffs, forged from silver-mana alloy, were missing.
Even the small spatial ring she wore on her right thumb, the one containing her emergency rations and sea-charts, had been cleanly stripped from her hand.
Her bare thumb looked strangely small without it.
’That’s... impossible,’ she thought, a cold prickling sensation washing over her skin, instantly cutting through the alcohol haze.
She hadn’t carried much physical cash into the tavern as she hated hauling heavy iron coin when traveling ashore, but her gear alone was worth a small fortune.
Desperate to leave, she unclasped the heavy masterwork brass gauntlet from her left forearm and slammed it onto the counter.
"This is forged from fourth-grade volcanic brass," she rasped, not waiting for his reply.
"It covers the tab three times over...
Keep the change."
She didn’t wait for his answer.
She burst through the swinging doors of the tavern, breaking into a dead sprint down the cobblestone incline leading to the docks of Kuvikui Island.
The morning air hit her face feeling cold and smelling of dead fish and low tide.
She vaulted over the wooden barricades, running straight onto the high stone pier, her sharp purple eyes scanning the forest of masts anchored in the harbor.
...The Cinder Maiden wasn’t there.
The slip was empty.
Only two frayed mooring ropes bobbed uselessly in the murky water, severed cleanly by a serrated knife.
She stood on the empty slip for a long moment, staring at the two frayed ends as though they might explain themselves.
"Looking for the crimson sloop, are you?"
Elowynn whirled around and standing near the harbormaster’s toll booth was a portly one-eyed dockmaster, chewing on a matchstick.
"Where is my ship?" she demanded, her voice shaking with a dangerous crackling heat.
"Cleared the breakwater four hours past midnight," the dockmaster replied casually, spitting into the harbor.
"Your quartermaster signed the departure slip, she said the captain was resting below decks... paid the harbor tax in full and sailed east."
Elowynn’s breath hitched in her throat as her hands fell limp to her sides.
’They... left without me.’
The realization struck her with the sickening concussive weight of a falling spear.

chapters.title: Chapter 678: Elowynn Embershade [III / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: She waited for the anger.
A captain robbed by her own crew ought to be furious, ought to be tearing the dockside apart plank by plank, and she searched herself for that fire and found only a cold hollow quiet.
’The gems, the cuffs, the ring... fine,’ She thought. ’Take it all. I would have given you every coin if you had only asked.’
A hollow agonizing ache blossomed deep in her chest, and it had nothing to do with money.
These weren’t random sell-swords she had picked up in a dive bar.
...She had sailed with this specific crew for over fifty years, most of those girls were the daughters and granddaughters of her original crew from the southern archipelagos.

She had watched them take their first steps on a rolling deck... she had bandaged their sword wounds, taught them how to weave mana into their cutlasses, and shared every single copper of plunder equally down to the last scrap of bread.
They had called her their Captain and some of them had even called her their mother as well.
’Why...?’ she thought, her vision blurring as she looked at the empty gray water. ’Why didn’t you just trust me enough to tell me you wanted to go...?’
Anger would have been easier as anger burned hot and burned out but this feeling...
This sat in her chest like a stone and when she finally put a name to it, the name was disappointment.
’I’m so stupid...’
She was not furious with them, Elowynn was disappointed, in the tired way a mother is disappointed in a child she raised better than that but for her... It hurt far more.
She reached for her neck, searching for the mana transponder that could ping her ship’s helm but it was gone.
Her neck was bare.
She had been left stranded.
Alone, without a single copper to her name, without a weapon, and without a vessel to call her own, standing in the cold rain of a lawless pirate haven...
A quiet bitter laugh slipped past her lips.
It grew, bubbling up from her parched throat into a dry broken chuckle that made the dockmaster take a cautious step back.

"Well," Elowynn whispered, turning her back on the sea, quoting the old corsair proverb she had heard a thousand times on the docks. "Trust the sea to drown you, trust the wind to turn on you, and trust a pirate to show you who they truly are..."
What else was there to do? Cry in the mud?
She pulled her hood up, buried her bare hands into her pockets, and walked back into the squalor of Kuvikui Island.
The next few days passed in a gray sunless blur.

Kuvikui Island was an infamous sanctuary for the worst filth the shattered seas had to offer, a lawless volcanic rock where outlaws with six-figure bounties congregated to trade stolen cargo and drink themselves into an early grave.
Elowynn’s own bounty was substantial, but compared to the legendary names that frequented the deep coves, she was barely a footnote so she needed a way off the rock.
She definitely wasn’t going to crawl into a ditch and die... She was an Ember Corsair.
If she didn’t have a ship, she would do what pirates had done since the dawn of the realms... She would steal one.
Her eyes were already set on a sleek twin-masted schooner anchored in the private bay of the merchant guilds.
The security along the docks was tight as high-tier mercenaries armed with heavy mana rifles had been hired.
It would be a suicide run in broad daylight, but at night, beneath the cover of the torrential rainstorms that battered the island... it was nothing she couldn’t carve her way through.
Until night fell, there was only one thing to do... Drown the silence.
Elowynn sat in the corner of a dingy smoke-filled tavern near the lower docks, watching the rain hammer against the greasy windows.
Outside, the sky was pitch-black with lightning tearing across the low clouds in jagged violent forks.
She lifted a bottle of cheap, burning grain alcohol to her lips, gulping down half the contents in a single, desperate swallow.
The liquid burned her esophagus, but it did nothing to numb the hollow gnawing ache in her chest.
"Hey, miss," the tavern-keeper called from behind the counter, scowling as he dried a mug. "You haven’t paid for that third bottle yet."

Without looking, Elowynn reached into her pocket, pulled out a small leather pouch of silver coins she had "liberated" from a drunken privateer in the alley two hours prior, and tossed it across the floor.
The pouch landed on the counter with a heavy clink.
"Bring me two more," she muttered, staring blankly at the dark rain.
Before the barkeep could reach for the shelf, the tavern’s front door was kicked off its iron latch.
BANG!
A soaking-wet scout, his leather cloak dripping with rainwater, stumbled into the common room with his chest heaving and his face looking as pale as a corpse.
"The Dread Queen!" the man screamed, his voice cracking with hysterical terror. "It’s Morwenna! The Dread Queen of the Seas and the entire crew of the Leviathan’s Wake... they’re gone!"
The tavern went dead silent... The drunken brawlers, the card-cheats, the hardened captains, every single soul in the room froze mid-breath...
"What are you screaming about, boy?" a scarred veteran growled from the corner. "Morwenna doesn’t sink so who took her?"

"Not a fleet!" the scout choked out with his knees trembling. "The Corporate Deities of the Righteous Pantheon! Lord Aurelius himself! They came down on the Nebula of Orinon with three hundred golden dreadnoughts! They didn’t capture her... they annihilated the entire sector! Burned the sea until it boiled! Morwenna... she’s dead! They killed her!"
Shatter!
The bottle in Elowynn’s hand slipped.
It struck the stone floor with the dark glass exploding into a hundred jagged fragments as cheap alcohol pooled in a bitter puddle around the toes of her boots.
Elowynn sat frozen with her breath caught in her throat and the world around her turning into a silent ringing void.
Her lips parted, trembling violently as a single broken whisper escaped her.
"Mor... Morwenna... is dead...?"
’Five hundred years...’
Elowynn opened her eyes, drawing a sharp shuddering breath as the damp freezing mist of the high seas bit into her skin.
She sneezed, it was a pathetic wet sound that echoed across the silent water and aggressively wiped her red nose with the frayed cuff of her sleeve.
Beneath her, the small solitary rowboat rose and fell on the dark ink-black swells.
The air here was dead lacking any sort of wind or bird-calls while carrying that lingering metallic tang of slaughter... In short a lot of blood had been spilled in this very location.
To Elowynn, this was the coordinate.

The exact forgotten graveyard where the Corporate deities had unleashed their judgment five centuries ago, boiling the sea to bedrock and extinguishing the brightest fiercest flame the oceans had ever known.
"I tried my best, Morwenna..." Elowynn whispered into the dark, her voice cracking with five hundred years of accumulated exhaustion.
She had tried... Gods above, how she had tried...
After that night on Kuvikui, she had spent two centuries hunting the ghosts of that battle.
She had sailed alone, built a new foundation from blood and salvage, and eventually tracked down one of the lower-ranked arbiters who had participated in the purge.
She had launched herself at the divine construct with suicidal fury, burning her own life-force to unleash every drop of her Ember Corsair foundation.
...And she had failed.

The entity had crushed her fleet with a flick of its mechanical wrist, fracturing her core, stripping her levels, and leaving her to rot in the outer drifts under a festering soul-rending curse that had slowly poisoned her pathways ever since.

"I couldn’t do it," she choked out with hot tears finally spilling over her cheeks, cutting clean tracks through the salt-grime on her face. "After all this time... I couldn’t even avenge you. Five hundred years, and I couldn’t lay a single scratch on the people who took you."
Her hands clenched into fists, hammering against the wooden gunwale of the rowboat until her knuckles bled.

"Useless," she sobbed, burying her face in her arms. "I’m useless... completely useless! A captain without a crew! A warrior who can’t hold her steel and to make it even more pathetic... five hundred years later, and I’m still a virgin, for heaven’s sake! What kind of legendary pirate dies an untouched miserable drunk in the middle of nowhere?!"
She grabbed the neck of an empty bottle rolling in the bilge, her fingers trembling with rage, and shattered it against the mast.
CRASH!
A violent pathetic hiccup tore through her chest.
She leaned back against the thwarts, staring up at the empty, starless sky while wiping her tears with the back of her dirty hand.
Her thoughts drifted, as they sometimes did, back to the girls of the Cinder Maiden.
She had actually found them once, some eighty years after Kuvikui, in a quiet harbor town on the southern archipelago...
Sabine with gray in her hair, Vanya hauling nets, a clutch of children running underfoot.

She had stood on the pier for an hour with her hood pulled low, and not one of them had looked up... then she had turned around and sailed away without a word, too disappointed to forgive them and too fond of them to spoil their peace.
’I hope they had good lives,’ she thought, in passing, and found that she meant it.
"What would you say if you saw me right now, you arrogant ape...?" she whispered to the empty dark. "You’d probably laugh until your lungs gave out, wouldn’t you...?"
Then...
[Ding!]
A sound chimed through the stillness.
It wasn’t the creak of wood or the whisper of the waves.
It was a crisp crystalline chime that resonated directly inside her soul, vibrating with the harmonic frequency of dimensional authority.
A glowing blue holographic tab flared to life in the air before her tear-stained eyes.
[You have been summoned to be a Hero for a Lord.]
[Y / N]
Elowynn blinked with her amethyst eyes wide, staring at the glowing letters in pure alcohol-dazed bewilderment.
’Summoned as a Hero...?’
She let out a raspy self-deprecating snort.
’Do I look like a hero to anyone? I’m a broken, washed-up corsair drifting in a dinghy with a liver full of cheap rum.’
Yet, she didn’t hesitate. Her finger reached out, hovering over the golden rune.
What did she have left here? A ruined sea? An empty grave?
Her alcohol supply had run out two days ago, and she was so goddamn sick of the pirate life she could vomit just looking at a sail.
"Yes," she muttered aloud, tapping Y. "I just hope to the gods they have something decent to drink wherever we’re going..."
The interface flared, and a second box materialized over the first.
[Your level will be forcefully reset from Level 430 —> Level 1. You will lose some of your Priority Skills; however, you will retain the remaining foundation of your Original Skill Tree.]
Elowynn stared at the numbers.
A manic, breathless chuckle bubbled up from her throat.
’Level 430... down to Level 1...’
All these centuries, she had clung to Level 430, a fraction of what she had once been before the divine arbiter’s curse broke her pathways.
She had thought she was holding onto her pride, but in truth, she had just been clinging to a corpse.

’How could I have let myself become this weak...?’ she thought, a fierce bitter determination suddenly stirring in the ashes of her heart. ’If Morwenna were still alive... she’d be standing at the absolute peak by now... She wouldn’t be crying over lost levels.’
"Yes," Elowynn whispered, her voice firming for the first time in centuries. "Take it... Strip it clean..."
VUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!
A blinding celestial pillar of pure golden energy erupted from the base of her sou as the rowboat, the dark water, the weeping sky, everything vanished into a sea of incandescent warm light.

Elowynn felt the weight of five hundred years of cold stagnant grief lift from her shoulders as her consciousness was pulled upward through the dimensional rift, soaring past shattered planes and starlit nebulae.
FLASH!
The spatial updraft cleared with a chiming sound and the first thing that hit Elowynn was the scent.
...It wasn’t salt-water, it wasn’t rot, or smoke, or dead fish either.

It was the clean scent of wild mountain pine, fresh loamy soil, and blooming roses that was mingled rather intensely, with the heavy sour reek of cheap grain alcohol currently radiating from her own rumpled clothes.
Elowynn was sitting flat on her backside upon a platform of immaculate polished white quartz.
She blinked rapidly, rubbing her pounding temples with her amethyst-purple eyes struggling to focus through the lingering spatial glare.
Standing three paces in front of her was a small, extraordinarily cute girl with long flowing blue hair and wide, brilliant blue eyes that were practically sparkling with childish wonder.
The girl was wearing a soot-stained tunic and small leather boots, looking at her with an expression of pure awe.

chapters.title: Chapter 679: Elowynn And Morwenna [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: ’What a cute kid...’ Elowynn thought, her dazed brain slowly piecing reality together. ’Is this my Lord? She looks like she belongs in a dollhouse, not a war-camp...’
Her gaze drifted past the blue-haired girl, scanning the perimeter of the quartz altar.
She saw a tall ethereal High Elf with blond hair and pale green robes, watching with serene aristocratic poise.
She saw another tall, silver-armored elf with silver hair and cold blue eyes scowling in the corner.

Beside them stood a radiant silver-haired woman in jade-and-silver robes, emerald eyes watching Elowynn with the polite smile of someone sizing up a rival and on the steps sat a colossal golden-haired woman with a flagon in one hand and a half-eaten roast boar leg in the other, grinning at her as though she had just found a new drinking partner.
And then... her eyes stopped.
Standing by the silver balustrade was a young man.
He was tall, broad-shouldered, with a lean dangerous frame clad in tailored charcoal linen.
His messy dark hair danced lightly in the mountain breeze, framing a face that was so effortlessly handsome that Elowynn felt her breath violently catch in the back of her throat.
His blue eyes, ringed with gold, were calm and steady... These were the eyes of a person who had fought wars and emerged victorious.
A sudden dizzying heat rushed straight from Elowynn’s chest down into her stomach.
Her heart hammered against her leather corset with terrifying violence.
In all her centuries of sailing the seas, she had never seen a man look like that.
He wasn’t greasy or swaggering, and he didn’t bark orders like an insecure captain.

He had a full thick head of dark hair, unlike ninety percent of the bald, scarred pirate brutes who populated the trade ports, and his presence carried a quiet magnetic gravity that made her skin tingle.
Elowynn hiccuped loudly with her face instantly turning a bright flustered pink as she stared at him like a star-struck schoolgirl.
The seductive smirk she had honed on three centuries of lecherous captains slid straight off her face.
Her competitive streak, her shameless charm, her whole femme-fatale arsenal, all of it simply switched off and left her gaping like a fish.
She tossed her ember-red hair back and tried to give him her best smile... the one that had talked her out of three hangings but it came out crooked.
Before she could scramble to her feet and wipe the booze from her chin, a raspy and utterly unmistakable voice cut through the quiet air.
"Elowynn...?"
Elowynn froze.
The universe seemed to tilt on its axis.
Slowly, her amethyst eyes pulled away from the handsome young man, drifting two feet to the left.
Standing right beside him with one hand resting on Tidebringer’s hilt and her jaw hanging wide open in complete shock... was Morwenna.
Elowynn’s eyes went wide as dinner plates.
Elowynn sat flat on the polished quartz flagstones of the summoning dais, blinking through a dense alcohol-soaked haze.
Her vision doubled with the lavender twilight of Vineworld swimming in lazy circles around the edges of her sight.
She rubbed her temples with two trembling soot-stained fingers, her amethyst eyes widening as they locked onto the tall, scarred figure standing a mere five paces away.

"No... no way," Elowynn muttered, her voice slurring heavily as a pathetic hiccup rattled her corseted chest. "I’m dreaming... That’s it... I drank the whole reserve barrel on the dinghy and now my dying brain is hallucinating. Not only am I seeing a breathtakingly handsome young man after five hundred miserable years of staring at rotten driftwood... but my pickled skull is actually serving up Morwenna as dessert, I am way too goddamn drunk for this level of theater."
Morwenna’s jaw tightened.
The dark-haired pirate queen closed her eyes, exhaling a long shuddering breath through her nose that sounded like a furnace venting steam.
The casual slouch she had worn earlier vanished, replaced by the exasperated exhaustion of a woman whose past had just climbed out of a shallow grave and vomited on her boots.
"Give me a minute," Morwenna muttered to the group, not looking back as she rolled her shoulder joints with a sharp crack.
Silas leaned sideways, watching the exchange with an arched eyebrow.
"You two actually know each other?"
"Unfortunately," Morwenna grunted, stepping up onto the raised dais. "We crossed cutlasses across the western trade lanes a while back."
Silas watched her approach the dazed corsair, scratching the back of his neck as a faint, deadpan smirk tugged at his lips.

’Is this whole territory run on bizarre coincidences?’ Silas mused. ’First, Aki accidentally summons Ther’Abella, who used to serve under Eluned’s royal guard... Now her very next ticket pulls a high-seas relic straight out of Morwenna’s old pirate days... What’s next on her third roll? Aeliana’s long-lost second cousin from the silver groves? Not that I’m complaining about free high-tier women for the vassal seat, I’m just curious what she pulls next—’
PAH!
A concussive deafening crack ripped through the courtyard.

Morwenna’s open palm struck Elowynn across the left cheek with the concussive force of an iron broadside as the shockwave peeling off the impact was so violent that the surrounding flowerbeds flattened, sending a storm of violet rose petals swirling twenty feet into the air.
Silas flinched.
Aeliana subtly took half a step backward, smoothing her robes, while Aki let out a tiny horrified squeak.
Elowynn sat frozen, her head violently jerked to the right with a bright crimson handprint swelling across her pale porcelain skin.
She blinked, her tongue running over her numbed lips as she slowly turned her dazed, amethyst eyes back toward the towering corsair.
"Mor... Morwen—"
CRACK!
Without waiting for the syllable to clear, Morwenna’s arm whipped back in a vicious unyielding backhand.
The knuckles connected squarely with Elowynn’s jaw and the rotational torque lifted her bountiful frame completely off the flagstones, sending her skidding three yards across the quartz.
Two broken molars and a fine spray of crimson blood splattered onto the pristine white stone, hissing faintly where her residual ember-mana reacted with the ambient air.
’Two teeth...?!’ Elowynn’s tongue probed the gap in horror. ’Those were expensive!’
Morwenna shook out her hand, standing over the groaning corsair with her boots planted wide.
"You back in your goddamn senses yet, Embershade?"
Elowynn pushed herself onto one elbow, coughing up a mouthful of copper-tinted phlegm.
She reached up with a bruised hand, wiping the blood from her swollen lip, her fox-like eyes wide with a mixture of dazed shock and wild desperate realization.
"Yes... holy shit, yes," Elowynn wheezed, shaking her head until her flickering, ember-red hair danced like sparks. "I can’t believe it... you’re actually—"
Morwenna took half a step forward to yank her up by the scruff, but the second she leaned down, the full stench of five-hundred-year-old fermented grain mash washed over her face.
"Ugh—cough!"
Morwenna violently recoiled, clutching her nose and coughing so hard her ribs shook.
Her face contorted into pure disgust as she stumbled backward down the steps of the altar.
"Gods above! What in the name of the deep did you bathe in?! It smells like a drowned still in a sun-baked swamp! Don’t move! Stay right there! Don’t you dare exhale in my direction!"
Elowynn pouted, sitting up and pulling her knees against her heavy chest, adjusting the leather laces of her corset with an aggrieved childish huff.
"Come on, Morwenna! It isn’t that bad! A little aged rum never killed an honest sailor!"
"That isn’t rum, that’s industrial bilge water!" Morwenna bellowed from ten paces away, violently fanning the air with Tidebringer’s flat.
Aki blinked rapidly, her small boots pattering against the flagstones as she nervously approached Silas’s side.
She looked between the bruised disheveled crimson-haired beauty and the furious pirate queen with her head tilting in bewilderment.
"Um... Morwenna?" Aki asked softly, pointing a hesitant finger toward the newcomer. "What... what exactly is your relationship with this woman?"
Morwenna crossed her arms tightly over her chest, scowling fiercely.
"We were alli—"

"We were friends!" Elowynn cut in brightly, scrambling to her feet and dusting off the seat of her dark leather shorts, completely ignoring the fact that she was missing two teeth and dripping blood onto her cleavage.
A dazzling shameless smile split her small face.

"Sisters-in-arms! Comrades of the open brine! We plundered the western straits together, traded blows beneath the blood moons, and swore eternal rivalry! Until... well, until she went and got herself murdered by those pompous Corporate bastards five centuries ago!"

"Don’t listen to a single word falling out of that shameless mouth!" Morwenna snapped, pointing Tidebringer’s tip straight at Elowynn’s nose. "Believe nothing until you verify it with your own eyes! I didn’t die! The fleet went down, but I survived through spite, which is why I’m standing right here in one piece and we were not sisters-in-arms, you lying wretch! You spent three decades trying to set my rudder on fire!"
"Details, details!" Elowynn laughed, her amethyst eyes sparkling with manic unbridled relief.

She took a step forward, her hands clapping together in delight. "Who cares about the old skirmishes?! You’re alive! I’m here! We’re serving under the same Lord! The seas of this realm won’t know what hit them once the two of—"
"Wait, wait," Aki interrupted, stepping between them with her hands raised in a small, authoritative barrier. "Excuse me, Miss Elowynn... You aren’t serving under Morwenna’s Lord. I am your Lord..."
Elowynn stopped dead in her tracks as she looked down at Aki.
She looked at the long flowing blue hair, the brilliant, youthful blue eyes, and the oversized pastel pink Keep looming in the background behind the quartz terrace.
She blinked once and twice.
"You...?" Elowynn murmured, her brow furrowing in genuine, drunken confusion.

"Yes, me," Aki nodded with solemn dignity, puffing her chest out slightly. "This place is known as Vineworld, or more specifically, Aki’s Wonderland... It is an official Vassal Territory tied directly to the High Seat of Blessed Land. The main territory, and Morwenna’s Lord, is him."
Aki turned her small hand, gesturing toward Silas.
Elowynn’s eyes followed the gesture, and the lingering alcohol fog in her skull seemed to evaporate in a fraction of a second.
Silas stood leaning casually against the balustrade.
The afternoon wind ruffled his dark untamed bangs, once again framing a sharp composed jawline and a pair of deep blue eyes, ringed with gold, that observed her with quiet amused calculation.
A sudden breathless heat rushed straight from Elowynn’s collarbones down into her stomach again.
’Again...?’
Her posture shifted instantly.
The drunken slouch vanished, replaced by the effortless serpentine grace of a born seductress.

She pushed her chest forward, letting her voluminous bust strain against the worn leather of her coat with her lips parting into a sultry half-lidded pout as she ran a delicate calloused finger down the side of her neck, right over the tiny beauty mark beneath her left eye.

"Well now..." Elowynn purred, her voice dropping into a smoky melodic tone that dripped with promise. "A vassal territory, you say and you’re the master of the main house, handsome? Tell me... does the High Lord accept private late-night audiences to inspect the... unique talents of newly arrived pirates? Because I assure you, my flexibility on the deck is entirely unmat—"
Silas didn’t blink, flush, or even shift his weight.
He casually walked straight through her carefully rehearsed aura of lethal temptation, stepping right up to the edge of the altar.
Without a word of acknowledgment for her shameless proposition, Silas extended a firm calloused right hand.

"Welcome to the family, Elowynn," Silas said, his voice calm and steady, utterly grounding. "I’m Silas Graves... Be a good Hero for Aki. She’s young, she’s building this territory from scratch, and she’s going to need someone with your naval instincts and combat awareness to help her achieve everything she wants in this life."
Elowynn froze.
Her outstretched finger hovered in the air and her prepared arsenal of dirty quips and pirate innuendos died in the back of her throat.
She looked down at his broad warm hand.
Slowly, she slipped her own fingers into his grasp and his grip was solid, lacking any sort of hesitation or grease, treating her with the clean unadorned respect of a sovereign greeting an ally.
Before she could recover her swagger, Silas leaned in slightly with a teasing conspiratorial smirk dancing in his gold-ringed blue eyes.

"By the way," Silas murmured in a low whisper, "since you two have such a long history... you wouldn’t happen to have any embarrassing gossip about Morwenna’s former life, would you? Did she always shout at clouds, or is that a recent development?"
THUD!

paragraphs: The flat of Morwenna’s Tidebringer slammed squarely into Silas’s lower back.
"Ow—!" Silas grunted, arching forward with a grimace.
"Keep your damn ears shut, Captain!" Morwenna snarled, grabbing Silas by the back of his charcoal tunic and aggressively hauling him away from the altar like an unruly hound.
Her face was flushed a dark dangerous crimson with her teeth gritted as she shoved him down the stone steps.

"Don’t spend another second around this shameless hussy! She’s a degenerate who spends half her life seducing merchants and the other half sleeping off barrel-wine... If you let her poison your head, I’ll throw your dinner into the river!"
"Hey, I was just asking for historical context!" Silas laughed, raising his hands in mock surrender as she physically pushed him toward the gate.

"Historical context my ass!" Morwenna yelled, casting a panicked, mortified glare over her shoulder toward Elowynn. "Don’t you dare ruin my reputation in his head, you little vixen! If you breathe a single word about the kraken festival, I’ll feed you your own cutlasses!"
Standing by the perimeter, Eluned covered her mouth with a delicate silk sleeve, her emerald eyes dancing with pure delight.

"I shall return shortly, Aki dear," Eluned chimed gracefully, stepping down from the grass to join Silas’s side. "A devoted wife must see her Hubby safely off to the transit gates, lest stray women attempt to stow away in his coat pockets."
Aki nodded with a bright understanding smile.
"Of course, Lady Eluned! Take your time!"

Aeliana fell into step beside them, her regal blond composure intact, though her pointed ears twitched with quiet amusement as Silas continued to bicker with Morwenna all the way to the marble transit dais.
HUUUUUUUUUM!
The emerald and silver spatial runes on the platform flared with brilliant light.

The pillar of dimensional displacement roared upward, swallowing Silas, Eluned, Morwenna, and Aeliana in an eye-blink, leaving behind only the gentle rustle of starlight-lilies in the mountain breeze.
Aki stood in place, watching the fading particles of light with a soft affectionate warmth lingering in her chest.
BURRRRRRRRRP!
A thunderous earth-shaking belch tore through the quiet clearing, rattling the quartz balustrades.
Thor floated down from the boughs of a weeping willow, wiping a streak of boar grease from her chin with the back of her wrist.
She tossed her empty wooden flagon toward a patch of soft clover, rolling her broad, muscular shoulders with an eager grin.

"Well, Silas has gone to run his errands," Thor boomed, her golden hair catching the lavender twilight. "Come on, little rabbit. Let’s head inside that ridiculous pink barn of yours... It’s time I taught you how to properly circulate and hone that energy before you blow your other eyeball out of its socket."
Aki pouted, crossing her small arms defensively. "It isn’t a pink barn! It’s a palace meant for a Lord!"
Still, she didn’t argue.
Her right eye still carried a faint dull throb from the backlash of her earlier Destruction blast, and she knew the thunder goddess’s guidance was invaluable.
She turned back toward the quartz altar, waving her hand toward the two Heroes.
"Ther’Abella! Elowynn! Follow us inside, please. I’ll explain the territory and assign your quarters... but honestly, my legs are completely exhausted right now, so let’s take it slow."
Elowynn stood frozen in place on the altar, her hand still raised where Silas had shaken it.
The warmth of his calloused palm seemed to burn into her skin like a brand.
She slowly curled her fingers into a tight fist, pressing it against her heart with her breath catching in her throat as a dazzling unhinged grin spread across her lips.
"Yes, my Lord," Elowynn answered softly, her voice barely carrying over the wind.
Her mind was spinning, completely untethered from the lingering alcohol.
’I... I’ve fallen in love,’ she thought, a dizzying electric shudder running straight down her spine.
It was ridiculous and it was insane.
She had sailed the treacherous seas for five hundred years, dodging people and rejecting prince-consorts without batting an eyelash.
But that man... the quiet certainty in his eyes, the casual way he looked right through her practiced seduction, the unadorned strength humming in his bones... he was magnificent.

’And Morwenna wants him too,’ she realized, her grin widening into something fiercely competitive. ’Her face was practically on fire when she shoved him away... She likes him... She’s terrified of him finding out about her past because she wants him to look at her as a woman.’
A low purring chuckle rumbled in Elowynn’s throat.
’Well then, old friend... it looks like we’re back in the ring. If there’s one battlefield where I know I won’t lose to a rough-edged pirate queen, it’s this body.’
Her hands brushed down her narrow waist, tracing the dangerous heavy curves of her hips.
Her body, her fox-like smile, her effortless allure... Those were the weapons that had brought whole taverns of cutthroats to their knees.
Yet... as the thought formed, a tiny shadow of doubt flickered behind her purple eyes.
’Wait...’
Silas hadn’t even looked down at her chest.
When she had pressed her bust forward, he had simply looked straight into her eyes, asked her to protect Aki, and shook her hand like a trusted soldier.
’If he doesn’t care about curves... what else do I even have?’ she thought, her brow furrowing in genuine panic. ’He didn’t flinch! What kind of weird, terrifying man is he?!’
SHREEEEEK!
A blinding high-frequency lance of crystallized starlight tore through the air, aimed directly at her temple.
Elowynn’s combat instincts, honed over centuries of naval slaughter, flared instantly.

Her body moved on pure muscle memory as she snapped her head back by three inches, feeling the superheated starlight singe the loose hairs of her bangs with her right arm whipping out to parry the shaft with the heavy brass plate of her remaining vambrace.
CLANG!
The deflection threw off the trajectory with the starlight spear burying itself into the quartz terrace and detonating into a shower of white sparks.
Elowynn spun, baring her teeth.
"What the hell was that for?!"
Standing five paces away was Ther’Abella.
The tall silver-armored elf stood in a razor-sharp vanguard stance, her silver hair whipping in the wind, her cold blue eyes burning with pure disgusted hatred.

"Not only do you reek of foul degenerate spirits," Ther’Abella hissed, her voice shaking with righteous fury, "but your eyes are already glazed with lust for that usurper! That profane web of his is already tightening around you! As Lady Aki’s faithful soldier, I will knock his charm out of that rotten skull before you drag this territory into his gutter!"
Elowynn blinked, her jaw slacking in pure bewilderment.
Before she could process the accusation, Ther’Abella moved.
She didn’t bother with spells or another spear.
Her footwork was blindingly fast... It was a displacement of speed that bypassed Elowynn’s depleted Level 1 perception completely!
’She’s fast...!’ Elowynn thought with her stomach dropping.
WHAM!
An armored steel sabaton drove directly into the center of Elowynn’s cheekbone.
BAM! CRUNCH!

The velocity of the kick smashed Elowynn’s face flat against the quartz flagstones for the third time that afternoon, leaving her sprawling in the dirt with stars exploding behind her eyes as she groaned into the gravel.
"Why... does everyone... keep hitting... my face...?"
Ther’Abella lowered her leg, brushing a speck of dust from her greave.
"Clear yet, wretch? Or shall I kick it out of you again?"
Elowynn stared up at the blurry ceiling of sky as the honeyed fog of lust in her head had scattered like startled gulls.
’Okay...’ she thought groggily. ’That actually worked. I hate it.’
FLASH!
The spatial pillar collapsed with a gentle hum, depositing Silas, Eluned, Morwenna, and Aeliana back onto the grand terrace of Blessed Land.
The difference in atmosphere was immediate.
Where Vineworld was bathed in a whimsical lavender starlight, Blessed Land possessed an suffocating grandeur.
"Ah..." Silas sighed, rolling his shoulders and taking a deep lungful of the pristine air. "Nothing beats home."
Footsteps clicked against the flagstones nearby.
A young spearwoman clad in Blessed Land’s dark steel plate passed by the perimeter balustrade, conducting her scheduled patrol.
The moment she spotted Silas, her back straightened into a rigid, textbook salute, her spear butt striking the stone with a crisp clack.
"Greetings, Lord Silas! Welcome back to the Keep!"
Silas smiled warmly, stepping off the dais and walking over to the young guard.
He reached out with an easy casual gesture, patting the top of her leather-trimmed helmet twice.
"Good work on the rounds," Silas said gently.
The spearwoman’s breath caught in her throat.
Her eyes fluttered, her shoulders melting under his touch as a soft helpless purr escaped the back of her throat with her cheeks turning a bright radiant scarlet beneath her visor.
Silas chuckled at her reaction, tilting his head slightly. "Hey, have you seen Aurelia around today?"
A brief pang of quiet guilt stirred in his chest.

’I really haven’t been focusing on her much lately...’ Silas thought, his gaze drifting toward the training grounds in the distance. ’Between the tournament, the World Council negotiations, and managing the vassal territories, I’ve barely spent a new hour with her... Lupina and Morrighan too. Sure, they’re living luxurious peaceful lives in Blessed Land now, but they’re still my Heroes. I need to do better about checking in on them... though for this trip to Central City, I can only bring a very limited team.’
The spearwoman quickly recovered her composure, her eyes shining with eager pride as she delivered her report.

"Aurelia departed two hours ago with the third auxiliary squad, my Lord! They went down into the western thickets for a wild hunt! She seemed extraordinarily happy, laughing and practicing her blade arts before they crossed the perimeter!"
"Hunting, huh? Good. She gets restless when she stays indoors too long from what I know." Silas smiled.
He leaned in slightly, brushing his lips softly against the pale expanse of the girl’s forehead in a gentle affectionate kiss.
"Thanks for the update," Silas said, stepping back with a warm wink and the guard froze completely.
Her pupils dilated to the size of saucers.
Her hands began to tremble around the shaft of her spear, a deep incandescent crimson rushing across her face all the way to her collarbones.
"I... I am never washing this forehead again," the girl whispered in a dazed religious trance, clutching her brow with trembling fingers. "Never... For the rest of my natural life."
Silas burst out laughing.
"Don’t be ridiculous. You’ll smell terrible. Besides, if you ever want more forehead kisses, my mouth isn’t going anywhere... Keep up the good work on patrol."

The spearwoman let out a high-pitched, mortified squeak, turned on her heels, and practically sprinted down the flagstone avenue as fast as her armored boots could carry her, leaving behind a faint trail of dust.
Standing behind Silas, the temperature abruptly dropped twenty degrees.
Morwenna’s stormy gray eyes were narrowed into razor-thin slits of unbridled fury.
Eluned’s sweet ethereal smile had locked into an icy terrifying mask, her emerald eyes pulsing with wood-mana that caused the weeds between the stone slabs to twist into thorny barbs.
Both women were glaring at his lower back with an intense synchronized urge to plant their steel-capped boots squarely into his rear end and launch him outside the walls.

"You really can’t help yourself, can you?" Morwenna growled, her knuckles whitening around Tidebringer’s hilt. "Flirting with the perimeter guards in broad daylight? Do you have no shame whatsoever, Captain?!"
Silas turned around, completely unfazed by their homicidal glares, holding his hands up with an innocent unbothered grin.
"Alright, that’s enough standing around," Silas said, seamlessly steering the conversation.
He looked at Morwenna and Aeliana. "Morwenna, Aeli, go down to the Foundry and finalize your gear preparations... Pack light and ensure you have enough things... We leave for Central City shortly."
Morwenna crossed her arms, her jaw setting with sharp suspicion. "And what are you doing?"
"I have some private business to handle with Eluned first," Silas replied smoothly. "We’ll meet you at the central transit node in an hour."
Morwenna shot Eluned a sharp jealous glare with her lips pressing into a thin line.
She clearly wanted to object, but Silas’s tone had shifted into his commanding one.
With a frustrated huff, she turned on her heel and stomped toward the Warlord Foundry, Aeliana offering a graceful bow before gliding after her.
Once they were out of earshot, Silas turned back toward the Keep’s grand mahogany doors, gesturing for Eluned to follow.

sentences.text: The flat of Morwenna’s Tidebringer slammed squarely into Silas’s lower back.
"Ow—!" Silas grunted, arching forward with a grimace.
"Keep your damn ears shut, Captain!" Morwenna snarled, grabbing Silas by the back of his charcoal tunic and aggressively hauling him away from the altar like an unruly hound.
Her face was flushed a dark dangerous crimson with her teeth gritted as she shoved him down the stone steps.
"Don’t spend another second around this shameless hussy!
She’s a degenerate who spends half her life seducing merchants and the other half sleeping off barrel-wine...
If you let her poison your head, I’ll throw your dinner into the river!"
"Hey, I was just asking for historical context!" Silas laughed, raising his hands in mock surrender as she physically pushed him toward the gate.
"Historical context my ass!" Morwenna yelled, casting a panicked, mortified glare over her shoulder toward Elowynn.
"Don’t you dare ruin my reputation in his head, you little vixen!
If you breathe a single word about the kraken festival, I’ll feed you your own cutlasses!"

"A devoted wife must see her Hubby safely off to the transit gates, lest stray women attempt to stow away in his coat pockets."
Aki nodded with a bright understanding smile.
"Of course, Lady Eluned!
Take your time!"

Aeliana fell into step beside them, her regal blond composure intact, though her pointed ears twitched with quiet amusement as Silas continued to bicker with Morwenna all the way to the marble transit dais.
HUUUUUUUUUM!
The emerald and silver spatial runes on the platform flared with brilliant light.

The pillar of dimensional displacement roared upward, swallowing Silas, Eluned, Morwenna, and Aeliana in an eye-blink, leaving behind only the gentle rustle of starlight-lilies in the mountain breeze.
Aki stood in place, watching the fading particles of light with a soft affectionate warmth lingering in her chest.
BURRRRRRRRRP!
A thunderous earth-shaking belch tore through the quiet clearing, rattling the quartz balustrades.
Thor floated down from the boughs of a weeping willow, wiping a streak of boar grease from her chin with the back of her wrist.
She tossed her empty wooden flagon toward a patch of soft clover, rolling her broad, muscular shoulders with an eager grin.
"Well, Silas has gone to run his errands," Thor boomed, her golden hair catching the lavender twilight.
"Come on, little rabbit.
Let’s head inside that ridiculous pink barn of yours...
It’s time I taught you how to properly circulate and hone that energy before you blow your other eyeball out of its socket."
Aki pouted, crossing her small arms defensively.
"It isn’t a pink barn!
It’s a palace meant for a Lord!"
Still, she didn’t argue.
Her right eye still carried a faint dull throb from the backlash of her earlier Destruction blast, and she knew the thunder goddess’s guidance was invaluable.
She turned back toward the quartz altar, waving her hand toward the two Heroes.
"Ther’Abella!
Elowynn!
Follow us inside, please.
I’ll explain the territory and assign your quarters... but honestly, my legs are completely exhausted right now, so let’s take it slow."
Elowynn stood frozen in place on the altar, her hand still raised where Silas had shaken it.
The warmth of his calloused palm seemed to burn into her skin like a brand.
She slowly curled her fingers into a tight fist, pressing it against her heart with her breath catching in her throat as a dazzling unhinged grin spread across her lips.
"Yes, my Lord," Elowynn answered softly, her voice barely carrying over the wind.
Her mind was spinning, completely untethered from the lingering alcohol.
I’ve fallen in love,’ she thought, a dizzying electric shudder running straight down her spine.
It was ridiculous and it was insane.
She had sailed the treacherous seas for five hundred years, dodging people and rejecting prince-consorts without batting an eyelash.
But that man... the quiet certainty in his eyes, the casual way he looked right through her practiced seduction, the unadorned strength humming in his bones... he was magnificent.
’And Morwenna wants him too,’ she realized, her grin widening into something fiercely competitive. ’Her face was practically on fire when she shoved him away...
She likes him...
She’s terrified of him finding out about her past because she wants him to look at her as a woman.’
A low purring chuckle rumbled in Elowynn’s throat.
’Well then, old friend... it looks like we’re back in the ring.
If there’s one battlefield where I know I won’t lose to a rough-edged pirate queen, it’s this body.’
Her hands brushed down her narrow waist, tracing the dangerous heavy curves of her hips.
Her body, her fox-like smile, her effortless allure...
Those were the weapons that had brought whole taverns of cutthroats to their knees.
Yet... as the thought formed, a tiny shadow of doubt flickered behind her purple eyes.
’Wait...’
Silas hadn’t even looked down at her chest.
When she had pressed her bust forward, he had simply looked straight into her eyes, asked her to protect Aki, and shook her hand like a trusted soldier.
’If he doesn’t care about curves... what else do I even have?’ she thought, her brow furrowing in genuine panic. ’He didn’t flinch!
What kind of weird, terrifying man is he?!’
SHREEEEEK!
A blinding high-frequency lance of crystallized starlight tore through the air, aimed directly at her temple.
Elowynn’s combat instincts, honed over centuries of naval slaughter, flared instantly.

Her body moved on pure muscle memory as she snapped her head back by three inches, feeling the superheated starlight singe the loose hairs of her bangs with her right arm whipping out to parry the shaft with the heavy brass plate of her remaining vambrace.
CLANG!
The deflection threw off the trajectory with the starlight spear burying itself into the quartz terrace and detonating into a shower of white sparks.
Elowynn spun, baring her teeth.
"What the hell was that for?!"
Standing five paces away was Ther’Abella.
The tall silver-armored elf stood in a razor-sharp vanguard stance, her silver hair whipping in the wind, her cold blue eyes burning with pure disgusted hatred.
"Not only do you reek of foul degenerate spirits," Ther’Abella hissed, her voice shaking with righteous fury, "but your eyes are already glazed with lust for that usurper!
That profane web of his is already tightening around you!
As Lady Aki’s faithful soldier, I will knock his charm out of that rotten skull before you drag this territory into his gutter!"
Elowynn blinked, her jaw slacking in pure bewilderment.
Before she could process the accusation, Ther’Abella moved.
She didn’t bother with spells or another spear.
Her footwork was blindingly fast...
It was a displacement of speed that bypassed Elowynn’s depleted Level 1 perception completely!
’She’s fast...!’ Elowynn thought with her stomach dropping.
WHAM!
An armored steel sabaton drove directly into the center of Elowynn’s cheekbone.
BAM!
CRUNCH!

The velocity of the kick smashed Elowynn’s face flat against the quartz flagstones for the third time that afternoon, leaving her sprawling in the dirt with stars exploding behind her eyes as she groaned into the gravel.
"Why... does everyone... keep hitting... my face...?"
Ther’Abella lowered her leg, brushing a speck of dust from her greave.
"Clear yet, wretch?
Or shall I kick it out of you again?"
Elowynn stared up at the blurry ceiling of sky as the honeyed fog of lust in her head had scattered like startled gulls.
’Okay...’ she thought groggily. ’That actually worked.
I hate it.’
FLASH!
The spatial pillar collapsed with a gentle hum, depositing Silas, Eluned, Morwenna, and Aeliana back onto the grand terrace of Blessed Land.
The difference in atmosphere was immediate.
Where Vineworld was bathed in a whimsical lavender starlight, Blessed Land possessed an suffocating grandeur.
"Ah..." Silas sighed, rolling his shoulders and taking a deep lungful of the pristine air.

Footsteps clicked against the flagstones nearby.

chapters.title: Chapter 681: Rika’s New Resolve [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: As they ascended the wide sunlit marble staircase toward the residential quarters, Eluned’s icy demeanor vanished instantly.
She closed the distance, wrapping her slender arms around Silas’s bicep, pressing her soft bust firmly against his side as a wicked playful purr rumbled in her throat.

"Oh, my darling..." Eluned whispered, her breath warm against his ear, her voice dripping with shameless perverted delight. "A private matter, you say? Just the two of us behind locked doors before your long journey? Don’t tell me... you simply couldn’t bear to depart for Central City without thoroughly dicking your lawful wife down first...? You want to leave your seed within me so I won’t be lonely, don’t you~?"
Silas sighed, rolling his eyes as he gently nudged her forehead with his knuckles.
"Get your mind out of the gutter, Elu... That’s not what this is about."
Eluned paused, blinking up at him in surprise.
"It isn’t?"
"No," Silas said, his expression sobering as they reached the quiet corridor of the third floor. "I need your help with Rika."
The playful mockery drained from Eluned’s face, replaced instantly by solemn quiet understanding.
"Ah..." Eluned murmured, her gaze dropping toward the closed oak door at the far end of the hallway. "Rika..."
"She hasn’t left her quarters in days, has she?" Silas asked softly, stopping outside the threshold.

"No," Eluned sighed, shaking her head with genuine sorrow. "She takes her meals when Kadi leave them, but she speaks to no one... She sits in the dark for hours. I can feel the resonance of her soul through the air roots, Silas. She... she views herself as less than nothing, a broken relic that brings no honor to your Keep."
Silas looked down at his own hand, his jaw tightening with resolve.
"That’s exactly what we’re going to fix," Silas said firmly. "I have something for her... Something that will change everything..."
Inside the quiet room, the heavy velvet drapes were pulled tight, allowing only a sliver of golden afternoon light to cut across the dark cedar floorboards.
Sitting curled up on a low cushions in the corner was Rika.
The Goddess of Beasts, High Warden of the Primeval Brood, looked devastatingly small.
Her wild midnight-black hair hung in tangled neglected waves over her pale fragile shoulders.
Her vivid emerald eyes, which had once commanded the terrifying legions of the fanged courts, were dull and fixed blankly on an untouched porcelain plate resting on the low table before her.
A thick savory steak of roast dire-boar sat cold on the dish with its juices looking congealed as it had been ignored.
’I’m just freeloading...’
The bitter suffocating thought turned in Rika’s chest like a rusty dagger.
Every single bite of food she took in this magnificent Keep felt like stolen bread.
Every breath of pristine air from the territory felt like an unearned luxury.

’Lord Silas is far too kind...’ she thought, her small porcelain-pale hands gripping the fabric of her skirt until her knuckles turned bone-white. ’He is too noble, too generous for a useless pathetic wretch like me...’

She remembered the grand sweeping promises she had made when he had first arrived to save her, how she had spoken of forging invincible divine mounts, of weaving beast contracts that would allow his armies to tear down the gates of empires.
She had stood tall, claiming the authority of the fanged courts, promising him the dominance of the wild blood.
And what had she delivered?
...Nothing... Absolutely nothing...
Her vitality was drained to the dregs, a single clumsy kick from a common soldier would bruise her ribs and leave her bedridden for days.

Her core had a massive ceiling, but without an active bonded beast to anchor her pathways, every single one of her divine authorities, her Fang Authority, her Beast Contract Weaving, and everything else, was completely sealed.
She was an empty vessel, a weapon without an edge.

’So useless,’ she tortured herself with tears welling hot and silent at the corners of her green eyes. ’He summons soldiers, heroes, builders, craftspeople... people who can bleed for him, fight for him, build his dominion with their own hands but he never summons for me... He never calls my name... Because he knows...’
Her throat tightened with raw agonizing shame.
’What can I even offer him?’
Did he want her body? Was that what she had been reduced to? If she stripped her robes and offered herself to his bed, would that be enough to pay for her keep?
’What makes me any different from a common prostitute then...?’ she cried internally, burying her face into her knees with her frame shaking in quiet suppressed sobs.

’Stop it,’ she scolded herself, scrubbing her cheek with the heel of her hand. ’Lord Silas has never once looked at me like that. He tucked a blanket around me and fed me stew with his own hands. He’s kind... he’s just kinder than I deserve.’
And the terror ran deeper still.
Even if a beast were brought before her, the cold paralyzing dread in her marrow screamed at her to run.
What if she failed the bond? What if the beast rejected her broken soul? What if the same catastrophic severance that had shattered her divine court in the ancient era happened all over again?
’Would I just be weak forever...? A laughingstock who drags his name into the mud...?’
CREAK!
The heavy oak door swung open with a soft gentle click and Rika flinched violently.
She scrambled off the cushion, her knees hitting the hard wood as she dropped flat onto the floor, pressing her forehead against the cedar planks in desperate trembling submission.

"L-Lord Silas!" she cried, her voice cracking with hysterical terror, hot tears spilling freely across her pale cheeks onto the wood. "P-Please! Please don’t cast me out! I know... I know I am useless! I know I eat your food and provide nothing in return! I will scrub the stables! I will wash the armor in the courtyards! I will serve the lowest scullery maids! J-Just please... don’t discard me into the rifts... I have nowhere else to go...!"
"Rika, Stop..."
The voice wasn’t cold or harsh.
Before she could beg again, a pair of warm strong hands slipped beneath her arms, gently but firmly lifting her off the cold wood.
Silas knelt down directly on the floor in front of her, ignoring the dust with his gold-ringed blue eyes level with hers.
Behind him, Eluned stepped into the room, softly closing the door, her emerald eyes watching the broken beast goddess with infinite maternal sorrow.
Silas reached up with his thumb, gently wiping the tears from beneath Rika’s emerald eyes.

"Take a breath," Silas said softly, his voice carrying a comforting warmth that cut straight through her panic. "Look at me... Nobody is casting you out. Nobody is making you scrub stables... You are a Hero of Blessed Land, Rika. My Hero and I don’t abandon my people."
’His hands are so warm...’ Rika thought, hardly daring to breathe. ’He said I’m his Hero. He said it like it was simple, like it was true.’
Rika trembled, her small chest hitching as she looked into his steady, unblinking blue eyes.
"B-But... my Lord... I have no beasts. Without a bond, my authorities are dead. I am just... dead weight..."
"Then we get you a beast," Silas said simply.
Rika blinked through her tears, sniffing pathetically.
"W-What kind...? The wild drakes in the basin... my soul cannot bond with such low-tier vermin, It would fracture my meridians..."
Silas smiled... it was a slow confident grin.
"Have you ever heard of a Phoenix before?"
Rika froze as the air in the room seemed to vanish.

’A... Phoenix...?’ Rika’s thoughts stalled out, her dazed mind struggling to process the word. ’The Primordial Phoenix? The legendary apex avian of the higher celestial seas? The supreme guardian of ancient civilizations, whose very feathers cycle physical annihilation into immortal rebirth...?’
She let out a faint disbelieving whimper.
"My Lord... those are mythic legends from the Old Era. Their line was extinguished in the celestial wars. Where... where in all the infinite realms could you ever find a—"
FWIP!
Silas reached into his primary spatial inventory.
With a soft metallic thud, a massive object materialized between them, resting upon a folded cloth of velvet.
Rika’s breath stopped... It was an egg.
Standing fourteen inches tall, the size of a massive ostrich egg, it was fashioned entirely of solid unrefined gold.
Rough, overlapping scale-like ridges covered its surface, cold and lifeless to the touch.

It carried no glowing runes and emitted no humming mana, looking for all the world like an ancient piece of unrefined slag, the very "auric slag" the World Council’s foolish alchemists had failed to crack for three decades.

"This is a Phoenix’s Egg," Silas said, resting his hand gently against the golden shell. "The embryonic soul fell into suspended pseudo-death from prolonged starvation of natural power... It cannot hatch in cold lightless places, and it cannot process common elemental fire. It requires a domain saturated with pure concentrated Nature Mana and high-tier vegetative life-force to reignite its embryonic rebirth flame."
He looked straight into Rika’s trembling green eyes, his voice ringing with certainty.

"This is going to be your first contracted beast, Rika and this afternoon, you’re coming with me to Central City... We are going to scour the high markets, the beast sanctuaries, and the exchanges. I am going to ensure that every single beast you bind to your soul from this day forward is state-of-the-art and worthy of the Goddess of Beasts."
A fresh torrential wave of tears broke from Rika’s eyes, but this time, they weren’t tears of terror.
Her hands flew to her mouth with her shoulders shaking violently as a sob of pure overwhelming gratitude tore from her chest.

’He didn’t forget me...’ her soul wept, every broken, neglected corner of her heart flooding with incandescent warmth. ’He didn’t think I was useless... he was waiting. He was searching for something worthy of me...’
Silas picked up the heavy golden egg and turned, offering it to Eluned.
"Elu. Do it."
Eluned stepped forward, her divine emerald eyes glowing with radiant majesty.
She knelt beside them, placing both of her delicate pale palms against the golden ridges of the egg.
Rika watched Eluned’s hands on the shell, her nails digging into her palms.
’What if it hatches, takes one look at me, and just... turns away?’ she thought. ’What if my soul is too cracked for even a newborn to trust?’
Silas’s hand settled on her shoulder feeling warm and steady. He said nothing, and he didn’t need to.
’...No. Lord Silas believes in this and I believe in him.’
VUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!
The world answered her call.

Beneath the floorboards of the Keep, lines of emerald mana thrummed with a deep heartbeat and a crystalline torrent of emerald-green Nature Mana surged through Eluned’s arms, pouring directly into the inert golden shell.
Seconds became a minute, then two, then five...
Sweat beaded on Eluned’s brow and her silver-emerald hair lifted around her in the rising green glow, but her hands never wavered.
"Come on, little one," she whispered to the shell. "Wake up... She needs you!"
The cold metal began to warm.
The dull lifeless gold suddenly ignited with brilliant inner luminescence.
CRACK!
A hair-thin fissure appeared along the central ridge.
From within the fracture, a blinding razor-sharp ray of pure golden flame shot outward, illuminating the shadowed room in a sea of warm celestial light.
CRACK-CRACK-SHATTER!
The shell fractured like a blooming lotus.
The ancient golden shards dissolved into pure molten light, and from the heart of the radiance, a magnificent creature emerged.
It was small... scarcely larger than a falcon, but its presence was colossal.
Its feathers were woven from pure, liquid solar fire, shifting between incandescent gold and deep, radiant ruby.
Its eyes were two gleaming specks of starlight, and its long elegant tail feathers trailed ribbons of living embers that drifted through the air without burning the cedar floor.
The newborn Phoenix tilted its head, letting out a crystalline bell-like trill that washed over the room like a divine blessing.
"Creeeee~"
It didn’t look at Silas and it didn’t look at Eluned either.
...Its starlit eyes locked squarely onto Rika.
Rika gasped, her chest seizing.
Deep within her dormant soul-seat, an instinctual authority broke free from its chains.
’My authority...’
Three shimmering translucent chains woven from emerald light and wild primeval blood burst from Rika’s chest...
They didn’t strike with violent force, they drifted through the air like ribbons of silk, wrapping softly and tenderly around the Phoenix’s wings and chest.
BZZZZZZZZT!
The moment the bond locked into place, the embryonic phoenix let out a joyful soaring cry.
It unfolded its blazing wings and glided forward, dissolving into a stream of pure golden celestial energy that poured directly into Rika’s open heart!
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A cataclysmic eruption of golden divine mana detonated from Rika’s frame.
The stagnant drained weakness in her marrow was violently swept away, replaced by the roaring infinite vitality of a Primordial Beast.
Her pale skin flushed with radiant divine color as her tangled black hair lifted, floating in the mana storm like silk threads, and her emerald eyes ignited with the majesty of the Primeval Brood.
She fell forward, burying her face into Silas’s knees while clutching the fabric of his trousers with trembling reverent hands.
"Thank you..." she wept, her voice trembling with a devotion that transcended life and death. "Thank you... thank you so much, my Master... my Lord... my everything..."
The golden light surged, swallowing her vision and the room around her.
