"She hasn’t left her quarters in days, has she?" Silas asked softly, stopping outside the threshold.
"No," Eluned sighed, shaking her head with genuine sorrow.
"She takes her meals when Kadi leave them, but she speaks to no one...
She sits in the dark for hours.
I can feel the resonance of her soul through the air roots, Silas.
She... she views herself as less than nothing, a broken relic that brings no honor to your Keep."
Silas looked down at his own hand, his jaw tightening with resolve.
"That’s exactly what we’re going to fix," Silas said firmly.
"I have something for her...
Something that will change everything..."
Inside the quiet room, the heavy velvet drapes were pulled tight, allowing only a sliver of golden afternoon light to cut across the dark cedar floorboards.
Sitting curled up on a low cushions in the corner was Rika.
The Goddess of Beasts, High Warden of the Primeval Brood, looked devastatingly small.
Her wild midnight-black hair hung in tangled neglected waves over her pale fragile shoulders.
Her vivid emerald eyes, which had once commanded the terrifying legions of the fanged courts, were dull and fixed blankly on an untouched porcelain plate resting on the low table before her.
A thick savory steak of roast dire-boar sat cold on the dish with its juices looking congealed as it had been ignored.
’I’m just freeloading...’
The bitter suffocating thought turned in Rika’s chest like a rusty dagger.
Every single bite of food she took in this magnificent Keep felt like stolen bread.
Every breath of pristine air from the territory felt like an unearned luxury.

’Lord Silas is far too kind...’ she thought, her small porcelain-pale hands gripping the fabric of her skirt until her knuckles turned bone-white. ’He is too noble, too generous for a useless pathetic wretch like me...’

She remembered the grand sweeping promises she had made when he had first arrived to save her, how she had spoken of forging invincible divine mounts, of weaving beast contracts that would allow his armies to tear down the gates of empires.
She had stood tall, claiming the authority of the fanged courts, promising him the dominance of the wild blood.
And what had she delivered?
...Nothing...
Absolutely nothing...
Her vitality was drained to the dregs, a single clumsy kick from a common soldier would bruise her ribs and leave her bedridden for days.

Her core had a massive ceiling, but without an active bonded beast to anchor her pathways, every single one of her divine authorities, her Fang Authority, her Beast Contract Weaving, and everything else, was completely sealed.
She was an empty vessel, a weapon without an edge.

’So useless,’ she tortured herself with tears welling hot and silent at the corners of her green eyes. ’He summons soldiers, heroes, builders, craftspeople... people who can bleed for him, fight for him, build his dominion with their own hands but he never summons for me...
He never calls my name...
Because he knows...’
Her throat tightened with raw agonizing shame.
’What can I even offer him?’
Did he want her body?
Was that what she had been reduced to?
If she stripped her robes and offered herself to his bed, would that be enough to pay for her keep?
’What makes me any different from a common prostitute then...?’ she cried internally, burying her face into her knees with her frame shaking in quiet suppressed sobs.
’Stop it,’ she scolded herself, scrubbing her cheek with the heel of her hand. ’Lord Silas has never once looked at me like that.
He tucked a blanket around me and fed me stew with his own hands.
He’s kind... he’s just kinder than I deserve.’
And the terror ran deeper still.
Even if a beast were brought before her, the cold paralyzing dread in her marrow screamed at her to run.
What if she failed the bond?
What if the beast rejected her broken soul?
What if the same catastrophic severance that had shattered her divine court in the ancient era happened all over again?
’Would I just be weak forever...?
A laughingstock who drags his name into the mud...?’
CREAK!
The heavy oak door swung open with a soft gentle click and Rika flinched violently.
She scrambled off the cushion, her knees hitting the hard wood as she dropped flat onto the floor, pressing her forehead against the cedar planks in desperate trembling submission.
"L-Lord Silas!" she cried, her voice cracking with hysterical terror, hot tears spilling freely across her pale cheeks onto the wood.
"P-Please!
Please don’t cast me out!
I know...
I know I am useless!
I know I eat your food and provide nothing in return!
I will scrub the stables!
I will wash the armor in the courtyards!
I will serve the lowest scullery maids!
J-Just please... don’t discard me into the rifts...
I have nowhere else to go...!"
"Rika, Stop..."
The voice wasn’t cold or harsh.
Before she could beg again, a pair of warm strong hands slipped beneath her arms, gently but firmly lifting her off the cold wood.
Silas knelt down directly on the floor in front of her, ignoring the dust with his gold-ringed blue eyes level with hers.
Behind him, Eluned stepped into the room, softly closing the door, her emerald eyes watching the broken beast goddess with infinite maternal sorrow.
Silas reached up with his thumb, gently wiping the tears from beneath Rika’s emerald eyes.
"Take a breath," Silas said softly, his voice carrying a comforting warmth that cut straight through her panic.
"Look at me...
Nobody is casting you out.
Nobody is making you scrub stables...
You are a Hero of Blessed Land, Rika.
My Hero and I don’t abandon my people."
’His hands are so warm...’ Rika thought, hardly daring to breathe. ’He said I’m his Hero.
He said it like it was simple, like it was true.’
Rika trembled, her small chest hitching as she looked into his steady, unblinking blue eyes.
"B-But... my Lord...
I have no beasts.
Without a bond, my authorities are dead.
I am just... dead weight..."
"Then we get you a beast," Silas said simply.
Rika blinked through her tears, sniffing pathetically.
"W-What kind...?
The wild drakes in the basin... my soul cannot bond with such low-tier vermin, It would fracture my meridians..."
Silas smiled... it was a slow confident grin.
"Have you ever heard of a Phoenix before?"
Rika froze as the air in the room seemed to vanish.
Phoenix...?’ Rika’s thoughts stalled out, her dazed mind struggling to process the word. ’The Primordial Phoenix?
The legendary apex avian of the higher celestial seas?
The supreme guardian of ancient civilizations, whose very feathers cycle physical annihilation into immortal rebirth...?’
She let out a faint disbelieving whimper.
"My Lord... those are mythic legends from the Old Era.
Their line was extinguished in the celestial wars.
Where... where in all the infinite realms could you ever find a—"
FWIP!
Silas reached into his primary spatial inventory.
With a soft metallic thud, a massive object materialized between them, resting upon a folded cloth of velvet.
Rika’s breath stopped...
It was an egg.
Standing fourteen inches tall, the size of a massive ostrich egg, it was fashioned entirely of solid unrefined gold.
Rough, overlapping scale-like ridges covered its surface, cold and lifeless to the touch.

It carried no glowing runes and emitted no humming mana, looking for all the world like an ancient piece of unrefined slag, the very "auric slag" the World Council’s foolish alchemists had failed to crack for three decades.
"This is a Phoenix’s Egg," Silas said, resting his hand gently against the golden shell.
"The embryonic soul fell into suspended pseudo-death from prolonged starvation of natural power...
It cannot hatch in cold lightless places, and it cannot process common elemental fire.
It requires a domain saturated with pure concentrated Nature Mana and high-tier vegetative life-force to reignite its embryonic rebirth flame."
He looked straight into Rika’s trembling green eyes, his voice ringing with certainty.
"This is going to be your first contracted beast, Rika and this afternoon, you’re coming with me to Central City...
We are going to scour the high markets, the beast sanctuaries, and the exchanges.
I am going to ensure that every single beast you bind to your soul from this day forward is state-of-the-art and worthy of the Goddess of Beasts."
A fresh torrential wave of tears broke from Rika’s eyes, but this time, they weren’t tears of terror.
Her hands flew to her mouth with her shoulders shaking violently as a sob of pure overwhelming gratitude tore from her chest.
’He didn’t forget me...’ her soul wept, every broken, neglected corner of her heart flooding with incandescent warmth. ’He didn’t think I was useless... he was waiting.
He was searching for something worthy of me...’
Silas picked up the heavy golden egg and turned, offering it to Eluned.
"Elu.
Do it."
Eluned stepped forward, her divine emerald eyes glowing with radiant majesty.
She knelt beside them, placing both of her delicate pale palms against the golden ridges of the egg.
Rika watched Eluned’s hands on the shell, her nails digging into her palms.
’What if it hatches, takes one look at me, and just... turns away?’ she thought. ’What if my soul is too cracked for even a newborn to trust?’
Silas’s hand settled on her shoulder feeling warm and steady.
He said nothing, and he didn’t need to.
Lord Silas believes in this and I believe in him.’
VUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!
The world answered her call.

Beneath the floorboards of the Keep, lines of emerald mana thrummed with a deep heartbeat and a crystalline torrent of emerald-green Nature Mana surged through Eluned’s arms, pouring directly into the inert golden shell.
Seconds became a minute, then two, then five...
Sweat beaded on Eluned’s brow and her silver-emerald hair lifted around her in the rising green glow, but her hands never wavered.
"Come on, little one," she whispered to the shell.
"Wake up...
She needs you!"
The cold metal began to warm.
The dull lifeless gold suddenly ignited with brilliant inner luminescence.
CRACK!
A hair-thin fissure appeared along the central ridge.
From within the fracture, a blinding razor-sharp ray of pure golden flame shot outward, illuminating the shadowed room in a sea of warm celestial light.
CRACK-CRACK-SHATTER!
The shell fractured like a blooming lotus.
The ancient golden shards dissolved into pure molten light, and from the heart of the radiance, a magnificent creature emerged.
It was small... scarcely larger than a falcon, but its presence was colossal.
Its feathers were woven from pure, liquid solar fire, shifting between incandescent gold and deep, radiant ruby.
Its eyes were two gleaming specks of starlight, and its long elegant tail feathers trailed ribbons of living embers that drifted through the air without burning the cedar floor.
The newborn Phoenix tilted its head, letting out a crystalline bell-like trill that washed over the room like a divine blessing.
"Creeeee~"
It didn’t look at Silas and it didn’t look at Eluned either.
...Its starlit eyes locked squarely onto Rika.
Rika gasped, her chest seizing.
Deep within her dormant soul-seat, an instinctual authority broke free from its chains.
’My authority...’
Three shimmering translucent chains woven from emerald light and wild primeval blood burst from Rika’s chest...
They didn’t strike with violent force, they drifted through the air like ribbons of silk, wrapping softly and tenderly around the Phoenix’s wings and chest.
BZZZZZZZZT!
The moment the bond locked into place, the embryonic phoenix let out a joyful soaring cry.
It unfolded its blazing wings and glided forward, dissolving into a stream of pure golden celestial energy that poured directly into Rika’s open heart!
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A cataclysmic eruption of golden divine mana detonated from Rika’s frame.
The stagnant drained weakness in her marrow was violently swept away, replaced by the roaring infinite vitality of a Primordial Beast.
Her pale skin flushed with radiant divine color as her tangled black hair lifted, floating in the mana storm like silk threads, and her emerald eyes ignited with the majesty of the Primeval Brood.
She fell forward, burying her face into Silas’s knees while clutching the fabric of his trousers with trembling reverent hands.
"Thank you..." she wept, her voice trembling with a devotion that transcended life and death.
"Thank you... thank you so much, my Master... my Lord... my everything..."
The golden light surged, swallowing her vision and the room around her.

chapters.title: Chapter 682: Soul Space And Pheonix Blessings [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Rika floated in a silent boundless expanse that she recognized with an ache deep inside her marrow.

This was her internal soul realm, the spiritual domain where her divine beast contracts had once anchored themselves like towering pillars of celestial iron, where legendary broods of primordial predators had once roared beneath the banners of the Fanged Courts.
Now, the horizon stretched onward in hollow lifeless gray.
There were no roars and there were no beating wings either... The vast expanse was an empty graveyard of barren cracked stone.
A hollow suffocating sorrow wrapped around her ribs, so heavy it pressed the breath from her lungs.
’I’m sorry...’ she thought, curling her knees to her chest as she drifted in the dead void. ’I’m so sorry... all of you...’
The phantom weight of her lost broods cut into her like broken glass.
If it hadn’t been for that arrogant, ruthless Ice Goddess who had descended upon her place with those forever ice spells, none of this ruin would have ever come to pass.
Her beasts wouldn’t have been butchered, their vital essences stripped away to feed foreign domains, leaving their warden shattered and discarded.
Yet, as she drifted, a quiet almost paradoxical clarity settled over her scattered thoughts.
She had been a deity in that ancient era, yes, but even at her apex, her potential had been hopelessly bottlenecked.
She had cobbled her foundation together from whatever wild drakes and apex earth-beasts she could bind through sheer attrition, clawing her way into the lower echelons of the divine hierarchy.

Deep down, she had always known the bitter truth... no matter how hard she bled, no matter how many centuries she spent refining her beast bloodlines, she would never have stood as an equal beside true battle deities like Thor or the cosmic sovereigns of the celestial pantheons.
...She had reached her ceiling, and the ceiling was fragile.
Then, the void began to shift.
From the bottom of her soul domain, a faint radiant warmth began to bleed upward.
It was not the dull white glow of common mana, but a pure unblemished incandescent shade of gold.
VUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!
The golden light surged like an ocean tide, washing over the cracked barren plains of her soul space.
The moment the light touched her core, several dormant authorities that had been ripped from her pathways slammed back into her soul with the concussive force of a physical battering ram.
Her wild midnight-black hair whipped violently around her shoulders as the divine backlash rippled through her meridians.
’This... this is unbelievable!’ Rika gasped internally, her porcelain-pale skin shivering as warmth flooded every long-dead pathway.

These weren’t even her primary master-level authorities, only her minor passive skills, yet the power coursing through them now was vastly superior to anything she had commanded when she had sat upon her throne at supposedly "full" power!
The purity of the mana, the structural density of the spiritual law... it eclipsed everything she had ever known.
’Your starting beast...’ the realization struck her like lightning, leaving her breathless. ’Your very first bond truly makes all the difference in the world!’
A mortal foundation bound to a lizard yielded a stronger lizard but a soul forged alongside an immortal apex entity of absolute rebirth?... It fundamentally rewrote the structural laws of the vessel.
The golden sea beneath her feet deepened, warming from brilliant yellow into a vibrant molten gradient of burning crimson and rich roaring orange.
The ambient temperature of her soul realm soared, but it didn’t burn her. It felt like stepping into a warm spring after an eternity of freezing in the dark.
From the heart of the orange horizon, a magnificent silhouette glided upward.
The Primordial Phoenix beat its wings, trailing ribbons of liquid solar fire and starlit embers through the void.
It rose with effortless divine elegance, circling her drifting form once, twice, before slowing its descent and gliding directly toward her outstretched arms.
Rika’s emerald eyes dissolved into brilliant molten gold.

"Thank you..." she whispered, her voice cracking with a reverent overwhelming awe as the radiant creature nestled its head against the curve of her neck. "Thank you for choosing someone as broken and small as me... I swear to you, I will never let you starve. I will never let you fall. I will carve an empire worthy of your wings..."
The fledgling phoenix let out a series of high-pitched melodic trills that sounded like silver chimes echoing across an ancient cathedral.
It nuzzled its cheek against her jaw, completely unbothered by her vows as though it was simply content to share its primordial warmth.
As it trilled, intricate glowing glyphs began to etch themselves directly into the fabric of her soul.
They were ancient celestial runes, script from the boundless celestial sea of the higher realms that mortals were never meant to read.
They pulsed along her spiritual collarbones and down her arms, locking her soul to the bird’s eternal cycle.
’What are these...?’ Rika wondered in dazed fascination, watching the golden characters burn softly into her marrow. ’They aren’t beast-mastery seals... they’re...’
POP!
The boundary of the soul realm shattered with the soft elastic snap of displacing mana.
The smell of cedar wood and mountain breeze rushed back into her nose.
"Haa—"
Rika gasped, her eyelids fluttering open as reality slammed back into place.
She was sitting on the floorboards of her private quarters in the Keep of Blessed Land with her knees pressed against the rug.
Her smaller pale hands weren’t clutching empty air... they were warmly enveloped inside a pair of broad calloused palms.
Silas knelt directly before her with his dark hair falling across his forehead and his gold-ringed blue eyes looking down into hers with quiet patient focus.
"You back with me, Rika?" Silas asked gently, his thumbs tracing reassuring circles over the backs of her wrists. "Is everything alright?"
A furious incandescent blush detonated across Rika’s pale cheeks.
’He’s... he’s holding my hands so gently...’
Her heart did a frantic chaotic flip inside her ribs.
Gazing up into his steady unblinking blue eyes, ringed with gold, was almost intoxicating.
It was no cold calculating stare of an auditor and nothing like the leering, hungry gaze of a barbarian evaluating a prize.
It was the look of a devoted lover staring back at his partner attentively.
...It was addictive... Terrifyingly addictive...
’Why...?’ she thought, her breath hitching as her chest grew tight.
This man had taken her into his domain even after discovering her humiliating powerless past.

He had listened to her failures, shrugged them off like dust, and told her that none of it mattered and now... now he had personally placed an SSS-Rank Divine Beast, a Primordial Phoenix egg, into her hands, an impossible treasure that an entire empire of sovereigns would have gone to war to possess, just so she wouldn’t feel useless.
It defied all logic. It went against every single harsh transactional rule of the divine courts.
Thump...!
’Why is my Lord such a dummy...?’
Thump...! Thump...!

’Why didn’t he just cast me aside like everyone else did? Doesn’t he realize that the Goddess of Beasts is a pathetic laughingstock among the pantheons? A disgraced deity who couldn’t even protect her own broods, who was ridiculed by Thor and spat upon by the frost courts?’
Thump...! Thump...! Thump...!
Yet, even knowing every single scrap of her disgrace, he had stood right here.
He had held her trembling hands, wiped her tears away, and promised to build her an apex foundation from the ground up.
’I will never fail you,’ the vow carved itself into her soul in lines of molten iron. ’Never... Not in this life, not in the next...’
Rika didn’t pull her hands back.
Instead, she surged forward on her knees.
Her frame crossed the small distance between them in an instant as she closed her eyes, threw her arms around Silas’s neck, and pressed her soft trembling lips firmly against his mouth.
Behind them, near the closed oak door, Eluned’s emerald eyes went wide as dinner plates.
"R-Rika?!" Eluned gasped, her hands flying to her cheeks in pure shock.
Rika didn’t care... she didn’t want to let go.
FWOOSH!
From her back, a magnificent pair of ethereal golden-red phoenix wings unfolded, wrapping completely around Silas’s shoulders and her own small frame like a protective flaming cocoon.
The incandescent light cast long, dancing shadows across the cedar walls, sealing them together in a private world of celestial warmth.

’I’ll share everything...’ Rika thought with desperate fierce devotion as she deepened the kiss with her smaller tongue hesitantly tracing his lips, offering every scrap of her existence to the man who had redeemed her. ’Every single blessing, every spark of authority, every drop of primordial vitality this beast brings to my soul... I will give it all to my Lord!’
There was no territorial law that forbade sharing divine resonance.
If she was his Hero, then her blessings belonged to him.
The stronger she grew, the more potent the divine flow would become, but why wait?
Why hoard a single drop of this miracle for herself when she could pour it directly into the foundation of the man she adored?
The kiss lingered becoming deep and breathless, until Silas gently rested his hands on her waist, guiding her back so they could draw breath.
A thin glistening strand of saliva bridged the gap between their lips for a fleeting second before snapping.
"Mmh~ So good~"
Silas blinked with his posture stiffening as an intense unnatural vibration rippled through his dantian.
His Gold Core began to beat with ferocious speed... for some reason, the golden sphere began expanding and contracting like a miniature star.
A cascade of crystalline golden system prompts materialized directly in his field of vision.
[Notice: The Blessings of the Primordial Phoenix have been shared with you through divine soul-resonance!]
[You have acquired: Phoenix’s Blessing of Rebirth!]
Effect: Even should your physical vessel suffer absolute destruction, the eternal spark within your soul will cycle death into life, allowing you to resurrect from absolute demise once.
[You have acquired: Phoenix’s Blessing of Flames of Tribulation!]
Effect: Your elemental fire mana has been permanently infused with the conceptual authority of Tribulation!
Silas’s eyes widened slightly.
’Flames of Tribulation...?’ Silas thought, his brow furrowing as he read the title. ’What the hell is that?’
Almost instantly, an expanded explanatory window snapped open beneath the notification.
[Flames of Tribulation (Flames of Misfortune):]

A conceptual sub-element born from the wrath of celestial beings. If you choose to activate it, you may weave the element of Tribulation into your flames... Any target struck by these flames will suffer from catastrophic karmic misfortune, drawing accidents, and disastrous twists of fate upon themselves. The severity and duration of the misfortune scale directly with the depth of your personal hatred and contempt toward the target.
Silas’s breath hitched in his throat.

’Are Phoenixes not supposed to be holy celestial birds of pure grace and healing...?’ Silas mused with a bead of cold sweat forming at his temple as he processed the description. ’Why in the world does an immortal firebird possess an active curse of weaponized bad luck that scales with how much I hate someone?! That’s completely crazy!’
Still, beneath the shock... an appreciative smirk slowly tugged at the corners of his mouth.
He certainly wasn’t going to complain.

Having an extra life in his back pocket via the Blessing of Rebirth was an absurdly broken defensive trump card, and the ability to curse his enemies with literal misfortune just by setting them on fire was a terrifyingly practical utility.
It was a monstrous addition to his combat repertoire.
In front of him, Rika sat back on her heels with her chest heaving, looking up at him with wide anxious green eyes that still carried flecks of gold.
"Is... is it good, my Lord?" she stammered, her voice tiny and trembling. "Are you... are you happy with me?"
Silas chuckled warmly, shaking his head at her nervous vulnerability.
He reached out and placed his palm squarely on top of her head, giving her soft midnight-black hair an affectionate thorough ruffle.
"These blessings are incredible, Rika," Silas said honestly, his smile bright and reassuring. "More than good... You did amazing..."
Rika’s expression completely melted.
Her eyes fluttered half-closed with a soft dazed sigh slipping past her lips as a tiny undignified trail of drool escaped the corner of her mouth.

’His hand...’ she thought, her entire brain turning into sweet warm mush under his palm. ’His headpats feel so impossibly good... It feels like... like his warmth is sinking straight down into my belly... like he’s putting babies inside me just by touching my hair...’
She snapped back to reality with a violent shudder, hurriedly wiping her chin with the sleeve of her tunic with her face burning hotter than her new flames.
"I-I apologize!" she squeaked, bowing her head frantically. "I lost my composure! Forgive me!"
Silas simply laughed, retracting his hand.

Doesn’t he realize that the Goddess of Beasts is a pathetic laughingstock among the pantheons?
A disgraced deity who couldn’t even protect her own broods, who was ridiculed by Thor and spat upon by the frost courts?’
Thump...!
Thump...!
Thump...!
Yet, even knowing every single scrap of her disgrace, he had stood right here.
He had held her trembling hands, wiped her tears away, and promised to build her an apex foundation from the ground up.
’I will never fail you,’ the vow carved itself into her soul in lines of molten iron. ’Never...
Not in this life, not in the next...’
Rika didn’t pull her hands back.
Instead, she surged forward on her knees.
Her frame crossed the small distance between them in an instant as she closed her eyes, threw her arms around Silas’s neck, and pressed her soft trembling lips firmly against his mouth.
Behind them, near the closed oak door, Eluned’s emerald eyes went wide as dinner plates.
"R-Rika?!" Eluned gasped, her hands flying to her cheeks in pure shock.
Rika didn’t care... she didn’t want to let go.
FWOOSH!
From her back, a magnificent pair of ethereal golden-red phoenix wings unfolded, wrapping completely around Silas’s shoulders and her own small frame like a protective flaming cocoon.
The incandescent light cast long, dancing shadows across the cedar walls, sealing them together in a private world of celestial warmth.

’I’ll share everything...’ Rika thought with desperate fierce devotion as she deepened the kiss with her smaller tongue hesitantly tracing his lips, offering every scrap of her existence to the man who had redeemed her. ’Every single blessing, every spark of authority, every drop of primordial vitality this beast brings to my soul...
I will give it all to my Lord!’
There was no territorial law that forbade sharing divine resonance.
If she was his Hero, then her blessings belonged to him.
The stronger she grew, the more potent the divine flow would become, but why wait?
Why hoard a single drop of this miracle for herself when she could pour it directly into the foundation of the man she adored?
The kiss lingered becoming deep and breathless, until Silas gently rested his hands on her waist, guiding her back so they could draw breath.
A thin glistening strand of saliva bridged the gap between their lips for a fleeting second before snapping.
"Mmh~ So good~"
Silas blinked with his posture stiffening as an intense unnatural vibration rippled through his dantian.
His Gold Core began to beat with ferocious speed... for some reason, the golden sphere began expanding and contracting like a miniature star.
A cascade of crystalline golden system prompts materialized directly in his field of vision.
[Notice: The Blessings of the Primordial Phoenix have been shared with you through divine soul-resonance!]
[You have acquired: Phoenix’s Blessing of Rebirth!]
Effect: Even should your physical vessel suffer absolute destruction, the eternal spark within your soul will cycle death into life, allowing you to resurrect from absolute demise once.
[You have acquired: Phoenix’s Blessing of Flames of Tribulation!]
Effect: Your elemental fire mana has been permanently infused with the conceptual authority of Tribulation!
Silas’s eyes widened slightly.
’Flames of Tribulation...?’ Silas thought, his brow furrowing as he read the title. ’What the hell is that?’
Almost instantly, an expanded explanatory window snapped open beneath the notification.
[Flames of Tribulation (Flames of Misfortune):]
A conceptual sub-element born from the wrath of celestial beings.
If you choose to activate it, you may weave the element of Tribulation into your flames...
Any target struck by these flames will suffer from catastrophic karmic misfortune, drawing accidents, and disastrous twists of fate upon themselves.
The severity and duration of the misfortune scale directly with the depth of your personal hatred and contempt toward the target.
Silas’s breath hitched in his throat.

’Are Phoenixes not supposed to be holy celestial birds of pure grace and healing...?’ Silas mused with a bead of cold sweat forming at his temple as he processed the description. ’Why in the world does an immortal firebird possess an active curse of weaponized bad luck that scales with how much I hate someone?!
That’s completely crazy!’
Still, beneath the shock... an appreciative smirk slowly tugged at the corners of his mouth.
He certainly wasn’t going to complain.

Having an extra life in his back pocket via the Blessing of Rebirth was an absurdly broken defensive trump card, and the ability to curse his enemies with literal misfortune just by setting them on fire was a terrifyingly practical utility.
It was a monstrous addition to his combat repertoire.
In front of him, Rika sat back on her heels with her chest heaving, looking up at him with wide anxious green eyes that still carried flecks of gold.
"Is... is it good, my Lord?" she stammered, her voice tiny and trembling.
"Are you... are you happy with me?"
Silas chuckled warmly, shaking his head at her nervous vulnerability.
He reached out and placed his palm squarely on top of her head, giving her soft midnight-black hair an affectionate thorough ruffle.
"These blessings are incredible, Rika," Silas said honestly, his smile bright and reassuring.
"More than good...
You did amazing..."
Rika’s expression completely melted.
Her eyes fluttered half-closed with a soft dazed sigh slipping past her lips as a tiny undignified trail of drool escaped the corner of her mouth.
’His hand...’ she thought, her entire brain turning into sweet warm mush under his palm. ’His headpats feel so impossibly good...
It feels like... like his warmth is sinking straight down into my belly... like he’s putting babies inside me just by touching my hair...’
She snapped back to reality with a violent shudder, hurriedly wiping her chin with the sleeve of her tunic with her face burning hotter than her new flames.
"I-I apologize!" she squeaked, bowing her head frantically.
"I lost my composure!
Forgive me!"
Silas simply laughed, retracting his hand.

chapters.title: Chapter 683: The Goal Is To Prove Them Wrong [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Rika took a deep steadying breath, pressing her palms against her thighs as her expression shifted into fierce determination.

"My Lord, with the fledgling phoenix bonded to my soul, my pathways have reopened... I am going to initiate Spirit Cultivation immediately! If I refine the residual golden mana from the eggshells, I may be able to unlock several of my secondary authorities before nightfall!"

"Do it," Silas nodded, rising smoothly to his feet and offering her a hand up. "Focus on stabilizing your core... After you finish your preliminary cultivation, prepare your travel gear. You’re coming with me to Central City today."
Near the doorway, Eluned instantly puffed her cheeks out, crossing her arms with a pout.
"Hu-bby! I thought you said only Morwenna and Aeliana were accompanying you! I wanted to go to Central City with you, my heart!"

"You need to stay and hold the fort here, Elu," Silas said patiently, turning toward his High Lady with an affectionate knowing look. "Aki is still finding her footing with Vineworld and we need someone to take proper charge here... You’re the Goddess of Blessed Land too, the foundation falls apart without you."
Eluned sighed, though the praise visibly mollified her pride, a soft pleased smile returning to her lips.
Silas turned back to Rika, his expression steady and serious.

"Central City has the largest sovereign exchanges in the realm... With the trade tokens and connections we have, I’m going to secure higher-tier beast contracts for you. We’re going to build your menagerie until you’re back at the peak."
Rika stared at him, her heart swelling with an emotion so intense it felt like it would split her chest open.
Without warning, she dropped to her knees again, bowing her head until her forehead nearly brushed his boots.

"If my Lord requires anything of me... I offer my entire existence!" Rika declared, her voice trembling with passionate devotion. "My soul, my claws, my life! If you desire my body to bear your children, I will gladly offer my womb to you as many times as my Lord pleases! Use me however you see fit!"

"Whoa, whoa, stand up, please," Silas sweatdropped, quickly reaching down to haul her back onto her feet by her elbows. "None of that is necessary right now... We don’t need to barter your womb for beast contracts."
He looked straight into her wide earnest green eyes, his voice dropping into a firm tone.
"Right now, the mission is simple... we have to prove all the people who looked down on you wrong. Right?"
Rika blinked.

"Thor," Silas continued, a dangerous confident smirk playing on his lips, "the other deities who mocked you, the frost goddess who thought you were easy prey... we’re going to make every single one of them eat their words until they choke. Understood?"
Rika’s breath caught.
’Eat their words...’
The phrase echoed through her mind like a battle horn.
The memories of sneering gods and booming laughter in the celestial halls flashed before her, but this time, the cold shame was completely burned away by the golden flame in her chest.
Silas raised his right hand, curling his fingers into a loose fist and Rika didn’t hesitate.
She lifted her own pale fist and bumped it firmly against his knuckles.
"Yes!" she declared, her eyes blazing with fierce, golden-flecked radiance. "We will make them eat every single word!"
A few moments later, Silas and Eluned stepped out into the quiet corridor, the heavy oak door clicking shut behind them.
Inside the room, the sliver of sunlight filtering through the drapes had taken on a rich shimmering golden hue as Rika immediately sat in the lotus position, beginning her spiritual refinement.

"She is remarkably happy, my darling," Eluned murmured, a fond, soft smile gracing her lips as she walked beside him. "I can feel the golden warmth of that primordial bird settling into the Keep’s upper floorboards. It is a good omen..."

"It’s about time she caught a break," Silas said, looking down at his palms. "Once we establish her initial menagerie in Central City, I want to see if we can locate a high-tier wind or shadow beast for Reina as well... If Rika can weave a proper contract for Reina, her stealth arts and aerial reconnaissance will become ten times more lethal."
"Always thinking of your girls," Eluned chuckled softly.
Silas reached down and took her delicate pale hand, his fingers intertwining with hers.
Eluned paused, a lovely blush rising to her cheeks as she looked up at him.

"My heart? What is it? If this is about leaving for Central City, you need not worry. I am not truly angry about staying behind. Though... I wouldn’t mind if you took my camera and captured a few landscapes of the city for me..."
Silas didn’t answer.
Instead, he guided her toward a vacant guest chamber two doors down the hall, turned the brass knob, and pulled her inside.
He kicked the heavy oak door shut behind them with the heel of his boot, the latch clicking into place with a sharp decisive clack.
Before Eluned could speak, Silas stepped forward, catching her by the waist and smoothly shoving her backward toward the massive four-poster feather bed.
Eluned let out a startled breathless gasp as she landed flat on her back amidst the silken cushions with her emerald skirts billowing around her slender thighs.
She looked up at him, her wide green eyes shimmering with a dazed delicious surprise.
Her breath hitched as deep radiant crimson rushed from her collarbones straight to the tips of her pointed ears.
’He pushed me...?’
It was so remarkably rare to see Silas on the aggressive dominating end of their interactions.
Usually, she was the one draping herself over his lap, teasing him with shameless whispered promises, while he stood like an amused unyielding mountain.
But now... standing over the bed, his gold-ringed blue eyes carried a sharp glint that made a delicious liquid shiver shoot straight down her spine.
Silas reached down to his waist, his fingers catching the silver buckle of his leather belt.
Clink!
With slow deliberate agonizing leisure, he unfastened the clasp, sliding the thick leather strap free from the loops of his trousers.

"There’s still an hour before the others finish gathering their gear before we depart," Silas murmured, his voice dropping a bit as he tossed the belt onto a nearby chair. "And since you were complaining earlier about me leaving for Central City without saying a proper goodbye... why don’t we get you full as usual?"
Eluned’s jaw parted with a ragged shuddering gasp catching in her throat.
Her earlier composure shattered completely into pieces.

A bright intoxicating giggle bubbled past her lips as she reached down, gathering the delicate silk hem of her pale robes, and shamelessly spread her long porcelain thighs wide apart across the bedding.
"Oh, you cheeky, insolent boy..." Eluned purred, her voice trembling with adoring delight as she held her arms out toward him. "Come here, then. Fill your lawful wife to the brim."
She hooked one slender leg around his hip as he leaned over her, her fingers curling into his collar to drag his ear down to her lips.

"And don’t you dare be gentle, my darling," she breathed, her voice sounding like a hot honeyed whisper against his skin. "I want to feel you with every single step I take all the way to heaven’s gate~"
Roughly an hour later.
The afternoon sun hung high over the lush, rolling hills of the southern sector of Blessed Land.
A gentle mountain breeze rustled through the emerald canopies of the spirit groves, carrying the sweet clean scent of blooming orchard fruit.
Walking down the wide, crushed-gravel path leading toward the Keep was Silas Graves and Evelyn.
Evelyn was slouched inside her signature oversized dark-gray hoodie, the sleeves hanging well past her fingertips, paired with her frayed denim shorts and heavy scuffed combat boots.

Clamped firmly in her left hand was a massive porcelain bowl piled high with three generous scoops of sweet clotted cream, shaved ice, and candied honey-berries that Silas had pulled from the Keep’s cold pantry.
She held a small silver spoon between two fingers, shoveling sweet cream into her mouth with intense single-minded focus.
"You don’t have to hover right next to me," Evelyn grumbled through a mouthful of frozen berries, not looking up. "Especially when I’m eating. It’s annoying."
Silas walked beside her with his hands resting easily in the pockets of his fresh charcoal trousers, an amused smirk tugging at his lips.
"I’m just making sure you don’t trip over your own boots. You walk like a sleep-deprived zombie when you have food in your hands."

"I walk fine, you arrogant prick," she scoffed, scooping another massive mound of cream. "I survived four war-zones and three sieges on three hours of sleep and bad rations... I think I can handle a gravel footpath."
"Could’ve fooled me," Silas chuckled. "At least I’m not an old woman whose lungs are seventy percent cigarette smoke."
Evelyn’s head whipped around so fast her messy black bun wobbled.
She brandished the silver spoon directly in front of his nose like a dagger, her sharp dark eyes flashing with pure, unadulterated outrage.
"I am NOT an old woman!" she hissed, her voice cracking with indignation. "I am twenty-two! Twenty! Two! That is the literal prime of human youth!"
Silas tilted his head, giving her a deadpan, analytical once-over.
"Twenty-two is basically ancient in cultivator years. You’re practically a grandmother."

"I will stab you in the throat with this spoon," Evelyn snarled, her eye twitching violently as she aggressively shoved another bite of ice cream into her mouth, looking for all the world like she wanted to rip her own hair out. "I swear to the heavens, Graves, if you call me old one more time, I’m charging you five hundred thousand credits for this whole thing..."
Silas burst out laughing, enjoying her predictable outrage as they crested the final lap leading to the Keep’s grand front courtyard.
Waiting near the base of the wide marble steps was their traveling party.
Morwenna stood one hand resting on Tidebringer’s hilt, clad in her dark leather armor beneath a heavy dark-green traveling cloak bearing the crest of Blessed Land embroidered in silver thread.
Beside her stood Aeliana, the Elf princess looking radiant and serene as ever with her pale green robes tucked neatly beneath a matching cloak.
And standing slightly behind them, looking a bit small and self-conscious, was Rika.
The Beast Goddess had washed her face, her wild midnight-black hair brushed into a neat cascade that fell past her shoulder blades.
Clutched closely against her chest, tucked inside the folds of her green cloak, was the fledgling Primordial Phoenix.
The tiny golden-feathered bird poked its head out, its starlit eyes blinking curiously at the open sky, trilling softly whenever Rika gently stroked its nape with her thumb.
Standing at the top of the marble steps, leaning lightly against one of the carved balustrades, was Eluned.
The Goddess of the World Tree looked... distinct.
Her hair was arranged with its usual regal perfection, and her flowing gown was immaculate, but across her pale, porcelain cheeks was a deep distinctly flushed pink that refused to fade.
Furthermore, as she took a slow step forward to greet them, her legs gave a tiny unmistakable wobble with her inner thighs trembling slightly beneath the heavy silk of her skirts.
Silas caught the movement, his mouth twitching as he struggled to maintain a straight face.

’She’s definitely doing that on purpose,’ Silas thought, rolling his eyes in silent amusement. ’Walking with that exaggerated waddle just to make sure every single person in the courtyard knows exactly what went down in that guest room... Unbelievable.’
Eluned glided down the steps, wobble and all, and walked straight up to Silas.
She wrapped her slender arms around his neck, pulling him down into a warm lingering hug.
"Heh."
Elu leaned in, pressing a soft sweet kiss onto the center of his forehead, her lips lingering against his skin with open unabashed tenderness.
"Come back to me in one piece, my heart," Eluned whispered softly, her emerald eyes glowing with radiant devotion.
Silas smiled, reaching up with his index finger and giving the tip of her small elegant nose a playful boop.
"Always," Silas promised.
Eluned giggled, stepping back, and turned her gaze toward the rest of the traveling party.
"Safe travels to you all," Eluned chimed, offering Aeliana and Rika a warm nod.
She turned on her heel, beginning her slow swaying walk back toward the Keep’s grand entrance.
Morwenna’s stormy gray eyes tracked the Lady’s wobbly stride with razor-sharp suspicion.
’Why the hell is she walking like she just survived a cavalry charge...?’ Morwenna thought, her scarred brow furrowing into a deep scowl.

paragraphs: A sudden sharp intuition flared in the back of her pirate skull, followed immediately by the realization that if she actually asked aloud, she was going to hear an answer that would make her want to gouge her own ears out with a shucking knife...
Before Morwenna could even look away, Eluned paused at the heavy oak doors.
The Lady turned her head over her shoulder, caught Morwenna’s glare, and offered her a sweet venomous smile.
"Farewell, virgin~" Eluned purred.

SLAM!
The massive mahogany doors swung shut, the latch clicking into place.

Her face turned a violent shade of purple-red.
Her fingers clenched around Tidebringer’s hilt so hard that the leather groaned under the pressure with her knuckles turning bone-white.
She looked genuinely on the verge of ripping out handfuls of her own hair and screaming a stream of profanity loud enough to shatter the clouds.
"THAT OVERGROWN HOUSEPLANT—!" Morwenna roared, Tidebringer’s tip swinging toward the door.
"Morwenna, breathe," Silas chuckled, placing a firm, calming hand on her shoulder armor. "Save the aggression for Central City."
He turned toward the Elf princess.
"Aeli, take us to the coordinates... In front of the Wall."
Aeliana smiled serenely as she was accustomed to the domestic chaos.
She raised her right hand and snapped her fingers.
SNAP!
Space warped around the entire group, folding the coordinates of Blessed Land in a single heartbeat.
FLASH!
The spatial displacement cleared with a rush of cold high-altitude wind as the lush green hills and floral scents of Blessed Land vanished, replaced by the vast rugged expanse of the Umbral Basin.
Standing before them, squatting across the badlands on its massive steel treads, was The Unmovable Wall.
Three stories of blackened iron-plated hull rose above the rock.
Silas had laid eyes on the mobile fortress several times now, but every encounter still carried a distinct weight.

Each colossal tread plate stood as tall as a house, and above them the armored hull bristled with heavy defense turrets and long-range rail-cannons recessed into the plating, their crystalline targeting arrays humming with a low vibration that traveled straight through the soles of their boots.
The glowing iron emblem of the Wall burned across the bow.
Evelyn swallowed the last spoonful of her ice cream, tossing the empty porcelain bowl into her spatial inventory with a practiced flick of her wrist.
She reached into the deep pouch of her dark hoodie, pulling out a heavy matte-black full-face helmet constructed from dense, vacuum-sealed mythril alloy.
The visor was a strip of opaque, dark-red polarized glass, fitted with internal rune-modulators that disguised voice, breathing, and facial heat signatures.
"Alright," Evelyn said, her voice dropping into a brisk, business-like tone. "Let’s put on our masks... The moment we step into it, we’ll be on our way to Central City."
She lifted the helmet and slid it over her messy bun.
Psssshhhh-CLACK!
The pneumatic seals engaged with a pressurized hiss.
In an instant, the petite tired foul-mouthed twenty-two-year-old girl in an oversized hoodie ceased to exist...
Standing before them was Lord Sky, the legendary cold thirty-year-old male commander of the Unmovable Wall.
The posture shifted entirely, adopting the wide imposing stance of an iron-fisted veteran who had been viewed by millions of followers through his many streams, defeating lords effortlessly.
Silas reached into his coat pocket, pulling out a sleek translucent silver ring inscribed with subtle shifting illusion runes.
It was the dual-polarity Disguise Artifact, forged by Thora’s father in the Underground Mountain Realm, and the exact paired counterpart of the masculine helmet Evelyn had just put on.
He slipped the band onto his right index finger.
Flicker!
A subtle prismatic shimmer rolled down his frame.
His dark hair lengthened and deepened into glossy black.
His features softened into the delicate lines of Kara White with a violet shimmer blooming in both eyes, and his left arm vanished into a neatly pinned sleeve.
His charcoal clothes smoothed into the pristine tailored cut of an elite, complete with subtle shimmering gold filigree along the lapels.

Beside him, Morwenna, Aeliana, and Rika pulled their heavy green traveling cloaks tight, adjusting their deep hoods until their faces were cast in impenetrable shadow, obscuring their features beneath the crest of Blessed Land.
HUUUUUUUUUM!
High above on the flank of the mobile fortress, a massive pressurized bulkhead groaned.

A wide hydraulic ramp slowly descended from the armor plating, clanking against the rocky ground with a heavy metallic thud, revealing the illuminated corridor leading into the heart of the fortress’s spatial jump chambers.
Lord Sky turned with the voice modulator projecting a deep baritone that carried the chill of steel.
"The path is clear... Let’s move."
Kara White smiled, smoothing the pinned left sleeve of her pristine coat, and turned toward the cloaked figures behind her.
"Alright, ladies," Kara said smoothly, her voice carrying the calm, effortless swagger of a woman stepping into her element. "Let’s head inside... Central City is waiting."
The massive hydraulic ramp shuddered, groaning under pneumatic pressure as it retracted into the fortified underbelly of the mobile fortress.

Behind them, the colossal exterior bulkheads sealed shut with a series of heavy echoing thuds, cutting off the wild howling of the northern badlands and plunging the entry bay into the steady mechanical hum of pressurized mana-generators.

’Thankfully I already placed the tile in the Keep so I’m okay...’ Silas thought, after asking the System a few questions, he had managed to make sure that he would be able to plant the tile’s exit coordinates in Central City. ’I wonder where I should put it...’
He couldn’t let the World Council be able to access it after all.

The entry bay opened into the lower industrial holds becoming a maze of steel girders, automated overhead cranes and reinforced containment vaults, and beyond it the main corridor ran paved with interlocking sheets of cold vulcanized steel, lit by long recessed strips of pale cerulean runes along the vaulted ceiling.
Everywhere they looked, personnel were moving with practiced military precision.
Infantry in dark plate, artificers bearing runic wrenches and diagnostic slates, and logistics officers clutching thick ledgers bustled past with their boots ringing crisply against the metal floor.
The moment the imposing figure in the mythril armor and dark-red visor stepped off the ramp, the bustling corridor snapped to attention.
"Lord Sky!"
Crisp salutes rippled through the ranks.
Both male and female troops halted mid-stride, their fists clattering against their breastplates in uniform reverence to the commander of the Unmovable Wall.
Lord Sky offered a disciplined nod.
"At ease. Finalize all cargo stabilization... We initiate the long-range spatial jump within the hour."
"Sir! Yes, sir!" the soldiers chorused, immediately scattering back to their stations with renewed urgency.
Sky turned slightly, gesturing down the wide, illuminated central spine of the vessel.

"I didn’t show you this sector the last time you boarded." His voice rumbled, directing Kara and her cloaked entourage past a secondary security checkpoint lined with heavy kinetic turrets. "This spine connects the lower maintenance rings straight to the primary bridge and control center... It’s where every navigational array, shield node, and dimensional anchor is monitored in real time."
Kara adjusted the pinned left sleeve of her impeccably tailored coat, stepping lightly over the steel threshold.
Her black hair swayed softly against her collar, and her purple eyes scanned the dense conduit lines humming behind reinforced glass with quiet interest.

"Impressive engineering," Kara murmured smoothly, her melodious feminine voice carrying an effortless relaxed swagger. "Though I have to ask... doesn’t living in a massive tin can full of grinding gears and humming conduits get exhausting after a while? You’re surrounded by cold metal twenty-four hours a day."
Sky rolled his armored shoulders with a faint clink of overlapping plates.
"You get used to it. Metal doesn’t rot, metal doesn’t complain, and when three tons of explosive ordnance hit your bedroom wall, thick plating is remarkably comforting compared to garden hedges."
"To each their own," Kara replied with a low amused chuckle. "I’ll take the scent of pine needles and fresh soil over burning machine oil any day."
Behind them, Morwenna, Aeliana, and Rika followed in tight formation, their heavy dark-green cloaks drawn closely around their frames.

The insignia of Blessed Land catching the blue overhead light as beneath her hood, Rika kept both hands tucked against her midsection, cradling the tiny fledgling phoenix resting warm against her collarbone, while Morwenna’s hand never strayed far from Tidebringer’s hilt with her pirate instincts constantly measuring the width of the blast doors.
They reached the end of the central spine, where a pair of reinforced obsidian doors stood framed by complex hydraulic locks.
Sky stepped forward, raising an armored palm toward the polished crystalline panel mounted at eye level.
BZZZZ-CHIRP!
A grid of crimson scanning beams swept across the mythril gauntlet, reading the intricate bio-mana frequencies woven into the suit.
[Biometric Signature Verified: Commander ’Lord Sky’.]
[Welcome to the Command Bridge.]
With a deep hiss, the obsidian doors parted down the center, sliding into the bulkheads to reveal the command center.
The room was broad, occupying the highest forward deck on the fortress’s third story.

A sweeping panoramic observation window composed of multi-layered reinforced quartz curved across the entire front wall, offering an unobstructed view of the rugged basin stretching toward the horizon.
In the center of the chamber sat an elevated command dais surrounded by sunken pit-consoles, where dozens of specialist operators tapped away at glowing interfaces.
Holographic charts, frequency maps, and telemetry readouts floated lazily through the air, casting a vibrant cerulean glow over the polished steel decking.
"Take your seats," Sky commanded, gesturing toward the semi-circular row of high-backed leather chairs arranged near the primary hololithic table.
Standing beside the central tactical console was a woman they hadn’t seen during the chaotic clashes of the Lord War.
She wore a fitted officer’s uniform of dark navy and silver, her sharp, focused eyes glowing with faint amber calculation runes as she tracked three separate floating displays simultaneously.
The moment Sky stepped onto the dais, the officer snapped a rigid, textbook salute.

"Command Bridge fully synchronized, Lord Sky. All secondary turbines are pre-heated, kinetic baffles are pressurized to maximum tolerance, and the dimensional jump array is primed to coordinate specs..."
"Good work," Sky nodded, walking past and sinking into the high-backed captain’s chair in the center of the dais.

Kara smoothly took the seat directly to Sky’s right, crossing one elegant silk-clad leg over the other, while Morwenna, Aeliana, and Rika filed into the adjacent chairs with their eyes scanning the strange machinery in sharp fascination.
A heavy latch clicked on the starboard elevator lift, and a handful of figures stepped onto the bridge.
"Lord Sky!"
Elm bounded forward with a cheerful spring in every step, her long white hair swaying behind her and her bright silver eyes practically sparkling.
A warm affectionate smile lit up her face as she offered an enthusiastic wave to her commander before plopping into the seat beside Sky’s chair.
Her silver eyes slid over to Kara, and her smile softened into something grateful.
She dipped her head in the smallest of bows.
...Elm hadn’t forgotten who had pulled her out of that glass tank.
Behind her came Hiro, Kassandra, and two women in long white cloaks.
Hiro, the tall blindfolded swordsman, moved as still and disciplined as a drawn line.
The black blindfold sat securely across his eyes, and the hilt of his massive double-edged broadsword rose over one shoulder, its sheath strapped across his back.
Despite the blindness obscuring his vision, his posture was faultless, moving through the labyrinth of consoles without a single wasted motion.
He halted three paces before Sky’s chair, dropping to one knee, his head bowed low in solemn contrition.
"Master. I offer my deepest apologies for my disgraceful performance during the Lord War... I failed to hold the perimeter and allowed dishonor to fall upon the—"
"Save it, Hiro," Sky’s synthesized voice cut in calmly, raising a hand to stall the apology. "We’ll review combat later, stand up and take your station."
Hiro paused, bowing his head once more before rising smoothly.
"Understood, Master."
He turned, his blindfold tilting toward Kara and her cloaked entourage, offering a courteous nod before stepping into the shadow of the central tactical pillar.
Kassandra stepped forward next, tall and straight-backed in her pink-tinted tower armor with her helm tucked under one arm and the Divine Aegis tower shield strapped across her back.
She stopped before Kara and the cloaked girls, set a fist over her breastplate, and bowed deeply.

"Lady White, Blessed Land has my thanks," she said, her voice steady and sincere. "After we lost, your people could have chained us. Instead they fed us, healed our wounded, and gave us beds. Even your maids... the one who served me could probably flatten a platoon, and she still smiled while she handed me a chicken thigh that tasted like heaven. I won’t forget it."
